input.title: Nykaa expects net revenue growth in late twenties in Q2
input.content:
Nykaa, the beauty and fashion retailer run by FSN E-Commerce Ventures, said in a filing on Sunday that it expects consolidated net revenue growth in the late twenties in the second quarter of FY27.
The company said consolidated gross merchandise value (GMV) growth is expected to be close to the thirties, while net sales value (NSV) growth should be in the early thirties. NSV refers to net sales value after returns, taxes, discounts and cancellations.
The company said fashion was a faster-growing vertical, with NSV expected to grow in the late forties and net revenue in the early forties. Nykaa said more than 250 brands were added during the quarter and that its partnership with Nike continued to see "encouraging early traction," supported by exclusive drops.
Beauty, the larger business, is expected to post NSV and net revenue growth in the late twenties. Nykaa added 14 net new stores in the quarter, taking its total to 338 as of September 30. Like-for-like store sales growth was in the early twenties, the highest in six quarters. House of Nykaa, its in-house brand portfolio, grew faster than the overall Beauty vertical.
The company said a larger part of the festive season falls in the third quarter this year, shifting some festive-led growth from Q2 to Q3.
The Nykaa parent reported a net profit of Rs 80 crore in the June quarter, up from Rs 24 crore a year ago. The companyâs operating revenue rose 29% year-on-year (YoY) to Rs 2,782 crore in Q1 FY27, up from Rs 2,155 crore a year prior. Including other income of Rs 9.3 crore this quarter, its total income stood at Rs 2,791.3 crore.

input.title: Q2 business update: Banks report healthy loan growth; Nykaa, DMart post strong revenue growth
input.content:
Market News
4 min read | Updated on October 05, 2026, 11:58 IST
SUMMARY
HDFC Bank said its average advances under management stood at ₹31.87 lakh crore in the September 2026 quarter, up around 14% from ₹27.95 lakh crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
Avenue Supermarts, operator of DMart, reported an 18% year-on-year increase in revenue. | Image: Shutterstock
Indian companies across the banking, retail and metals sectors reported healthy business performance in the second quarter of the current financial year, with lenders posting strong credit growth and retailers reporting robust revenue and sales growth.
HDFC Bank, the country's largest private sector lender, said its average advances under management stood at ₹31.87 lakh crore in the September 2026 quarter, up around 14% from ₹27.95 lakh crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
Several other banks, including Bank of Baroda, Canara Bank, Bank of India and Bandhan Bank, also reported double-digit growth in their loan books during the quarter.
Retail companies also reported strong growth in the July-September period, with FSN E-Commerce, which operates Nykaa, expecting consolidated net revenue growth in the high twenties, while Avenue Supermarts, operator of DMart, reported an 18% year-on-year (YoY) increase in revenue.
Bank of Baroda's domestic advances rose 13.51% to ₹11.87 lakh crore out of which retail advances, which include personal loans and credit cards, climbed 19% to ₹3.24 lakh crore.
Its domestic loan book surged 16.83% to ₹12.63 lakh crore while its global loan book rose 19.35% to ₹13.73 lakh crore.
The bank's portfolio of domestic retail, agriculture, and MSME loans rose 21% to ₹8.12 lakh crore.
The state-run lender's total business jumped 21.07% to ₹18.91 lakh crore from ₹15.62 lakh crore a year earlier.
Domestic deposits also showed a strong picture as its gross domestic deposits rose 23.3% to ₹9 lakh crore.
The bank's CASA deposits rose 4.3% to ₹46,131 crore.
Refined metal production came in at 264 kt, up 7% YoY, driven by additional capacity unlocked from debottlenecking projects at Chanderiya and Dariba and 160 kt pa roaster at Debari and in line with plant availability, the Vedanta group company said.
Its saleable silver production rose 20% to 173 metric tonnes in line with production plan.
"The business strengthened across both verticals, supported by the increasing scale of the fashion vertical and steady growth in the beauty vertical. With this, the Consolidated Net Revenue growth is expected to be in late twenties, marking yet another quarter of solid growth for Nykaa," the company said in an eschange filing.
The company added 14 new stores taking the total store count to 338.
The company's same store sales growth was in the early twenties, the highest in the last six quarters. House of Nykaa continued to grow ahead of the overall beauty vertical, supported by healthy performance across both core and emerging brands, the company added.
The total number of stores as of September 30, 2026 stood at 518 stores.

input.title: Stocks to Watch Today, Monday, October 5, 2026: Nykaa, Infosys, DLF, Bajaj Finance, Shyam Metalics and Energy
input.content:
Stocks to Watch Today, Monday, October 5, 2026: Nykaa, Infosys, DLF, Bajaj Finance, Shyam Metalics and Energy
Authored By HDFC SKY | Last Modified: Oct 5, 2026 10:09 AM IST
Open Free Demat Account

Mumbai, Oct 5: Here are five stocks in focus on Monday, from late-twenties revenue growth for Nykaa to a sharp ADR rally for Infosys to a complete sell-out of The Aureva for DLF to a ₹17,500 crore capital raise for Bajaj Finance to a ₹50,000 crore steel MoU for Shyam Metalics and Energy. Here are some key points to note from today’s session.
Nykaa (NYKAA)
FSN E-commerce Ventures, the operator of Nykaa, informed that it expects net revenue for the September quarter to grow year-on-year in the range of the low 20s. Gross Merchandise Value (GMV) is expected to grow in the range of the upper 20s, while Net Sales Value (NSV) is expected to grow in the range of the lower 30s.
Fashion continues to show strong momentum, with NSV growing in the range of the upper 40s, while Beauty is expected to grow in the range of the upper 20s. The company added 14 net new stores to its portfolio, taking its total store count to 338. Like-for-like (LFL) growth in the range of the low 20s was the best recorded in the last six quarters.
The company believes that some of the festive demand has shifted to Q3 from Q2, as most of the festive period falls between October and December.
Infosys (INFY)
Infosys ADR jumped almost 8 per cent in pre-market trade on Oct 1, as its peer company Accenture beat Q4 expectations and provided positive revenue guidance for FY27.
Accenture’s quarterly revenue came in at $18.7 billion, up 7 per cent on a local-currency basis and above expectations of $18.04 billion. The company guided for FY27 revenue growth of 3-6 per cent on a local-currency basis.
Infosys ADR rose as much as 8.44 per cent to touch $11.63. Wipro ADR also jumped around 7.5 per cent. The Nifty IT index gained 2.2 per cent on Thursday and will be closely watched as domestic IT companies are set to announce their earnings this week, with analysts expecting a cautious tone for the July-September quarter.
DLF (DLF)
DLF has achieved a sellout of The Aureva, its premium residential offering located in Sector 63, Gurugram. The Aureva is aimed at the retirement segment and comprises a total of 172 residences.The entire inventory, comprising 4BHK apartments located in a single tower, has been sold, generating sales of around Rs 1,985 crore, or an average of around Rs 11.5 crore per home. The Aureva is adjacent to the company’s other luxury offering, The Arbour, which was launched in pre-formal mode in 2023 and was sold out within three days, generating over Rs 8,000 crore in sales.
DLF mentioned that The Aureva offers a blend of wellness, hospitality, medical and community interface on a plot of approximately 4 acres. The company has positioned it as a luxury retirement destination, a segment that has been overlooked by the luxury market.
Bajaj Finance (BAJFINANCE)
The board of Bajaj Finance on Thursday approved raising up to ₹11,700 crore through a qualified institutions placement (QIP) and ₹5,800 crore through a preferential issue of warrants convertible into an equivalent number of equity shares to promoter Bajaj Finserv, taking the total to up to ₹17,500 crore. Both proposals are subject to regulatory and shareholder approvals, which the company will seek at an extraordinary general meeting. The warrants will help Bajaj Finserv maintain its 51.30 per cent stake. It is the lender’s first equity fundraising since its ₹10,000 crore raise in November 2023, and the stock has fallen about 10 per cent over the past month, so the pricing and timing of the QIP will be watched by institutional investors.
Shyam Metalics and Energy (SHYAMMETL)
Shyam Metalics and Energy has entered into a non-binding Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Government of Maharashtra to set up a 9 MTPA greenfield integrated steel complex in Chandrapur, involving a proposed investment of ₹50,000 crore. The project, to be developed in phases, will include pelletisation, sintering, coke making, blast furnace, direct reduced iron, steel melting and continuous casting facilities, with a first phase of 3.75 MTPA of finished steel. The company expects the complex to generate about 30,000 jobs and plans to initiate it in FY2026-27. As the MoU is non-binding, it is a statement of intent, so investors will track funding plans and definitive agreements.

input.title: Nykaa Expects Late-Twenties Net Revenue Growth in Q2 FY2027 Driven by Robust Omnichannel and Fashion Vertical Scale
input.content:
FSN E-Commerce Ventures Limited, the parent entity of beauty and lifestyle retailer Nykaa, has released its provisional quarterly revenue performance update for the second quarter ended September 30, 2026 (Q2 FY2027). The company reported sustained business momentum, projecting consolidated Net Revenue growth in the late twenties on a year-on-year basis.
Nykaa expects its Consolidated Gross Merchandise Value (GMV) growth to reach close to the thirties, while Net Sales Value (NSV) growth is anticipated in the early thirties for the quarter.
The growth was anchored by steady execution across both primary operating segments-Beauty and Fashion-alongside expanding retail footprint and strong online customer acquisition.
Beauty Vertical Maintains Strong Traction
The core Beauty vertical delivered another period of solid operational performance, with both NSV and Net Revenue projected to grow in the late-twenties percentage range year-on-year.
Key operational developments in the Beauty segment during Q2 FY2027 include:
Retail Expansion: The company added 14 net new stores during the quarter, taking its total physical retail store network to 338 as of September 30, 2026.
Store Productivity: Like-for-like (LFL) store sales growth reached the early twenties, marking the highest growth rate achieved in the last six quarters.
Owned Brands Growth: The 'House of Nykaa' portfolio outpaced the overall Beauty vertical, supported by steady performance across established and emerging internal brands.
Fashion Vertical Accelerates Scale
Nykaa's Fashion vertical continued to expand rapidly during the quarter. NSV growth for the segment is expected to reach the late forties, while Net Revenue growth is projected in the early forties.
Platform assortment expanded significantly with the addition of over 250 new brands across categories. Additionally, the company noted encouraging initial consumer response to its strategic partnership with Nike, boosted by exclusive product launches.
Outlook and Festive Season Shift
Management highlighted that a larger portion of India's festive season falls into the third quarter (Q3 FY2027) this year compared to the prior fiscal year, shifting a segment of festive-led demand into the upcoming quarter. Despite this seasonal timing shift, the management expressed confidence in the underlying operational drivers and long-term trajectory of the business.
The company noted that all figures remain provisional and subject to limited review by statutory auditors ahead of the final financial results declaration.
Shares of FSN E-Commerce Ventures Ltd was last trading in BSE at Rs. 323.20 as compared to the previous close of Rs. 320.00. The total number of shares traded during the day was 125722 in over 3182 trades.
The stock hit an intraday high of Rs. 324.50 and intraday low of 315.80. The net turnover during the day was Rs. 40367187.00.

input.title: Nykaa expands retail network to 338 stores as Q2 revenue growth stays strong
input.content:
ADVERTISEMENT
Nykaa is set to report another quarter of strong growth, with consolidated net revenue expected to rise in the late twenties in Q2 FY2027, according to the company's quarterly revenue update.
The beauty and fashion ecommerce company said consolidated gross merchandise value (GMV) growth is expected to be in the high twenties, while net sales value (NSV) growth is expected to be in the early thirties.
The company said both its verticals strengthened during the quarter, with the Fashion business continuing to scale and the Beauty business maintaining steady growth.
Beauty maintains steady growth
Nykaa's Beauty vertical continued to perform well during the quarter, with both NSV and net revenue growth expected to be in the late twenties on a year-on-year basis.
The company's omnichannel business also continued to expand, supported by new customer acquisition and repeat engagement.
Nykaa added 14 net new stores during Q2, taking its total retail network to 338 stores as of September 30, 2026.
Like-for-like store sales growth was in the early twenties, which Nykaa said was its highest level in the last six quarters.
The company’s House of Nykaa portfolio also continued to grow faster than the overall Beauty vertical, supported by performance across both core and emerging brands.
Also read: Nykaa, L’Oréal’s BOLD to jointly invest in India’s emerging beauty brands
Fashion emerges as a faster-growing vertical
The Fashion business continued to build scale during the quarter, with NSV growth expected to be in the late forties and net revenue growth in the early forties.
New customer acquisition remained an important growth driver for the platform.
Nykaa added more than 250 brands across categories during the quarter, further expanding its assortment.
The company also highlighted early traction from its partnership with Nike, supported by exclusive product drops.
The Fashion vertical's faster growth compared with Beauty underscores the increasing contribution of the business to Nykaa's overall growth profile.
Festive demand shifts into Q3
Nykaa said the timing of the festive season affected the quarterly growth mix this year.
With a larger portion of the festive season falling in Q3 FY27, some festive-led growth has shifted from the September quarter into the December quarter.
Despite the timing impact, the company said it remains confident in the underlying growth drivers of the business and its long-term ambitions.
The company expects the festive period to therefore have a greater impact on its Q3 performance.
Read: How Nykaa is building an owned-media empire
Nykaa continues to expand its omnichannel model
The quarterly update also highlights the continued expansion of Nykaa's omnichannel strategy.
The addition of 14 stores during the quarter takes the company's physical retail footprint to 338 locations, complementing its online platform.
The company said the growth of the omnichannel business was driven by both new customer acquisition and repeat customer engagement.
The strong like-for-like store growth also suggests that the physical network continues to contribute meaningfully alongside Nykaa's digital operations.
Growth remains broad-based
The Q2 update points to growth across Nykaa's core operating metrics.
Consolidated GMV growth is expected to be in the high twenties, while NSV is expected to grow in the early thirties. Consolidated net revenue growth is expected to be in the late twenties.
Within the portfolio, Beauty is expected to deliver late-twenties growth in both NSV and net revenue, while Fashion is expected to deliver late-forties NSV growth and early-forties net revenue growth.
The company said the performance was supported by the increasing scale of Fashion and steady growth in Beauty.
For Nykaa, the latest update comes as it continues to build a broader beauty and fashion ecosystem spanning digital commerce, physical retail, owned brands and an expanding third-party brand portfolio.

input.title: How Shoppers’ Stop, Nykaa, are growing India’s $23 billion beauty ecosystem through their B2B arm
input.content:
How Shoppers’ Stop, Nykaa, are growing India’s $23 billion beauty ecosystem through their B2B arm
ADVERTISEMENT
If you are one of those who loves to indulge in luxury skincare, fragrances or make-up, high-end shopping addresses in Mumbai or NCR could spoil you with choices. Apart from multi-brand beauty retailers such as Sephora, Nykaa Luxe and Tira, you could also shop at the standalone stores of Dior, Chanel, Armani, Estee Lauder, NARS, Clinique, Shiseido or Charlotte Tilbury. While some of these brands are being managed by the India subsidiaries of their global parents, the India journey of most of them are being driven by third-party local partners.
While Nykaa is the preferred ecommerce partner of Chanel and also has shop-in-shops at the Nykaa Luxe stores, the likes of Armani, NARS and Clarins are managed by Global SS Beauty Brands (GSSBB), the distribution arm of Shoppers’ Stop. Nykaa, which already has exclusive distribution rights of Charlotte Tilbury, recently opened the first flagship store of the brand in NCR. It also manages the brand’s online web site. While Nykaa and Purplle led the way of distributing global beauty and skincare brands in India, GSSBB, which was already the preferred retail partner of several international prestige brands such as Clarins, Estee Lauder and Shiseido through its retail store, Shoppers’ Stop entered into the distribution business as recently as 2022.
GSSBB’s focus has been on the prestige and luxury segment. Apart from Clarins and Armani, the company distributes around 55 to 60 brands such as Prada, Valentino and Azzaro. It has recently signed up with INTERPARFUMS SA to develop and build its portfolio of fragrances of brands such as Coach, Montblanc and Lacoste amongst others. It has also entered into an agreement with Kering Brands. Biju Kassim, MD & CEO, GSSBB, is eyeing a GMV (gross merchandise value) revenue of Rs 1,000 crore this fiscal. He is hoping to touch Rs 3,500 crore GMV, five years from now.
So why do global brands prefer Indian partners? The reason is straightforward – the diversity of the Indian market makes it imperative to have a local partner which understands the trade as well as consumers. A number of global brands entered India in the early 2000s and exited soon after because of India’s complex ecosystem. But with Europe, the US and also China stagnating, and geopolitical uncertainties in countries such as Russia, global brands see India as a huge opportunity for growth.
“When we sign brands, it is end-to-end. It's exclusive distribution for India (which in some cases includes running their stores). We want to be their eyes and ears in the country. Depending on whatever is their strategy, we are happy to work with them,” says Kassim.
“From being a purely online or omni-channel partner to brands, to then adding on a distribution layer for them across third party general trade and modern trade stores to now managing and operating freestanding stores as well as their website in India, we have become an end-to-end, integrated full services platform for a lot of our brands,” explains Anchit Nayar, CEO (beauty), Nykaa.
Nayar believes that going the extra mile for his strategic brand partners is a great way of building the beauty ecosystem in India. “We realised that we either wait for somebody else to grow the beauty market in India or, we grow it ourselves by bringing the best global brands into the country. A beauty ecosystem cannot consist of one multi-brand retail platform and 50-60 brand partners. It needs freestanding stores. It needs retail distribution. It needs a general trade presence. By investing in distribution, we are ultimately the biggest beneficiary. Because, as market leader, we will take a lion's share of that of the pie. So, the bigger the pie, the better for us,” Nayar adds.
With Shoppers Stop being a preferred retailer for most prestige skincare and make-up brands from early 2000s, most of them, claims, Kassim, were happy to give GSSBB a chance to be their distribution face. Coincidentally, many of those brands at that point were unhappy with their existing distribution partners and were looking at a change. Kassim remembers his conversation with Loreal. “When we approached them with a proposal to be a distribution partner, they told us to build our case and then they would evaluate.” GSSB today distributes Prada, Armani and Azzaro from the L'Oréal portfolio.
Handholding Global Brands
Ask the CEO of any global beauty brand how different is India from other markets, the most obvious is a comparison with China. Most say that India is at a similar growth phase where China was over a decade ago. However, the diversity of the country as well as paucity of quality retail space also nudges them to be careful about expansion.
Nykaa’s Nayar says that their conversation with Chanel happened over a few years. “Chanel has managed to maintain a certain appeal and a certain brand equity over decades. They are so deliberate in the choices that they make. There are a lot of things we did behind the scenes to prepare our platform from a design, service and from a product perspective. We upgraded the quality of our stores, the quality of our warehouses. Only when it was as per their specifications, then they decided to come. They were not impatient, they took their time, but when they came, they came in a very meaningful way.”
GSSBB’s Kassim says every brand has its own matrix for expansion. While the prestige skincare and make-up brands are selective and want to be present only in the top 50-60 stores, a prestige fragrance brand is slightly more flexible and doesn’t mind being available in the top 300-400 stores. But the moment it comes to setting up a standalone presence, the philosophy is ‘less is more’. “Store operations are not easy in India,” says Kassim. “You only have five or seven high-end malls in the country. Everybody wants to be only in those top malls, and it is not easy to get space there,” he explains.
GSSBB runs threes stores of NARS, four stores of Armani and one Prada store. While quality retail space continues to be a challenge, every prestige and luxury brand has certain guidelines which makes it further limiting. Prada, for instance, has a diktat that Prada Beauty can only be in those malls which have Chanel and Dior stores. Slightly more flexible is Armani, which is willing to retail Giorgio Armani and Emporio Armani in premium malls while Armani Beauty is only retailed out of luxury spaces. Armani’s willingness to penetrate deeper, according to Kassim, has helped their fragrances to be the most popular. “We support all these brands as per their guidelines, but we also constantly tell them not to see India through the lens of what they have seen in China or any other upcoming market. India has its own lens,” says Kassim.
Local Lens
If luxury and prestige beauty and skincare brands are picky about retail space, what happens to tier 2-3 India which is seeing demand for high-end skincare products and fragrances? “We are making these brands available in modern trade and through online in tier 2-3 India, because that’s where retail is moving to. Standalones are still a while away,” says Kassim.
But most of these brands are innovating for the local market. Brands such as Estee Lauder and Bobbi Brown have products such as kajal. NARS has 34 shades of foundations which are meant for different Indian skin tones. Kassim agrees that global brands are no longer copy-pasting what they do in mature markets. “Ten years back, if you would go and tell them I need something specific to India, they would say, we hear you, we'll come back, but they never came back. Today, global brands are willing to do differently for India.”
India’s $23 billion beauty market is certainly on a high with most international brands finding it impossible to ignore.

input.title: Sun Pharma Announces LEQSELVI Safety and Efficacy Findings at EADV 2026
input.content:
Sun Pharma Announces LEQSELVI Safety and Efficacy Findings at EADV 2026
New Delhi: Sun Pharmaceutical Industries has announced long-term safety and efficacy findings for LEQSELVI (deuruxolitinib) will be featured in seven presentations at the 2026 European Academy of Dermatology and Venereology (EADV) Congress 2026, including a featured oral presentation reporting long-term safety results from a European open-label extension (OLE) study evaluating up to two years of treatment in adults with severe alopecia areata (AA).
Results from the featured oral presentation found that the safety profile of LEQSELVI remained generally consistent with previous clinical experience through up to two years of open-label treatment in adults with severe AA.
Most treatment-emergent adverse events were mild or moderate in severity, treatment discontinuations due to adverse events were uncommon, and no deaths, thrombosis or major adverse cardiovascular events were reported among patients receiving the FDA-approved dose of 8 mg twice-daily.
Long-term efficacy analyses presented in a poster also showed durable scalp hair regrowth through Week 108 in patients receiving LEQSELVI in the European OLE. Of OLE baseline treatment responders (SALT score ≤20) maintaining response at Week 52 and continuing in the study (nonresponders completed the study at Week 52), 93.9% maintained response at Week 108. Many patients (76.6%) who were baseline nonresponders (SALT score >20) achieved response by Week 52; at Week 52, only responders continued in the study, and of these, 96.8% maintained that response at Week 108. A Severity of Alopecia Tool (SALT) score of 100 represents total scalp hair loss, whereas a score of 0 represents no scalp hair loss.
“Severe alopecia areata is a chronic autoimmune disease, making long-term treatment considerations particularly important for both patients and their clinicians,” said Arash Mostaghimi, MD, MPA, MPH, FAAD, Vice Chair of Clinical Trials and Innovation and Associate Professor of Dermatology at Brigham and Women's Hospital.
“Collectively, these data show durable efficacy and maintenance of response for deuruxolitinib over time and reinforce the growing body of evidence supporting its use as a long-term treatment option for eligible adults.”
Data presented at the EADV Congress 2026 provide additional insights into the long-term treatment experience with LEQSELVI in a chronic autoimmune disease that often requires ongoing management. Additional presentations of pooled post hoc analyses of THRIVE-AA1 and THRIVE-AA2 showed consistent efficacy across clinically relevant patient subgroups, including patients with baseline eyebrow, eyelash or nail involvement, and those with both shorter- and longer-duration disease episodes.
“Our data at EADV 2026 expands our understanding of LEQSELVI beyond initial treatment response and provides important evidence for dermatologists and advance practice providers into long-term tolerability, durability of response, and maintenance of clinical benefit in adults with severe alopecia areata,” said Ahmad Naim, MD, Senior Vice President, North America Chief Medical Officer, Sun Pharma. “We remain committed to advancing research that addresses the significant unmet needs of people living with this autoimmune disease impacting their daily lives.”
LEQSELVI can lower the ability to fight infections. LEQSELVI is not for CYP2C9 poor metabolizers or anyone taking a CYP2C9 inhibitor. Before and during treatment, test for TB and do bloodwork. Serious infections, blood clots, cancers including lymphoma, stomach or intestinal tears have occurred. People 50+ taking a JAK inhibitor with risk for heart disease may have a greater chance of heart attack, stroke, or death. Doctors should be informed about an infection, hepatitis B or C, or when patients are pregnant or planning or have any problems with low blood sugar. Please full Prescribing Information, including Boxed Warning and Medication Guide, and see below for Important Safety Information.
The LEQSELVI data presentation is one of 22 presentations from Sun Pharma across its dermatology and immunology portfolio.
LEQSELVI (deuruxolitinib) 8 mg tablets is an oral selective inhibitor of Janus kinases JAK1 and JAK2 FDA-approved for the treatment of adults with severe alopecia areata. Alopecia areata is an autoimmune disease in which the immune system attacks hair follicles, resulting in partial or complete loss of hair on the scalp and body. Alopecia areata may affect up to 2.5% of the United States and global population during their lifetime. The scalp is the most commonly affected area, but any hair-bearing site can be affected alone or together with the scalp. Onset of the disease can occur throughout life and affects both women and men. Alopecia areata can be associated with serious psychological consequences, including anxiety and depression. There are currently limited approved treatment options available for alopecia areata.
Sun Pharma Details LEQSELVI’s Indication and Safety Precautions
What is LEQSELVI (deuruxolitinib)?
LEQSELVI is used to treat adults with severe hair loss (alopecia areata). It is not known if LEQSELVI is safe and effective in children.
Who should not take LEQSELVI?
Do not take LEQSELVI if you are a poor metabolizer of CYP2C9 medicines or are taking moderate or strong CYP2C9 inhibitors. Before starting treatment, your healthcare provider should test you for CYP2C9 variants. Tell your healthcare provider if you take moderate or strong CYP2C9 inhibitor medicines. Ask your healthcare provider or pharmacist if you are not sure.
What is the most important safety information I should know about LEQSELVI?
- LEQSELVI is a medicine that affects your immune system and can lower the ability of your immune system to fight infections. Some people have had serious infections during treatment with LEQSELVI. Some people may die from these infections. Your healthcare provider should test you for TB before starting treatment with LEQSELVI and should watch you closely for signs and symptoms of TB during treatment. You should not start taking LEQSELVI if you have any kind of infection unless your healthcare provider tells you it is okay.
- There may be an increased risk of major cardiovascular events in people 50 years of age and older who have at least one heart disease risk factor and are taking a medicine in the class of medicines called JAK inhibitors, especially if they are a current or past smoker.
- LEQSELVI may increase your risk of certain cancers by changing the way your immune system works.
- Blood clots in the veins of your legs, lungs or brain (cerebral venous sinus thrombosis, CVT) can happen in some people during treatment with LEQSELVI. These may be lifethreatening.
- Some people taking LEQSELVI can get tears in their stomach or intestines.
- If you have diabetes, your healthcare provider may instruct you to check your blook sugar levels more often during treatment with LEQSELVI. Call your healthcare provider if you have any problems with low blood sugar (hypoglycemia).
- Before you start and taking LEQSELVI and during treatment, your healthcare provider should do blood tests to check for increased fat levels in your blood, Low white and/or red blood cell counts. You should not take LEQSELVI if your white blood cell or red blood cell counts are too low.
What should one tell the healthcare provider before starting LEQSELVI?
Tell healthcare provider if you have an infection; are a current or past smoker; have had a heart attack or other heart problems or stroke; have had blood clots in your legs, lungs or brain; have kidney problems; have liver problems; have any stomach area (abdominal) pain or have been diagnosed with diverticulitis or ulcers in your stomach or intestine; have low red or white blood cell counts; or have recently received or are scheduled to receive a vaccine.
Females who are able to become pregnant should use effective birth control (contraception) during treatment with LEQSELVI. Talk to a healthcare provider if one is planning to become pregnant. One should not breastfeed during treatment with LEQSELVI and for one day after the last dose.
What else should one be aware of when taking LEQSELVI?
Healthcare providers should do blood tests before start taking LEQSELVI and during treatment to check for increased fat (lipid) levels in your blood (triglycerides and cholesterol), low red blood cell counts, or low white blood cells.
How should I take LEQSELVI?
Take LEQSELVI 2 times a day with or without food.
What are the possible side effects of LEQSELVI?
The most common side effects of LEQSELVI include:
• acne
• headache
• pain or swelling of your nose or throat (nasopharyngitis)
• increased blood creatine phosphokinase
• increased blood cholesterol
• tiredness
• weight gain
• increased platelets in your blood (thrombocytosis)
• low red blood cell count (anemia)
• skin and soft tissue infections
• low white blood cell count (neutropenia)
• herpes simplex including cold sores
Further, it is noted that these are not all of the possible side effects of LEQSELVI. "Call your healthcare provider for medical advice about side effects," the release added.

input.title: Nykaa Fashion launches Hidden Gems accelerator for home-grown brands
input.content:
Nykaa Fashion has expanded its Hidden Gems proposition with the launch of a dedicated accelerator programme aimed at identifying, nurturing and scaling home-grown fashion and lifestyle brands with growth potential.
Since its inception, Hidden Gems has been an integral part of Nykaa Fashion’s offering, bringing distinctive designs from home-grown brands to discerning consumers.
Building on this, the new program marks a deeper commitment to supporting the next generation of independent founders, D2C innovators and emerging designers, creating a more structured pathway for them to grow their businesses and build lasting brand value.
As India’s fashion landscape evolves, a new generation of home-grown brands is redefining consumer preferences through distinctive design, cultural relevance and contemporary interpretations of Indian craftsmanship.
The expanded Hidden Gems program aims to go beyond enabling brand discovery by bringing together consumer reach, strategic support, data-led growth and access to Nykaa Fashion’s
wider capabilities.
As an introductory benefit, brands joining the program will receive zero commission for the first six months, enabling them to redirect their early investments towards brand building, inventory and customer acquisition while they establish themselves on the platform.
The program focuses on high-potential home grown brands across Indianwear, Westernwear, jewellery, bags and footwear, with participants gaining access to eight key growth pillars:
- Preferential Visibility: Enhanced visibility across relevant discovery and shopping journeys on Nykaa Fashion.
- Marketing Support: Opportunities to leverage Nykaa’s integrated marketing ecosystem to build awareness and drive customer discovery.
- Exclusive Mentorship Access: Strategic guidance and learning opportunities with senior Nykaa leadership.
- Strategic Account Management: Dedicated support from category experts to identify opportunities and continuously optimise brand performance.
- Monthly Growth Reviews: Regular reviews of consumer and business metrics, with customised action plans to unlock growth.
- Fast-Track Onboarding: A streamlined onboarding process designed to help brands get their collections live faster.
- Simplified Cataloguing: Digital cataloguing support to enable an efficient and seamless go-live experience.
- Growth Financing: Access to working capital solutions and financial partnerships to support inventory expansion and business growth.
Abhijeet Dabas, CEO, Nykaa Fashion, said, “India’s home-grown fashion landscape is at an exciting inflection point, with independent brands bringing fresh perspectives, distinctive design and new ideas to the market. As these brands look to scale, access to the right ecosystem, consumer insights and strategic support becomes increasingly important. With Hidden Gems, we aim to go beyond enabling brand discovery to actively supporting the next phase of their growth. By bringing together curated visibility, business mentorship and dedicated growth solutions, we want to help emerging brands build stronger consumer connections and create enduring businesses.”

input.title: Nykaa and SW Network take brand storytelling to the microdrama format with ‘Hotel Wanderlust’
input.content:
New Delhi : Beauty and personal care brand Nykaa has partnered with independent creative agency SW Network to launch ‘Hotel Wanderlust’, a six-episode microdrama series created for its experiential bath and body care brand Nykaa Wanderlust.
The series marks Nykaa Wanderlust’s first foray into the microdrama format, with SW Network leading the development of the entertainment-led campaign. Rather than using the format as an advertising vehicle, the campaign integrates the brand and its products directly into the narrative.
Set in a fictional hotel, ‘Hotel Wanderlust’ features comedian and actor Varun Thakur alongside Shachi, who plays a quirky receptionist. Each episode introduces a new guest, with creators including Srishti Garg, Pulkit Kochar and Mishall B appearing in different storylines built around relatable, everyday dilemmas.
Nykaa Wanderlust’s range of body mists, perfumes, shower gels and lotions are incorporated into the episodes as part of the characters’ experiences, allowing the products to feature within the story without interrupting the entertainment.
According to SW Network, the series has generated close to one million views across its six episodes within two weeks of launch. The agency said the campaign was developed using audience research and platform-specific storytelling techniques aimed at building engagement and strengthening the brand’s digital presence.
Himani Mangtani, Business Head, SW Network, shared her thoughts on the collaboration:“Social media is changing how people consume stories, and brands need to evolve with it. Hotel Wanderlust allowed us to build a format that feels native to the platform while giving Nykaa Wanderlust a distinctive world to play in. It’s also a reminder that when passionate people come together around a strong idea, great things can happen.”
Vinit Patil, Creative Director, SW Network, shared:”Microdrama has its own grammar, and we learned how to speak it. It’s about giving people a reason to stop, then a reason to stay, and finally a reason to share. That means putting the drama before an expensive production spectacle, and investing in the story, character arcs, popular faces and distribution that can make the story travel. With Hotel Wanderlust, that thinking shaped every beat.”
From the brand’s perspective, the campaign is designed to engage younger audiences through a format native to social media while bringing the travel-inspired positioning of Nykaa Wanderlust into an entertainment setting.
Omna Winston, Creative Head at Nykaa, said:“Gen Z doesn’t want brands to just talk to them; they want brands to create experiences they can be part of. Hotel Wanderlust was born from that thought. We wanted to take the travel-inspired world of Nykaa Wanderlust and turn it into a format that feels native to Instagram, bite-sized, entertaining and full of personality. The products are woven into that world naturally, making the brand part of the experience rather than an interruption.”
With all six episodes now available, ‘Hotel Wanderlust’ also serves as a platform for Nykaa Wanderlust to introduce its new fragrance line. The campaign adds to the brand’s digital content strategy while highlighting SW Network’s focus on platform-first, content-led brand storytelling.

input.title: Sun Pharma and LIB Therapeutics Sign Lerodalcibep Agreement
input.content:
Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Limited and LIB Therapeutics Inc have entered into an exclusive licensing agreement for lerodalcibep, a PCSK9 inhibitor used to lower low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C). Under the agreement, Sun Pharma will have exclusive rights to commercialise and manufacture lerodalcibep worldwide, except in the United States and China. LIB Therapeutics will receive an upfront payment and future milestone payments, along with royalties based on net sales in the licensed territories. Other financial terms of the agreement are confidential.
Lerodalcibep has been approved in the European Union under the brand name Lyrokaul for the treatment of adults with hypercholesterolaemia and mixed dyslipidaemia. The European approval was received on September 21, 2026. The medicine is a once-monthly PCSK9 inhibitor administered as a 300 mg/1.2 mL subcutaneous injection. The EU approval also allows the product to be stored at room temperature of up to 25°C for up to six months after removal from refrigeration, when kept in its original carton.
In the United States, lerodalcibep is approved by the US Food and Drug Administration under the brand name Lerochol as an addition to diet and exercise to reduce LDL-C in adults with hypercholesterolaemia, including those with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia (HeFH). The agreement adds a cardiovascular medicine to Sun Pharma’s Global Innovative Medicines portfolio. According to IQVIA, the PCSK9 inhibitor market outside the United States and China reached US$3.7 billion for the period ending Q2 2026 and grew at a 38% CAGR over the previous two years. Europe accounted for US$2.9 billion of the market during the same period.
“Once-monthly lerodalcibep dosing, with robust LDL-C reduction and the added benefits of a small-volume injection and six-month ambient storage, simplifies treatment for patients and offers greater convenience,” said Kirti W Ganorkar, Managing Director of Sun Pharma. “This agreement marks a significant step in strengthening our global Innovative Medicines portfolio, particularly in cardiovascular care. With exclusive rights outside the United States and China, we look forward to expanding access to this important treatment option for patients globally.”
Evan Stein, MD, PhD, Chief Operating and Scientific Officer and co-founder of LIB Therapeutics, said, “LIB is extremely pleased to partner with Sun Pharma, a well-established global pharmaceutical company with a growing focus on innovative medicines.” Lerodalcibep is an antibody-mimetic biologic and recombinant fusion protein that inhibits PCSK9. It is designed to provide sustained reductions in LDL-C with once-monthly dosing.
Sun Pharma will be responsible for seeking regulatory approvals for lerodalcibep in licensed territories where approvals have not yet been obtained. Sun Pharma is a global pharmaceutical company with businesses in Innovative Medicines, Generics and Consumer Healthcare. The company has operations and manufacturing facilities across multiple countries and sells medicines in more than 100 countries.

input.title: Sun Pharmaceutical (NSE:SUNPHARMA): Why Did It Publish Postal Ballot Notices in Newspapers?
input.content:
Sun Pharmaceutical Industries (NSE:SUNPHARMA) filed an intimation under Regulation 30 of SEBI's LODR Regulations on 2 October 2026, confirming it had published postal ballot and e-voting notices in all editions of the Financial Express in English and in the Ahmedabad edition of the Financial Express in Gujarati on the same date.
Key Highlights
- Sun Pharmaceutical Industries published postal ballot and e-voting notices in newspaper editions dated 2 October 2026, covering both English and Gujarati language readerships.
- The notices appeared across all editions of the Financial Express in English and the Ahmedabad edition of the Financial Express in Gujarati.
- The filing was made under Regulation 30 of SEBI's Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements Regulations, 2015, with the company secretary named as the compliance officer.
- Copies of the newspaper clippings were attached to the exchange filing and are also available on the company's official investor relations portal.
About the Company
Sun Pharmaceutical Industries (NSE:SUNPHARMA), headquartered in Mumbai with its registered office in Vadodara, Gujarat, is India's largest pharmaceutical company by revenue. The company manufactures and markets branded generics, specialty medicines, and active pharmaceutical ingredients across more than 100 countries, operating over 40 manufacturing facilities globally across therapy areas including dermatology, oncology, ophthalmology, and psychiatry.
Announcement in Detail
In its exchange filing dated 2 October 2026, Sun Pharmaceutical Industries stated that it had published advertisements containing information about a pending postal ballot and e-voting process. The notices were carried across all print editions of the Financial Express in English on that date, ensuring broad national coverage for shareholders who may not have received direct communication through digital channels.
The Ahmedabad edition of the Financial Express in Gujarati was separately cited in the filing, reflecting the company's registered office location in Gujarat and the statutory requirement to publish notices in a vernacular newspaper of the state of registration. The filing was signed by Anoop Deshpande, Company Secretary and Compliance Officer, bearing ICSI Membership No. A23983, and newspaper clippings were attached as Annexure-A to the intimation submitted to both NSE and BSE.
Impact on Investors
Investors will note that this filing is a procedural compliance step confirming that shareholders have been formally notified of an ongoing postal ballot and e-voting process through statutory newspaper publications. The filing itself does not disclose the specific resolutions being put to vote; shareholders will need to review the actual postal ballot notice to understand what decisions are being sought.
The disclosed terms indicate that the e-voting facility has been made available, which allows shareholders who could not participate through physical ballot to cast their votes electronically. Shareholders holding shares as of the relevant record date would be eligible to participate, and the filing shows the company is fulfilling its disclosure obligations under the SEBI LODR framework within prescribed timelines.
Sector / Market Context
India's pharmaceutical sector is among the most heavily regulated in terms of corporate governance and investor disclosure requirements. SEBI's LODR framework mandates that listed companies publish postal ballot notices in at least one English-language national newspaper and one vernacular newspaper in the state of the registered office, ensuring that shareholder voting information reaches a broad cross-section of investors. Sun Pharmaceutical, as one of India's largest listed pharma companies by market capitalisation, routinely files such disclosures in compliance with these statutory obligations.

input.title: Nykaa, L’Oréal’s BOLD back emerging Indian beauty brands in strategic venture deal
input.content:
Mumbai, India – Nykaa and L’Oréal’s corporate venture capital fund BOLD (Business Opportunities for L’Oréal Development) have partnered to invest in emerging Indian beauty and personal care brands.
Under the collaboration, Nykaa and BOLD will take minority stakes in selected beauty and wellness brands with consumer traction and distinct propositions. The investments will be purely financial, with founders retaining ownership control and continuing to run their businesses independently.
The partnership will also provide selected brands with mentorship and guidance, alongside access to L’Oréal’s global beauty expertise and Nykaa’s omnichannel retail network and consumer ecosystem.
Jacques Lebel, Managing Director at L’Oréal India, said, “India is one of the most exciting beauty markets in the world, and its energy comes both from an expanding base of demanding consumers with rapidly evolving needs and from its ecosystem of tremendous entrepreneurs.”
“Through BOLD and this partnership with Nykaa, we want to stand behind that talent — backing founders with capital, mentorship, and L’Oréal’s beauty expertise, while leaving them free to build their brands their way,” added Lebel.
“Our commitment to India is stronger than ever, and this is the next major milestone in a journey of partnership and growth that we began over three decades ago,” concluded Lebel. 
“Nykaa and L’Oreal have been partners in India for over a decade, working together on our shared vision of making India into one of the world’s largest and fastest growing beauty markets,” said Anchit Nayar, Executive Director and CEO at Nykaa Beauty.
“The experience and lessons we have learned along the way have allowed us to understand what it takes to build a promising brand into an enduring one,” added Nayar.
“Combining our strong consumer ecosystem, deep retail network and wide distribution, along with L’Oréal’s global beauty expertise will be an incredibly valuable asset to the next generation of founders as they look to build consumer brands that India can be proud of,” concluded Nayar.
The initiative aims to support Indian beauty founders as they scale their businesses in India and international markets, while allowing them to retain control over their brands and operations.

input.title: Sun Pharma’s Leqselvi sustains hair regrowth for over two years in long-term study
input.content:
- Research & Development
- 2 min read
Sun Pharma’s Leqselvi sustains hair regrowth for over two years in long-term study
According to a long-term efficacy analysis presented at the European Academy of Dermatology and Venereology (EADV) Congress, 93.9 per cent of patients who maintained a SALT score of 20 or less after 52 weeks of treatment and continued in the study maintained the response through the two-year follow-up.
The long-term efficacy analysis presented in a poster at the ongoing European Academy of Dermatology and Venereology (EADV) Congress in Vienna showed that, adult patients receiving the drug in an open-label extension after 52 weeks of treatment sustained their scalp hair regrowth through Week 108, with a SALT score of 20 or less—the benchmark response threshold.
According to the company, 93.9 per cent of patients who maintained a SALT score of 20 or less at Week 52 and continued in the study maintained their response through Week 108.
Patients who were baseline nonresponders (SALT score >20), 76.6 per cent of them, achieved the targeted score by Week 52, and 96.8 per cent of those responders maintained it through the two-year follow-up.
“Our data at EADV 2026 expands our understanding of Leqselvi beyond initial treatment response and provides important evidence for dermatologists and advance practice providers into durability of response, and maintenance of clinical benefit in adults,” said Ahmad Naim, Chief Medical Officer, Sun Pharma.
Sun Pharma purchased Leqselvi under its $576 million takeover of Concert Pharmaceuticals in 2023. The novel JAK inhibitor competes with Eli Lilly’s Olumiant (baricitinib) and Pfizer’s Litfulo (ritlecitinib)
Leqselvi is taken twice daily, while Lilly’s and Pfizer’s competing brands are dosed once daily and are also approved to treat pediatric patients aged 12 years and older. The Mumbai-based pharma is also exploring the new patient pool through an investigator-led trial.
Leqselvi entered the US market in July 2025 following a brief legal dispute with Incyte Corporation – which also discovered Lilly’s Olumiant — over alleged patent infringement. Under a subsequent settlement, Sun Pharma received a non-exclusive licence to certain US and related patents covering non-hematology-oncology indications, including alopecia areata.
At its Q1 earnings call, Sun Pharma management told investors, the brand had surpassed 1,000 prescribers as of June this year, and is showing positive uptake across the country.
A study by data-analytics firm GlobalData suggests, "with its efficacy edge SunPharma’s Leqselvi holds the potential to achieve sales of $700 million by 2033."
“Leqselvi higher dose of 8 mg twice daily, positions it in a stronger position as the higher dose will have a slightly better efficacy in comparison to Eli Lilly’s Olumiant that is taken at 2 mg or 4 mg per day.” several key opinion leaders interviewed by GlobalData had noted.

input.title: Cyient DLM sees next big opportunity in AI data centers, robotics, says CEO Rajendra Velagapudi
input.content:
NEW DELHI: Homegrown contract manufacturer Cyient DLM said it sees the next big business opportunities in the AI data center and robotics segments, and its sales teams are looking to secure contracts in the US market.“We are also getting into two new sectors, which are AI data centers and robotics. These two are the new sectors where we are focusing right now,” Rajendra Velagapudi, MD & CEO, Cyient DLM, told ETElectronicsWorld in an interview.“We have hired people (to drive our business push), and they are on the ground looking for the opportunities,” the chief executive added.According to its investor presentation filed with the exchanges, the Hyderabad-based company plans to expand into these two new segments between FY27 and FY29.The listed design-led manufacturer (DLM) and electronics manufacturing services (EMS) subsidiary of engineering firm Cyient Limited earns the majority of revenue from the aerospace, industrial, defense, and medtech verticals.It operates in the printed circuit board assembly (PCBA), box-build, and build-to-specifications (B2S) product segments.Velagapudi said that Cyient DLM will work with AI data center suppliers to provide power controllers, cables, and connectors. “Then the cooling systems…that is where our core competence is, as it combines our electronics and mechanical capabilities.”He added that the company’s expertise in PCBAs, power sensors, and other components will help it secure contracts in the robotics segment. “There are up to 60 to 70 different PCBs in humanoid robots. So, that is where our focus is to work with those companies, and where we can also do the designs and manufacture for them.”A strong boom in AI consumption over the last few quarters has sparked a rush to set up massive data centers to handle computing tasks and support demand. This has also spurred a gold rush for suppliers, including those that operate in optical fibre cables (OFC), power supplies, and liquid cooling categories.By contrast, humanoid robots are a nascent category but have applications in manufacturing, logistics, and other verticals.“Only in the data center space, there is $45 billion-plus potential, and people are just scratching the surface,” Velagapudi said. “How much (share) we can take will be defined in the coming quarters, once we start approaching customers. We already have a go-to-market strategy.”He added that Cyient DLM’s focus is predominantly in the US. “Our sales team is also focused on entering that market…in India, we have one company that is making a humanoid, and we are in touch with them. But the main focus is on the US market,” he said.The company, which was listed nearly three years ago, reported its highest-ever order book of ₹2,598.9 crore in Q1FY27, along with an order intake of ₹551.9 crore.Its revenue in the April-June period of FY27 reported a 34.3% year-on-year increase in revenue to ₹373.8 crore. EBITDA grew by 56.2% annually to ₹39.2 crore, with margins at 10.5%.Its profit after tax (PAT) more than doubled to ₹16.3 crore, registering 118.2% year-on-year growth, with margins at 4.4%, expanding by 168 basis points (bps) during this period.

input.title: Rasha Thadani & Rohit Saraf get ‘Lovestruck’ for Nykaa
input.content:
Nykaa Cosmetics has launched a three-film campaign for its Lovestruck Lipstick, starring Rasha Thadani, face of Nykaa Cosmetics, and actor Rohit Saraf.
The campaign, built around the idea of ‘Love At First Swipe’, gives the classic love-at-first-sight story a beauty-led twist. It follows a chance connection between Thadani and Saraf that develops through a series of playful encounters and flirtatious moments.
The first film features an unexpected encounter between the two, where a passing moment turns into a memorable first impression. The second brings them together at a party, where their chemistry becomes harder to ignore and the Lovestruck lipstick makes its introduction.
The third film brings another encounter, leaving the story open-ended and hinting at what could happen next.
The lipstick is integrated into the narrative, with the campaign using the product’s one-swipe payoff as part of the ‘Love At First Swipe’ idea. Lovestruck Lipstick offers rich velvet colour, a smooth matte finish and a lightweight formula powered by Velvet Flex Technology.
Available in 12 shades, the range covers everyday neutrals as well as more expressive colours. The lipstick is priced at Rs 799 and is available through Nykaa.com, the Nykaa app and Nykaa stores.

input.title: Nykaa Fashion expands ‘Hidden Gems’ with accelerator programme for home-grown brands
input.content:

- 1 min read
Nykaa Fashion expands ‘Hidden Gems’ with accelerator programme for home-grown brands
                    The programme will also offer monthly business reviews, fast-track onboarding, cataloguing support and access to working-capital solutions through financial partnerships.
                                    
            
        
                    
                    
                    
                                        Nykaa Fashion has expanded its ‘Hidden Gems’ proposition with a new accelerator programme aimed at onboarding and scaling emerging home-grown fashion and lifestyle brands.
The programme will target independent founders, D2C brands and emerging designers across Indianwear, Westernwear, jewellery, bags and footwear. Brands joining the programme will receive zero commission for the first six months, along with marketing support, preferential visibility, mentorship and strategic account management.
The programme will also offer monthly business reviews, fast-track onboarding, cataloguing support and access to working-capital solutions through financial partnerships.
According to Nykaa Fashion, the initiative is aimed at providing emerging brands with access to its consumer base and wider platform capabilities, while helping them strengthen inventory, customer acquisition and brand-building efforts.
“India’s home-grown fashion landscape is at an exciting inflection point, with independent brands bringing fresh perspectives, distinctive design and new ideas to the market,” said Abhijeet Dabas, CEO, Nykaa Fashion.
He added that the expanded Hidden Gems programme would bring together consumer reach, data-led insights, mentorship and growth solutions to support emerging brands as they scale.
The programme builds on Nykaa Fashion’s existing Hidden Gems proposition, which focuses on bringing home-grown brands to consumers on the platform.
Nykaa said the initiative is part of its broader focus on supporting emerging brands across fashion and lifestyle categories through its marketplace ecosystem.

input.title: ICICI Securities sees recovery in ER&D stocks in Q2; Tata Tech, Netweb, IKS, Cyient among top picks
input.content:
Among the expected growth leaders, Cyient is forecast to post 4.5 per cent quarter-on-quarter (QoQ) growth in dollar revenue to about $170 million. ICICI Securities said only 0.5 per cent of this would be organic, with the rest coming from $6.5 million in inorganic revenue from the partial consolidation of the Tao Digital acquisition.
Aerospace is expected to maintain double-digit growth, while a semiconductor fab modernisation deal won in Q4FY26 is seen adding momentum. However, EBIT margin is expected to fall about 66 basis points to 12.5 per cent because of integration costs.
Tata Technologies is expected to grow 2.7 per cent in dollar terms, or 3.2 per cent in constant currency, to around $180 million on a strong base. It cited support from anchor clients, a deal pipeline that includes a $100 million Tenneco deal and a Japanese OEM opportunity, and traction in its BMW-led joint venture.
EBIT margin is seen rising 54 basis points to 13.8% despite wage hikes. ICICI Securities expects double-digit organic growth from the company in FY27, although Volkswagen’s slowdown may weigh on its ES-Tech revenues. L&T Technology Services is estimated to grow 2 per cent in dollar terms to about $316 million as the impact of the divested low-margin SWC business fades.
The brokerage pointed to traction in sustainability, improved automotive demand and the company’s engineering intelligence pivot. It also noted the recently announced $75 million, five-year engagement with a global technology firm. EBIT margin is expected to rise 31 basis points to 16 per cent, though weak European automotive demand remains a drag.
At the weaker end, Tata Elxsi Ltd is forecast to grow 0.6 per cent in dollar terms to about $108 million as automotive OEMs remain cautious on discretionary spending and large deals are still absent. Indirect exposure to Middle East tensions may affect its luxury auto segment, while healthcare and media are expected to fare better.
Margin is seen expanding 53 basis points to 19.5%, partly offsetting a 150 basis point wage-hike impact. KPIT Technologies Ltd is expected to report a 0.7 per cent decline in dollar revenue to about $175 million, in line with its guidance for a muted quarter.
ICICI Securities said the recovery could be prolonged because of its software-heavy, software-defined-vehicle-led portfolio, which it said is vulnerable to AI-led deflation. EBIT margin is expected to remain flat at 11.4 per cent. The Caresoft acquisition is expected to help, while a possible 1 per cent revenue contraction in FY27 remains a key monitorable.
ICICI Securities’ top picks in the ER&D space are Tata Technologies Ltd and Cyient Ltd, alongside IKS Health, Indegene Ltd and Netweb Technologies India Ltd in its broader coverage. It expects Tata Technologies to benefit from its aerospace pivot and focus on non-anchor clients, and Cyient from its semiconductor push and the Tao Digital deal.
Key monitorables include headwinds from the Middle East, whether the FY27 pipeline matches expectations set in Q4FY26, automotive demand in Europe and the US, the effect of profit warnings from BMW and Volkswagen, traction in defence, aerospace, industrial machinery, plant engineering and micro-mobility, the outlook for battery electric vehicles and signs of AI-led deflation.
The brokerage also expects the wider group to gather momentum through FY27, with LTTS benefiting from engineering intelligence solutions and a recovery in hi-tech. The main risks, it said, are a prolonged West Asia conflict that could disrupt supply chains and delay recovery, and signs of a muted 2026 outlook from large automotive OEMs.

input.title: It started with a swipe: Rasha Thadani & Rohit Saraf star in Nykaa Cosmetics’ Lovestruck
input.content:
What happens when the right lipstick meets the right person at the right time? Things can get a little… Lovestruck.
With its latest campaign for Lovestruck Lipstick, Nykaa Cosmetics is giving “Love At First Swipe” a playful spin on the classic love-at-first-sight story. Starring Rasha Thadani, Face of Nykaa Cosmetics, alongside Rohit Saraf, the three-film campaign follows a chance connection that starts with a look, develops with a little flirting and leaves both wondering if this was simply a coincidence or something more. The first film kicks things off with an unexpected encounter between Rasha and Rohit, where a passing moment turns into a memorable first impression. The second brings them together again at a party, where the chemistry gets a little harder to ignore and Lovestruck makes its own introduction. By the third film, one final encounter leaves the story hanging on just the right note, proving that sometimes, the best love stories are the ones that leave you wanting another swipe. And while the chemistry takes centre stage, Lovestruck Lipstick is very much part of the plot. From the first swipe to the moments that follow, the lipstick moves naturally through the story, giving the campaign its beauty-meets-romance twist. After all, a lipstick that delivers rich velvet colour, a smooth matte finish and one-swipe payoff was always going to make a memorable first impression. Powered by Velvet Flex Technology, the formula creates a lightweight, flexible layer of colour designed for comfortable wear. Available in 12 shades, Lovestruck goes from easy everyday neutrals to more expressive hues, because when it comes to making an impression, there is more than one way to fall. At its heart, the campaign is a little love story with a beauty secret: sometimes chemistry is instant, sometimes it takes another encounter, and sometimes all it takes is one swipe.

input.title: Expanding innovative portfolio may drive gains for Sun Pharma stock
input.content:
Expanding innovative portfolio may drive gains for Sun Pharma stock
Lerodalcibep licensing deal, growth in the US portfolio and tariff relief offer triggers, while the proposed Organon acquisition could broaden its global reach
Listen to This Article
The outlook for Sun Pharma is expected to improve on the back of multiple positive triggers. These include scaling up of its US portfolio, expanding innovative portfolio and tariff deal/specialty drug tariff waiver.
 
The in-licensing deal with LIB Therapeutics to commercialise and manufacture cholesterol-lowering medication Lerodalcibep is also expected to strengthen its innovative medicines portfolio.
 
While the stock has underperformed its peers sharply over the last six months, there could be some gains given the triggers and target prices.
 
At the current price of ₹1,860, the stock is trading at 27 times its FY28 earnings estimates.
 
The immediate trigger for the stock is the licensing deal for Lerodalcibep which belongs to the PCSK9 class of drugs.
 
Also Read
The exclusive agreement for markets worldwide (excluding the US and China) will open up a $3.7 billion market for the company, growing at an annual rate of 38 per cent.
 
The global PCSK9 market is expected to be about $7 billion in 2026. LIB will receive upfront and future milestone payments, together with royalties based on net sales in licensed territories. And, Sun Pharma will be responsible for pursuing regulatory approvals in licensed territories where approval has not yet been obtained.   
 
360 ONE Capital Research says that the deal builds on Sun’s track record of strengthening its innovative portfolio through in-licensing and acquisitions.
Sun’s FY26 innovative medicines grew by 16.8 per cent to $1.42 billion.    
 
Plaque psoriasis drug Ilumya, which is the largest product, reported sales of $796 million in FY26 and grew 17 per cent year-on-year (Y-o-Y).
 
Near-term catalysts, according to Robit Bhat and Hrishikesh Patole of the brokerage, include the potential USFDA approval of Ilumya for psoriatic arthritis alongside continued ramp up of hairfall (alopecia areata) drug Leqselvi and skin cancer formulation, Unloxcyt.
 
Combined with the proposed $12 billion Organon acquisition, which adds scale across innovative medicines, women’s health and biosimilars, the company, according to the brokerage, is building a broader platform for sustained growth.
It has a buy rating with a target price of ₹2,250.
 
The other trigger is the tariff deal with the US which extended the most favoured nation drug pricing to state Medicaid programmes. In a positive, the arrangement, according to Kotak Research, excludes Medicare which, along with the commercial channel accounts for the vast majority of Sun Pharma’s innovative medicine sales.
 
The deal also provides tariff protection for Sun’s US branded portfolio until January 20, 2029.
 
The company’s proposed acquisition (expected to be completed by early 2027), Organon, is outside the scope of the deal and it would need to negotiate a separate agreement.
While lower Medicaid pricing is likely to weigh on earnings, the exclusion of Medicare and the tariff reprieve make the overall outcome marginally positive for Sun Pharma, says the brokerage.
 
It has an ‘add’ rating with a target price of ₹2,150. The specialty drug tariff wavier for specific medications will also help eliminate and lift the overhang of tariffs.
 
Geojit Research is also positive on the outlook for Sun Pharma. The recent approval of semaglutide in multiple markets, steady performance of its flagship brands, such as Ilumya, and progress in the commercialisation of new specialty products highlight its focus on innovation-led growth, says the brokerage.
The proposed Organon acquisition is expected to broaden its therapeutic presence through the women's health and biosimilars portfolios while further enhancing its global reach.
 
It has retained a ‘buy’ rating on the stock with a revised target price of ₹2,070.

input.title: Sun Pharma plans $1 billion rupee debt sale to refinance Organon acquisition loan
input.content:
Sun Pharma plans $1 billion rupee debt sale to refinance Organon acquisition loan
Indiaâs largest drugmaker by market capitalisation plans to raise around Rs 10,000 crore through domestic bonds to partly repay the bridge loan used to fund its $11.75 billion acquisition of Organon.
Sun Pharmaceutical Industries is planning to raise around Rs 10,000 crore ($1.04 billion) through a rupee-denominated debt sale to partly refinance a bridge loan taken to fund its acquisition of US healthcare company Organon & Co., three sources familiar with the matter told Reuters.
The proposed bond sale comes after Sun Pharma earlier this year closed syndication of a nearly $12 billion, 18-month bridge loan for the all-cash acquisition of Organon. State Bank of India was among the lenders participating in the financing, the sources said.
The sources, who requested anonymity as they were not authorised to speak to the media, said Sun Pharma plans to issue bonds with maturities of two, three and four years.
The planned fundraising comes as Indian companies increasingly turn to the domestic debt market as higher US Treasury yields make dollar-denominated borrowing more expensive.
The 10-year US Treasury yield is hovering near its highest level since June 2007, putting pressure on borrowing costs globally.
Bankers expect domestic corporate debt issuance in India to reach a record level this year as companies seek to lock in funding costs ahead of a potential interest-rate increase by the Reserve Bank of India.
Around $3 billion worth of rupee-denominated corporate debt issues are lined up over the next few days, one of the sources told Reuters.

input.title: Cyient DLM (NSE:CYIENTDLM): Why Has the Trading Window Been Closed?
input.content:
Cyient DLM Limited (NSE:CYIENTDLM) filed a trading window closure notice on 29 September 2026 with both BSE and NSE, stating that the window will remain shut from 1 October 2026 until 48 hours after the company disseminates its financial results for the quarter ended 30 September 2026.
Key Highlights
- The trading window for securities of Cyient DLM Limited closes from 1 October 2026, in compliance with SEBI's Prohibition of Insider Trading Regulations.
- The closure applies to the quarter ended 30 September 2026, and will lift 48 hours after the company publicly disseminates its Q2 FY27 financial results.
- The notice was signed by S. Krithika, Company Secretary and Compliance Officer, and filed simultaneously with BSE (scrip code 543933) and NSE (ticker: CYIENTDLM).
- The announcement details are being hosted on the company's investor relations page at the official Cyient DLM website under statutory filings.
About the Company
Cyient DLM Limited is an electronics manufacturing services company headquartered at Electronics City, Hebbal Industrial Area, Mysore, Karnataka, with a registered office at the GMR Aerospace and Industrial Park, Shamshabad, Hyderabad. Listed on NSE under the ticker CYIENTDLM, the company provides integrated electronics design, manufacturing, and life-cycle solutions primarily for aerospace, defence, medical, and industrial end markets. Its CIN is L31909TG1993PLC141346.
Announcement in Detail
In a filing dated 29 September 2026, Cyient DLM Limited notified the stock exchanges that its trading window will be closed beginning 1 October 2026, consistent with SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015, and the company's own Code of Conduct for Prohibition of Insider Trading. The closure is specifically linked to the financial reporting cycle for the quarter ending 30 September 2026, designated as Q2 of FY27.
The trading window will reopen only after 48 hours have elapsed from the moment the company formally disseminates its quarterly financial results to the exchanges. This 48-hour buffer is a standard regulatory requirement designed to ensure that designated persons who are privy to unpublished price-sensitive information cannot transact in company securities until that information becomes fully accessible to the broader investing public. The filing was acknowledged simultaneously by BSE and NSE.
Impact on Investors
Investors will note that this filing does not alter the company's financial position, business operations, or capital structure. However, the closure of the trading window is a material compliance milestone for designated persons, including promoters, directors, key managerial personnel, and other insiders covered under the company's insider trading code. The filing shows these individuals are restricted from buying or selling CYIENTDLM securities during the closure period.
Shareholders will observe that the lifting of the restriction is conditional on the publication of Q2 FY27 results, after which the 48-hour window takes effect. The disclosed terms indicate that the precise reopening date will depend on when the board of Cyient DLM convenes to approve and disseminate those results, a date that has not been announced in this particular filing.
Sector / Market Context
India's electronics manufacturing services sector has gained increased policy attention under the Production Linked Incentive scheme for electronics and components, with the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology tracking substantial capacity investments across aerospace, defence, and industrial electronics segments. Trading window closures ahead of quarterly results are a routine compliance obligation for all listed companies under SEBI's Prohibition of Insider Trading Regulations, 2015, reflecting the regulator's ongoing emphasis on fair and transparent price discovery in Indian equity markets.
