Located within Navi Mumbai’s key hardware and building materials hub, the facility enables visitors to interact with Blum’s product range and experience its functionality firsthand.
Maarten de Vries, Managing Director, Blum India said, "The booming residential ecosystem of Navi Mumbai demands a premier living experience. We opened Blum's experience centre in Vashi to make world-class Austrian engineering easily accessible to the city. The centre not only brings our furniture hardware here but also allows visitors to get hands-on with the motion, ergonomics, and quality that our solutions are loved for all over the globe. I want to thank our local partners at Vision Enterprises for bringing us closer to the people of Vashi and helping us set up this experience centre for the furniture makers and homeowners here."
Vijay Singh Chandaliya, Owner of Vision Enterprises shared, "I have been in the Navi Mumbai hardware market for years, so I know what clients around Vashi expect when they build a home. Partnering with Blum to open this space right here is fantastic because it means local designers and architects don't have to drive into Mumbai anymore just to see top-tier fittings. Everything they need is on display right here in Vashi. We want people to come in, use the setups, and see how much of a difference the right hardware makes."
The newly opened experience centre is now operational and welcomes walk-in visitors. In addition to product demonstrations, the facility offers opportunities for homeowners and builders to consult with modular kitchen designers and explore furniture layouts using Blum’s hardware solutions.
Real estate developer Trehan IRIS has announced the appointment of Prasad Rane as its Chief Business & Marketing Officer (CBMO) as the company looks to strengthen its growth strategy across residential, commercial, and retail real estate segments.
In his new role, Rane will oversee business growth, sales and marketing functions, bringing together commercial strategy, brand development, customer experience and go-to-market initiatives across the organization. The company said his mandate will focus on aligning business performance with brand strategy while creating differentiated value propositions across the Trehan IRIS portfolio.
Abhishek Trehan and Aman Trehan, Executive Directors, Trehan IRIS shared, “Prasad brings a strong combination of business, brand and consumer understanding, with experience across real estate, retail and consumer businesses. His mandate will be to bring business growth, sales and marketing closer together as we enter our next phase of growth. We are pleased to welcome him to the leadership team.”
Prasad Rane, Chief Business & Marketing Officer, Trehan IRIS said, “Real estate today is no longer only about what we build; it is increasingly about the experience, proposition and value we create around it. Trehan IRIS has a strong legacy and an exciting opportunity to build the next phase of the organisation around that foundation. My focus will be to bring business, sales, brand and customer experience closer together — creating propositions that are distinctive for the consumer and meaningful for the business.”
The appointment comes at a time when Trehan IRIS is expanding its presence across multiple real estate categories. With more than seven decades of industry experience, the company’s portfolio spans residential, commercial, retail and hospitality developments, with a focus on creating community-driven and customer-centric spaces.
Rane brings extensive cross-industry experience across real estate, retail, consumer brands, asset management, marketing and business development. Over the course of his career, he has worked on initiatives related to real estate asset management, retail destination development, and business growth strategies.
Before joining Trehan IRIS, Rane served as Chief Growth Officer at DailyObjects, where he led offline business expansion, physical retail growth and the development of new business channels.
Prior to that, he was associated with ICS Group, serving as Chief Marketing Officer at PPZ and CEO of SPACES. During his tenure, he worked across asset management, retail and mixed-use developments, technology parks and public spaces. His earlier experience in advertising and retail also contributed to his expertise in consumer behavior, brand building and business development.
Beauty and lifestyle retailer Nykaa has launched its K-Beauty Festival in Bengaluru, transforming Forum Mall into a dedicated Korean Beauty Village that will remain open until September 27.
The experiential beauty event brings together a wide range of Korean skincare, makeup and haircare brands, offering consumers an opportunity to explore some of the most popular names in the global K-beauty industry under one roof.
The skincare portfolio at the festival includes brands such as Dr. Althea, Beauty of Joseon, COSRX, Anua, Biodance, SKIN1004, Round Lab, Arencia, Aestura, Illiyoon, Medicube, The Face Shop, Mirabelle Korea and Laneige. In the makeup segment, shoppers can discover products from D’alba Piedmont, TIRTIR, Tonymoly and Mamonde, while Korean haircare brands including La’dor, Mise En Scene and Ryo are also featured at the event.
Beyond product displays, the K-Beauty Village has been designed as an interactive experience. Visitors can test products, participate in games and activities, and receive samples and prizes. The event also includes promotional offers, with discounts of up to 20 percent available across selected K-beauty brands.
The initiative reflects growing consumer interest in Korean beauty products in India, particularly in categories such as skincare, sun care, sheet masks and advanced beauty formulations. By creating a dedicated experiential format, Nykaa aims to provide consumers with greater access to international beauty brands while allowing them to engage with products before making a purchase.
The festival caters to both long-time K-beauty enthusiasts and first-time shoppers interested in exploring Korean skincare and beauty trends. Consumers can browse a variety of products across categories, ranging from cleansers and moisturizers to makeup essentials and haircare solutions.
The event is part of Nykaa’s broader strategy to strengthen its beauty retail presence through curated brand experiences and global beauty offerings. Over the years, the retailer has expanded its portfolio of international beauty brands and introduced experiential formats aimed at increasing consumer engagement.
With the launch of the K-Beauty Festival in Bengaluru, Nykaa is further capitalizing on the rising popularity of Korean beauty products in India while creating an immersive retail experience that combines shopping, product discovery and interactive engagement.
The Korean Beauty Village at Forum Mall, Bengaluru, will continue to welcome shoppers until September 27, offering access to a wide selection of K-beauty brands, product trials and exclusive festival offers.
AceVector Ltd, the parent company of Snapdeal, has announced the launch of its initial public offering (IPO) on September 25, seeking a post-issue valuation of approximately Rs 1,741 crore. The company has fixed a price band of Rs 30-32 per equity share, with the public issue set to close on September 29.
At the upper end of the price band, the IPO is expected to raise around Rs 420 crore and value the e-commerce company at approximately Rs 1,741.4 crore. The anchor investor portion will open on September 24, ahead of the public subscription. The IPO comprises a fresh issue of shares worth up to Rs 287 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) by existing shareholders. Investors including SoftBank-backed Starfish and Nexus Venture Partners are among those participating in the OFS.
AceVector had earlier proposed a larger public issue but has revised the size of both the fresh issue and the OFS. The company plans to deploy the fresh capital towards marketing and business promotion, technology infrastructure investments, acquisitions, and general corporate purposes.
Founded by Kunal Bahl and Rohit Bansal, AceVector operates a digital commerce ecosystem spanning multiple businesses, including value-focused e-commerce marketplace Snapdeal, e-commerce enablement platform Unicommerce, and consumer brand business Stellaro Brands.
According to its latest filings, the company reported revenue of Rs 510.4 crore in FY26, up 29.2 percent from the previous fiscal year, while its net loss narrowed significantly during the period. The IPO comes amid renewed activity in India’s primary market, with several technology, e-commerce and digital-first companies tapping public markets to fund growth and strengthen their balance sheets.
Menswear brand Wrogn, backed by cricketer Virat Kohli, reported a recovery in revenue during FY26, although the company continued to face profitability pressures as losses increased during the year.
Wrogn’s operating revenue rose 9 percent to Rs 244 crore in FY26, compared to Rs 223 crore in FY25, when the company had recorded a decline in sales. Despite the growth, the brand remained significantly smaller than fast-growing competitors such as Snitch and Rare Rabbit, which reported revenues of approximately Rs 900 crore and Rs 1,100 crore, respectively.
Founded in 2014 and operated by Universal Sportsbiz Private Limited (USPL), Wrogn offers a range of casual menswear products, including T-shirts, shirts, denim, and accessories. The Bengaluru-based company is backed by investors including Virat Kohli, Accel, and Aditya Birla Group, and distributes its products through both online and offline retail channels.
Product sales continued to account for the majority of the company's income. In addition, Wrogn generated Rs 10.17 crore through non-operating income sources such as interest earnings and gains from financial assets. As a result, the company’s total income increased to Rs 254 crore in FY26, up from Rs 232 crore in the previous fiscal year.
On the expenditure side, raw material costs remained the company’s largest cost component, contributing around 35 percent of total expenses. However, material costs declined by 5 percent to Rs 119.7 crore, compared to Rs 125.7 crore in FY25.
Additional expenses, including depreciation, amortization, and finance-related costs, contributed Rs 78.6 crore to the overall expenditure base.
As a result, Wrogn’s total expenses increased 9.5 percent to Rs 342.4 crore in FY26 from Rs 312.6 crore a year earlier.
The higher spending on marketing and brand-building initiatives impacted profitability. The company reported a net loss of Rs 88.4 crore, representing a 17 percent increase from Rs 75.5 crore in FY25.
Despite the widening losses, Wrogn showed some improvement in operational efficiency, with its EBITDA margin improving to negative 27.6 percent from negative 30.8 percent in the previous fiscal year.
The company spent approximately Rs 1.40 to generate every rupee of operating revenue during FY26, highlighting the continued pressure on margins as it invests in growth.
Wrogn ended the fiscal year with cash and bank balances of Rs 24.3 crore, significantly higher than Rs 9.7 crore reported a year earlier. Its current assets stood at Rs 181 crore, compared with Rs 177.2 crore in FY25.
Looking ahead, the company has indicated stronger momentum in FY27. In a recent statement, Wrogn said its gross merchandise value (GMV) grew 40 percent year-on-year to Rs 125 crore during the first quarter of FY27, while EBITDA losses narrowed by 34 percent. The brand also reported that its adjusted EBITDA loss reduced to Rs 38 crore in FY26, compared to Rs 54 crore in FY25.
Hyderabad-based saree retail startup Pinit has launched an app-based quick commerce platform that enables customers to browse and receive curated saree collections at home within 45 minutes, subject to location and slot availability. The platform combines digital shopping with an assisted in-home experience, allowing customers to explore sarees before making a purchase. Through the app, users can browse collections, select preferred styles, and schedule a shopping session.
A Pinit delivery vehicle then brings the selected sarees along with a trained stylist to the customer's doorstep. During the session, the stylist sets up a temporary display using lighting and a mirror, enabling customers to view, compare, drape, and evaluate multiple sarees from the comfort of their homes. The model aims to replicate the experience of visiting a physical saree store while offering the convenience of app-based ordering.
Pinit offers sarees across various price points, ranging from approximately Rs 1,000 to Rs 20,000. Its portfolio includes handloom sarees, regional weaves and designer collections catering to everyday wear, festive occasions, and wedding shopping. To support faster deliveries, the company operates a network of location-based fulfilment centres that dispatch collections from nearby hubs. Pinit also runs an all-electric delivery fleet as part of its logistics operations.
The startup employs more than 150 people and sources products directly from weavers and weaving clusters across India. The company said its sourcing model is focused on connecting traditional textile artisans with consumers through technology-enabled retail.
Founded by saree entrepreneur Sangeetha Rajesh, Pinit builds on her 16 years of experience in the saree and textile industry. Rajesh is also the founder of Sangeetha's Saree Emporium and was among the early saree retailers to adopt Facebook Live-based selling in 2015.
Over the years, her saree business has sold more than one million sarees, built a social media community of over eight lakh followers and organised more than 190 exhibitions. The business also operates a 5,000 sq ft saree emporium in Banjara Hills, Hyderabad, housing more than 15,000 sarees, including Kalamkari and other regional textile collections.
Sangeetha Rajesh, Founder, Pinit said, "Every saree carries a weaver's skill. Pinit takes that skill to the doorstep, creates dignified jobs for women, and does it without polluting our cities. This is business with a purpose."
The company said its model differs from conventional online saree platforms by combining app-based discovery, stylist-assisted shopping and quick commerce fulfilment. By bringing curated collections directly to customers' homes, Pinit is seeking to bridge the gap between physical saree retail and digital commerce.
Titan Company is evaluating opportunities to acquire or invest in smaller watch brands as it strengthens its presence in the premium and luxury watch market. The move comes at a time when demand for higher-priced watches is growing faster than the mass-market segment in India. Ranjani Krishnaswamy, Chief Marketing Officer at Titan Company, said the watchmaker is open to both organic and inorganic growth opportunities that align with its long-term strategy and help expand its presence across categories and markets.
Discussing potential acquisitions, Krishnaswamy said Titan has previously pursued investments and acquisitions in its jewellery business and could consider a similar approach in the watch category.
"I think we have always felt that when the time is right, and the partner is right, it will certainly be interesting for us to do that. So, we have always been open to inorganic growth as well as organic growth. It just seems it has to be complementary and help us build our larger growth journey," she said.
The comments come as several India-focused micro watch brands gain traction among younger consumers and premium buyers. Titan believes the emergence of new players is helping expand the overall watch market rather than creating a challenge for established brands.
"I have always believed that the most lonely thing that can happen to you is to be the only person in the category. I think competition is a big, big boon to the market leader. It makes the market leader more agile; it makes the market leader more innovative and inventive," Krishnaswamy said.
Titan is also seeing strong momentum in its premium watch portfolio. According to the company, the premium segment is expanding nearly twice as fast as watches priced below Rs 25,000. In contrast, the sub-Rs 1,000 segment is witnessing slower demand as consumers increasingly view watches as fashion and lifestyle accessories. Limited-edition collections and higher-priced watches continue to attract interest from buyers.
The company recently introduced Vetra, its branded movement platform developed to strengthen its capabilities in mechanical watchmaking and premium horology. Titan said the initiative supports its ambition to build a stronger presence in the global watch industry.
"We set ourselves a dream, a vision, saying we want to be the third force in the world of watches. We have the Swiss, we have the Japanese, and we want to be the third force," Krishnaswamy said.
Titan also expects healthy festive season demand, supported by wedding purchases and consumer spending trends. The company operates a broad watch retail network through Titan World, Fastrack and Helios, while also retailing international brands including Tommy Hilfiger, Kenneth Cole, Police, Cerruti and Roamer in India.
Youth fashion brand Wrogn has set a target of reaching Rs 600 crore in gross merchandise value (GMV) in FY27 after reporting Rs 125 crore GMV in the first quarter, reflecting 40 percent year-on-year growth. The apparel brand is also accelerating its retail expansion and strengthening its direct-to-consumer (D2C) business as it scales operations across India.
According to the company, its EBITDA loss narrowed by 34 percent during the quarter, indicating improved operational efficiency. Wrogn reported net revenue of Rs 244 crore in FY26, while its adjusted EBITDA loss reduced to Rs 38 crore from Rs 54 crore in FY25. The company also improved its EBITDA margin by 8.5 percentage points after excluding a one-time non-operational expense.
Owned channels emerged as a major growth driver for the fashion retailer. Revenue from its D2C platform and exclusive brand outlets increased 120 percent year-on-year, highlighting growing consumer engagement through brand-owned channels. Wrogn currently has a presence across more than 250 retail touchpoints through large-format retail partners including Pantaloons, Shoppers Stop, Fashion Factory and Centro, in addition to its marketplace business.
As part of its expansion strategy, the brand plans to grow its owned retail network to over 100 stores by March 2027. The company is also focusing on category diversification, with Wrogn Active and its footwear business together delivering an annualised revenue run rate of Rs 60 crore. Backed by TMRW, the digital-first venture of Aditya Birla Group, and Accel, Wrogn is strengthening its position in India's organised fashion retail market through a combination of offline expansion, D2C growth, and category extensions.
Ubalance Naturals has introduced a new brand identity, ‘The Forest Within’, across its portfolio of nine products and 18 SKUs, as the premium Ayurvedic wellness brand looks to expand its presence in India’s growing wellness market. The company is targeting revenue of Rs 100 crore by FY30.
The new identity is based on the brand’s systems-led approach to wellness, which focuses on the interconnected nature of different bodily systems rather than individual health concerns. The rebrand will be rolled out across packaging, digital platforms, e-commerce and retail touchpoints from September 2026.
The company said the new visual language draws inspiration from Indian forests, folk art and botanical illustrations. It uses elements such as linework, stippling, hatching and organic patterns, along with subtle gold-foil accents. Different illustrations represent themes associated with each product, including roots for resilience, water for renewal, bloom for radiance and heartwood for steadiness.
Gurmeet Kaur, Co-founder, Ubalance Naturals, said, “Our customers have always trusted us for what’s inside the bottle. Now, the outside reflects the same authenticity and purpose. The Forest Within brings our philosophy of interconnected balance to life through a refined visual identity rooted in nature and true to who we have always been.”
The company combines Ayurvedic principles with contemporary scientific understanding and uses plant-based ingredients in its formulations. Its portfolio is predominantly made up of liquid products, covering areas such as energy, stress response, digestive and liver wellness, metabolic health, respiratory wellness and mobility.
Kaur added that the company is working towards expanding its reach to 100,000 families by 2028. “Building on its established approach to wellness, Ubalance Naturals combines wild-sourced botanicals, careful processing to preserve ingredient integrity, and liquid Ayurvedic formulations designed for ease of consumption and efficient nutrient delivery,” she said.
According to industry estimates cited by the company, India’s Ayurvedic wellness market was valued at around USD 11.9 billion in 2025 and is projected to reach USD 43.2 billion by 2034, growing at a compound annual growth rate of nearly 15 percent.
The rebrand comes as wellness consumers increasingly seek products positioned around preventive and holistic health. Ubalance Naturals said its new identity is intended to create a consistent brand experience across consumer touchpoints while communicating its focus on interconnected wellbeing.
Devendra Kumar Oberoi, Co-founder, Ubalance Naturals, said, “Our purpose has always been rooted in a simple belief: when the body and mind find balance, human potential flourishes. The Forest Within brings this philosophy to life, giving our belief in interconnected wellbeing a new expression inspired by nature. Our identity has evolved, but our purpose remains unchanged.”
Ubalance Naturals was co-founded by Gurmeet Kaur and Devendra Kumar Oberoi. The company’s formulations are manufactured by AMV Botanics Pvt. Ltd. at facilities adhering to GMP and ISO-certified quality management standards. The company also reports independent batch testing across various safety and efficacy parameters.
FMCG companies are likely to hold prices through the festive season even amid rise in the prices of commodity like sugar due to geopolitical disruptions. Companies seek to protect the consumer demand and maintain volume growth as the consumption improves.
Leading industry executives said companies have already implemented measured price increases of around 2-5 per cent in the June quarter to partly offset higher input costs and are unlikely to raise prices further before the end of the festive season, even as margins remain under pressure.
The sector is facing renewed cost pressures, with sugar prices touching a new high, along with a sharp increase in the costs of key inputs such as edible oils, coffee, cocoa and crude oil derivatives used in packaging. Geopolitical disruptions and supply concerns in global markets have further added to the pressure.
While most companies have absorbed a significant portion of the inflation through cost-control initiatives and portfolio management, they remain focused on protecting volume growth even as margin pressures remain elevated, industry executives said.
ITC Chief Executive Officer, Foods Division, and Executive Director Hemant Malik said the company would maintain prices through the festive season despite cost inflation.
"We are attempting to hold prices," Malik said, noting that companies have been absorbing a large part of the increase in commodity prices through cost management initiatives and portfolio actions.
Referring to the impact of the GST rate reduction on several consumer products last year, Malik said the move had led to buoyancy in volumes across multiple categories and supported market demand.
However, he indicated that companies may have to revisit pricing decisions later in the financial year if cost pressures persist.
"Maybe in quarter three or quarter four, we will have to look at some corrections on prices," he said, adding that most FMCG firms have so far implemented only modest price hikes of around 3-5 per cent despite facing much higher cost increases.
Home-grown FMCG major Dabur India, which has also taken calibrated pricing actions on select products to partly mitigate input costs, is monitoring the situation.
"We have taken up prices on a few products over the past few months to partly mitigate the inflationary impact due to the geopolitical situation, while keeping the competitive intensity in mind. Going forward, we will be closely watching the situation as it develops," said Dabur India CFO Ankush Jain.
Parle Products Chief Marketing Officer Mayank Shah said most FMCG firms are expected to hold prices at least until Diwali, citing strong demand across urban and rural markets and a recent easing in sugar prices due to government measures.
"Most companies would probably be holding the price right now. They will not increase prices because of the festive season. Nobody would like to disrupt demand," Shah said.
According to Shah, demand has been encouraging across both urban and rural markets, and companies would prefer to sustain the momentum rather than risk slowing consumption through price increases.
He said easing prices of certain commodities, particularly sugar, following government interventions has also provided some relief to manufacturers.
"My understanding is that at least till the festive time, as in till October-November, we will not see any major price hike coming in FMCG categories," Shah said.
He added that companies are focusing on operational efficiencies and cost optimisation measures to protect profitability while prioritising volume-led growth.
"Companies would prefer volume growth rather than increasing the pricing right now," Shah said.
The comments come amid several FMCG makers grappling with higher costs of key inputs, including edible oils and packaging materials, amid supply-chain disruptions and geopolitical uncertainties.
Titan Company, the Tata Group's watch and jewellery major, is open to exploring acquisitions and investments in emerging watch brands as it looks to strengthen its position across different market segments, according to a senior company executive.
"The company is also expecting a strong festive season this year, supported by healthy consumer demand and an early wedding season that overlaps with a later-than-usual Diwali," said Ranjani Krishnaswamy, Chief Marketing Officer, Titan Company.
The company is currently working to match rising consumer demand with adequate production capacity.
"We are looking at a very robust demand. We are seeing a very healthy start to the festive season. We are very optimistic and, hand on heart, we are struggling to ensure we have the capacity to service demand," commented Krishnaswamy.
Krishnaswamy said Titan remains open to opportunities that align with its long-term growth plans and help expand its presence across categories and markets.
Referring to Titan's experience with acquisitions and investments in the jewellery business, including CaratLane and international ventures, she said the company could consider similar opportunities in the watch segment.
Krishnaswamy said the possibility of acquiring or investing in watch brands has been discussed within the company.
"I think we have always felt that when the time is right, and the partner is right, it will certainly be interesting for us to do that. Titan as a company has done it on the jewellery side of the business, whether you look at CaratLane or some of the other investments we have made abroad," further stated Krishnaswamy.
According to Krishnaswamy, any acquisition strategy would need to complement Titan's broader business objectives and contribute meaningfully to its long-term expansion.
Her comments come at a time when several India-focused micro watch brands are gaining visibility by offering products inspired by local culture, design aesthetics, and craftsmanship. These brands have been attracting interest from younger consumers and affluent buyers seeking differentiated products.
Rather than viewing these players as competitors, Krishnaswamy described their emergence as beneficial for the overall watch industry.
"I have always believed that the most lonely thing that can happen to you is to be the only person in the category. I think competition is a big, big boon to the market leader. It makes the market leader more agile; it makes the market leader more innovative and inventive," she said.
Last week, Titan introduced Vetra, its branded movement platform, which marks a significant step in the company's efforts to strengthen India's presence in global watchmaking. The name combines "Veda," meaning knowledge, and "Tra," meaning instrument.
Highlighting Titan's ambitions in the global watch industry, Krishnaswamy said the company is working towards establishing India as a major force in watchmaking alongside established markets such as Switzerland and Japan.
"We set ourselves a dream, a vision, saying we want to be the third force in the world of watches. We have the Swiss, we have the Japanese, and we want to be the third force," Krishnaswamy said, adding that the company was pursuing the goal with "a lot of pride and a lot of hard work".
On market trends, Krishnaswamy said Titan continues to witness strong momentum in its premium watch portfolio, with the segment growing nearly twice as fast as categories priced below Rs 25,000.
At the same time, she pointed out that the mass-market segment priced below Rs 1,000 has been experiencing slower demand, as consumers increasingly view watches as fashion and lifestyle accessories. Demand for premium and limited-edition timepieces, meanwhile, remains strong.
Honasa Consumer Ltd, the parent company of beauty and personal care brand Mamaearth, has outlined plans to double its revenue over the next five years, targeting Rs 5,550 crore by FY31 while aiming to improve profitability through margin expansion. Founders Ghazal Alagh and Varun Alagh said the company aims to become one of the fastest-growing FMCG businesses in India to achieve the Rs 5,000 crore revenue milestone.
According to the founders, Honasa expects to reach the Rs 5,500 crore revenue mark by FY31 by continuing to build consumer-focused brands across its portfolio. The company also expects its EBITDA margin to expand to 15 percent over the same period.
The founders stated that the company plans to achieve this growth by “building brands that are loved by Indian consumers” and aims to reach a 15 pc Ebitda margin, “unlocking a further 500 basis points as mix and scale move our way.”
For FY26, Honasa Consumer reported a total income of Rs 475.53 crore, reflecting a 15.37 percent year-on-year increase.
Despite setting ambitious financial goals, the founders emphasized that revenue and profitability targets are outcomes rather than primary objectives.
The company plans to continue focusing on core categories including face cleansers, shampoos, sunscreens, moisturisers, face serums, lipsticks, and baby care products, which currently account for around 80 percent of its revenue. At the same time, it intends to explore additional segments within both existing and emerging categories.
Discussing the performance of its flagship brand Mamaearth, the founders said the brand strengthened its position during FY26, gaining both Value Market Share and Share-Amongst-Handlers in the face cleanser and shampoo categories across General Trade and Modern Trade channels, according to NielsenIQ data.
"The brand that built this company is growing again and is better built now for what comes next," they said.
The founders also highlighted shifts in consumer behavior, noting that beauty discovery is increasingly happening through digital platforms and content creators rather than traditional mass-media advertising.
According to them, consumers are increasingly prioritizing product efficacy and ingredient transparency over generic beauty offerings.
The company also sees Gen Z consumers playing a key role in shaping future demand, with younger shoppers adopting products earlier and expecting greater innovation from brands.
Drawing comparisons with global markets, the founders said: “We have watched this story unfold before, in the US, in China, in Indonesia: wherever e-commerce has surged, it is the home-grown challengers who gain the most. India's online share of retail is still in its early innings and set to roughly double by the turn of the decade. We intend to be standing exactly where that wave breaks."
Beauty and cosmetics brand Swiss Beauty has strengthened its offline retail network with the launch of a new Swiss Beauty Select Exclusive Brand Outlet (EBO) at Phoenix United Mall, Bareilly. The latest store opening forms part of the company’s broader retail expansion strategy as it continues to increase its presence across India’s beauty and personal care market.
The newly opened outlet is expected to offer consumers in Bareilly easier access to Swiss Beauty’s range of makeup, skincare, and beauty products through a dedicated brand experience.
Eyewear retailer Lenskart Solutions has increased its shareholding in Dimension NXG, the parent company of extended reality (XR) startup AjnaLens, after making an additional investment of nearly Rs 8 crore.
Lenskart acquired a 1.8 percent stake in Dimension NXG for Rs 7.99 crore, with the transaction being completed on September 13, 2026.
The latest investment marks Lenskart’s third stake acquisition in the company this year. The company had earlier purchased an additional 0.68 percent stake in February and 1.69 percent in July. Following these transactions, Lenskart’s ownership in Dimension NXG has risen from 4.84 percent to 9.01 percent.
Across the three investments made in 2026, Lenskart has deployed a total of Rs 18.5 crore, increasing its stake by 4.17 percent in the XR technology company.
The company said the investment aligns with its strategy of strengthening ties with the extended reality, artificial intelligence (AI), and smart wearable technology ecosystem, while also supporting innovation opportunities in the smart eyewear segment.
Lenskart first partnered with AjnaLens in July 2025 as part of its efforts to develop AI-powered smart glasses. The collaboration combines Lenskart’s capabilities in eyewear design and engineering with AjnaLens’ expertise in XR technologies.
Established in 2014 by Pankaj Raut, Abhijit Patil, and Abhishek Tomar, AjnaLens develops XR-based hardware and software solutions and serves sectors including defence and enterprise technology.
Financially, Dimension NXG reported a decline in revenue, with turnover falling 35 percent to Rs 10.36 crore in FY26, compared to Rs 15.97 crore in FY24.
The investment comes as Lenskart continues to expand its presence in the smart eyewear category. The company has already introduced products such as Phonic audio glasses and is actively developing AI-enabled smart glasses. It has also partnered with Qualcomm to build the technology stack for its upcoming smart eyewear offerings.
Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Limited (ABFRL) has completed the acquisition of the remaining stake in Imperial Online Services Private Limited, taking its ownership in the fashion and apparel company to 100 percent.
The transaction was executed through ABFRL’s wholly owned subsidiary, Aditya Birla Digital Fashion Ventures Limited (ABDFVL), which acquired an additional 15.62 percent equity stake in Imperial on September 17, 2026. Following the completion of the deal, Imperial has become a wholly owned subsidiary of ABDFVL and a step-down wholly owned subsidiary of ABFRL.
The acquisition was carried out in accordance with the Share Subscription and Shareholders’ Agreement signed on July 11, 2022, which outlined specific milestones for the gradual increase in ABDFVL’s ownership in the company.
Founded in 2012, Imperial Online Services operates in the fashion, apparel, and accessories segment. The company is best known for manufacturing, marketing, and distributing fashion apparel under the Urbano brand, with products sold through both online and offline retail channels.
Imperial has reported steady business growth over the past three financial years. The company recorded a turnover of Rs 119.38 crore in the financial year ended March 31, 2026, compared to Rs 77.93 crore in FY2025 and Rs 66.78 crore in FY2024.
The stake acquisition was completed through a cash transaction under previously agreed terms and conditions. No regulatory approvals were required for the deal. With this acquisition, ABDFVL’s shareholding in Imperial has increased from 84.38 percent to 100 percent.
The move strengthens ABFRL’s position in the fashion and apparel sector by bringing the Urbano business entirely under its subsidiary network. It also aligns with the company’s broader strategy of expanding and consolidating its portfolio across key segments of the Indian fashion market.
Headquartered in Mumbai, ABFRL operates a diversified portfolio of fashion and lifestyle brands and continues to strengthen its presence across premium, value, and digital-first fashion categories in India.
Titan Company Ltd is strengthening its presence in India's premium watch market with the launch of Vetra, a new mechanical movement platform designed to support the company's expansion in the high-end horology segment. The leading watchmaker expects its mechanical watch business to grow by around 30 percent this fiscal year, reaching approximately Rs 350 crore.
The category generated nearly Rs 270 crore in revenue in the previous financial year and currently contributes about 9-10 percent of Titan's total watch revenues. According to Kuruvilla Markose, CEO, Watches Business Division, Titan Company Ltd, the mechanical watch category is expected to maintain strong momentum over the next four to five years.
"The mechanical watch segment is expected to witness strong momentum over the next four to five years, with the category projected to grow at around 35 percent CAGR. This growth will be driven by increasing consumer appreciation for craftsmanship and precision engineering associated with mechanical timepieces, alongside a growing shift towards premium watches," Markose said.
The newly launched Vetra platform will serve as the foundation for Titan’s future mechanical watch innovations and premium timepieces. The name combines 'Veda' (knowledge) and 'Tra' (instrument), reflecting the company's focus on engineering and watchmaking capabilities. Titan said the platform is expected to strengthen its position in the premium watch and luxury watch segment, where consumer interest in analogue and mechanical watches has been increasing globally.
Markose noted that consumers are increasingly looking for products that emphasize engineering, craftsmanship, and exclusivity.
"People want watches that have something special about them. At a fundamental level, a mechanical watch is a micro-engineered device. It is a highly precise and sophisticated engineering device," he said.
He added that the category has benefited from changing consumer preferences following the pandemic.
"I think that is a trend that we are seeing. We are seeing our mechanical watches grow quite significantly, and that is why we felt it was important to create a branded platform," Markose added.
Titan has reported nearly a fivefold increase in mechanical watch sales over the last three years. The company said advancements in its watchmaking capabilities and product sophistication led to the development of a dedicated platform for its mechanical movements. With Vetra, Titan aims to establish stronger recognition for its in-house movement technology. The company plans to build awareness around the platform like branded processor ecosystems, while further enhancing its watchmaking expertise.
"The Titan Watches Division purpose statement is that Titan exists to make India a force in modern horology," Markose said, adding that achieving this vision could take five to ten years and would require support from the broader Indian manufacturing ecosystem.
The Vetra platform debuts with Titan's 7 Series, built on 7,000-calibre movements, including a newly developed 72-hour power reserve movement, an improvement over the company's earlier 40-hour reserve technology.
As part of its premiumisation strategy, Titan expects watches priced above Rs 25,000 to contribute nearly one-fourth of its revenue over the next two to three years. The company is also targeting approximately $2 billion in sales by FY30, with premium and luxury watch retail chains Helios and Helios Luxe expected to play a significant role in future growth. The move reflects the growing demand for premium watches, luxury timepieces, mechanical watches, and Indian watchmaking innovation as consumers increasingly gravitate toward higher-value categories within the watch industry.
Kothari Industrial Corporation Limited (KICL), the flagship company of the D.C. Kothari Group, has entered the fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) sector with the launch of its beverage portfolio under the CHUSIP brand. The company has introduced CHUSIP Coco Twist, a tender coconut water beverage, marking its diversification into India's growing health drinks and non-carbonated beverage market.
The newly launched beverage is available in a 200 ml pack priced at Rs 50, while a one-litre pack is expected to be introduced at a later stage. According to the company, the product contains 100 percent natural tender coconut water with no added sugar or preservatives. KICL also plans to expand the portfolio with additional flavours and products, including fruit drinks, beverages with and without pulp, and offerings containing Nata De Coco.
As part of its market expansion strategy, KICL will initially focus on strengthening its presence in South India. The company plans to appoint 100 distributors and trade partners across Tamil Nadu, Kerala, and Karnataka before expanding into other regions, digital commerce channels, and international markets.
Jinnah Rafiq Ahamed, Executive Director, KICL said, "Our research findings show there is a trend emerging in India of consumers moving towards healthy, natural and authentic choices. We strongly believe this is the right time to bring back the purity of nature in the form of coconut water sourced from the finest coconut farms. This launch marks KICL’s foray into the FMCG sector and is the first step towards building a portfolio that is rooted in nature, health and trust."
The company has also outlined long-term growth plans for its beverage business and aims to build a Rs 2,500 crore beverage portfolio by 2035. The launch comes at a time when demand for healthy beverages, natural drinks, coconut water, and wellness-focused FMCG products continues to grow across India's food and beverage sector.
Myntra has introduced Italian fashion brand Sisley in India, expanding its portfolio of international fashion labels as demand for premium global brands continues to grow among Indian consumers. Sisley is part of the Benetton Group and operates in more than 40 countries through over 400 points of sale worldwide.
The latest Sisley collection is now available on Myntra and includes apparel across categories such as T-shirts, shirts, tops, knitwear, trousers, jeans, skirts, coats, blazers, and jackets for men and women. The launch strengthens Myntra’s presence in the premium fashion and international apparel segment in India.
Sisley was established in Paris in 1968 and became part of the Benetton Group in 1974. The brand has built a global presence across key fashion markets and is now looking to expand its reach among Indian consumers through Myntra’s digital commerce platform.
Venu Nair, SVP, Chief of Strategic Partnerships and Omni-channel, Myntra said, “India has emerged as one of the world's most dynamic fashion markets, and Myntra is uniquely positioned to enable iconic global brands like Sisley to tap into this massive opportunity and strategically scale their presence. The brand brings a distinctive premium contemporary Italian fashion perspective to the fashion-forward Indian shoppers.”
Nicola Capone, CEO, Distribution, Benetton Group said, “The launch of Sisley in India through Myntra represents an important step in strengthening the brand’s presence in a market of strategic relevance. We believe that Indian consumers will appreciate Sisley’s distinctive identity as an urban lifestyle brand, combining creativity, contemporary design, and a unique interpretation of fashion trends. This partnership provides a solid foundation for expanding the brand’s reach and supporting its long-term development in India.”
The launch comes as international fashion brands continue to gain traction in India, with consumers increasingly seeking premium apparel, global fashion trends, and international labels through online retail channels. Myntra currently offers a portfolio of more than 500 international brands on its platform.
Global SS Beauty Brands Limited (GSSBB), a subsidiary of Shoppers Stop Limited, has entered into an exclusive strategic partnership with INTERPARFUMS SA to distribute, develop, and grow its portfolio of prestige fragrance brands in India. The partnership marks a significant move in India's luxury beauty and fragrance market, with GSSBB taking responsibility for the distribution, market development, and brand-building of INTERPARFUMS SA’s fragrance portfolio across the country.
Founded in 1982, INTERPARFUMS SA designs, manufactures, and distributes prestige fragrances and fragrance-related products through licensing and other agreements with international brand owners. The company operates in more than 120 countries and manages fragrance brands including Coach, Montblanc, Jimmy Choo, Lacoste, Rochas, Lanvin, Karl Lagerfeld, and Van Cleef & Arpels.
The collaboration aims to strengthen the presence of global luxury fragrance brands in India, a market witnessing growing demand for premium beauty and personal care products. By combining INTERPARFUMS SA’s international fragrance portfolio with GSSBB’s retail expertise, market insights, and consumer reach, the companies plan to expand their footprint in the Indian luxury fragrance segment.
Philippe Benacin, Co-founder and CEO, INTERPARFUMS SA, said, “India is one of the most promising luxury fragrance markets globally, driven by a young, aspirational consumer base and a growing appreciation for prestigious international brands. At INTERPARFUMS our portfolio is built on decades of craftsmanship, innovation, and enduring brand equity. We are delighted to introduce our brands to Indian consumers with a partner that possesses deep market expertise and a strong understanding of the luxury beauty landscape. Global SS Beauty Brands brings the retail excellence and strategic insight needed to build our brands with purpose, and we look forward to a long-term, successful partnership.”
Biju Kassim, MD and CEO, Global SS Beauty Brands Ltd said, " Our partnership with INTERPARFUMS SA marks another important milestone in our journey to strengthen the luxury fragrance category in India. As consumer demand for globally renowned prestige brands continues to grow, our focus is on building these brands for the long term through thoughtful market development, meaningful consumer engagement, and exceptional retail experiences. INTERPARFUMS' portfolio represents some of the world's most iconic fragrance brands, and we are excited to partner with them to unlock their full potential in India while further reinforcing Global SS Beauty Brands as the partner of choice for leading global beauty brands.”
The agreement is expected to support the expansion of premium fragrance brands in India while strengthening GSSBB’s position in the luxury beauty retail and prestige fragrance categories.
Bhumika Realty, the real estate arm of Bhumika Group, has announced the signing of Lifestyle for a 24,000 sq. ft. anchor store at The Icon, Faridabad, further strengthening the retail mix at its flagship mixed-use development. The new store will span the ground and first floors of the project and is expected to bring one of India’s leading fashion and lifestyle retail destinations to consumers in the city.
Lifestyle, part of the Dubai-based Landmark Group, operates more than 170 stores across eight countries and has established a strong presence in the fashion and lifestyle retail segment. In India, the retailer has a network of over 77 stores across 44 cities, offering customers access to more than 300 international brands across categories including fashion, footwear, beauty, and accessories.
The addition of Lifestyle is expected to enhance the retail offering at The Icon, which is being developed as an integrated destination combining retail, entertainment, hospitality, and residential components.
Uddhav Poddar, CMD, Bhumika Group said, “Faridabad is evolving into an important consumption and retail market within the NCR, with consumers increasingly looking for leading brands and quality experiences closer to home. Bringing Lifestyle to The Icon is an important addition to our retail mix and reinforces our vision of creating a destination that combines leading retail, entertainment and hospitality. Along with PVR INOX, Lifestyle further strengthens the brand ecosystem we are building at The Icon.”
The announcement follows the recent addition of a 25,000 sq. ft. PVR INOX multiplex at the project, strengthening its entertainment component and supporting Bhumika Realty’s strategy of creating a comprehensive lifestyle destination in Faridabad.
The Icon has been designed by Bentel Associates, South Africa. The project is planned as a mixed-use development integrating premium retail spaces, entertainment options, hospitality offerings, and residential units within a single destination.
Pet care platform WAGR is broadening its offerings beyond pet products by bringing together shopping, AI-powered guidance, service discovery, and personalized pet information into a single ecosystem. The move comes as pet ownership in India continues to grow, with consumers increasingly seeking integrated solutions for nutrition, grooming, training, wellness, and healthcare needs.
The company aims to address challenges faced by pet parents who often rely on multiple platforms and service providers to manage different aspects of pet care. By combining products, guidance, and services in one place, WAGR is positioning itself as a comprehensive platform for pet owners.
WAGR currently offers products from established pet care brands including Royal Canin, Pedigree, Whiskas, Sheba, Drools, and Temptations, alongside emerging brands such as Bruni Boi, Cuddl, Cure By Design, Halalicious, Moe Puppy, and Let’s Wag. Its portfolio spans categories including pet food, treats, grooming products, wellness solutions, toys, accessories, and daily essentials for dogs and cats.
The company said its strategy is centered on supporting pet parents throughout their journey rather than focusing solely on product purchases.
Fredun Medhora, Director, WAGR said, “We don’t want WAGR to be another place where pet parents shop; we want it to become a companion they turn to. The opportunity is to bring together products, answers, trusted services and technology around the everyday reality of pet parenting. We are building for that future, even if it means taking bets the category has not taken before.”
As part of this approach, WAGR has introduced TOTO, an AI-powered pet-parenting companion designed to help users navigate everyday concerns related to feeding, nutrition, activity, grooming, behavior, and general pet care. The tool is intended to provide guidance and information, particularly for first-time pet owners, while helping them make more informed decisions. The company clarified that TOTO is not intended to provide veterinary diagnosis, treatment, or replace professional medical advice.
WAGR has also expanded its platform through its Discover feature, which connects pet parents with service providers such as groomers, trainers, walkers, boarding facilities, veterinary clinics, and other pet-care professionals. The initiative is aimed at simplifying the process of finding trusted service providers, a challenge often faced by new pet owners.
In addition, the platform’s Pet Profile feature allows users to maintain important pet information, health records, and other details in one place. According to the company, integrating pet profiles with shopping, guidance, and service discovery enables a more personalized experience for users.
L Catterton has acquired a minority stake in Bengaluru-based restaurant company Nandhana Foods, which operates the Nandhana Palace and RNR brands.
According to media reports, the investment is estimated at around USD 30 million, although the exact deal value and stake size have not been officially disclosed.
Nandhana Foods has built its business around Andhra and Karnataka cuisine and has a presence across Bengaluru and Chennai. The company operates more than 30 locations and was developed under the leadership of Dr. Ravichandar and his daughters Shweta, Ramya and Ravina.
The investment comes as regional restaurant chains continue to attract investor interest amid the expansion of India’s organised food services market. L Catterton said the partnership will support the company’s next phase of growth, with a focus on strengthening operations and expanding into existing and new markets.
“South Indian cuisine is one of the largest segments of India’s burgeoning food services market,” L Catterton said.
The investment firm said the segment is being supported by increasing per-capita spending on dining out and food delivery, along with a rise in consumption occasions. L Catterton also sees scope for Nandhana to expand its presence across South India and enter additional markets.
“We are thrilled to announce the partnership of L Catterton with Nandhana Palace, a legendary culinary institution that has been delighting food lovers across South India for over three decades,” said Sanjiv Mehta, Executive Chairman India, L Catterton, in a LinkedIn post.
The partnership is expected to focus on professionalising the business while retaining its established heritage and values. L Catterton also plans to work with the founding family on scaling operations and expanding the restaurant network.
The transaction adds to the growing investor activity in India’s foodservice sector, particularly around established regional brands with multi-city operations. For Nandhana, the partnership comes at a time when restaurant operators are looking to increase their footprint while building more structured business and operational systems.
Jewellery retailer BlueStone has appointed Amit Jain, Co-founder and Chief Executive Officer of CarDekho Group, as a Non-Executive Non-Independent Director, effective September 14, 2026.
The appointment was approved during the company’s 15th Annual General Meeting. Jain succeeds Sameer Dileep Nath, who retired by rotation and did not seek reappointment to the board.
Founded in 2011, BlueStone operates as an omnichannel jewellery retailer, combining its online platform with a growing network of physical stores across India. The company offers a wide range of jewellery products and has continued to strengthen its presence in the organised jewellery retail market.
BlueStone describes itself as India’s second-largest digital-first omnichannel jewellery brand. During the first quarter of FY27, the company expanded its retail footprint by opening 12 new stores, taking its total store count to 352 outlets across 139 cities. The brand currently serves customers across more than 12,660 PIN codes, with nearly half of its stores located in Tier II and Tier III cities.
The company also reported strong financial performance during the quarter. In Q1 FY27, BlueStone recorded Rs 737 crore in operating revenue, reflecting a 49 percent year-on-year growth. The jewellery retailer posted a net profit of Rs 6 crore, compared to a net loss of Rs 35 crore during the corresponding period last year, marking a return to profitability.
BlueStone's improving financial performance comes amid continued expansion in India's organised jewellery sector, where it competes with major players including CaratLane, Tanishq, Kalyan Jewellers, Senco Gold, PC Jeweller, and Thangamayil Jewellery.
With Amit Jain joining its board, BlueStone aims to strengthen its leadership team as it continues to scale its omnichannel jewellery business and expand its retail presence across the country.
Samsung India expects its digital appliances business to deliver double-digit year-on-year growth in the second half of 2026, supported by festive season demand and increasing consumer preference for premium home appliances, according to a senior company executive.
Ghufran Alam, Vice President, Digital Appliances Business, Samsung India, said the company has witnessed encouraging sales trends beginning with the Onam season and expects the momentum to continue through upcoming festivals, including Dussehra and Diwali.
The company remains optimistic about consumer spending despite inflationary concerns and global economic uncertainties.
Commenting on market demand, Alam said, "Independence Day sales, which were before the Onam period (August 26), we have seen robust demand. So, Diwali also, and coming festivals also, we see good growth prospects for the appliances business in India."
The Onam season, which traditionally marks the start of India's festive shopping period, delivered strong results for the home appliances sector. Samsung reported high double-digit growth during the period, reflecting sustained consumer interest across product categories.
On pricing, Samsung said it is closely monitoring commodity costs, including copper prices, but has not made any decision regarding price increases ahead of the festive season.
"Whether we are going to increase the price in Diwali or before the festival, we do not have any kind of, at this moment, we do not know currently, because it is all very dynamic," Alam noted.
The company also highlighted the growing trend of premiumisation within India's consumer electronics and home appliances market. Samsung said average selling prices are increasing at a faster pace than overall volumes, indicating stronger demand for premium products across both urban and rural markets. Flexible financing options such as no-cost EMI schemes are also encouraging consumers to upgrade to higher-value products.
Among key categories, room air conditioners (RACs) are expected to remain Samsung's fastest-growing segment during the second half of the year, followed by washing machines and refrigerators. The company attributed this growth to sustained cooling demand in southern India and increased festive purchases.
Within the refrigerator category, Samsung is witnessing stronger demand for French-door and side-by-side refrigerators, particularly models with capacities exceeding 450 litres. In washing machines, consumers are increasingly opting for larger-capacity products ranging between 10 kg and 14 kg across both front-load and top-load segments.
Ahead of the festive season, Samsung has expanded its premium appliance portfolio with the introduction of new air conditioner models, including a cassette AC and a room AC. The company has also upgraded the artificial intelligence capabilities of its Family Hub refrigerators through Gemini integration, enhancing food recognition features beyond the previously supported range.
Amazon has launched Alexa+ in India, introducing a new generative AI-powered version of its voice assistant designed to offer more natural conversations, personalized experiences, and deeper integration with smart home devices, shopping services, entertainment platforms, and daily utility applications. The company said Alexa+ is now available under Early Access at no additional cost for eligible Echo smart speakers, smart displays, Fire TV devices, and the Alexa mobile app. The launch marks Amazon's latest push into the rapidly growing artificial intelligence, smart home, voice technology, and digital assistant segments in India.
Teena Sidana, Country Manager for Alexa, Amazon India said, "Indian households are multi-generational, multilingual, and beautifully complex. Alexa+ was designed for that complexity. She understands intent, adapts to your household’s preferences, and lets each family member interact in the way that feels most natural to them. India is home to one of the most diverse set of customers in the world, and we're excited for them to experience how much smarter, personalized, and more intuitive Alexa+ has become. It was truly built around the way they live. We want to make everyday life simpler for hundreds of millions of people who speak, shop, and live differently from one another and build the world's best personal assistant.”
According to Amazon, Alexa+ has been built to understand conversational speech patterns and user intent, allowing customers to interact naturally without repeatedly using the wake word. The assistant supports English, Hindi, and Hinglish, enabling users to switch languages during conversations while maintaining context.
Amazon said additional Indian language support will be introduced in the future.
Alexa+ is designed to work with a range of connected devices and services used by Indian consumers. The platform supports smart home products from brands including Atomberg, Qubo, Dreame, and Wipro, enabling voice-based control of appliances and connected devices.
Users can also access recipe recommendations through Sanjeev Kapoor Recipes and discover music, podcasts, movies, and TV shows across platforms such as Amazon Music, Spotify, Apple Music, JioSaavn, Prime Video, and Netflix.
Amazon further revealed that integrations with EazyDiner, Swiggy, District by Zomato, MakeMyTrip, Home Triangle, and TripAdvisor will be introduced soon, expanding Alexa+'s capabilities across food delivery, restaurant reservations, travel bookings, home services, and event planning.
The company said Alexa+ uses voice and visual identification technologies to recognize individual family members and tailor responses based on preferences and routines. The assistant can remember dietary preferences, entertainment choices, and daily schedules, allowing it to provide customized recommendations and reminders for different household members.
Amazon has also integrated shopping-focused features into Alexa+, enabling customers to create shopping lists, track Amazon orders, receive price-drop alerts, compare products, summarize verified customer reviews, and discover related products through voice interactions.
The company added that customers will soon be able to order groceries and everyday essentials using voice commands through Amazon Now, completing purchases through natural conversations.
Amazon said Alexa+ has been developed with a strong focus on Indian languages, cultural references, and communication styles. The assistant can understand local expressions, relationship terms, measurements, and commonly used phrases that are part of everyday conversations across Indian households.
The company noted that a significant portion of the technology powering Alexa+'s cultural and linguistic understanding was developed by teams based in Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune, and Chennai.
Alexa+ is powered by Amazon Bedrock, which connects more than 70 large language models, including Amazon-developed AI models and models from Anthropic. Amazon said the platform automatically selects the most suitable model depending on the task being performed.
The company also highlighted privacy and security features, including access to the Alexa Privacy Dashboard, voice recording controls, microphone and camera settings, and transparency tools that allow customers to review interactions.
Alexa+ is currently available through eligible Echo devices, Fire TV products, and the Alexa app in India. Browser access is expected to be introduced at a later stage.
The service will remain free during the Early Access period. After Early Access concludes, Alexa+ will continue to be available at no additional cost for Prime plan members. For Prime Lite, Prime Shopping Edition, and non-Prime customers, access will be offered through a standalone subscription priced at Rs 2,000 per month or through an eligible Prime membership plan.
Amazon also introduced new Alexa+-optimized devices, including the Echo Show 8, Echo Show 11, Echo Dot Max, and Echo Studio, which have been designed with enhanced processing power and next-generation hardware capabilities.
Real estate major DLF Limited has appointed Nimit Porwal as Vice President, responsible for driving the growth and development of its DLF5 business in Gurugram. Porwal shared the update in a LinkedIn post, saying he was beginning a "new mandate" at a familiar organization and looked forward to contributing to DLF5's continued expansion.
In his new role, he will oversee business strategy, product development, project execution, and profit and loss (P&L) management across DLF5's luxury residential and retail portfolio. The appointment comes as DLF continues to strengthen its presence in India's luxury real estate, premium housing, and retail real estate segments.
Prior to joining DLF, Porwal served as Strategy and P&L Lead for Indore at Godrej Properties, where he led the company's entry into the city. His responsibilities included land acquisitions, project planning, residential project launches, office and team setup, along with sales and marketing operations. Porwal is no stranger to DLF. He previously spent nearly two years with the company as Cluster Business Head, leading business strategy, product management, and P&L operations for the DLF5 super-luxury portfolio.
During his earlier tenure, he led the conceptualization and launch of The Dahlias, a luxury residential project that generated topline revenue of more than Rs 30,000 crore. He also contributed to DLF5's master planning initiatives and played a role in the development strategy for projects such as The Grove and The Summit Plaza.
With experience across real estate development, asset management, investment risk management, and consulting, Porwal has also worked with CBRE India, Piramal Capital and Housing Finance, and KPMG India. The leadership appointment is expected to support DLF's ongoing focus on expanding its luxury residential, mixed-use, and retail real estate portfolio in Gurugram, a key market for the company's long-term growth strategy.
Tata Group-backed jewellery retailer CaratLane has launched a dedicated e-commerce platform for Australia, marking the company's latest step in expanding its international presence. The new website will allow customers across Australia to browse and purchase CaratLane's diamond and gold jewellery collections directly through a localized online platform.
The launch is aimed at improving accessibility for customers in Australia, particularly the Indian diaspora, while strengthening CaratLane's growing global jewellery business. The platform offers a localized shopping experience, including product discovery, online transactions, and nationwide delivery services.
Saumen Bhaumik, Managing Director, CaratLane said, “Indian consumers in Australia have long shown a strong desire for CaratLane designs, making this launch a natural progression for the brand. By introducing a localised platform, we’re removing cross-border friction to deliver a seamless shopping experience directly to their doorsteps, marking a major milestone in our global growth story. It’s part of our larger vision to make CaratLane the most loved jewellery brand amongst Indian women, and Australia plays a critical role in that journey.”
The Australia launch expands CaratLane's international footprint beyond its existing operations in markets including the United States, Canada, Singapore, and the United Kingdom. The company currently serves customers in more than 30 countries and has been increasing its focus on overseas growth through a mix of online and offline channels.
CaratLane has also been strengthening its retail network and omnichannel strategy in India. The jewellery retailer recently outlined plans to add new stores across multiple markets while continuing investments in digital capabilities and customer experience initiatives.
The Australia-focused platform will offer certified jewellery products supported by insured shipping and authenticity documentation. The move reflects the growing trend among Indian jewellery brands to expand internationally through digital commerce, targeting overseas consumers seeking access to Indian-designed jewellery and diamond collections. As global demand for Indian jewellery continues to rise, CaratLane's latest expansion underscores the increasing role of cross-border e-commerce and omnichannel retail strategies in driving growth for Indian jewellery brands.
EBG Group has announced its entry into India’s toy retail and children’s lifestyle market with the launch of Adhira and Appa Toys, a new homegrown toy brand focused on play, learning, and family experiences. The company plans to open its first retail store in Hyderabad by the end of 2026 and invest more than Rs 50 crore to expand the brand to 50 stores across India by 2027.
The brand will offer a wide range of products designed for children from infancy to pre-teen years, spanning categories such as STEM toys, educational toys, robotics kits, science kits, sensory-development products, puzzles, board games, arts and crafts, pretend-play toys, dolls, action figures, ride-ons, plush toys, outdoor play products, electronics, and collectibles.
Irfan Khan, Founder and Chairman, EBG Group said, “We are not building another toy store. We are building a world where children can explore, imagine, learn, and dream. For us, a good toy should create joy today, curiosity tomorrow, and memories that stay with a child for years. The first portfolio features 1,335 products for children from infancy through the pre-teen years. Parents will be able to choose from STEM and educational toys, construction and building sets, robotics and science kits, sensory-development toys, puzzles and board games, arts and crafts, pretend-play products, dolls and action figures, remote-control vehicles, ride-ons and tricycles, plush toys, outdoor play products, electronics and collectibles.”
The launch comes as India's toy manufacturing sector continues to gain momentum under the Government of India's Vocal for Local and Made in India initiatives. Adhira and Appa Toys said it is working with domestic manufacturing partners to develop products for Indian consumers while supporting local production capabilities.
According to government data, India became a net exporter of toys in FY 2025-26, with toy imports declining by 37.5 percent and toy exports increasing by 89.1 percent. Indian-made toys are being exported to markets including the United States, the United Kingdom, Germany, and the Netherlands, reflecting growing international demand for products manufactured in India.
The company's strategy aligns with the broader growth outlook for the toy industry. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman has previously encouraged Indian toy manufacturers to target opportunities beyond the projected $5 billion Indian toy market by 2034 and capture a larger share of the projected $179 billion global toy market by 2032.
Beyond retail expansion, Adhira and Appa Toys plans to integrate sustainability measures into its operations. The company will focus on domestic and regional sourcing, explore recyclable and reusable packaging solutions, reduce inventory-related wastage, and adopt energy-efficient practices where feasible.
Hari Haran Chandrasekharan, who leads the Adhira and Appa Toys vertical within EBG Group, highlighted sustainability and local sourcing as key focus areas supporting both operational efficiency and Indian manufacturing. The company also plans to expand beyond traditional toy retailing through Adhira and Appa Game Zones, experiential play areas, creative workshops, children's merchandise, gifting solutions, and parent-child engagement formats. An omnichannel platform is also under development to connect online and offline customer experiences.
EBG Group said its first Hyderabad store will serve as a pilot location to understand customer preferences and refine operational processes before scaling across major metropolitan markets and high-growth Tier I and Tier II cities. Future expansion will include flagship stores, mall-based formats, compact stores, and shop-in-shop models. As part of its domestic manufacturing strategy, Adhira and Appa Toys is collaborating with Aditi Toys, a Rajkot-based toy manufacturer, to strengthen local production capabilities and support India's growing toy ecosystem.
The initial public offering (IPO) of SS Retail Ltd, a multi-brand consumer electronics and mobile retail chain, opened for subscription on September 16 and will remain available for bidding until September 18. The public issue has attracted attention in the primary market, with the grey market premium (GMP) indicating potential listing gains of around 31 percent, reflecting strong investor interest ahead of the listing.
The company aims to raise Rs 500 crore through the IPO, comprising a fresh issue of Rs 360 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of Rs 140 crore. The IPO is priced in the range of Rs 403 to Rs 424 per share. Ahead of the public issue, SS Retail raised Rs 146 crore from anchor investors, with participation from institutional investors including ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund and Kotak Mutual Fund. The company allotted 34.52 lakh shares at Rs 424 apiece during the anchor round.
SS Retail operates a network of more than 500 stores across over 200 cities, primarily catering to consumers in Tier II and Tier III markets. The retailer focuses on the sale of mobile phones, accessories, and consumer electronics products.
According to market data, the grey market premium stood at around Rs 128 per share, indicating an estimated listing gain of nearly 30 percent over the upper price band. Market experts note that GMP is an unofficial indicator of investor sentiment and should not be considered a guarantee of listing performance. The company plans to utilize proceeds from the fresh issue for capital expenditure requirements and working capital needs as it continues to expand its retail presence.
SS Retail derives a significant portion of its business from Maharashtra and remains focused on the consumer electronics retail segment, a category witnessing growing demand across India's non-metro markets. Industry observers will be closely tracking subscription trends from retail, institutional, and high-net-worth investors over the three-day bidding period.
Amazon India has announced that its quick commerce service, Amazon Now, has crossed $1 billion in annualized gross sales in India during the past three-month period. The company said Amazon Now orders have doubled every quarter since launch, making it the fastest-growing e-commerce business unit in Amazon India's history.
Ahead of the festive season, Amazon has expanded Amazon Now to more than 60 cities and towns across India, increasing its footprint fourfold in less than 10 weeks. In addition to major metropolitan markets, the service is now available in locations including Padubidri, Tirupati, Guntur, Gurdaspur, Jalandhar, Vellore, Dharwad, Warangal, and Berhampur. The quick delivery service operates through a network of over 750 micro-fulfilment and urban fulfilment centers, enabling delivery of products within minutes.
Samir Kumar, Country Manager, Amazon India said, “In a short period of time, Amazon Now has crossed $1 billion in annualized gross sales in India, making it the fastest-growing e-commerce business unit in Amazon India’s history. We are humbled by the customer response, with orders doubling every quarter. We are on track to expand to 100 cities by Diwali, taking delivery-in-minutes from Gurdaspur and Hoshiarpur in the north to Vembayam and Alamcode in the south. Customers across the country can look forward to the widest selection delivered at the fastest speeds this festive season.”
The development follows Amazon's June 2026 announcement to build what it described as India's largest delivery-in-minutes network by expanding Amazon Now to more than 300 cities nationwide. The company continues to invest in its quick commerce and fulfilment infrastructure to support faster deliveries across categories. Amazon said the network enables sellers to offer tens of thousands of products for delivery within minutes or a few hours, more than one million products for same-day delivery, over four million products for next-day delivery, and millions more through Prime delivery services.
Amazon currently offers a broad range of products, including groceries, fresh fruits and vegetables, frozen food, personal care items, fashion and beauty products, small appliances, and home and kitchen essentials. The service is part of the growing quick commerce segment in India, where retailers and e-commerce platforms are expanding rapid delivery capabilities to meet rising consumer demand.
Fresh commerce platform Handpickd has expanded its product portfolio beyond fresh fruits and vegetables, entering the daily kitchen staples category with freshly prepared and additive-free food products. The company said it is strengthening its supply chain to offer consumers a wider range of fresh essentials, including made-to-order atta (flour), freshly pounded spices, cold-pressed oils, farm dairy products, small-batch spreads, fresh flowers, and ready-to-cook items.
Handpickd expects categories such as freshly milled flour and hand-pounded spices to play a significant role in its growth strategy over the coming year as demand for fresh, minimally processed food products continues to increase. The company operates on a zero-inventory model, designed to reduce storage time and connect consumers directly with sourcing and preparation processes. According to Handpickd, the approach focuses on local sourcing and faster delivery to maintain freshness and product quality.
Anant Goel, Founder and CEO, Handpickd said, “There are two sides to food being modified to last long. Something bad added to it. Or something good taken out. Product companies around the globe have been over investing in it for decades so they can make it centrally and distribute globally. Your local 'halwai' doesn't know that science. Neither does your local 'atta chakki'. The problem there is adulteration of raw material. Handpickd is tackling both in one go - Pure raw material, prepared clean and delivered fresh. Fresh food items that will go bad when they are supposed to because fresh is science-less.”
The company stated that every batch in its staples portfolio is sourced from selected farms and mills and prepared closer to the point of delivery. The model is intended to extend the same level of sourcing visibility and transparency that the platform currently offers in the fresh produce category.
The move comes as India's fresh food retail, grocery delivery, quick commerce, food technology, clean-label food, organic food, and direct-to-consumer grocery segments continue to witness rising consumer demand for transparency, quality, and minimally processed products.
