Handpickd said the expansion forms part of its broader strategy to build a full-stack fresh commerce ecosystem covering a wider range of everyday household essentials. With the addition of staples, the company aims to strengthen its position in the growing fresh food delivery market while expanding beyond produce into high-frequency consumption categories.
Premium dairy brand Epigamia has announced key leadership appointments as it prepares for its next phase of growth, with plans to achieve an annualised revenue run rate of over Rs 1,000 crore in the next financial year and double its business over the next 24-30 months. The company has appointed Mansi Modi to lead its marketing function from the end of September, while Rahul Bhagat will take charge of manufacturing operations. The appointments come at a time when the company is expanding its footprint in India's dairy products, yogurt, healthy snacking, packaged food, quick commerce, and FMCG sectors.
Ritesh Gauba, CEO, Epigamia, said, “We are confident that with Mansi and Rahul joining in, their leadership will help us solidify our growth momentum and strengthen our market leadership. Our strong growth, and fundamentals is a testament to our focus on our core innovative products and brand strength. With Mansi and Rahul joining our leadership team, we want to expand into newer formats and keep focusing on our DNA of innovation.”
Rahul Bhagat brings experience in manufacturing and operations, having worked with companies including Danone, Britannia, ITC Foods, and Tata Consumer. At Epigamia, he will focus on strengthening manufacturing capabilities as the company scales its operations across India. Mansi Modi joins the company with more than 14 years of experience in marketing and brand leadership. Her previous roles include positions at Hindustan Unilever, Oziva, Airtel, and Britannia. She will work with the leadership team to support brand development and business growth initiatives.
Alongside the new appointments, Epigamia announced that Ankur Goel, Chief Operating Officer, will be stepping down from the company. According to the company, he is leaving after a decade in the startup ecosystem to focus on personal health and family commitments. Backed by the Mirchandani family, founder Rohan Mirchandani, and investors including Verlinvest, Sauce, and DSG Consumer Partners, Epigamia has built a presence in India's premium dairy market.
The company said it has expanded distribution to more than 150 cities and continues to strengthen its reach through modern trade, general trade, e-commerce, and quick commerce platforms, including Blinkit, Instamart, Amazon, and Zepto. The latest leadership changes come as the company looks to accelerate growth, expand product formats, and deepen its presence across India's organised dairy and packaged food market.
Horlicks has expanded its nutrition portfolio with the launch of Horlicks Protein Powder, targeting growing consumer demand for convenient, everyday protein intake beyond fitness-focused use cases. As awareness of protein consumption grows across India, consumers are increasingly seeking nutrition products they can easily incorporate into their daily routines.
Responding to this trend, Horlicks has introduced a new protein powder designed for on-the-go consumption, work schedules, travel, and busy lifestyles. The newly launched product delivers 24 g of protein and 4 g of prebiotic fibre per serving and is available in single-serve sachets aimed at improving convenience and portability.
Rajneet Kohli, Executive Director, Foods, Hindustan Unilever Limited said, “Horlicks has a legacy of over 100 years, built on strong science and nutrition credentials. As we continue to evolve with the changing needs of consumers, protein is a natural extension for the brand. We see an opportunity to make it more relevant and accessible for everyday lifestyles. When we spoke to consumers, one insight that really stood out was that ‘life is a gym’, whether it is rushing through a busy workday, navigating a long commute, carrying groceries or simply keeping up with everything the day demands. This insight led to our larger thought, ‘Your Day Is the Real Workout.’ With Horlicks Protein Powder, our ambition is to make quality protein easier to incorporate into the everyday lifestyles of millions of Indians.”
According to the company, the formulation is based on fermented yeast protein, a complete protein source that contains all nine essential amino acids required by the body. The product also has a PDCAAS (Protein Digestibility-Corrected Amino Acid Score) of 1.0, a globally recognised benchmark used to assess protein quality and digestibility.
The formulation includes inulin, a prebiotic fibre, and papain, a plant-derived digestive enzyme. Fermented yeast protein is also naturally lactose-free, catering to consumers looking for alternative protein sources.
Sujatha Jayaraman, Vice President and Head, Foods R&D and Regulatory Affairs, Hindustan Unilever Limited said, “As consumers become more aware of protein, the conversation also needs to move from simply how much protein a product contains to the quality and completeness of that protein. That thinking shaped the science behind Horlicks Protein Powder. Fermented yeast protein provides all nine essential amino acids, while the finished product has a PDCAAS score of 1.0, a recognised measure of protein quality and digestibility. We have complemented this with inulin, a prebiotic fibre, and papain, a plant-derived proteolytic enzyme that aids protein digestion. The result is a science-led formulation that brings together high-quality complete protein with ingredients selected to support protein digestion and gut-friendly nutrition in one product.”
The launch reflects a broader shift in the health and wellness, functional nutrition, protein supplements, and packaged nutrition segments, where brands are increasingly positioning protein as part of everyday nutrition rather than only sports and fitness-focused consumption.
Horlicks Protein Powder is available in Chocolate, Coffee, and Unflavored variants. Each 1 kg pack contains 28 single-serve sachets, eliminating the need for measuring scoops and making consumption more convenient throughout the day. The product is now available across retail stores and select e-commerce platforms in India.
India's retail fashion market is set to see a fresh festive offering as Max Fashion launches its Festive 2026 collection under Max Project New, bringing together traditional Indian craftsmanship, contemporary design, and inclusive fashion collaborations. The new festive collection features actor and brand ambassador Kalki Koechlin as the face and creative collaborator. Developed around themes of individuality, fusion fashion, and modern occasionwear, the collection combines heritage-inspired design with contemporary silhouettes aimed at today's festive fashion consumers.
Kalki Koechlin, Brand Ambassador, Max Fashion said, "Fashion has always been my way of saying something without saying it outright, and this collection let me do that on a much bigger scale. Both the drops in this collection, in their own way, are about looking at festive dressing differently. That felt worth being part of."
One of the key highlights of the collection is the fusion of Rajasthan's traditional Sanganeri hand block printing with Japanese-inspired floral motifs. The designs feature elements such as cherry blossoms, lotus medallions, Jaipuri block-print borders, geometric textures, and subtle gold detailing.
The collection traces its origins to Sanganer, Rajasthan, a hub known for hand block printing. Max Fashion said the first design was created entirely by artisans using traditional carving, colouring, and printing techniques. While the collection was later scaled for wider retail distribution, the craftsmanship remained central to its development. The colour palette includes powder pink, blush sakura, ivory, off-white, sage green, pista green, lavender, and coral shades, designed to suit both daytime and evening festive occasions.
The range includes fluid dresses, kurta sets, and kalidar silhouettes made from fabrics such as viscose blends, Chanderi blends, cotton dobby, and cotton flex. Design details include contrast piping, fabric buttons, potli accents, coordinated dupattas, zari work, mirror embellishments, beadwork, and tassel finishes. Alongside this craft-led collection, Max Fashion has introduced another line developed in partnership with the Kairassi Foundation, a Chennai-based organisation that supports artists with disabilities.
The collaboration showcases artworks created by Simron Raj, Pavithra, and Manas, whose original paintings have been adapted into wearable fashion pieces, including dresses, shirts, skirts, scarves, tote bags, and other apparel. According to the company, the garments were designed around the artwork, allowing the artists' visual identities to remain central to the collection.
Sumit Chandna, CEO, Max Fashion said, "Every festive season, we ask ourselves how to make the collection feel new, not just in design but in what it stands for. This year, that answer came from craft and creativity working together, from Sanganer's artisans to the artists we found through Kairassi. Max Project New is our way of building festive fashion that people actually connect with."
The retailer said the Festive 2026 collection reflects evolving consumer preferences for occasionwear that combines cultural influences, artistic expression, and contemporary styling. The collection will be available across Max Fashion stores, the brand's website, and mobile app across India from September, with a second launch scheduled for October.
Pricing starts at Rs 599 for menswear shirts and T-shirts, Rs 899 for womenswear dresses, skirts, and shirts, and Rs 999 for Indian wear categories including fusion dresses, fusion blazers, culottes, and kurta sets. Prices across the collection go up to Rs 1,999.
Da Milano Group has appointed Piyush Singh as its Group CEO as the company looks to accelerate growth and strengthen its presence across markets. Singh brings more than 18 years of experience across consumer businesses, retail, business strategy, transformation and leadership. Over the course of his career, he has worked on business growth initiatives, consumer-focused strategies and operational transformation across competitive markets.
The appointment comes as Da Milano Group continues to focus on expanding its business, strengthening its brand portfolio and enhancing customer engagement across channels. The company said Singh will play a key role in shaping and executing its growth strategy during the next phase of development.
Piyush Singh, Group CEO, Da Milano Group said, “I am delighted to join Da Milano Group at an exciting stage in its journey. The Group has built a strong presence in the luxury lifestyle space, and I look forward to working closely with the team to build on this foundation and unlock the next phase of growth. Our focus will be on strengthening our brands, deepening our customer connect, building operational excellence and creating sustainable value as we scale the business across markets and channels.”
In his new role, Singh will oversee initiatives focused on strengthening the company’s brand portfolio, improving operational efficiency across the value chain and driving business performance across retail and emerging channels. He will also be responsible for supporting the company’s long-term growth objectives and expanding its presence across multiple consumer touchpoints.
The leadership appointment reflects Da Milano Group’s ongoing efforts to build a stronger management structure as it expands its operations. The company is also exploring opportunities across retail, direct-to-consumer (D2C) platforms and emerging distribution channels as part of its broader business strategy. With Singh taking over as Group CEO, Da Milano Group aims to build on its existing market presence while pursuing new growth opportunities across the luxury accessories, lifestyle and fashion retail sectors.
India is assured to emerge as a global hub for gems and jewellery in the coming years, Union Home Minister Amit Shah said on Sunday, urging the industry to take the lead in building a complete, India-owned value chain for the emerging lab-grown diamond market.
India’s rich jewellery heritage
The Home Minister highlighted the contribution of Indian artisans and craftsmen to the development of the country's jewellery traditions over centuries.
He noted that royal patronage during the medieval period helped jewellery craftsmanship reach new heights, while regions such as Rajasthan and Kolkata developed distinctive traditions, including Kundan and Meenakari.
Jaipur, Shah said, continues to be renowned globally for its coloured gemstones.
Lab-Grown diamonds present new opportunity
According to Shah, changing consumer preferences and the emergence of lab-grown diamonds present a significant opportunity for India's gems and jewellery sector.
He said the era of lab-grown diamonds is set to emerge, with the market expected to grow to nearly 50 times the size of the current diamond market.
Shah stressed that the entire ecosystem and manufacturing value chain should be under Indian ownership, spanning the manufacture of machinery, production of lab-grown diamonds, jewellery manufacturing, branding and global retail.
“From manufacturing the machines to the showroom where the jewellery ultimately reaches a woman’s hand, India must have ownership of the entire ecosystem,” Shah said.
India Jewellery Park to drive investment
Shah said the India Jewellery Park is a landmark project expected to attract investments of around INR 50,000 crore and generate direct and indirect employment for one lakh people.
The project is expected to strengthen India's jewellery manufacturing ecosystem while creating opportunities across manufacturing, processing, design, branding and retail.
India’s growing global jewellery footprint
In his speech, the Union Home Minister also highlighted India's growing position in the global jewellery trade. He said India has emerged as a major source of jewellery imports for markets including the United States, the Middle East, Hong Kong and Europe.
Conclusion
India's gems and jewellery industry is at an important inflection point, with its traditional craftsmanship now intersecting with new-age opportunities such as lab-grown diamonds. Building an India-owned value chain could help the country move beyond its established strengths in manufacturing and craftsmanship towards greater control over technology, branding and global retail. With large-scale investments such as the India Jewellery Park, the sector could further strengthen India's position as a global jewellery hub while creating significant employment and business opportunities.
Reliance Consumer Products Limited (RCPL), the FMCG arm of Reliance Industries Limited, has launched its beverage brand Campa in Australia, marking the brand’s entry into a new international market. New Sunrise has become the first petrol and convenience retail network in Australia to introduce Campa across its stores.
The launch brings the beverage brand, which has a legacy spanning nearly five decades, to Australian consumers through the New Sunrise national retail network. The move is part of RCPL’s broader international expansion strategy as it continues to strengthen its presence in global consumer goods markets.
Since acquiring Campa in 2022 and reintroducing the brand in India in 2023, RCPL has expanded the portfolio beyond carbonated soft drinks to include juices and packaged drinking water. The company has been growing Campa’s presence across multiple beverage categories within the Indian FMCG and beverage sectors. Australia becomes the latest market in RCPL’s international expansion journey, following the company’s growing footprint across GCC countries, Nepal and Sri Lanka.
The initial Campa product range is now available nationwide through approximately 1,200 New Sunrise petrol and convenience stores. The partnership provides the brand with immediate access to a large retail distribution network and strengthens its reach within Australia’s convenience retail and on-the-go beverage segments.
The company believes the Australian market presents opportunities for value-focused beverage brands as consumers increasingly seek affordability, convenience and product variety. Through its partnership with New Sunrise, Campa will be positioned within a retail channel that serves a significant share of impulse and convenience purchases.
The rollout also highlights the growing international ambitions of Indian FMCG companies and beverage brands seeking expansion opportunities beyond domestic markets. With Australia now added to its international portfolio, RCPL continues to build Campa’s presence across key global markets. The launch is expected to support wider brand visibility and distribution while strengthening RCPL’s position in the global non-alcoholic beverages industry.
Amazon India has announced a major expansion of its logistics and supply chain network ahead of the festive shopping season, with plans to add 20 fulfilment centres, six sort centres and 150 delivery stations across the country. The expansion is aimed at strengthening the company's e-commerce infrastructure and enhancing its ability to manage higher order volumes during one of the busiest shopping periods of the year. The additional facilities are expected to improve inventory storage, order processing, and last-mile delivery capabilities across multiple regions.
With the planned additions, Amazon is increasing capacity across key stages of its operations network. Fulfilment centres will support inventory storage for sellers, while sort centres will help streamline package movement between facilities. The new delivery stations are expected to strengthen last-mile logistics and improve delivery efficiency in both metropolitan and emerging markets.
The announcement comes as online retailers prepare for increased consumer spending during festive sales events. E-commerce platforms typically experience a sharp rise in demand across categories such as electronics, smartphones, fashion, beauty, home appliances and consumer goods during this period.
Amazon has continued to invest in its logistics network in India, including fulfilment infrastructure, delivery operations and quick commerce capabilities. The company recently expanded its operations network, created more than 160,000 seasonal work opportunities and increased investments in fulfilment and delivery infrastructure to support growing customer demand.
The expanded network is also expected to support Amazon's seller ecosystem by enabling faster order fulfilment and wider reach across serviceable pin codes. The company currently serves millions of customers and works with a large base of sellers across India through its fulfilment, sorting and delivery infrastructure.
As competition intensifies in India's e-commerce and quick commerce sectors, logistics capacity has become a key area of investment for online retailers. Amazon's latest expansion highlights the industry's focus on warehousing, supply chain optimisation and last-mile delivery ahead of the festive shopping season.
Adie Broswon Group has expanded its flavoured vodka portfolio by launching MOOOZ Cranberry Vodka in Uttar Pradesh. The introduction of the new variant strengthens the company’s presence in North India and adds to its growing range of vodka offerings in the Indian alcohol beverage market.
Uttar Pradesh continues to be a key market for alcohol beverage companies due to its scale, evolving retail ecosystem, and increasing demand for premium and flavoured spirits. The launch of MOOOZ Cranberry Vodka aligns with the company’s efforts to expand distribution and reach consumers seeking new flavour profiles within the vodka category.
MOOOZ is produced in Punjab using rice grains and undergoes a triple distillation process along with a multi-stage filtration system. The brand has already established a presence in markets including Delhi, Punjab and Chandigarh and has been expanding across North India through new product launches and market entries.
The launch comes at a time when flavoured vodka is gaining traction in India, particularly among younger adult consumers and cocktail-focused occasions. Industry trends indicate increasing demand for innovative spirit categories, with flavoured variants emerging as an important growth segment within the vodka market.
The addition of Cranberry Vodka further broadens the MOOOZ portfolio, which has recently seen the introduction of new flavour-led variants as the company continues to diversify its offerings in the Indian spirits industry. With the Uttar Pradesh launch, Adie Broswon continues to strengthen its footprint across key markets in North India, focusing on portfolio expansion and wider availability in the country's evolving alcobev sector.
Parag Milk Foods is expanding its nutrition portfolio beyond conventional protein products, entering the snacking segment with Avvatar Popped Protein Chips as consumers increasingly look for convenient ways to include protein in everyday eating.
The launch marks the latest move under the company’s New Age Business, extending Avvatar from its existing range of protein powders, ready-to-drink beverages and bars into a familiar snacking format.
Akshali Shah, Executive Director, Parag Milk Foods Ltd., said, “This launch marks an important step in Parag Milk Foods’ evolution from a dairy-led company to a broader nutrition-led food business.”
The company said the expansion is aimed at creating more consumption occasions for protein, including those beyond traditional sports and active nutrition.
Avvatar Popped Chips are available in Magic Masala and Pudina flavours. The non-fried chips provide 10 g of protein in a 30 g pack and are priced at INR 60.
The product contains no added sugar, palm oil, or preservatives, positioning it within the growing better-for-you snacking space while retaining the convenience of a packaged snack.
The chips are being distributed through Avvatar’s website, quick-commerce platforms, vending machines, general trade and modern trade outlets.
For Parag Milk Foods, the launch forms part of a broader effort to use its experience in dairy and protein to enter adjacent food categories. Avvatar is expected to play a role in this expansion as the company looks to build its presence across different nutrition formats and consumption occasions.
“We see a significant opportunity to take our expertise in dairy and protein and build it into categories that are increasingly relevant to the way consumers eat today,” Shah said.
She added, “With Avvatar, we are extending protein beyond traditional nutrition formats and into everyday consumption occasions, including snacking.”
The company’s approach reflects the wider shift in the packaged food market, where protein is increasingly being incorporated into convenient, ready-to-consume products rather than remaining limited to specialised nutrition products.
Established in 1992, Parag Milk Foods has built its business around dairy products and operates manufacturing facilities at Manchar and Thorandale in Maharashtra and Palamner in Andhra Pradesh.
Its portfolio includes milk, ghee, dahi and paneer under Gowardhan, while Go offers products such as cheese, UHT milk, buttermilk, lassi and flavoured milkshakes. The company also operates Pride of Cows, a premium farm-to-home dairy brand.
Avvatar represents its sports nutrition business and focuses on whey protein products. With the addition of popped chips, the company is now extending the brand into everyday snacking.
The move signals Parag Milk Foods’ attempt to build a broader nutrition portfolio where protein can be consumed across different parts of the day, from specialised sports nutrition to convenient snacks.
“Our ambition is to build a holistic protein ecosystem that brings together nutrition, convenience and accessibility across formats and lifestyles,” Shah said.
She added that entering snacking is “a strategic step towards creating a larger, more contemporary food and nutrition business with protein at its core.”
The House of Rare, the company behind fashion brands Rare Rabbit, Rareism, Rare’Z and Rare Ones, is ramping up its growth plans through an aggressive retail expansion strategy, new category launches and a stronger omnichannel presence across India.
The fashion retailer is aiming to achieve revenue of nearly Rs 1,600 crore in the current fiscal year, marking a significant increase from Rs 1,100 crore recorded in the previous year. The growth target comes as the company continues to expand its physical footprint and diversify its product portfolio across multiple fashion segments.
Launched over a decade ago with the introduction of Rare Rabbit, The House of Rare has evolved into a multi-brand fashion platform covering menswear, womenswear, kidswear and sneakers. The company currently operates 210 stores across its portfolio and plans to increase the count to at least 285 stores by the end of this fiscal year. An additional 50 outlets are expected to be added in the following year.
Rare Rabbit continues to be the company’s largest business segment, contributing around 70-72 percent of overall revenue. Womenswear brand Rareism accounts for nearly 20 percent, while Rare’Z and Rare Ones together contribute approximately 8-9 percent.
As part of its diversification efforts, The House of Rare is entering several new product categories, including fragrances, women’s handbags, open footwear, ballerinas, heels, belts and jewellery. The fragrance range is scheduled to launch next month. Meanwhile, its men’s innerwear label, Innerv, already contributes about 3 percent of Rare Rabbit’s menswear business and is being scaled further.
Currently, The House of Rare has a presence across more than 1,100 points of sale. Around 97 percent of its outlets are company-owned and company-operated. Its stores typically span between 1,100 and 1,200 square feet, with capital expenditure averaging Rs 3,400-3,500 per square foot. Metro cities and Tier I markets contribute roughly 60-65 percent of total revenue, though the company sees substantial growth opportunities emerging from Tier II and Tier III cities.
Offline channels remain the primary revenue source, accounting for around 60 percent of total sales, while online channels contribute the remaining 40 percent. The average selling price online ranges between Rs 1,600 and Rs 1,800, whereas the average order value in physical stores stands at approximately Rs 4,500-5,000.
The company has also reported strong customer growth, with its customer base expanding by nearly 50 percent this year. Repeat customers currently account for around 40 percent of total shoppers.
Allied Blenders and Distillers Ltd (ABDL) is planning to enter the single malt whisky segment with an investment of up to Rs 115 crore. The company’s Management Committee has approved the additional capital infusion into its subsidiary, Minakshi Agro Industries LLP (MAILLP).
The investment will be used to set up a malt distillery-cum-maturation warehouse in Aurangabad, Maharashtra. The proposed facility is expected to have an annual production capacity of around 3 million bulk litres and is targeted to be commissioned by the third quarter of FY28.
The proposed facility will support ABDL’s planned entry into the provenance-led single malt whisky category. The company said the investment forms part of its broader strategy to expand its presence in premium spirits.
“The proposed investment is aligned with the Company's long-term strategic vision of expanding and strengthening its premium spirits portfolio through entry into the provenance-led Single Malt Whisky segment,” the company said.
The move comes as Indian consumers have shown growing interest in premium and luxury spirits, with domestic single malt brands gaining greater visibility in recent years. ABDL currently has a portfolio spanning whisky and other spirits and is seeking to add a new category to its business.
Alongside the Rs 115 crore investment, the company has approved an additional capital contribution of up to Rs 10 crore for previously approved projects under MAILLP.
The additional funding will address cost overruns linked to a bottling unit and a distillery. According to the company, the increase in project costs is partly due to higher prices of key metals. A marginal expansion of the bottling hall and mezzanine area is also planned to accommodate longer automated bottling lines.
ABDL is the company behind brands including Officer’s Choice and has operations across the Indian spirits market. The company is also present in international markets and exports to 39 countries, according to the company filing.
The Aurangabad facility is expected to add manufacturing capacity for single malt whisky once commissioned. The investment will also mark ABDL’s entry into a segment that requires longer maturation periods and dedicated production infrastructure.
With the proposed investment and ongoing capacity projects, the company is expanding its manufacturing base while adding premium categories to its spirits portfolio.
Milky Mist Dairy Food Limited has commissioned a new Skyr and Greek Yogurt manufacturing facility at its integrated plant in Perundurai, Tamil Nadu, strengthening its presence in India's growing high-protein dairy and packaged food market. Built with an investment of approximately Rs 40 crore, the new facility uses Ultrafiltration Technology and has a processing capacity of up to 150 tonnes per day. The expansion is aimed at increasing production of high-protein dairy products and meeting rising consumer demand for protein-rich nutrition.
Milky Mist was among the first companies in India to introduce Ultrafiltration Technology for the production of Skyr and Greek Yogurt in 2022, targeting a category that has seen increasing consumer adoption over the last few years. The company's initial customised multi-product yogurt facility, established in 2022, had a production capacity of around 20 tonnes per day. Since then, annual demand for the category has grown by more than 50 percent, while demand for high-protein yogurts has more than doubled in recent months, according to the company.
The newly commissioned plant has been developed following an evaluation of international manufacturing technologies. Milky Mist said the facility will help improve production scale, maintain product consistency, and support the development of new high-protein dairy products for a broader consumer base. The project is part of the company's wider expansion and modernisation programme at its Perundurai facility and aligns with the objectives outlined during its initial public offering (IPO). The investment is expected to strengthen operational capacity in the value-added dairy segment, which continues to be one of the fastest-growing categories within India's food and beverage industry.
Dr. K Rathnam, Whole-time Director and Chief Executive Officer, Milky Mist Dairy Food Limited said, “High-protein nutrition is moving from a niche preference to an increasingly mainstream consumption trend. The strong growth in demand for Skyr and Greek Yogurt validates our early investment in this category and reinforces its long-term potential within India’s value-added FMCG market. The commissioning of our advanced manufacturing facility represents a strategic expansion of our technological capabilities. With processing capacity of up to 150 tonnes per day, it provides us with the scale to serve rising demand, accelerate innovation and expand the category. This investment strengthens Milky Mist’s position in the high-protein segment and creates a robust platform for sustained profitable growth.”
The expansion comes at a time when consumer interest in protein-rich foods, functional nutrition, and value-added dairy products is rising across urban and semi-urban markets. Industry demand for products such as Greek Yogurt, Skyr, high-protein snacks, and nutritional dairy products continues to grow as health-conscious consumption gains momentum.

input.title: Cyient DLM (NSE:CYIENTDLM): Why Did Its US Subsidiary Get a New Name?
input.content:
Cyient DLM Limited (NSE:CYIENTDLM) filed an intimation on 23 September 2026 under Regulation 30 of SEBI LODR, disclosing that its US-based step-down subsidiary has been renamed from "Altek Electronics, Inc." to "Cyient DLM Electronics Inc," effective from the same date.
Key Highlights
- The US step-down subsidiary formerly known as Altek Electronics, Inc. has been officially renamed Cyient DLM Electronics Inc, as disclosed on 23 September 2026.
- The name change is intended to align the US entity with the global Cyient DLM brand identity, according to the exchange filing.
- The company confirmed that ownership, business operations, assets, liabilities, contractual arrangements, and legal status of the entity remain entirely unchanged.
- The disclosure was made to both BSE and NSE pursuant to Regulation 30 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015.
About the Company
Cyient DLM Limited (NSE:CYIENTDLM) is an electronics manufacturing services company headquartered in Mysore, Karnataka, with a registered office in Hyderabad, Telangana. The company specialises in design-led manufacturing, offering printed circuit board assemblies, box-build products, and integrated solutions primarily for aerospace, defence, medical, and industrial sectors across domestic and international markets.
Announcement in Detail
In its Regulation 30 filing dated 23 September 2026, Cyient DLM Limited informed stock exchanges that the name of its step-down subsidiary incorporated in the United States has been changed from "Altek Electronics, Inc." to "Cyient DLM Electronics Inc." The company stated that this change is driven by the intent to bring the US entity in line with the broader Cyient DLM global brand, ensuring consistent brand representation across all international operations.
Critically, the filing confirmed that the renaming does not affect the subsidiary's ownership structure, day-to-day business operations, asset or liability positions, existing contractual arrangements, or legal standing under applicable US law. The step-down nature of the entity means it sits below a direct subsidiary in the corporate structure, and no shareholding change at any level has been disclosed in connection with this update.
Impact on Investors
Investors will note that the disclosed name change is administrative in nature. The filing explicitly states that there is no alteration to ownership, liabilities, or contractual terms, meaning that the financial exposure of Cyient DLM Limited to this subsidiary remains structurally unchanged. Shareholders will observe that no fresh equity issuance, dilution, or asset transfer has been associated with this action.
The filing shows that the company's US operations continue under the same legal entity, now carrying a name that reflects its parent brand. This reduces the risk of brand fragmentation across geographies, though the disclosed terms indicate no immediate financial impact to the consolidated entity arising from this change alone.
Sector / Market Context
India's electronics manufacturing services sector has seen expanding global footprints among domestic players, supported by the government's Production Linked Incentive scheme for electronics. Brand consolidation across international subsidiaries is a recognised practice among Indian manufacturers scaling operations in North America, as it supports uniform compliance, procurement, and client recognition across markets. Cyient DLM operates in the aerospace and defence electronics sub-segment, which has recorded increased order activity from both domestic and export customers in recent years according to industry body data.

Platinum Jasmine sells 2.01% stake in Lenskart Solutions
- Platinum Jasmine A 2018 Trust sold 3.5 crore Lenskart shares on September 21, 2026
- The sale represented 2.01% of total paid-up equity capital valued at ₹2,426.31 crore
- Post-sale holding reduced from 9.77% to 7.75% of total voting capital
- Transaction executed via on-market mode at ₹687.95 per share

The company’s operational performance remained robust, with EBITDA rising 16% YoY to ₹17,731 crore. Gross margins also saw a steady upward trajectory, reaching 80.2% in FY26.
Segment-wise Revenue Performance
The revenue mix highlights the company's diversified global footprint, with international markets contributing significantly to the top line. India formulations remain the largest segment by contribution, followed closely by US formulations.
Emerging Markets demonstrated strong momentum with sales growing 19% YoY to ₹11,187 crore. The Rest of World segment also posted healthy growth, with revenues expanding 19% YoY to ₹8,568 crore. In contrast, US Formulations grew at a moderate pace of 3.6% YoY, reaching ₹16,824 crore.
What the Numbers Show
A divergence is visible between the robust double-digit revenue growth and the single-digit net profit expansion. While top-line figures expanded 12%, net profit grew only 5%. This gap is largely attributable to exceptional items disclosed in the financial notes. The adjusted net profit, which excludes these non-recurring provisions, stood at ₹12,402 crore, showing a more modest 3% increase. The reported profit includes adjustments for items such as GxMDL provisions and wage code impacts, which weighed on the bottom line despite strong operational cash flows.

input.title: Lenskart Solutions (NSE:LENSKART) Sees Major Block Deal as Shareholding Changes Draw Attention
input.content:
Highlights
- Lenskart Solutions witnessed a sizeable block transaction involving a meaningful portion of its outstanding equity.
- The transaction appears to involve an existing institutional shareholder reducing part of its holding.
- The company’s underlying eyewear operations are not directly altered by the secondary-market transaction.
- Large block deals can temporarily influence market activity because substantial quantities of shares change hands at once.
- Investors may focus on subsequent shareholding disclosures for confirmation of ownership changes.
Lenskart Solutions Limited (NSE:LENSKART) came into focus after a large block transaction involving around 3.53 crore shares, representing approximately 2% of the company’s equity, was reported in the market. The transaction appears to involve a partial exit by an existing institutional shareholder, although the final identities of all buyers and sellers would need to be established through relevant disclosures. The development primarily represents a change in ownership between shareholders rather than a change in Lenskart’s day-to-day business operations.
Block Deal Brings Ownership Structure Into Focus
A block deal is a large transaction in which a substantial number of shares change hands between market participants through a dedicated trading mechanism. Such transactions are generally used by institutional or large shareholders because executing the same quantity through ordinary market trades could create greater disruption.
In Lenskart’s case, approximately 3.53 crore shares were reported to have changed hands through the transaction. Reports ahead of the deal had indicated that an existing institutional shareholder could sell up to around 3 crore shares, equivalent to approximately 1.7% of Lenskart’s equity.
The company’s earlier ownership disclosures show that the shareholder associated with the proposed transaction was among Lenskart’s larger non-promoter investors. The latest transaction could therefore reduce that investor’s ownership while introducing or increasing the holdings of other investors.
However, a secondary share sale does not provide new capital to the company. The shares simply move from one investor to another, meaning the transaction should be distinguished from a fresh issue of shares in which the company itself raises funds.
Why Large Block Transactions Attract Attention
Large shareholder transactions often attract market attention because they can alter the ownership structure of a recently listed company. When a substantial investor reduces its stake, market participants may assess whether the transaction reflects portfolio rebalancing, partial monetisation or another shareholder-specific decision.
It is important, however, not to automatically interpret such a transaction as a judgment on the underlying business. Institutional investors may sell shares for several reasons unrelated to a company’s operating performance, including fund maturity, liquidity requirements, asset allocation or portfolio concentration.
A block transaction can also temporarily increase the supply of shares available in the market. Because a large quantity is being placed at one time, transaction pricing may differ from prevailing market levels to facilitate execution.
Once the transaction is completed, attention generally shifts toward the identity of the buyers and the revised ownership structure. Future shareholding disclosures can provide more clarity on how the company’s investor base has changed.
Core Eyewear Business Remains Separate From the Deal
The block transaction does not directly change Lenskart’s operating business. The company continues to operate in the eyewear market through its integrated retail, digital and supply-chain model.
For readers assessing the development, separating ownership changes from business fundamentals is useful. The sale of shares by an existing investor does not change customer demand, store operations, manufacturing capabilities or the company’s ability to execute its commercial strategy.
Lenskart has also continued to make corporate and strategic disclosures during 2026, including activity related to acquisitions and business restructuring. Its investor-relations records show ongoing corporate developments beyond the shareholding transaction, indicating that the company continues to pursue its wider operating strategy.
The significance of the block deal therefore lies mainly in shareholder composition and market liquidity rather than in any immediate operational change.
What Could Change After the Transaction
The most visible impact of a large secondary transaction is likely to be reflected in future ownership disclosures. If the reported seller reduced its stake materially, its percentage holding would decline while buyers participating in the transaction may emerge as larger shareholders.
A broader institutional investor base can also change the distribution of ownership in a listed company. Depending on who acquired the shares, the transaction could increase holdings among domestic or international institutions, funds or other eligible investors.
Official disclosures following settlement will provide the clearest confirmation of these changes. Until then, reported seller identities should be treated as provisional where they have not been formally confirmed.
For Lenskart, the transaction comes after its transition into a publicly listed company, making changes in institutional ownership a more visible part of its market profile.
Key Insights
Lenskart Solutions’ large block deal represents a meaningful secondary-market ownership transaction rather than a change in the company’s operating business. Approximately 3.53 crore shares were reported to have changed hands, while an existing institutional shareholder had earlier been expected to reduce part of its holding. The main issues to monitor are confirmation of the final buyers and sellers and the resulting shareholding pattern. The company’s underlying retail operations, customer strategy and business execution remain separate from the ownership transfer.
FAQs
Q: What happened in the Lenskart block deal?
A: A large quantity of Lenskart Solutions shares changed hands through a block transaction involving approximately 3.53 crore shares.
Q: What is a block deal?
A: A block deal is a large share transaction executed through a dedicated trading mechanism, generally involving institutional or large investors.
Q: Does the transaction provide funds to Lenskart?
A: No. It is a secondary-market transaction between shareholders rather than a fresh issue of shares by the company.
Q: Does the deal change Lenskart’s business operations?
A: No. The transaction primarily changes share ownership and does not directly alter the company’s eyewear operations.
Q: What should be monitored next?
A: Subsequent ownership disclosures may provide confirmation of the buyers, sellers and the revised shareholding structure.

input.title: Lenskart Vs Eternal: Which High-PE New-Age Stock Has The Stronger Investment Case?
input.content:
Fast-growing consumer companies often trade at expensive valuations when investors expect them to become much bigger over time. Lenskart and Eternal are both in that category, but their businesses are very different. Lenskart is expanding its eyewear business in India and overseas, while Eternal already has a profitable food-delivery business and is now betting heavily on Blinkit for its next phase of growth.
But there is one thing both stocks have in common: they are extremely expensive. Lenskart currently trades at a PE ratio of around 181 times, while Eternal trades at nearly 737 times earnings. At valuations like these, investors are not paying for what the companies earn today.
They are paying for what they could earn several years from now. That makes the real question simple: which company has the stronger business to support such a high valuation?
Two Premium Valuations With Different Growth Engines
Lenskart’s growth story is relatively easy to understand. It sells eyewear, adds stores, gets more people tested, sells more pairs and gradually moves customers towards higher-value products. In Q1FY27, revenue grew 33.6 percent year-on-year, pre-Ind AS EBITDA grew 95 percent and PAT rose 2.8 times to Rs. 228 crore. Volumes grew 25.7 percent, while India same-store sales growth remained strong at 18.3 percent.
That growth is also broad-based. India revenue grew 30.7 percent to Rs. 1,531 crore, while international revenue grew 38 percent to Rs. 1,203 crore. Lenskart added 132 net stores during the quarter, taking the network to 3,459 stores. More importantly, consolidated product margin crossed 70 percent for the first time.
Eternal is growing faster, largely because Blinkit is scaling at a much quicker pace. In Q1FY27, Blinkit’s NOV jumped 86 percent YoY to Rs. 17,132 crore, helped by more stores, a wider product range and customers ordering more frequently in existing markets. Food delivery also grew more than 20 percent, while District grew 60 percent. This pushed Eternal’s overall B2C NOV up 54 percent.
However, Eternal’s headline adjusted revenue growth of 173 percent needs some context. Blinkit has shifted towards owning inventory, which means Eternal now records the full value of goods sold as revenue. On a like-for-like basis, adjusted revenue still grew a strong 66 percent.
Lenskart Is Turning Growth Into Better Economics
The biggest point in Lenskart’s favour is that the operating model is already showing leverage. Its gross margin moved from 69.2 percent in Q2FY26 to 68.9 percent in Q3, 69.6 percent in Q4 and 70.3 percent in Q1FY27. At the same time, EBITDA margin moved from around 19.9 percent in Q2FY26 to 21.7 percent in Q1FY27.
This is happening even while the rupee has weakened against the RMB (Chinese Yuan), which matters because frames and components have China linked costs. Management’s answer has been to manufacture more in-house, increase backward integration and use scale to negotiate better costs.
The Hyderabad facility, which is being built for around 50 million pairs annually, is an important part of this strategy. Management had already highlighted in Q3FY26 that higher in-house manufacturing could allow future margin gains that were then being absorbed by rupee-RMB depreciation.
There is also growth at both ends of the customer base. Lenskart says its Rs. 500 offering can now be sold sustainably, while premiumisation is moving faster than expected. Owndays premium lenses are generating more than Rs. 1,500 crore of annual prescription eyewear sales, while Rodenstock and Tokai together contribute around Rs. 250 crore.
Most importantly, accounting profit is turning into cash. Q1FY27 operating cash flow was Rs. 297 crore against roughly Rs. 207 crore of store and plant capex. ROCE improved to 23.2 percent from 14.6 percent in FY26. That gives Lenskart room to keep opening stores and investing in manufacturing without the growth story depending entirely on fresh capital.
Eternal Is Increasingly A Blinkit Story
Eternal’s food-delivery business is now the stabilising engine. Zomato’s food-delivery NOV grew more than 20 percent in Q1FY27 to Rs. 10,769 crore, while adjusted EBITDA margin reached 5.6 percent of NOV. That produced Rs. 606 crore of adjusted EBITDA, up 34 percent year-on-year.
The bigger excitement, however, is Blinkit. Its NOV grew 86 percent to Rs. 17,132 crore, 200 net stores were added and the network reached 2,443 stores. Blinkit also moved from an adjusted EBITDA loss of Rs. 162 crore in Q1FY26 to a profit of Rs. 102 crore in Q1FY27.
The journey across the last year matters. In Q2FY26, management was still saying that overall Blinkit profitability was a moving average between mature profitable markets and the cost of new stores, cities and customers. It was willing to keep spending while customer acquisition costs and lifetime value remained healthy. By Q3FY26, the business had reached adjusted EBITDA break-even, although management continued to caution that competitive intensity could make the margin journey uneven.
By Q1FY27, management had enough visibility to point towards the upper end of its long-term 5-6 percent adjusted EBITDA margin range. Older Blinkit customers are also spending around three times more than they did three years ago. Management says this is mainly because they are ordering more often, not because each order has become much bigger. Growth continues to come mainly from existing cities.
The Capital Intensity Gap Matters
This is where the two investment cases separate sharply. Blinkit is not an asset-light marketplace anymore. Eternal says quick commerce operates around 19 million square feet of store and warehousing space across more than 300 cities and has absorbed around Rs. 3,000 crore of capex over the past four years. Inventory ownership also pushed net working capital to Rs. 2,545 crore at the end of Q1FY27.
In Q1FY27 alone, Blinkit capex reached roughly Rs. 711 crore, materially above previous quarters, largely because of warehousing capacity additions. Quick-commerce free cash burn was around Rs. 778 crore. Eternal can afford the investment, with its quarter-end cash balance at Rs. 18,288 crore, but investors still need that capital to eventually generate attractive returns.
Lenskart’s capital intensity is different, but it is not disappearing. The company is making a large manufacturing bet through its Hyderabad facility, which is being built for around 50 million pairs annually. That means capex will remain important as Lenskart tries to bring more production in-house.
There is also a currency angle. Lenskart still has exposure to the rupee-RMB movement, particularly in frame manufacturing, and management has said some of the margin benefit from greater in-house production was being absorbed by currency depreciation. The Hyderabad investment could therefore do two things over time: support capacity growth and reduce some of that dependence on imported inputs.
That makes the comparison more balanced. Lenskart is already generating cash from its existing business, but it is still committing capital today to manufacturing expansion and lowering currency dependence. Blinkit is committing even larger amounts to stores, warehouses and inventory as it builds scale. In both cases, the investment case depends on whether today’s spending leads to stronger margins and returns later.
Valuation Leaves Very Little Room For Execution Mistakes
Both stocks are expensive, so the key question is whether earnings can grow fast enough to bring those valuations down. For Lenskart, Motilal Oswal estimates adjusted PAT rising from around Rs. 534 crore in FY26 to Rs. 899 crore in FY27 and Rs. 1,283 crore in FY28. That implies profit growth of around 69 percent in FY27 and another 43 percent in FY28. As earnings grow, its PE falls from 181 times currently to 113.1 times in FY27 and 79.3 times in FY28.
Eternal has a much sharper expected earnings jump. Motilal Oswal estimates adjusted PAT rising from around Rs. 366 crore in FY26 to Rs. 2,072 crore in FY27 and Rs. 4,143 crore in FY28. That means profit is expected to grow more than five times in FY27 and then roughly double again in FY28. As earnings scale, its PE is expected to fall sharply from 737 times currently to 125.2 times in FY27 and 62.6 times in FY28.
That creates a clearer trade-off. Eternal has the faster expected earnings growth and therefore sees its valuation multiple fall much faster. But achieving that depends heavily on Blinkit continuing to scale, margins improving and the large amount of capital being invested earning good returns. Lenskart’s earnings growth is slower, but its current profit is already more established.
The risk profiles are also different. Eternal still has to manage competition, dark-store economics, warehouse capex, working capital and continued spending on newer businesses. Lenskart faces execution risks around new stores, the Hyderabad manufacturing expansion, international growth and currency exposure, especially to the rupee-RMB movement.
The Choice Is Between Visibility And Optionality
So which has the stronger investment case? Based on the numbers today, Lenskart looks easier to understand. Revenue is growing above 30 percent, margins are improving, cash flow is supporting its expansion, and both India and international businesses are getting stronger. The valuation is still expensive, but the earnings growth needed to justify it is already starting to show.
Eternal offers more upside if Blinkit delivers. Food delivery is profitable, Blinkit is growing much faster, District is expanding and the company is building more businesses around the same customer base. If Blinkit keeps growing quickly and margins improve, Eternal’s profits could rise very fast.
That does not make Lenskart cheap or Eternal unattractive. Both stocks are priced for strong growth, but the path to justify those valuations is different. Lenskart needs to keep growing while steadily improving margins and returns. Eternal needs Blinkit’s massive scale to eventually turn into equally massive profits. At these valuations, the winner may not be the company that grows the fastest, but the one that delivers closest to what investors are already paying for.

input.title: Lenskart shares fall 2% after Rs 2,468-crore block deal; 2.07% equity stake sold
input.content:
Shares of Lenskart Solutions fell more than 2 percent in early trade on September 21 after a large block deal worth Rs 2,468 crore took place in the eyewear retailer, marking another sizeable secondary-market transaction in the stock in recent weeks. Around 3.6 crore Lenskart shares, equivalent to 2.07 percent of the company's equity, changed hands through block deals at Rs 688 apiece.
Lenskart shares were trading at Rs 692 in early trade, down 2.2 percent for the day. Despite Monday's decline, the stock has gained 57.5 percent so far in 2026, compared with a 10.7 percent decline in the Nifty 50. The company's market capitalisation stood at around Rs 1.2 lakh crore.
The transaction came after reports that Platinum Jasmine A 2018 Trust was looking to sell shares in Lenskart. The proposed transaction had initially been pegged at around Rs 2,047.4 crore, representing about 1.7 percent of the company's equity, at a floor price of Rs 682.45 per share.
The floor price represented a 3.5 percent discount to Lenskart's previous closing price. The actual block trades on Monday were larger than the size indicated earlier, with 3.6 crore shares changing hands for Rs 2,468 crore at Rs 688 apiece. According to the earlier deal terms, shares sold through the transaction would be subject to a 90-day lock-up on any further sale of shares.
Monday's transaction follows two other large block deals in Lenskart shares in August. In late August, Alpha Wave Ventures sold 2.95 crore shares, or 1.7 percent equity, for Rs 1,857 crore at an average price of Rs 630 per share. National Pension System bought 78.57 lakh shares, or 0.45 percent equity, for Rs 495 crore in that transaction, while ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund purchased 60.3 lakh shares, equivalent to 0.35 percent equity, for Rs 380 crore. WhiteOak Capital Mutual Fund acquired another 15.87 lakh shares, or 0.1 percent equity, for Rs 100 crore.
Earlier in August, SVF II Lightbulb sold 4.5 crore Lenskart shares worth Rs 2,887.9 crore on the BSE. Societe Generale ODI bought 1.07 crore shares worth Rs 688.92 crore in the transaction, which was executed at an average price of Rs 641.75 per share.
The latest block deal also comes after Lenskart reported a sharp improvement in its first-quarter earnings. Net profit rose to Rs 222 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 60 crore a year earlier, while revenue increased 43.3 percent year-on-year to Rs 2,714.2 crore. EBITDA climbed 75.1 percent to Rs 588.5 crore, with the EBITDA margin expanding to 21.7 percent from 17.7 percent a year earlier. The company's PAT margin rose 443 basis points to 8.4 percent, while consolidated product margin crossed 70 percent for the first time, reaching 70.3 percent during the quarter.

input.title: Abu Dhabi Investment Authority sells over 2% stake in Lenskart Solutions
input.content:
Platinum Jasmine A 2018 Trust, owned by the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority (ADIA), sold more than 2 percent equity stake in Gurgaon-based eyewear maker Lenskart Solutions via open market transactions on September 21.
The stake sale impact has also been seen in the stock price which fell 3.3 percent to end at Rs 683.85 after a day of hitting record high of Rs 725 on the National Stock Exchange.
As per the bulk deals data, Platinum Jasmine A 2018 Trust has offloaded 3.5 crore equity shares, representing 2.01 percent of paid-up equity, in Lenskart for Rs 2,390.57 crore. The selling price was Rs 683.02 per share.
ADIA through Platinum Jasmine A 2018 Trust held 9.77 percent equity stake in Lenskart as of June 2026.
360 ONE Pipe Fund buys Anupam Rasayan shares worth Rs 105 crore, Ashapura Commodities offloads 1.3% stake
360 ONE Asset Management's 360 ONE Pipe Fund has acquired 9 lakh shares, representing 0.79 percent of paid-up equity, in specialty chemicals maker Anupam Rasayan India for Rs 104.85 crore. The buying price was Rs 1,165 per share.
However, Ashapura Commodities sold 15.02 lakh shares or 1.3 percent stake, for Rs 175.02 crore at a price of Rs 1,165.16 per share.
Anupam Rasayan shares were under pressure, falling 3.88 percent amid big volumes to end at Rs 1,160.8, the lowest closing level since November 19, 2025.
Prudent Equity offloads 0.61% stake in CP Capital
Prudent Equity, founded by Siddharth Oberoi, has sold 1.11 lakh shares or 0.61 percent stake in CP Capital, the non-banking financial company (NBFC), for Rs 1.66 crore at a price of Rs 149.09 per share.
However, despite stake sale, the stock saw strong buying interest, soaring 8.07 percent to Rs 1565.9 amid high volumes on the NSE.
Croll Reynolds International sells 0.56% stake in Mazda
US-based Croll Reynolds International Inc, which specialises in industrial process vacuum systems, thermos-compressors, and air pollution control equipment, sold 1.12 lakh shares, representing 0.56 percent of paid-up equity, in Mazda, for Rs 2.89 crore at a price of Rs 256.58 per share.
In previous session, too, Croll Reynolds International has offloaded 0.74 percent stake in Mazda, which specialises in vacuum and heat transfer technologies.
The stake sale was out of the shareholding of 7.23 percent held by Croll Reynolds International Inc in Mazda as of June 2026.
Mazda shares plunged 4.64 percent to Rs 253.90 amid big volumes on the NSE.

input.title: Block deal alert: Lenskart Solutions slips 3% amid heavy volume on NSE
input.content:
Block deal alert: Lenskart Solutions slips 3% amid heavy volume on NSE
As of 09:27 AM on Monday, as many as 39.18 million shares representing 2.25 per cent of total equity of Lenskart changed hands on the NSE, the exchange data shows.
Listen to This Article
Lenskart Solutions share price movement
Lenskart Solutions (Lenskart) share price slipped 3 per cent to ₹683 on the National Stock Exchange (NSE) in Monday’s intra-day deals amid huge volume. 
 
Till 09:27 AM, as many as 39.18 million shares representing 2.25 per cent of Lenskart's total equity, changed hands on the NSE, the exchange data shows. The names of the buyers and sellers were not ascertained immediately.
 
Meanwhile, the stock price of one of the leading direct-to-consumer (D2C) eyewear players in India, with presence across select international markets, hit a record high of ₹725 on Friday, September 18, 2025. The stock zoomed 104 per cent from its listing day low of ₹355.70 on the BSE. The company made its stock market debut on November 10, 2025. Currently, Lenskart quotes 80 per cent higher against its issue price of ₹402 per share. 
 
Despite of today’s decline, thus far in the calendar year 2026, Lenskart outperformed the market by soaring 58 per cent, compared to a 6.3 per cent decline in the Nifty 200 index and 10.5 per cent fall in the Nifty 50. 
Also Read
Over 2% equity change hands on the NSE
According to reports, a block deal worth around ₹2,047.4 crore was expected to take place in the eyewear retailer Lenskart Solutions. Reports suggested that Platinum Jasmine A 2018 Trust would offer shares at a floor price of ₹682.45 apiece (a 3.5 per cent discount to Friday's closing of ₹707.2 per share).
 
Brokerages view on Lenskart
According to analysts at ICICI Securities, the rising prevalence of refractive errors in India, growing awareness of eyecare, and a shift to organised players will help India’s eyewear market grow at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 13 per cent to ₹1.48 trillion over FY25-30, expanding by 3x the global eyewear industry. Refractive errors amongst India’s population are expected to rise to 62 per cent by FY30 (highest amongst teenagers & children at 75 per cent) from 43 per cent in FY20.
Lenskart, with a strong business model, domestic manufacturing capacity of 25 million units (another 50 million unit facility will commence in Hyderabad), and an extended store network of 2,725 stores in India (as of Q1FY27), is well capitalised to grab a large share in the Indian eyewear market with a focus on growing the market share from the current 5 per cent in the coming years, the brokerage firm said.
 
With strong cash generation, analysts expect Lenskart to cumulatively generate free cash flow (FCF) of ₹5,300 crore over FY26-29E. The brokerage firm initiated coverage on Lenskart with a 'Buy' rating and a target price of ₹850 (valuing at 43x FY28E EV/EBIDTA).
Meanwhile, India’s optical retail infrastructure remains significantly underpenetrated, with management noting the country has materially fewer opticians relative to other consumer retail categories. This underpins confidence in opening thousands of additional stores over time.
 
Lenskart’s portfolio spans products from $5 to $500, enabling broad market coverage across price points. Separately, emerging insurance-led eye-care programmes could become an incremental demand driver over time, improving affordability and increasing adoption rates, analysts at Jefferies said. Disclaimer: Views and outlook shared on the stock belong to the respective brokerages and are not endorsed by Business Standard. input.title: Sun Pharma Launches Fashion-Inspired Alopecia Areata Awareness Campaign Featuring Designer Christian Siriano
input.content:
Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Limited has unveiled a new educational campaign called Regrowth Restyled, aimed at supporting adults living with severe alopecia areata.
The campaign launched during Alopecia Areata Awareness Month and takes an unconventional fashion-led approach to raising awareness of the autoimmune condition.
Sun Pharma partnered with renowned fashion designer Christian Siriano to create a one-of-a-kind wearable garment inspired by the hair regrowth journey experienced by patients.
The collaboration brought together Siriano and patient advocates to explore themes of confidence, identity, and self-expression through clothing and personal style.
People living with alopecia areata often say the condition affects far more than their physical appearance, touching deeply on their sense of self and emotional wellbeing.
A panel featuring Siriano and three members of the patient community formed a central part of the campaign’s public-facing activities and outreach efforts.
Sun Pharma’s head of marketing, Stephanie Loiseau, discussed the strategy behind the Siriano partnership and explained why pharma brands should look beyond the usual roster of celebrity spokespeople.
John Bujnoski, Vice President, Head of Dermatology and Immunology, U.S. Innovative Medicines at Sun Pharma, said: “Through this campaign, we hope to inspire confidence, celebrate self-expression, and encourage patients to speak with their dermatologist about treatment options, including LEQSELVI, that may help them achieve their hair regrowth goals.”
LEQSELVI, known generically as deuruxolitinib, is an FDA-approved medicine for adults with severe alopecia areata that works by blocking certain signals thought to play a role in hair loss.
Clinical trial data showed that around 3% of patients were able to regain almost all their hair in as little as eight weeks after beginning treatment with LEQSELVI.
By the 24-week mark in clinical trials, approximately one-third of patients had regained almost all of their hair, demonstrating the treatment’s potential for significant regrowth outcomes.
The Regrowth Restyled campaign reflects a broader shift in pharmaceutical marketing toward more human-centred storytelling that connects treatment to lived patient experience.

input.title: Lenskart Shares Slip 3% After ₹2,468 Cr Block Deal
input.content:
Lenskart Solutions fell sharply on Monday after a large block deal worth ₹2,468 crore hit the counter, dragging the stock to its day’s low.
A chunk of Lenskart’s equity changed hands through block deals on the exchange.
As many as 3.6 crore shares, or 2.07% of the company’s total equity, were traded for a combined value of ₹2,468 crore, at an average price of ₹688 per share.
The identity of the buyers and sellers has not been officially confirmed yet. However, market sources suggest the seller was Platinum Jasmine A 2018 Trust, an investment vehicle linked to the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority.
As per standard block deal norms, the seller will not be able to sell any further shares in the company for the next 90 days.
This is not an isolated event. It is actually the third such block deal in Lenskart over the past month.
On August 24, SoftBank’s Vision Fund sold close to 4.5 crore shares worth nearly ₹2,888 crore.
Then on August 28, Alpha Wave Ventures sold around 2.9 crore shares valued at roughly ₹1,857 crore, with buyers such as the National Pension System, ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund and WhiteOak Capital Mutual Fund picking up stakes in that deal.
Despite the string of block deals, Lenskart’s stock has held up reasonably well over a longer stretch.
As of 10:00, the stock is trading at ₹691.25 well above its IPO issue price of ₹402 and is up close to 57% since the start of the year.
It also remains sharply higher than its listing price of ₹395 from November last year, even after today’s fall.

Lenskart Solutions Share Price Target at Rs 850: ICICI Securities
ICICI Securities has initiated coverage on Lenskart Solutions with a BUY rating and a 12-month target of Rs 850, implying about 23 percent upside from the current price of Rs 693. Tagging it a Conviction Pick, the brokerage argues that India's largest direct-to-consumer eyewear player is riding a rare mix of a fast-widening market and a deep, self-built moat — vertical manufacturing that undercuts rivals, an AI-led omnichannel network of nearly 3,500 stores, and a house of brands. It expects consolidated revenue, operating profit and net profit to compound at 27, 37 and 59 percent a year through FY29, valuing the stock at 43 times FY28E operating profit.
Lenskart: a clear vision of growth, with the moat already in place
Vertical manufacturing that makes eyewear for a fraction of the industry's cost, a technology-led store network spanning India and Asia, and a market still barely a third penetrated — ICICI Securities begins coverage with conviction.
35-40%
Lower input costs vs the industry
50-70%
Cheaper retail vs local opticians
69%
Gross margin, FY26
1.6 crore
Annual transacting customers, FY26
A market only a third penetrated
The opportunity begins with how few Indians who need glasses actually own a proper pair. Eyeglass penetration sits at just 35 percent, against 69 percent in Japan and 88 percent in the United States — each square below is one percentage point of the Indian population.
India — 35% eyeglass penetration
The tailwinds are structural. Refractive errors are set to afflict 62 percent of Indians by FY30 — as high as 75 percent among teenagers and children — from 43 percent in FY20. As awareness rises and buyers shift to organised brands, whose share is seen climbing to 31 percent by FY30 from 22 percent in FY20, the domestic eyewear market is projected to grow at a 13 percent compound rate — roughly three times the pace of the global industry — from Rs 78,800 crore in FY25 to about Rs 1,48,300 crore by FY30. Lenskart holds only about 5 percent of it today.
The moat: making eyewear for less
Lenskart's edge is that it owns the entire chain. Its Bhiwadi facility — running at 75 percent automation — integrates procurement, lens coating, edging, cutting, polishing, assembly and dispatch, while AI-led design, remote eye-testing and an omnichannel platform speed innovation and cut cost. The result is a structural price advantage: frame and lens costs run 35 to 40 percent below the Indian industry average, letting Lenskart sell 50 to 70 percent cheaper than local opticians.
That integration is deepening. Prescription eyeglasses made at its centralised plants rose to 1.75 crore units in FY26 from 1.01 crore in FY24; in-house frames climbed to 78 lakh from 53 lakh and lenses to 56 lakh from 25 lakh. A new Hyderabad facility will add roughly 5 crore units of capacity on top of the current 2.5 crore, extending the cost advantage as volumes scale. Cheap, reliable supply has helped annual transacting customers roughly double to 1.6 crore in FY26 from 77 lakh in FY23.
A house of brands on an omnichannel net
Above the supply chain sits a multi-brand storefront, each label aimed at a different customer and occasion but sharing Lenskart's technology, sourcing and distribution.
John Jacobs
Owndays
Meller
Hooper
Vincent Chase
Le Petit Lunetier
India, about 60 percent of revenue, remains the core, with international markets — led by Japan and Southeast Asia — the other 40 percent. Ambition is scaling in step: management aims to run 10 crore eye tests a year, up from roughly 2 crore today.
From losses to compounding profit
The financial arc is the clincher. Revenue has compounded at 33 percent to Rs 8,814 crore over FY23-26, but the sharper move is in profitability: EBITDA margins have widened from 7 percent in FY23 to 19.9 percent in FY26, dragging the business from a small loss to real earnings.
Looking ahead, ICICI expects revenue, EBITDA and net profit to compound at 27, 37 and 59 percent respectively over FY26-29E, with margins reaching 25 percent and return on capital employed climbing to 28 percent. Net profit swings from a marginal loss in FY24 to about Rs 2,058 crore by FY29E, and the company is expected to throw off cumulative free cash flow of roughly Rs 5,300 crore across the period.
The target for investors
ICICI Securities initiates with a BUY and a target of Rs 850, an upside of roughly 23 percent, valuing Lenskart at 43 times FY28E operating profit. This is unambiguously a premium-multiple growth stock — it trades at around 234 times FY26 earnings, easing to about 58 times on FY29E estimates as profits compound — so the case rests on execution rather than cheapness. With the stock near its 52-week high of Rs 698 after a powerful run off the Rs 356 low, the measured approach is to accumulate on market-linked dips and hold for the multi-year penetration and margin story, rather than chase the price.
Key risks
What ICICI Securities flags
Medical advances denting demand. Improvements in medical infrastructure and vision-correction technology could, over time, reduce demand for corrective eyewear.
Innovation slowdown. Lenskart's growth leans on rapid product launches; a slower cadence of innovation or fewer launches could blunt the momentum.
Valuation sensitivity. At a rich multiple on early-stage profits, the shares leave little room for disappointment — any execution stumble or demand wobble would be felt sharply in the price. (Flagged by TopNews, given the valuation.)
Sources & disclosures
Based on the ICICI Securities (ICICI Direct Research) “Conviction Pick” initiating-coverage report on Lenskart Solutions Ltd (NSE: LENSKART), dated September 10, 2026. Research analysts: Kaustubh Pawaskar, Abhishek Shankar and Sonal Rajpal. The Rs 850 target values the company at 43 times FY28E EV/EBITDA.

In Q1 FY27, the company added 132 net stores, comprising 116 stores in India and 16 internationally, taking its total store count to 3,459, up around 23% YoY. Amid sustained demand for prescription eyewear, the company reported a net profit of ₹228 crore, compared with ₹61 crore in the same period last year, marking a 273% year-on-year increase.
