input.title: Sun Pharma to Zydus: Healthcare stocks outperform broader market despite price pressure; can they sustain growth?
input.content:
Market News
6 min read | Updated on September 18, 2026, 15:57 IST
SUMMARY
Healthcare stocks have consistently outperformed the broader markets over the past months as investors focus on sectors with visible earnings potential ahead amid the geopolitical crisis.
Nifty Healthcare outperformed NIFTY50 index delivering close to 15% returns to investors in the last 6 months. | Image: Shutterstock
Indian healthcare sector stocks have significantly outperformed the broader market indices over the past few months, as investors focus on the potential for further growth despite the elevated price pressure and geopolitical supply headwinds in the market.
Companies like Sun Pharmaceuticals, Zydus Lifesciences, Laurus Labs, Aurobindo Pharma, among several other defensive healthcare stocks, have added to the gains, while the broader markets suffer from the impact of the geopolitical crisis in West Asia.
Experts predict that earnings visibility, pricing power, regulatory developments, product pipelines and valuations, among other factors, should remain in focus of investors in the healthcare sector.
While the US business remains important for pharma companies, hospitals and diagnostics firms should be analysed based on their occupancy, realisations, margins and capacity addition factor.
“We believe the market is pricing in domestic market growth and price headwinds in vanilla generics in US market, but not the rainmakers and Emerging Markets growth,” said analysts from Bernstein Research.
Saikat Kumar, Board Member of Red Lions Capital, ADGM MD & CEO, DIP Market, said that with the stock market facing macro and geopolitical volatility, investors are gravitating towards sectors with relatively visible earnings like healthcare.
“Healthcare’s relative outperformance reflects a combination of defensive characteristics, resilient earnings and improving fundamentals across hospitals, diagnostics and select pharma segments,” said Saikat Kumar.
However, Kumar also highlighted that the impact of the same is increasingly becoming differentiated across companies depending on their product mix, complex generics, speciality portfolio and new launches.
NSE data showed that the sectoral benchmark Nifty Healthcare has outperformed the benchmark NIFTY50 index, delivering close to 15% returns to investors in the last six months, while the broader index lost nearly 2% of its value in the same period.
The chart attached below further showed that on a one-year basis, Nifty Healthcare has gained almost 12% while the benchmark NIFTY50 index has lost around 8%, according to the exchange data.
Market experts predict that regulatory concerns, along with pricing pressure from the US generics market, are expected to remain key challenges for Indian healthcare companies in the upcoming period.
Despite the price pressure, the US generics import market remains a key source of revenue for Indian healthcare companies, with domestic companies exporting a major chunk of general prescription drugs and healthcare equipment to America.
“Headwinds include elevated valuations in some pockets, regulatory intervention, pricing pressure in generics and higher input or compliance costs,” said Saikat Kumar.
Investors should also know that factors like increasing patient volumes, along with the premiumisation of healthcare services, capacity expansion, and rising healthcare penetration will act as key tailwinds alongside the ability to adapt with AI and automation.
On the AI use case front, analysts from Japanese investment firm Nomura said that Lupin undertaking artificial intelligence (AI) and automation in multiple use cases and across functions is expected to drive efficiency gains and cost savings that have not been quantified at this stage.
Bernstein analysts expect AI leveraging, a lifestyle shift towards image consciousness, along with a rise in disposable income, will create around $400 billion in opportunities for the sector in the next few years.
US-based investment firm Bernstein analysts said India’s Healthcare sector has a constructive outlook for the coming years, with key focus on increasing penetration of health infrastructure in emerging economies.
Six areas including – 505(B)(2) NDAs; Orphan indications; Drug-device combinations; Drug repurposing in niche therapies, metabolic peptides, and RNA; and cellular therapies like CAR-T, will produce rainmakers for Indian biopharma.
Rainmakers are emerging catalyst sectors or business streams which have the potential to bring in higher revenues, in this case, high-growth ventures in the healthcare industry.
“We expect over the next decade these rainmakers to add $70-75 billion to Industry size and total Industry to grow by 4 times to $195 billion,” said Bernstein analysts.
Companies like Zydus, Lupin, and Sun Pharma, among others are key companies which operate in the sector.
As per the latest advisory from the Union Health Ministry, the States and Union Territories’ have been directed to oversee and ensure strict compliance on government and private clinics which are involved in stem cell research, treatment, promotion or administration.
The directive also said that the authorities will ensure strict compliance with the applicable framework governing stem cell research and therapy.
This advisory was released on September 17 in response to a Supreme Court ruling in a case which highlighted facilities which failed to comply with the standards now facing consequences, including professional misconduct.
While this move serves as a caution for unproven and experimental stem cell treatments, it also provides a push towards heavily regulated and proven therapies which are offered by several companies that have succeeded in clinical trials.
Capital markets experts predict that the longer-term outlook for the Indian healthcare sector will be supported by several factors like rising demand, increased affordability, innovation opportunities in niche therapies and complex specialities, among other things.
“The long-term case remains supported by structural under-penetration of healthcare, rising affordability, formalisation and increasing demand for quality care,” said Saikat Kumar.
The analyst said that although the sector may have support from the structural tailwinds, outperformance in the stock market will ultimately depend on company-specific earnings growth relative to valuations.
In line with expectations, Bernstein analysts also said that they have a positive sector view on the Indian healthcare sector, with a key focus on niche therapies and complex specialities, which is expected to drive Indian Biopharma’s revenue acceleration and sustainable scale-up in earnings.

input.title: Lenskart Block Deal: Platinum Jasmine set to sell 1.7% stake worth Rs 2,047 crore, reports CNBC-TV18
input.content:
A block deal worth around Rs 2,047.4 crore is set to take place in eyewear retailer Lenskart Solutions Ltd, with Platinum Jasmine A 2018 Trust likely to sell a 1.7% stake at a floor price of Rs 682.45 per share, sources told CNBC-TV18.
The floor price represents a 3.5% discount to Lenskart’s last closing price, according to the deal details. The offer size is around 1.7% of Lenskart’s total equity, with the transaction valued at approximately Rs 2,047.4 crore.
Shares sold through the block deal will be subject to a 90-day lock-up on any further sale, according to the deal details.
Lenskart Q1 Results
Lenskart Solutions reported a net profit of Rs 222 crore for the first quarter of FY27, compared with Rs 60 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
Profit after tax (PAT) margin expanded 443 basis points year-on-year to 8.4%, from 4%. Revenue grew 43.3% year-on-year to Rs 2,714.2 crore, compared with Rs 1,894.5 crore a year earlier.
EBITDA rose 75.1% year-on-year to Rs 588.5 crore, from Rs 336.1 crore, while the EBITDA margin expanded to 21.7% from 17.7% in the year-ago quarter.
EBITDA before Ind AS 116 rose to a margin of 13.3% from 9.1% in Q1 FY26.
Consolidated product margin crossed 70% for the first time, rising to 70.3% in Q1 FY27 from 68.7% a year ago. This came despite the rupee depreciating against the Chinese yuan.
India product margin improved to 64.2% from 63.4%, while international product margin rose to 77.1% from 75.9%.
India revenue grew 30.7% year-on-year, while international revenue increased 38%.
Operating cash flow stood at Rs 297 crore, higher than capital expenditure of around Rs 207 crore. Capex included Rs 75 crore for stores and Rs 132 crore for the Hyderabad-led plant step-up.

input.title: Lenskart Solutions zooms 98% from November low; stock hits new high
input.content:
Lenskart Solutions zooms 98% from November low; stock hits new high
Lenskart's share price hit a new high of ₹703.85 on the BSE in Friday's trade. The stock now trades at a 75 per cent premium to its issue price of ₹402 per share.
Listen to This Article
Lenskart Solutions share price movement
Lenskart Solutions (Lenskart) share price hit a new high of ₹703.85, gaining nearly 4 per cent on the BSE in Friday’s intra-day deals in an otherwise range-bound market. The stock price of one of the leading direct-to-consumer (D2C) eyewear players in India, with presence across select international markets, surpassed its previous high of ₹703.75 touched on September 10, 2025. In comparison, the BSE Sensex was up 0.15 per cent at 74,428 at 11:40 AM.
 
In the past month, Lenskart outperformed the market by surging 12 per cent, against a 3.6 per cent decline in the BSE Sensex. The stock has nearly doubled or zoomed 98 per cent from its listing day low of ₹355.70 on the BSE. The company made its stock market debut on November 10, 2025. Currently, Lenskart quotes 75 per cent higher against its issue price of ₹402 per share.
 
Brokerages remain bullish on Lenskart
Rising prevalence of refractive errors in India, growing awareness of eyecare, and a shift to organised players will help India’s eyewear market grow at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 13 per cent to ₹1.48 trillion over FY25-30, expanding by 3x of the global eyewear industry. Refractive errors amongst India’s population are expected to go up to 62 per cent by FY30 (highest amongst teenagers & children at 75 per cent) from 43 per cent in FY20, according to analysts at ICICI Securities. 
Penetration level for eyeglasses in India is low at 35 per cent compared to the US and Japan at 88 per cent and 69 per cent respectively. Strong business models are aiding organised D2C players in gaining high demand through affordability, omni-channel presence and better services. Organised brand’s share is expected to move to 31 per cent by FY30 from 22 per cent in FY20. 
Also Read
Lenskart, with a strong business model, domestic manufacturing capacity of 25 million units (another 50 million unit facility will commence in Hyderabad), and an extended store network of 2,725 stores in India (as of Q1FY27), is well capitalised to grab a large share in the Indian eyewear market with a focus on growing the market share from the current 5 per cent in the coming years, the brokerage firm said.
With store additions across India/international markets expected to grow at 13 per cent CAGR, a better product mix through innovation and transacting customers growing at 22 per cent CAGR over FY26-29E, analysts at ICICI Securities expect consolidated revenue/ earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA)/profit after tax (PAT) to grow at 27 per cent/37 per cent/59 per cent CAGR over FY26-29E.
 
With strong cash generation, analysts expect Lenskart to cumulatively generate free cash flow (FCF) of ₹5,300 crore over FY26-29E. The brokerage firm initiated its coverage on Lenskart with a Buy rating and target price of ₹850 (valuing at 43x FY28E EV/EBIDTA).
Meanwhile, India’s optical retail infrastructure remains significantly underpenetrated, with management noting the country has materially fewer opticians relative to other consumer retail categories. This underpins confidence in opening thousands of additional stores over time. 
 
Lenskart’s portfolio spans products from $5 to $500, enabling broad market coverage across price points. Separately, emerging insurance-led eye-care programmes could become an incremental demand driver over time, improving affordability and increasing adoption rates, analysts at Jefferies said.
 
Further, Lenskart has built strong moats in a difficult-to-scale category through: i) a centralized, highly automated manufacturing facility; ii) strong backward integration; iii) large omnichannel presence; iv) leveraging technology to ease constraints in scaling up; and v) house-of-brands architecture spanning mass to premium eyewear, analysts at Motilal Oswal Financial Services (MOFSL) said.
The brokerage firm raised its FY27-28E consolidated pre-IND AS EBITDA by 4 per cent/8 per cent, driven by higher store additions in India and operating leverage across India and International.
 
Analysts at MOFSL model 27 per cent/46 per cent/59 per cent CAGR in revenue/pre-Ind-AS EBITDA/adjusted PAT over FY26-29E, driven by 29 per cent/25 per cent revenue CAGR in India/International. The brokerage firm expects pre-IND AS EBITDA margin to expand to 19.4 per cent/13.5 per cent in India/International by FY29. It reiterates a BUY rating on Lenskart with a revised target price of ₹800 (earlier ₹705), based on a 49x Sep’28 blended pre-IndAS EBITDA multiple (55x for India, 37.5x for International). Disclaimer: Views and outlook shared on the stock belong to the respective brokerages and are not endorsed by Business Standard. input.title: Cyient Schedules Analyst and Investor Meeting for September 22
input.content:
Cyient Schedules Analyst and Investor Meeting for September 22
Cyient is scheduled to engage with analysts and institutional investors on September 22, 2026, to discuss business strategies and performance. In its latest Q1 FY27 results, the company displayed strong margin resilience, with its core DET normalized EBIT margin expanding to 13.2% (up 114 basis points YoY), despite a minor revenue degrowth of 0.9% YoY in constant currency. These upcoming meetings provide a key platform for management to discuss growth scaling in its semiconductor segment and updates on capital allocation strategies.
Market snapshot: Cyient Limited has announced its participation in analyst and investor meetings scheduled for September 22, 2026. The engagement will allow the company's senior leadership, including Executive Vice Chairman Krishna Bodanapu and Chief Financial Officer Shrinivas Kulkarni, to interact with institutional investors. These interactions come on the heels of Cyient's resilient Q1 FY27 profitability performance, which was marked by notable margin expansion in its core Digital Engineering and Technology (DET) business despite soft top-line growth.
Data Snapshot
- The Digital, Engineering, and Technology (DET) segment recorded an operating revenue of ₹1,540 crore in the first quarter of the fiscal year 2027, growing 10.6% year-on-year.
- The core DET segment's normalized EBIT margin expanded to 13.2% in Q1 FY27, representing a year-on-year expansion of 114 basis points.
- The company successfully completed a fundraise for Cyient Semiconductors Private Limited with EAAA India Alternatives Limited, valuing the subsidiary at a post-money valuation of $500 million.
- The group's design-led manufacturing subsidiary, Cyient DLM, recorded its highest-ever order book of ₹2,598.9 crore in Q1 FY27.
What's Changed
- The core Digital Engineering & Technology (DET) segment's normalized EBIT margin expanded by 114 basis points year-on-year to 13.2% from 12.1% in Q1 FY26, driven by optimized cost discipline.
- Cyient DLM's order backlog reached a historic high of ₹2,598.9 crore, up sequentially from ₹2,416.6 crore in Q4 FY26, highlighting strong mid-term visibility.
- Cyient Semiconductors completed a strategic fundraise with EAAA India Alternatives, which set a post-money valuation of $500 million for the subsidiary, facilitating capital injection to scale its operations.
Key Takeaways
- Cyient's senior management will interact directly with analysts and institutional investors on September 22, 2026, offering clarity on mid-term strategies and performance.
- The company's core DET business continues to face short-term revenue growth headwinds, with constant currency revenue contracting slightly by 0.9% year-on-year.
- Operating margins have proved highly resilient, with sequential improvements of 79 basis points and year-on-year growth of 114 basis points to hit 13.2% in Q1 FY27.
- The semiconductor business and the DLM manufacturing subsidiary (order book of ₹2,598.9 crore) represent key growth engines that are expanding faster than the traditional engineering segments.
SAHI Perspective
The upcoming analyst meeting on September 22, 2026, provides Cyient's management with a critical opportunity to rebuild investor trust regarding its top-line recovery timeline. While the core DET business has shown admirable cost control and margin expansion to 13.2%, the persistent softness in traditional engineering verticals remains a concern for valuation multiples. Investors should look for updates on the integration of Kinetic Technologies and whether the deferred EBIT margin target of 15% remains on track for H1 FY28. Direct discussions on capital allocation, particularly regarding the execution of its share buyback, will also be pivotal.
Market Implications
The direct engagement with long-term institutional investors is expected to reinforce structural support for the stock, particularly as the IT-services index faces volatile global demand. While the market has responded cautiously to Cyient's deferred profitability targets, clarity on semiconductor scaling and the utilization of the $500 million valuation milestone could catalyze positive sentiment. Over the medium term, execution of the record ₹2,598.9 crore order book at Cyient DLM and stabilization of the core DET revenue growth will be the primary drivers of stock rerating.
Trading Signals
Market Bias: Neutral
Cyient's scheduled meetings at the JP Morgan Investor Meetings on September 22 and Anand Rathi G-200 Summit on September 21-22 will provide platforms to highlight its Q1 FY27 normalized EBIT margin expansion to 13.2% (up 114 bps YoY), despite a flat constant currency revenue decline of 0.9% YoY in the core DET segment.
Overweight: IT Enabled Services, Digital Engineering & Technology
Trigger Factors:
- Management commentary on the timeline for achieving the 15% EBIT margin target (currently deferred to H1 FY28).
- Growth progress in the newly acquired Kinetic Technologies and the Cyient Semiconductors segment (valued post-money at $500 million).
- Consolidated revenue recovery across key segments like energy and aerospace.
Time Horizon: Near-term (0-3 months)
Industry Context
The engineering research and development (ER&D) sector is undergoing a transition, where traditional connectivity and industrial projects are seeing localized delays due to global macroeconomic uncertainties. In this environment, Indian service providers are shifting focus toward high-margin niches. Cyient's strategic focus on semiconductors, lifecycle engineering, and artificial intelligence mirrors this industry-wide pivot. The successful fundraising at a post-money valuation of $500 million for its semiconductor arm reflects the strong appetite among institutional investors for specialized chip design and fabrication-linked services.
Key Risks to Watch
- Decision-making and project execution delays in traditional segments like energy and connectivity, which could drag down core DET revenue growth.
- Operational integration risks associated with the recent acquisition of Kinetic Technologies and the execution ramp-up of the semiconductor business.
- Execution timelines of Cyient DLM's large order book (₹2,598.9 crore) amid global supply chain and inventory bottlenecks.

input.title: Sun Pharma and Christian Siriano Launch "Regrowth Restyled" to Inspire Adults Living with Severe Alopecia Areata
input.content:
New awareness campaign celebrates confidence and self-expression through fashion while encouraging adults with severe alopecia areata to learn more about treatment options such as LEQSELVI® (deuruxolitinib)
PRINCETON, N.J., Sept. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Limited (Reuters: SUN.BO, Bloomberg: SUNP IN, NSE: SUNPHARMA, BSE: 524715, "Sun Pharma" and includes its subsidiaries and/or associate companies) announced the launch of Regrowth Restyled, an educational campaign that celebrates how beauty, confidence, and self-expression continue throughout the hair regrowth journey for adults living with severe alopecia areata.
Kicking off in Alopecia Areata Awareness Month, this fashion-inspired campaign spotlights the experience of severe alopecia areata patients. As part of this collaboration, Sun Pharma has partnered with renowned fashion designer Christian Siriano to create a one-of-a-kind wearable garment inspired by the journey of hair regrowth. The piece will debut following New York Fashion Week on September 17, 2026.
"As a designer, I've always believed style is a form of self-expression – and for adults living with severe alopecia areata, hair loss can complicate that expression in ways that go far beyond appearance," said Siriano. "I'm excited to participate in this campaign because it creates a platform to broaden the conversation around alopecia areata and reminds anyone navigating this condition that self-expression is uniquely theirs and does not have to wait."
Alopecia areata is an autoimmune disease where the body's immune system mistakenly attacks hair follicles, causing hair loss. Hair may fall out in small, round patches, or in some cases, patients can lose all of their hair on their scalp and/or body. Impacting an estimated 300,000 U.S. adults, severe alopecia areata causes more than hair loss; it also carries a significant physical and psychosocial burden for patients. Alopecia areata can negatively change how patients feel about themselves, potentially leading to increased anxiety, depression, feelings of isolation, and reduced self-esteem.
"When people think about alopecia areata, they often focus on hair loss itself," said dermatologist Dr. Meena Singh, Board Certified Dermatologist and Dermatologic Surgeon, Skin and Hair Center in Overland Park, KS. "But as dermatologists, we consider the full spectrum of each patient's journey from initial hair loss to the psychological impacts alopecia areata can bring leading to a decision to explore treatment to address rapid hair regrowth."
Treating severe alopecia areata can look different for everyone. For people interested in regrowing their hair, fast results matter. Seeing bald patches shrink or new hair growth appear may help patients feel more comfortable in their journey and inspire them to take steps toward reclaiming their identity.
"Regrowth Restyled reflects our commitment to supporting people living with severe alopecia areata at every stage of their journey," said John Bujnoski, Vice President, Head of Dermatology & Immunology, U.S. Innovative Medicines, Sun Pharma. "Through this campaign, we hope to inspire confidence, celebrate self-expression, and encourage patients to speak with their dermatologist about treatment options, including LEQSELVI, that may help them achieve their hair regrowth goals."
LEQSELVI® (deuruxolitinib) is an FDA-approved medicine for adults with severe alopecia areata. It works by blocking certain signals in the body that are thought to play a role in hair loss. In clinical trials, LEQSELVI demonstrated rapid results. Some patients (3%) were able to get almost all their hair back as fast as 8 weeks. By 24 weeks, about one-third of patients regained almost all their hair. Even if some patients didn't regrow most of their hair, many still experienced visible regrowth.
LEQSELVI may cause serious side effects including infections, cancer, immune system problems, blood clots, and stomach tears. Do not take LEQSELVI if you are a poor metabolizer of CYP2C9 medicines or if you take moderate or strong CYP2C9 inhibitor medicines. The most common adverse events were headache, acne, nasopharyngitis, blood creatine phosphokinase increased, and hyperlipidemia. Please full Prescribing Information, including Boxed Warning and Medication Guide, and see below for Important Safety Information.
Visit RegrowthRestyled.com to learn more about the campaign and LEQSELVI as a treatment option.
About LEQSELVI®
LEQSELVI (deuruxolitinib) 8 mg tablets is an oral selective inhibitor of Janus kinases JAK1 and JAK2 FDA-approved for the treatment of adults with severe alopecia areata. Alopecia areata is an autoimmune disease in which the immune system attacks hair follicles, resulting in partial or complete loss of hair on the scalp and body. Alopecia areata may affect up to 2.5% of the United States and global population during their lifetime. The scalp is the most commonly affected area, but any hair-bearing site can be affected alone or together with the scalp. Onset of the disease can occur throughout life and affects both women and men. Alopecia areata can be associated with serious psychological consequences, including anxiety and depression. There are currently limited approved treatment options available for severe alopecia areata.
Please click here for full Prescribing Information Including BOXED WARNING and Medication Guide.
LEQSELVI Important Safety Information & Use
What is LEQSELVI (deuruxolitinib)?
LEQSELVI is used to treat adults with severe hair loss (alopecia areata).
It is not known if LEQSELVI is safe and effective in children.
Who should not take LEQSELVI?
Do not take LEQSELVI if you are a poor metabolizer of CYP2C9 medicines or are taking moderate or strong CYP2C9 inhibitors. Before starting treatment, your healthcare provider should test you for CYP2C9 variants.  Tell your healthcare provider if you take moderate or strong CYP2C9 inhibitor medicines. Ask your healthcare provider or pharmacist if you are not sure. 
What is the most important safety information I should know about LEQSELVI?
LEQSELVI is a medicine that affects your immune system and can lower the ability of your immune system to fight infections. Some people have had serious infections during treatment with LEQSELVI. Some people may die from these infections... Your healthcare provider should test you for TB before starting treatment with LEQSELVI and should watch you closely for signs and symptoms of TB during treatment. You should not start taking LEQSELVI if you have any kind of infection unless your healthcare provider tells you it is okay
There may be an increased risk of major cardiovascular events in people 50 years of age and older who have at least one heart disease risk factor and are taking a medicine in the class of medicines called JAK inhibitors, especially if they are a current or past smoker.
LEQSELVI may increase your risk of certain cancers by changing the way your immune system works.
Blood clots in the veins of your legs, lungs or brain (cerebral venous sinus thrombosis, CVT) can happen in some people during treatment with LEQSELVI. These may be life-threatening.
Some people taking LEQSELVI can get tears in their stomach or intestines.
If you have diabetes, your healthcare provider may instruct you to check your blook sugar levels more often during treatment with LEQSELVI. Call your healthcare provider if you have any problems with low blood sugar (hypoglycemia).
Before you start and taking LEQSELVI and during treatment, your healthcare provider should do blood tests to check for increased fat levels in your blood, Low white and/or red blood cell counts. You should not take LEQSELVI if your white blood cell or red blood cell counts are too low.
What should I tell my healthcare provider before starting LEQSELVI?
Tell your healthcare provider if you have an infection; are a current or past smoker; have had a heart attack, or other heart problems or stroke; have had blood clots in your legs, lungs or brain; have kidney problems; have liver problems; have any stomach area (abdominal) pain or been diagnosed with diverticulitis or ulcers in your stomach or intestine; have low red or white blood cell counts; or have recently received or are scheduled to receive a vaccine. 
Females who are able to become pregnant should use effective birth control (contraception) during treatment with LEQSELVI. Talk to your healthcare provider if you are planning to become pregnant. You should not breastfeed during treatment with LEQSELVI and for one day after the last dose.
What else should I be aware of when taking LEQSELVI?
Your healthcare provider should do blood tests before you start taking LEQSELVI and during treatment to check for increased fat (lipid) levels in your blood (triglycerides and cholesterol), low red blood cell counts, or low white blood cells.
How should I take LEQSELVI?
Take LEQSELVI 2 times a day with or without food.
What are the possible side effects of LEQSELVI?

Novartis India Limited (NSE: NOVARTIND) is laying out a comprehensive strategy aimed at revitalizing its presence in the pharmaceutical market. Company and Market Overview
With a legacy spanning over 79 years, Novartis India has become an established name in the pharmaceutical industry, having been publicly listed for 27 years. The company has strategically positioned itself within the Indian pharmaceutical market, leveraging a deep-rooted brand portfolio that includes six flagship products generating revenues exceeding ₹30 crore. Amidst these dynamics, Novartis India reports a revenue decline of 2% for FY23, with a projected compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of -2% through FY26.

The company outlined a clear strategic playbook focused on compounding equity and expansion across key therapeutic areas, including cardiology and neurology. This includes an enhanced specialist engagement approach, where Novartis plans to deploy over 900 field representatives to interact with around 150,000 healthcare professionals nationwide. The intent is to capture greater market share and improve brand recall among prescribers, a segment significantly affected by historical outsourcing and marketing strategies.
Recent M&A Developments
Novartis India's acquisition of the rights to the 'Minipress' brand represents a pivotal move aimed at augmenting its portfolio in the cardiac treatment domain. This deal, valued at ₹1,250 crore, is anticipated to impact the company's growth trajectory positively as Minipress has historically been a market leader, showcasing a consistent revenue growth rate. Such investments are a part of Novartis' strategy to fill in gaps and expand presence in high-value therapeutic segments.
Flagship Brands and Market Leadership
Novartis India boasts an impressive roster of top-selling products, including Voveran® and Calcium-Sandoz®, contributing significantly to an RPM exceeding ₹2,010 crore. Notably, products like Methergin® and Myfortic® continue to lead their categories, reflecting the company's enduring prescriber loyalty and brand equity. However, the lack of an in-house sales force has been identified as a challenge, with plans to rectify this by re-establishing direct field promotion to revitalize brand engagement.
Strong Governance and Future Outlook
With an experienced board and a governance framework emphasizing compliance and strategic oversight, Novartis India aims to navigate regulatory demands effectively. The company remains focused on disciplined capital allocation, ensuring investments are targeted towards high-return growth opportunities. As operational efficiencies improve through an asset-light model and robust supply chain management, Novartis India is well-poised to capitalize on emerging market opportunities.
Conclusion on Future Growth
Overall, Novartis India presented a multidimensional approach to future growth, with strategies rooted in strong product positioning and enhanced market engagement. While facing financial headwinds illustrated by past revenue declines, the commitment to revamp its operating strategies and expand through M&A indicates a positive outlook for stakeholders and investors alike.

Sun Pharma share price was largely unchanged, up 0.18 percent to Rs 1,845.30, after the company's subsidiaries, Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Inc, Taro Pharmaceutical Industries and Taro Pharmaceuticals USA Inc, signed a settlement agreement with a plaintiff in the In re Generic Pharmaceuticals Pricing Antitrust Litigation in Pennsylvania, US, for a confidential amount. The settlement was entered into without any admission of wrongdoing, and the subsidiaries will make the settlement payment in exchange for a full release of all claims asserted against them in this action.
Sun Pharma share price traded largely flat after the company disclosed that its US subsidiaries have settled a long-running generic drug pricing antitrust litigation in Pennsylvania, resolving one thread of a broader industry-wide legal matter that has involved numerous generic pharmaceutical manufacturers.

Under the terms of the settlement, the subsidiaries will make a payment in exchange for a full release of all claims asserted against them in this specific action, with other terms of the settlement remaining confidential.
Importantly, the company clarified that the settlement agreement was entered into without any admission of wrongdoing in the action, a standard and common feature of settlements in complex, multi-defendant litigation of this kind, where companies often choose to resolve claims to avoid the cost, uncertainty and management distraction of prolonged litigation, rather than because they concede the underlying allegations.

Given the scale and duration of this litigation, which has spanned multiple years and involved numerous separate claims and defendants, individual settlements of this nature by specific companies, resolving discrete portions of the broader case, are a fairly routine occurrence as the litigation gradually works its way toward resolution across the industry.

Stocks to watch today: HDFC Bank, Sun Pharma, Tata group shares and more in focus
The stock market appears to be under continuous pressure. Rising crude oil prices and an increase in US bond yields have intensified this pressure. There is also the rate hike expectation from the US Fed. In this climate there are several stocks which will be on the radar of investors due to a variety of developments.
Kolkata: Several shares will be on the radar of investors today (September 15, 2026) in the Indian stock market. The movement in these shares will be triggered by corporate announcements and business updates. These include HDFC Bank, Coforge, HFCL, Sun Pharma, Varun Beverages, and Tata Group companies. The stock market remains under pressure due to rising crude oil prices and increasing US bond yields. Let’s have a look at some of these stocks.
Stocks in focus
HDFC Bank: Reports indicate that two candidates have been shortlisted for the position of HDFC Bank’s next MD and CEO. These include the bank’s current deputy managing director, Kaizad M Bharucha. The second candidate is reportedly a senior executive from a private bank. Additionally, HDFC Bank’s ADR rose by approximately 6.5% in the US market on Friday.
HDFC Life: A major GST-related issue concerning HDFC Life Insurance, covering the period from July 2017 to March 2022, has surfaced. The Commissioner (Appeals-III) of CGST and Central Excise, Mumbai, has upheld a tax demand of ₹942.18 crore against the company. Additionally, a penalty of ₹2,422.97 crore and applicable interest are included.
HFCL: HFCL’s board has approved an expansion of production capacity for optical fiber, optical fiber cables, and preforms. The company will increase its optical fiber capacity by 46 lakh fiber kilometers per annum, optical fiber cable capacity by 56.4 lakh fiber kilometers, and preform capacity by 300 metric tonnes per annum. An additional capital expenditure (capex) of approximately ₹820 crore will be incurred for this expansion.
Sun Pharma: Sun Pharma’s US subsidiaries have reached a settlement with one of the parties in an antitrust lawsuit concerning generic drug prices. The case was pending in the Eastern District of Pennsylvania, USA. The settlement amount has not been disclosed.
Coforge: A significant board-level change has taken place at the IT company Coforge. D K Singh, an independent director and chairperson of the Nomination and Remuneration Committee (NRC), has resigned with immediate effect. Beth Boucher has been appointed as the new Chairperson of the NRC in his place.
Varun Beverages: Varun Beverages’ Kenya-based subsidiary, VBL Industries (Kenya), has launched two new brands—BOLT UP and XTREME FIZZ—in the region. The company aims to strengthen its presence and product portfolio in the Kenyan beverage market.
Tata Group shares: The RBI has rejected Tata Sons’ application to voluntarily surrender its registration certificate. This means Tata Sons must proceed towards listing in accordance with existing RBI regulations. This development could have an impact in the prices of major Tata group company shares.
Granules India: Dr Krishna Prasad Chigurupati, a promoter of Granules India, sold approximately 1.72 crore shares on September 11 through block and open market transactions. According to the company, the proceeds from this transaction will be utilized for the second tranche of the preferential issue and for the company’s growth plans.
UNO Minda: The board of UNO Minda has approved the setting up of a new plant for two-wheeler alloy wheels in Kharkhoda, Haryana. It will have an annual capacity of 3.3 million (33 lakh) units. Additionally, the existing capacity of 2 million (20 lakh) units from the Supa plant in Maharashtra will be shifted to the Kharkhoda plant. The company will also establish a new greenfield facility in Hosur, Tamil Nadu.
Aurobindo Pharma: The US FDA inspection of Aurobindo Pharma’s API manufacturing unit in Andhra Pradesh has concluded. The FDA did not record any observations during the inspection, which took place from September 7 to September 11, 2026.
Raymond: Raymond’s aerospace subsidiary has secured new business from a major Indian aerospace and defense company. This order is expected to generate annual revenue of approximately ₹33 crore. The order encompasses over 300 part numbers and more than 37,000 components annually.
Jubilant Pharmova: The US FDA has classified Jubilant Pharmova’s US-based Spokane CMO facility as ‘Voluntary Action Indicated’ (VAI). This classification follows an FDA inspection conducted between June 8 and June 17, 2026.
Lemon Tree Hotels: Carnation Hotels, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Lemon Tree Hotels, has entered into a joint venture agreement with RJ Corp regarding Arum Hotels. Arum Hotels is a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) formed for the development and operation of the Aurika project in Shillong.
Waaree Renewable Technologies: Waaree Green Data Centers has incorporated a new wholly-owned subsidiary named Aurovolt Data Centers. The new company was formed on September 14, 2026.

input.title: Sun Pharma Subsidiaries Settle US Generic Drug Pricing Antitrust Litigation For Confidential Amount
input.content:
Sun Pharma Subsidiaries Settle US Generic Drug Pricing Antitrust Litigation For Confidential Amount
Sun Pharma's U.S. arms (SPII, Taro Ltd., and Taro USA) have settled the multi-year 'In re Generic Pharmaceuticals Pricing Antitrust Litigation' in Pennsylvania. The settlement amount is confidential, and the deal involves no admission of wrongdoing. This move, along with a recent favorable appellate ruling on Lipitor, significantly reduces the company's outstanding U.S. legal overhangs.
Market snapshot: Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Limited's key U.S. subsidiaries have executed a confidential settlement agreement in the long-running generic drug pricing antitrust litigation in Pennsylvania. This agreement guarantees a complete release of all asserted claims without any admission of wrongdoing by the company's arms. The resolution closes a major chapter of legal uncertainty for the drugmaker as it consolidates its global specialty business.
Data Snapshot
- Sun Pharma's key U.S. subsidiaries signed a settlement in the Eastern District of Pennsylvania generic drug pricing antitrust litigation.
- The company reported consolidated revenue of ₹15,183 crore for Q1 FY27, representing a 10% year-on-year growth.
- India formulation sales recorded a strong growth of 16% year-on-year, reaching ₹5,475 crore during Q1 FY27.
What's Changed
- Outstanding US generic antitrust litigation claims have been fully released for SPII, Taro Ltd., and Taro USA.
- Sun Pharma's market share in India rose to 8.5% (MAT June 2026) from 8.2% in the previous period.
- US litigation overhangs are substantially reduced following both this confidential settlement and the favorable Lipitor appellate court ruling.
Key Takeaways
- Subsidiaries SPII, Taro Ltd., and Taro USA secured a full release of all claims in exchange for a confidential payment.
- The agreement contains an explicit clause of no admission of wrongdoing or liability in the pricing litigation.
- Strong Q1 FY27 operational results (₹15,183 crore revenue, up 10% YoY) provide a robust financial cushion for any settlement costs.
- Resolution of long-standing litigation allows Sun Pharma to sharpen focus on innovative medicines and the Organon integration.
SAHI Perspective
The settlement represents a calculated, risk-mitigating decision by Sun Pharma. Historically, antitrust litigation in the US has severely impacted profitability—for instance, previous US settlements in FY26 led to significant exceptional hits. By settling this generic pricing litigation for a confidential sum without admitting liability, Sun Pharma puts an end to indefinite litigation costs. Supported by robust cash flows and high-margin domestic business (up 16% to ₹5,475 crore in Q1 FY27), the financial impact is expected to be well-contained.
Market Implications
The removal of regulatory and legal headwinds in the US is a positive signal for investors. While US generic sales dropped 9.7% to $427 million in Q1 FY27, the overall consolidated performance remains steady due to premium products. Settling this litigation protects the company from large jury-dictated damages and allows management to focus on closing the $11.75 billion Organon acquisition by early 2027.
Trading Signals
Market Bias: Bullish
The resolution of major U.S. antitrust litigation reduces cash outflow uncertainty. Strong fundamental momentum, highlighted by 10% YoY growth in Q1 FY27 revenue to ₹15,183 crore, supports a constructive outlook.
Overweight: Pharmaceuticals, Healthcare
Trigger Factors:
- Any future details or impact of the confidential settlement payment in upcoming quarterly disclosures.
- Regulatory and operational progress of the Organon acquisition expected to close by early 2027.
- Sustained expansion of premium domestic formulation revenues.
Time Horizon: Medium-term (3-12 months)
Industry Context
The Indian pharmaceutical sector has frequently faced pricing scrutiny and antitrust challenges in the U.S. generic market. Over the years, major players have transitioned from pure generics to innovative and complex specialty products to escape severe price erosion. Sun Pharma's shift towards innovative medicines, which continue to offset generics pain, reflects a broader industry transition toward higher-value IP.
Key Risks to Watch
- Potential one-time exceptional charge in the upcoming financial statements depending on the quantum of the confidential settlement.
- Price erosion pressure in the core US generic formulations business.
- Integration risks associated with the massive proposed $11.75 billion Organon acquisition.
Recent Developments
In August 2026, the US Court of Appeals ruled in favor of Sun Pharma, bringing the Lipitor antitrust dispute to a close. Additionally, in September 2026, Moody's and S&P assigned investment-grade credit ratings (Baa1 and BBB+ respectively) with a Stable outlook, reflecting Sun's strong global franchise and disciplined financial profile ahead of the Organon deal.
Closing Insight
Resolving legal liabilities while maintaining a dominant domestic market share of 8.5% highlights Sun Pharma's resilience. With credit ratings higher than India's sovereign rating, the company is well-prepared to transition into a global specialty powerhouse.

input.title: Lenskart raises AjnaLens stake to 9% as it doubles down on AI-powered smart glasses
input.content:
Peyush Bansal-led Lenskart has acquired an additional 1.80% of Dimension NXG Private Limited, the parent of extended reality startup AjnaLens, for Rs 7.99 crore, taking its holding to 9.01% on a fully diluted basis.
The transaction was completed on 13 September and disclosed in a regulatory filing.
It is the third time Lenskart has increased its stake in the company this year. The company said the investment strengthens its association with the extended reality, AI and smart wearable technology ecosystem, and supports technology-led opportunities in smart eyewear.
Lenskart made its first investment in AjnaLens in July 2025, for around Rs 21 crore, to work on AI-powered smart glasses. By the time Lenskart went public it held 5.05% of Dimension NXG. It then acquired an additional 0.68% on 26 February this year, a further 1.69% on 4 July, and 1.80% on 13 September for Rs 7.99 crore, which took the total to 9.01%.
The three tranches completed in 2026 together represent 4.17% of the company for an aggregate Rs 18.5 crore.
What the numbers say about AjnaLens
Dimension NXG reported turnover of about Rs 15.97 crore in FY24, Rs 12.8 crore in FY25 and Rs 10.4 crore in FY26. That is a decline of roughly 19% in the most recent year, and about 35% over two years.
AjnaLens was founded in 2014 by Pankaj Raut, Abhijit Patil and Abhishek Tomar, and builds hardware and software using extended reality. Its customers are in defence and enterprise rather than consumer markets, where sales cycles are long, order sizes lumpy, and revenue in any single year says less about the business than it would for a consumer company.
Why an eyewear retailer is buying XR technology
Smart glasses are becoming a real product category, and the companies building them keep running into the same problem. Most people who wear glasses need prescription lenses, and fitting prescription lenses into a frame packed with displays, cameras, batteries and audio is genuinely difficult.
Technology companies have the computing. What they lack is lens-making, frame engineering, optical fitting and a network of stores where a customer can have their eyes tested and the product fitted.
Lenskart has the optical and retail infrastructure, while AjnaLens brings deeper expertise in XR and spatial computing. The investment buys Lenskart a position in the technology without acquiring the company outright or building a research division from scratch.
The AjnaLens stake sits inside a broader effort. Lenskart has launched Phonic, a line of audio glasses, and has said it is working on AI-powered smart glasses. It has partnered with Qualcomm for the technology stack underpinning those glasses.
The company is in a strong position to fund this.
Founded in 2010, Lenskart operates across India, the UAE, Singapore and Japan, and had 3,459 stores as of 30 June 2026. In the first quarter of FY27 it reported net profit of Rs 228.4 crore, up 273% year-on-year.

input.title: Sun Pharma Gets CDSCO Panel Nod for Phase IV Sovateltide Trial
input.content:
Sun Pharma Gets CDSCO Panel Nod for Phase IV Sovateltide Trial
New Delhi: Sun Pharma Laboratories Limited has received a recommendation from the Subject Expert Committee (SEC) under the Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO) to conduct a Phase IV clinical trial of Sovateltide for Injection 30 µg.
This came after firm presented Phase-IV Clinical Trial protocol of the drug Sovateltide for Injection 30 μg, (Protocol No. SP/Neurology/Sovateltide/PIV-01-2025, Version No. 1.0; Dated 03 Nov 2025) before the committee.
Sovateltide is an endothelin-B receptor agonist used in India for cerebral ischaemic stroke. It has been studied as a treatment alongside standard care for patients with acute cerebral ischaemic stroke.
At the recent SEC meeting for Neurology and Psychiatry, the expert panel examined the Phase-IV Clinical Trial protocol of the drug Sovateltide for Injection 30 μg, presented by Sun Pharma Laboratories.
The committee, however, asked the company to remove the control arm and include all patients in the drug arm.
After deliberation, the committee observed that the proposed study did not include sufficient government centres. It said the clinical trial sites should be geographically distributed across the country, including more government centers.
Finally, the committee recommended a grant of permission to conduct Phase IV clinical trial as the protocol presented by the firm. In line with the above, the expert panel asked the firm to submit Phase IV clinical trial report to CDSCO for further review by the committee.

input.title: Buy Lenskart; target of Rs 800: Motilal Oswal
input.content:
Motilal Oswal's research report on Lenskart
Since its listing (Nov’25), Lenskart’s share price has risen ~70%. We note that the strong performance has largely been driven by strong earnings momentum, leading to consistent upgrades in consensus estimates (FY28 PAT up by ~30%) and roll-forward, rather than multiple re-rating (~8.5%). Given its best-in-class store economics (store payback in <10 months, 33%+ store EBITDA margin), limited organized competition, under-penetrated category, and robust FCF generation (despite front-ended capex for Hyderabad plant), we expect Lenskart to ramp-up store additions and reach ~4.5k stores in India by FY29 (vs. ~4.3k stores earlier). Lenskart’s international segment margins have consistently surprised us, with the company achieving 10.5% pre-IND AS EBITDA margin in 1QFY27 (vs. our initial estimate of ~9.2% by FY28). Notably, the strong margin performance was despite a sharp ~45% YoY growth in marketing spends (~50-60bp higher YoY) during the last two quarters. We raise our FY27-28E consolidated pre-IND AS EBITDA by 4%/8%, driven by higher store additions in India and better operating leverage both in India and international. We model 27%/46%/59% CAGR in revenue/pre-IndAS EBITDA/adj. PAT over FY26-29E, driven by ~29%/25% revenue CAGR in India/International. We expect pre-IND AS EBITDA margin to expand to 19.4%/13.5% in India/International by FY29.
Outlook
We reiterate BUY with a revised TP of INR800, based on a 49x Sep’28 blended pre-Ind AS EBITDA multiple (55x for India, ~37.5x for Int’l).

Novartis India zooms 51% in 3 days; what's driving the pharma stock?
Novartis India acquired the Minipress and Minipres trademarks in India and certain related intellectual property rights from Pfizer Inc and Pfizer Products Inc for ₹1,250 crore.
Listen to This Article
Novartis India share price movement
Novartis India extended its rally, hitting a new high of ₹2,474.90, soaring 13 per cent on the BSE in Thursday’s intra-day deals. 
 
In the past three trading days, the stock price of the pharmaceutical firm zoomed 51 per cent after the company acquired Minipress brands from Pfizer for ₹1,250 crore.
 
At 10:16 AM, Novartis India quoted 13 per cent higher at ₹2,475.95, compared to a 0.04 per cent decline in the BSE Sensex.
 
Novartis India buys Minipress brands from Pfizer for ₹1,250 crore
Novartis India acquired the Minipress and Minipres trademarks in India and certain related intellectual property rights from Pfizer Inc and Pfizer Products Inc for ₹1,250 crore, expanding its cardiovascular portfolio with an established hypertension brand.
 
The company’s board approved the transaction on Monday, September 7, 2026, following which Novartis India executed an asset purchase agreement and trademark assignment deeds with Pfizer Inc and Pfizer Products Inc.
Also Read
As per IQVIA MAT July’26 data, Minipress XL recorded revenue of ₹228.6 crore and has been growing at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 6.3 per cent for the past four years while the category has been growing at a 9 per cent CAGR for the past four years.
 
Minipress XL (containing prazosin) is primarily indicated in India for treating hypertension (high blood pressure) and managing the urinary symptoms of benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH).
Novartis India – Outlook
Novartis India is primarily engaged in the business of trading Pharmaceuticals.
 
According to the company, initiatives such as the Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission, new regional medical hubs, and public–private partnerships in hospital development are projected to enhance service capacity, especially outside major cities. Digital health and telemedicine expansions, including eSanjeevani, the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission and a formalized e–pharmacy regulatory framework once in place, are expected to integrate health services, improve telehealth access and make healthcare delivery more efficient nationwide.
 
The company in its financial year 2025-26 (FY26), released on September 2, 2026, said the forecast period will be marked by new high–impact drug launches anticipated to drive market value. The introduction of novel anti–obesity and diabetes treatments, such as Eli Lilly’s Mounjaro and Novo Nordisk’s Wegovy, in 2025 and beyond is expected to bolster sales, particularly in metabolic and cardiovascular therapy areas. 
These therapies address India’s large and growing diabetic and overweight populations and are projected to achieve substantial uptake. The patent expiry of semaglutide in 2026 will likely lead to multiple Indian companies launching affordable generic or biosimilar versions, expanding patient access while sustaining market growth, the company said.
 
Healthcare providers and pharmaceutical companies are expected to expand further into Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities, where demand is rising as awareness and access improve. The expansion of pharmacy retail chains and online pharmacies, with hybrid online–offline models, will modernize drug distribution and improve last–mile availability of medicines across India. In the hospital sector, private hospitals and clinics will continue attracting investment and expanding capacity, supported by insurance coverage and rising medical tourism interest in India’s high–quality, cost–effective care offerings, Novartis India said.

input.title: Novartis-Pfizer trademark deal has opposite impact on their stock prices; Novartis India jumps 20% while Pfizer slips 3%
input.content:
A couple of days after Novartis India Ltd agreed to acquire Pfizer Inc’s trademarks for ‘Minipress’ and ‘Minipres’ in India, the development has had the opposite impact on their respective stocks.
NIL’s stock prices ended up 20 per cent at ₹2,188 on the BSE on Wednesday amid optimism involving the drug used to treat hypertension and manage urinary symptoms of benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH). Pfizer’s stock, however, ended the day down 3.3 per cent at ₹4,171.35 on the BSE.
The two companies had announced on Monday that NIL had inked an agreement with Pfizer Inc to acquire the trademarks for India, besides certain related intellectual property rights, for ₹1,250 crore. NIL is owned by private-equity firm ChrysCapital, after it acquired the entire 70.68 per cent stake in the company that was previously held by the Swiss parent company Novartis AG.
A note from the Systematix Group pointed out that Pfizer India would receive only ₹132 crore, as the trademark or brand ownership was with the parent. The divestment could impact Pfizer’s net earnings, it noted. The report expected a decline in annual EBITDA by approximately ₹60 crore, translating to about 4-5 per cent adverse impact on EPS.
For NIL, the Minipress acquisition gives a mass-market presence that can be leveraged to build on other mass-market brands, the report said. “Novartis will need to borrow to fund this transaction and hence the transaction may be accretive from only year 2 (two),” the report added. The inorganic route helps build market presence, the report said, adding that NIL could leverage its nephrologist connect to meaningfully expand the Minipress XL franchise.
Published on September 9, 2026

input.title: Nykaa bets on in-person discovery as Nykaaland returns to Delhi-NCR for fourth edition
input.content:
4 Min Read
Nykaa is once again putting its marketing muscle behind Nykaaland, the beauty and lifestyle festival it co produces with BookMyShow Live, as the event returns for a fourth edition, running October 23 to 25 at the NSIC (National Small Industries Corporation) Exhibition Grounds in Okhla, Delhi NCR. Bookings opened on BookMyShow on September 9.
The festival has become a reliable calendar fixture for the beauty industry's sampling and discovery playbook, an in person extension of what Nykaa otherwise does online through reviews, live commerce and its Global Store import business. This year's edition leans further into that role, with more than 60 brands taking stalls, ranging from mass K beauty imports to premium international names and Nykaa's own house of brands portfolio.
Anchit Nayar, Executive Director and Chief Executive Officer, Nykaa Beauty, said, “Nykaaland has become a celebration of the vibrancy and diversity of the growing beauty community in India. It is a chance for beauty enthusiasts to come together with the best brands, artists, experts, and content creators for a weekend of experience, education, and entertainment. As the festival enters its fourth year the participation, energy and excitement is reaching new highs, we look forward to seeing you in Delhi for our biggest Nykaaland yet.”
Naman Pugalia, Chief Business Officer, Live Events, BookMyShow, said, “With Nykaaland, we set out to create an experience that goes beyond beauty, bringing together artistry, music, culture, community and discovery to create moments that audiences can truly immerse themselves in. The overwhelming response to our debut in Delhi-NCR last year reaffirmed the incredible appetite for such immersive, world-class cultural experiences in the region, and marked an important milestone in Nykaaland’s journey. As we return for our fourth edition this year, we are building on that momentum to make Nykaaland even bigger, more immersive and more relevant than ever before. Our vision has always been to build an IP that brings the best of global and Indian beauty together with entertainment, culture, and live experiences, and this edition is another step towards establishing Nykaaland as a distinctive platform at that intersection of beauty and live entertainment.”
The event lands at a point where beauty retailers are competing hard for share of a category that's grown crowded. Reliance's Tira, Purplle, Amazon and quick commerce platforms have all pushed into beauty discovery and delivery over the past two years. For Nykaa, an owned festival property (intellectual property, or IP) offers something quick commerce can't easily replicate: a controlled environment to introduce new brands to Indian consumers before they hit the shelf online, and a data point it can cite to brand partners on footfall and engagement.
Rare Beauty's India festival debut is the clearest example. The Selena Gomez backed label enters at Nykaaland rather than through a conventional retail launch, a route Nykaa has used before to seed brands like K18 and JudyDoll through its Global Store partnership before they scale into full retail distribution.
The three day event pairs retail stalls with masterclasses (celebrity makeup artist Namrata Soni is headlining, alongside sessions tied to Huda Beauty and TIRTIR) and a nightly music line up. Bombay Rockers and Navjot Ahuja perform on day two, and Sukhbir closes out the weekend on day three. Tata Starbucks and Vedica Himalayan Spring Water are attached as sponsors, a sign the festival now functions as a broader lifestyle sponsorship property, not just a beauty trade show.
For now, Nykaaland remains a useful proxy for how India's beauty majors are thinking about growth: less about adding new online customers at the margin, and more about deepening engagement with the ones they already have, through experiences rather than discounts.

Whether the format can keep scaling attendance in a single city, or whether Nykaa eventually takes it to a second market, is the more interesting question than this year's brand list, and one the company hasn't addressed publicly.

input.title: Upper Circuit: Novartis India shares gain for eighth straight day to a record high
input.content:
2 Min Read
Shares of Novartis India extended their gains for the eighth consecutive day and were locked in a 20% upper circuit to hit a fresh record high of ₹2,186.40 apiece on Wednesday, September 9.
The stock has surged 47.1% in eight consecutive trade sessions since August 31, 2026. The last time the stock witnessed gains for eight days in a row was from March 2 to March 12, 2026, when it had only risen 6.2%.
This is also the stock's biggest single-day gain since February 20, 2026, when it had risen 20% as well, after its promoter, Novartis AG, agreed to sell its 70.68% stake in the company to a consortium led by ChrysCapital. The deal involves the sale of 1.74 crore shares to WaveRise Investments, ChrysCapital Fund X and Two Infinity Partners.
After the transaction, Novartis AG would cease to be the promoter, with the acquiring consortium taking control and becoming the new promoters. Novartis India was also to then change its name to remove references to the Novartis group within 120 days of the deal's completion.
Separately, last month, Dr Reddy's Laboratories ended its distribution and promotion agreement with Novartis India for select brands, following a change in Novartis India's controlling shareholding. Dr Reddy's would continue to commercialise the covered brands until September 30, 2026.
Earlier this week, Novartis India's board approved the acquisition of the 'Minipress' and 'Minipres' trademarks in India, along with related intellectual property rights, from Pfizer for a total consideration of ₹1,250 crore. The company signed the necessary agreements with Pfizer, with the signing and closing taking place simultaneously.
According to IQVIA data cited by Novartis India, Minipress XL reported revenue of ₹228.6 crore in the 12 months ended July 2026 and grew at a 6.3% compound annual growth rate (CAGR) over the past four years.
Novartis India shares have surged 36.02% over the past month. More than 53 thousand shares of the company changed hands in intraday trade before the stock hit its upper circuit, with trading volume at 2.77 times its 10-day average.

input.title: Novartis India to Acquire Pfizer’s BP Drug Brands for ₹1,250 Crore
input.content:
Novartis India Ltd signed an agreement to acquire the ‘Minipress’ and ‘Minipres’ trademarks in India, along with certain related intellectual property rights, from Pfizer Inc and Pfizer Products Inc. The transaction is valued at ₹1,250 crore. The acquisition will strengthen Novartis India’s presence in the cardiovascular and hypertension treatment segment while adding an established brand to its existing pharmaceutical portfolio.
Minipress XL Used for Hypertension and BPH
Minipress XL, which contains the active pharmaceutical ingredient prazosin, is primarily prescribed for the treatment of hypertension, or high blood pressure. It is also used to manage urinary symptoms associated with benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH). According to industry tracker IQVIA, Minipress XL generated ₹228.6 crore in revenue during the 12 months ended July 2026. The brand recorded a four-year growth rate of 6.3%, compared with 9% growth for the overall category during the same period, Novartis India said.
Acquisition Follows ChrysCapital’s Takeover
The latest deal comes shortly after private-equity firm ChrysCapital acquired a 70.68% stake in Novartis India Ltd, which was previously held by Swiss pharmaceutical major Novartis AG. Following the transaction, Novartis India has a new management team and is also expected to operate under a new name. Industry observers view the acquisition of the Minipress brands as part of a broader strategy to expand and strengthen the PE-owned company’s India business. Novartis India currently operates across several therapeutic segments, including pain management, calcium supplementation, gynaecology, neurosciences and transplant immunology. Its established brands include Voveran, Calcium Sandoz and Tegrital, among others.
Pfizer to Discontinue Minipress XL Sales
Pfizer India has announced that it will discontinue the marketing, distribution and sale of Minipress XL from September 7, 2026. The decision follows Pfizer Inc.’s move to discontinue the manufacture of Minipress XL. In connection with the decision, Pfizer India said it would receive a lump-sum payment of $13.9 million, or approximately ₹131.38 crore, from Pfizer Inc., USA. The transition is expected to pave the way for Novartis India to take control of the acquired trademarks and associated rights in the Indian market.
Novartis India Undergoing Business Transformation
The Minipress acquisition follows a broader restructuring of Novartis India. The listed Indian company was put up for sale after Novartis AG announced in 2024 that it was reviewing its stake in the business. In February 2026, the proposed transaction was valued at ₹1,446 crore. Following the change in ownership, the company is being rebuilt with a new management structure and a workforce of around 40 employees. At the same time, Novartis India continues to rely on its established network of contract manufacturers and business relationships as it develops its standalone operations. The company reported a turnover of ₹354 crore for the financial year ended March 2026.
Strategic Move to Strengthen India Operations
The acquisition of the Minipress and Minipres trademarks represents an important step in Novartis India’s efforts to expand its branded pharmaceutical portfolio. With an established hypertension brand, an existing customer base and significant annual revenue, the deal could provide the company with a stronger platform for growth in India’s chronic-care market. As reported by thehindubusinessline.com, as Novartis India transitions under its new ownership and management, further acquisitions and portfolio expansion could play a key role in shaping its next phase of growth.

input.title: Sun Pharma Secures Ratings Boost From Moody’s, S&P on $11.75-Billion Organon Acquisition Bid
input.content:
New Delhi: Sun Pharmaceutical Industries has secured investment-grade ratings from Moody’s Ratings and S&P Global Ratings as India’s largest drugmaker moves ahead with its proposed $11.75-billion acquisition of US-based Organon & Co.
S&P assigned Sun Pharma a preliminary ‘BBB+’ long-term issuer credit rating, while Moody’s gave the company a ‘Baa1’ long-term issuer rating. Both rating agencies maintained a stable outlook.
The ratings indicate adequate capacity to meet financial obligations, with moderate credit risk.
Organon Deal Could Nearly Double Revenue
The rating actions follow Sun Pharma’s binding bid in April 2026 to acquire 100% of Organon at an enterprise value of $11.75 billion. The transaction is expected to close by March 2027, subject to regulatory approvals.
S&P expects the Organon acquisition to significantly strengthen Sun Pharma’s business profile and nearly double its revenue base.
The agency estimates Sun Pharma’s revenue could reach around Rs 1.3 trillion, or approximately $14 billion, by FY28, compared with an estimated Rs 645 billion, or around $7 billion, in FY27 excluding Organon.
Organon is expected to contribute around 40%-45% of the combined group’s EBITDA following the acquisition.
Women’s Health, Biosimilars Get Boost
Moody’s said the acquisition would strengthen Sun Pharma’s scale, geographical presence and growth platforms, particularly in women’s health and biosimilars.
Organon’s presence in markets such as China and Korea could also provide Sun Pharma with opportunities to cross-sell products in countries where its presence is currently limited, S&P said.
S&P added that the enlarged company’s operating scale would become comparable with global pharmaceutical companies such as Teva Pharmaceuticals and Viatris, which generate annual revenues of about $14 billion-$17 billion.
To fund the transaction, Sun Pharma has secured a $12-billion committed acquisition bridge loan from a syndicate of international banks, according to Moody’s.
The pharmaceutical major also held approximately $3.6 billion in cash as of March 31, 2026.

input.title: Titan, Lenskart, DMart, Trent, Meesho, Nykaa, FirstCry: Price targets, risks for consumption stocks
input.content:
Four models in the next phase
Ambit said India’s next phase of online retail penetration will be split across four models rather than being captured by one. Traditional horizontal platforms will retain breadth, brands and higher-ticket demand, but may grow more slowly as quick commerce and value platforms take some cohorts. Quick commerce owns grocery frequency, while vertical platforms control category depth in areas such as fashion, beauty and personal care, and childcare.
Ambit said value commerce stands apart because it serves low average selling price, fragmented and unbranded supply that other models cannot serve profitably. It ranked value commerce highest on scalability, saying it remains asset-light and working-capital-light, unlike quick commerce, which needs density-led capital expenditure, and category verticals, which operate in a structurally smaller pool.
Penetration and monetisation
According to Ambit, value e-commerce is not just a beneficiary of rising online demand but a driver of penetration itself. By aggregating fragmented sellers, creating demand through discovery and keeping fulfilment asset-light, Meesho makes low-ticket commerce viable and helps bring offline consumers and categories online.
Ambit added that global platforms such as PDD, Shopee and MELI show how scale can shift monetisation from low-margin fulfilment to higher-margin advertising and services. It said PDD and Shopee delivered EBITDAM of 22 per cent and 20 per cent in CY25, against 24 per cent for Amazon, 3 per cent for Alibaba and 14 per cent for MELI, adding that the next leg in India will be monetisation rather than GMV growth.
Why Ambit prefers Meesho
Ambit said Meesho, which evolved from WhatsApp reselling into a discovery-led marketplace, is the only scaled Indian value platform. It leads on order volume, has 274 million AUTC and gets about 85 per cent of its users from outside the top eight cities. Ambit said Flipkart’s Shopsy and Amazon’s Bazaar remain constrained by search-led structures and larger-basket economics.
