input.title: Lenskart’s Insight into Online Eyewear Acceptance
input.content:
Lenskart’s Insight into Online Eyewear Acceptance
Industry and Competitive Context
India's eyewear industry presents one of the most structurally compelling retail opportunities in any emerging economy. According to a RedSeer report cited in Lenskart's Draft Red Herring Prospectus filed with SEBI in July 2025, the Indian eyewear market was valued at approximately USD 9.2 billion in FY25 and is projected to grow at a compound annual rate of roughly 13 percent, reaching approximately USD 17.2 billion by FY30. Prescription eyeglasses account for close to 73 percent of that value, followed by sunglasses at approximately 22 percent and contact lenses at approximately 5 percent.
Despite this scale, the market has been characterised by deep structural fragmentation. Lenskart CEO Peyush Bansal stated in a published interview with Business Today that approximately 90 percent of India's spectacles market is unorganised, dominated by local opticians operating with no supply chain integration and no standardised technology infrastructure. The country had only around 10,000 practising optometrists against a documented requirement for approximately 40,000. Only approximately 25 percent of Indians who need vision correction actually wear spectacles, despite more than 500 million people requiring it. This combination of a large unmet need, chronic market fragmentation, and an absent organised retail infrastructure defined the strategic theatre that Lenskart entered when it launched in November 2010.
The competitive landscape at founding was almost entirely offline. Titan Eye Plus, backed by the Tata Group, was the only significant organised optical retailer of note. Multinational brands such as EssilorLuxottica were present through wholesale distribution but not direct consumer retail. Amazon and eBay had both consciously avoided the eyewear category in India, recognising its fitting complexity. Lenskart therefore entered a market with virtually no organised digital competition but also no proof that Indian consumers would trust an online channel for a product category requiring accurate prescription, physical fit, and aesthetic approval simultaneously.
Brand Situation Prior to Strategic Inflection
Peyush Bansal, a former Microsoft Program Manager and IIM Bangalore alumnus, launched Lenskart in 2010 along with co-founders Amit Chaudhary and Sumeet Kapahi. The company had earlier validated a digital eyewear thesis in the United States through a venture called Flyrr.com, which provided proof that an online eyewear model could gain traction before Bansal chose to bring the concept to India. Lenskart launched by selling contact lenses first, a deliberate sequencing choice. Contact lenses are a standardised, commoditised product that do not require physical fitting or frame-to-face aesthetic matching, making them the lowest-risk entry point into a high-friction category.
Eyeglasses were added within months of launch, and sunglasses followed by March 2011. The early business operated purely online and faced an immediate and specific structural challenge that did not exist in adjacent e-commerce categories. In clothing, size guides could approximate fit. In electronics, specifications could be compared. In eyewear, a consumer needed to know whether a frame physically fit their temples, whether it suited their face shape, and whether it matched their personal aesthetic, all before completing a purchase online. As Business Standard documented at the time, buying spectacles online surprised Indian consumers because the category required touch, feel, and physical trial in ways that other products did not. This was not a general trust deficit toward e-commerce; it was a category-specific conversion barrier unique to eyewear, and it had to be solved architecturally before any significant online sales volume could be generated.
By 2016, Lenskart had become one of the two largest optical chains in India by store count, alongside Titan Eye Plus. Its Delhi manufacturing facility was producing approximately 300,000 glasses per month. A secondary factory in Zhengzhou, China, handled approximately 50 percent of its production volume. The company was simultaneously building a vertically integrated supply chain that would later become one of its most durable competitive moats.
Strategic Objective
Lenskart's defining strategic challenge was not awareness, pricing, or product variety. It was consumer acceptance of the online eyewear purchase decision itself. The company needed to collapse the psychological and functional gap between physical trial at an optical store and a digital purchase flow, in a category where trust and accuracy in product selection had direct implications for consumer health. Getting the wrong spectacle frame is not merely an aesthetic inconvenience; for prescription eyewear, it is a functional failure. Lenskart's strategic objective was therefore to engineer a consumer experience architecture that replicated or surpassed the in-store confidence-building process through technology, service design, and offline touchpoints, rather than simply transplanting a standard e-commerce model into a high-friction vertical.
Campaign Architecture and Execution
Lenskart's approach to building online eyewear acceptance was not a single campaign but a layered, multi-phase intervention that combined technology, service innovation, membership economics, and physical retail expansion.
The most consequential technology deployment was the 3D virtual try-on feature, initially powered by DITTO technology and later evolved into a proprietary AI-driven capability. As confirmed on Lenskart's official product pages and the Google Play Store listing, the feature allows users to upload a photo or use a live phone camera to try different frames virtually in 3D, viewing the result at 180-degree angles. The system scans and analyses the user's face, detects face shape and temple size, and suggests frames accordingly. This directly addressed the tactile barrier that had historically made online eyewear purchase uncomfortable for Indian consumers. According to Lenskart co-founder Ramneek Khurana, as quoted in published statements across APN News, Exchange4media, and MediaBrief, one in every four users visiting the Lenskart app began using the augmented reality feature after it was introduced. According to the company's DRHP filed in July 2025, Lenskart conducted 38.6 million virtual try-ons in India in FY25 and 37.9 million face and size measurements in the same period. These are not aspirational projections but operationally verified disclosures from a regulatory filing.
In parallel, Lenskart introduced the Home Try On service in India, where a trained optician visits the consumer at their residence with a selection of over 100 frame styles, conducts a professional eye examination, and facilitates the purchase. This service hybrid combined the convenience of online discovery with the precision of a physical professional interaction, which is significant in a market where optometrist shortages had historically left large urban populations without access to quality eye care. The Home Trial offering was further supported by a no-questions-asked exchange and return policy even for powered prescription glasses, a policy commitment that directly lowered the perceived risk of an online purchase.
The Lenskart Gold Membership programme became another pillar of its acceptance strategy. As disclosed on Lenskart's official website, the Gold Membership offers a Buy One Get One Free offer on eyeglasses and sunglasses, five percent additional cashback on future orders, free quarterly cleaning and repair services, and a 10 percent discount on Aqualens contact lenses. The Buy One Get One Free offer in particular addressed a key consumer psychology barrier, which is that paying full price for a product one cannot physically trial feels high-risk. The promotion effectively reduced the perceived unit cost and converted the trial decision into a low-stakes transaction. This is consistent with publicly documented commentary across multiple investor and industry reports describing Lenskart's early "free Buy One Get One" campaigns as a mechanism for driving trial among first-time online eyewear buyers.
Positioning and Consumer Insight
The consumer insight underlying Lenskart's entire market-building strategy was that Indian consumers did not resist online eyewear as a concept but rather as a confidence problem. They were willing to engage digitally if a credible system could assure them that the product would fit, look appropriate, and be accurate to their prescription. This nuance separated Lenskart's strategic response from what a conventional e-commerce brand might have offered. Rather than simply discounting to drive trial, Lenskart invested in confidence infrastructure: the 3D try-on, the home professional service, the liberal return policy, and the Gold Membership's economic safety net.
Peyush Bansal has framed Lenskart's vision publicly across multiple media engagements as democratising eyewear in India, positioning the brand analogously to how Maruti democratised automobile ownership. This positioning served a dual purpose. It communicated affordability relative to legacy optical retail, where unorganised local opticians had historically maintained opaque pricing with significant markups, and it positioned technology as an enabler of access rather than a premium feature. The brand's private label product range, including the John Jacobs label launched in 2017 and the Blu lens product addressing blue light from digital screens, extended this positioning across multiple consumer segments and use cases.
Lenskart's mobile-first channel architecture also reflected a sophisticated consumer insight about how Indian consumers engage with new categories. The app became the primary interface for the virtual try-on, Home Trial booking, and Gold Membership management, and was designed to lower the friction at every stage of the purchase funnel. According to the DRHP, the Lenskart mobile app had accumulated over 100 million downloads globally by FY25, and the platform recorded 104.97 million annual website visitors in FY25.
Media and Channel Strategy
Verified public information on Lenskart's paid media allocation and campaign-level creative strategy is limited to what is disclosed in the DRHP and public press statements. Lenskart's FY25 total marketing and promotion expenditure stood at Rs 448.41 crore, as disclosed in the DRHP and widely reported by financial publications including IndMoney and PL India. The company earmarked Rs 320.06 crore from its Rs 2,150 crore fresh IPO issue specifically for brand marketing and business promotion expenses to enhance brand awareness, reflecting a continued strategic investment in consumer-facing spending.
Performance marketing across Google, Facebook, and YouTube constituted a documented component of Lenskart's digital customer acquisition approach during its early scaling years, as referenced across multiple industry analyses and investor commentaries. The company also leveraged influencer campaigns and brand storytelling as Indian social media adoption accelerated. Peyush Bansal's high-profile participation in Shark Tank India, beginning with Season 1 in 2021 and 2022 as one of the permanent "sharks," provided Lenskart with sustained national broadcast visibility and significantly elevated Bansal's personal brand recognition, which in turn reinforced the corporate brand across a mass television audience. No verified public information is available on specific campaign creative executions, media mix percentages, or influencer partnership terms, as company disclosures at the level available are financial and operational rather than campaign-specific.
Business and Brand Outcomes
Lenskart's financial trajectory represents one of the most documented growth stories in Indian consumer-tech retail. Revenue from operations grew from approximately Rs 967 crore in FY20 to Rs 1,502 crore in FY22, then nearly tripled to Rs 3,788 crore in FY23, representing approximately 150 percent growth year on year. Revenue grew a further 43 percent to Rs 5,427 crore in FY24, and reached Rs 6,652 crore in FY25, representing 22.6 percent growth over the prior year. These figures are drawn directly from the DRHP filed with SEBI and widely corroborated by reporting from Kotak Neo, IndMoney, and PL India among others.
FY25 marked Lenskart's first full-year net profit, at Rs 297 crore, compared to a net loss of Rs 10 crore in FY24. Gross margin stood at approximately 70 percent in FY25, EBITDA margin reached 14.6 percent, and ROCE was 13.84 percent. According to the DRHP, revenues and EBITDA grew at a compound annual rate of 32.5 percent and 92.3 percent respectively between FY23 and FY25. The average payback period for new Company Owned Company Operated stores opened across India in FY25 was 10.3 months, as disclosed in a publicly available IPO note.
On digital engagement, 45 percent of Lenskart's India revenue was generated via digital touchpoints in FY25, as disclosed in the DRHP. The company's 38.6 million virtual try-ons in India alone during FY25 indicate that the technology, which was once a novel feature deployed to overcome consumer reluctance, had become a mainstream feature of the purchase journey at significant scale.
The store count expanded from approximately 700 stores to 2,700 plus stores globally between FY22 and mid-2025. Within India, Lenskart operated 2,067 stores across metro cities and Tier 2 and Tier 3 towns including Kota, Ranchi, and Mysore as of reporting periods, far exceeding Titan Eye Plus's approximately 900 stores. For comparative context, Titan Eye Plus recorded approximately Rs 796 crore in revenue for FY25, making Lenskart's revenue more than eight times that of its closest organised competitor.
In June 2022, Lenskart completed the acquisition of a majority stake in OWNDAYS, the Japanese eyewear company, at a valuation of $400 million. As reported by TechCrunch and Business Standard, the acquisition extended Lenskart's operational presence to 13 Asian markets including Japan, Singapore, Thailand, Taiwan, Philippines, Indonesia, and Malaysia. OWNDAYS operated 115 stores in Japan and 142 stores across 10 other Asian markets at the time of the transaction. As described by Peyush Bansal in the official Lenskart press release quoted by TechCrunch, the acquisition was framed around the mission to drive the transformation of how people buy eyewear globally.
Investor conviction tracked this trajectory. SoftBank Vision Fund invested $275 million in December 2019, bringing the valuation to $1.5 billion. ADIA invested $500 million in 2023 retaining the $4.5 billion valuation as reported by TechCrunch. Temasek and Fidelity invested a combined $200 million in a secondary round in June 2024 at approximately $5 billion. Fidelity subsequently marked up the valuation to $5.6 billion by November 2024 and to $6.1 billion by June 2025 according to Business Standard, ahead of the company's IPO which was listed on November 10, 2025. The company has raised a total of $981 million across 19 funding rounds from 57 investors as of available public records on Tracxn.
Strategic Implications
Lenskart's trajectory offers several analytically instructive implications for strategy in high-friction consumer categories. First, the case illustrates that online market creation in a tactile, safety-critical product category requires category-specific trust infrastructure, not merely category-agnostic e-commerce mechanics. Lenskart's investment in the virtual try-on, home professional service, and return policy were not marketing expenditures in the conventional sense; they were structural interventions that reengineered the consumer decision-making process. Discounting alone would not have overcome a barrier rooted in physical uncertainty about prescription accuracy and frame fit.
Second, the phased omnichannel architecture reflects a deliberate sequencing logic. Lenskart began online to achieve rapid geographic reach and catalogue scalability, then added offline stores not as a retreat from the digital model but as confidence anchors that reinforced the online brand. The resulting model, in which 45 percent of India revenue is generated via digital touchpoints while physical stores function as both showrooms and fulfilment centres, represents a genuine integration rather than a parallel-channel compromise.
Third, vertical integration in manufacturing provided a structural cost advantage that sustained the affordable positioning, which was itself the primary demand-generation lever in a market where 90 percent of consumers had historically purchased through unorganised local opticians. By manufacturing at scale in Delhi and through its China facility, Lenskart could price below traditional optical retail while maintaining product quality, making the online channel economically superior rather than merely more convenient.
Fourth, the OWNDAYS acquisition signals a broader strategic logic of acquiring market-specific consumer trust through established local brands rather than building it from scratch in each geography. OWNDAYS had built brand equity and physical presence across Southeast Asia over three decades. Lenskart's acquisition of that trust, rather than trying to replicate it organically, reflects a mature read of international retail dynamics in a category where consumer confidence in prescription accuracy and optical quality is non-trivially difficult to establish with an unfamiliar brand.
Fifth, the IPO filing and the earmarking of Rs 320.06 crore for brand marketing and promotion out of the fresh issue indicate that Lenskart views consumer awareness spending not as a growth-phase expense to be wound down at profitability but as an ongoing investment in category expansion. This is consistent with the company's own self-description as commanding only a 4 to 6 percent share of a highly fragmented total market, despite being the largest organised player. The scale of the opportunity ahead remains far larger than the share captured, and brand-building spending will remain central to growing that share.
Discussion Questions
- Lenskart pursued a strategy of building consumer confidence in online eyewear through technology, service design, and membership economics rather than relying primarily on price-based promotions. To what extent is this confidence infrastructure replicable by a well-funded competitor, and what elements of it constitute a defensible moat?
- Lenskart's omnichannel model evolved from a digital-first entry into physical retail rather than the reverse. How does this sequencing affect the strategic trade-offs a company faces in category trust, customer acquisition cost, and brand positioning compared to a retailer that begins with physical stores and adds digital?
- The OWNDAYS acquisition extended Lenskart's presence to 13 Asian markets but also introduced significant operational complexity in managing two brands, multiple regulatory environments, and divergent consumer preferences. Using the lens of market entry theory, evaluate whether acquisition was a superior strategy compared to organic international expansion for a category like eyewear.
- Lenskart self-reports commanding only 4 to 6 percent of the total Indian eyewear market despite being the largest organised player by revenue. What does this structural reality imply about the company's long-term growth ceiling, the risks associated with its current valuation, and the strategic priorities it must execute post-IPO?
- The 3D virtual try-on and home eye test service model were designed for urban, smartphone-literate, mid-income consumers. As Lenskart expands aggressively into Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities through franchise stores, what adaptations to its consumer acceptance strategy would be necessary to drive online eyewear adoption in markets where the technology infrastructure and consumer digital literacy profile may differ substantially?

input.title: Sun Pharma gets NSE, BSE nod to reclassify Valia family as public shareholders
input.content:
Sun Pharma gets NSE, BSE nod to reclassify Valia family as public shareholders
Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd received no-objection from NSE and BSE to reclassify Krishna, Sudhir, and Raksha Valia from promoter group to public category. The decision follows applications filed in May 2026 under SEBI Regulation 31A.
*this image is generated using AI for illustrative purposes only.
Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Limited has secured regulatory clearance from India’s premier stock exchanges to reclassify key members of its promoter group into the public category. The National Stock Exchange of India Limited (NSE) and BSE Limited (BSE) issued no-objection letters dated August 06, 2026, approving the request submitted by the company on May 26, 2026. This move alters the shareholding structure classification for Krishna Vrundavandas Valia, Sudhir Vrundavandas Valia, and Raksha Sudhir Valia, shifting them from the ‘Promoter Group’ to the ‘Public’ category in accordance with Regulation 31A of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015.
The reclassification follows a series of prior intimations issued by Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd on May 14, 2026, May 22, 2026, and May 26, 2026. The company notified stakeholders of its intent to seek this change, which is procedurally required when promoters wish to exit the promoter category or when their holding falls below specified thresholds, though the specific reason for this reclassification was not detailed in the exchange filings beyond the regulatory compliance aspect.
Reclassification Details
The no-objection letters from both exchanges confirm the approval for the following individuals:
The exchanges emphasized that Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd must ensure compliance with subsequent relevant disclosures of material events related to this reclassification, as mandated by Regulation 31A of the SEBI Listing Regulations. Copies of the no-objection letters are available on the company’s website at www.sunpharma.com .
Regulatory Compliance
The intimation was issued under Regulation 30 and Regulation 31A of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015. Anoop Anjanikumar Deshpande, Company Secretary and Compliance Officer of Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd, signed the disclosure. The registered office of the company is located at SPARC, Tandalja, Vadodara, Gujarat.
This reclassification impacts how the shareholding pattern is reported in future quarterly disclosures. Shares held by the named individuals will now be aggregated under the public category rather than the promoter group, potentially affecting metrics related to promoter pledge limits and public float calculations, although the immediate financial impact remains neutral as it is a structural classification change rather than a transactional event.

input.title: Sun Pharma Advanced Research Company Share Price Target 2027, 2028 and 2030: Long Term Analyst Forecast
input.content:
Sun Pharma Advanced Research Company Share Price Target 2027, 2028 and 2030: Long Term Analyst Forecast
CMP Rs 251.04. FY26 EPS Rs 54.3 (one-time PRV sale; core is loss-making). Target 2027: Rs 335 (+33%). Target 2028: Rs 375 (+49%). Target 2030: Rs 470 (+87%).
Updated: 6 Aug 2026 • 11:20 am
Posted by:
Sun Pharma Advanced Research Company is a novel drug discovery and development spin-off from Sun Pharmaceutical Industries, and it is one of the most misread income statements in Indian pharma. In FY26, SPARC reported a net profit of approximately Rs 1,552 crore, making it look like a profitable research company. It is not. The entire profit came from a single sale of a US Rare-Paediatric-Disease Priority Review Voucher for USD 195 million (approximately Rs 1,840 crore booked as other operating revenue). Core operating revenue actually fell 51 percent in FY26 as key research programmes transitioned phases. The SPARC share price target of Rs 335 for 2027, rising to Rs 470 by 2030, should be understood as a research-pipeline valuation, not a trailing-earnings multiple.
Backed by Sun Pharma's 54 percent stake and access to clinical and regulatory infrastructure, SPARC is essentially a listed biotech incubator with a novel molecule pipeline in oncology, dermatology, and ophthalmology. For investors comfortable with biotech-style pipeline risk and long development timelines, SPARC represents India's most credible listed novel drug discovery vehicle. This article covers the SPARC share price target 2027, 2028, and 2030 based on analyst estimates as of August 2026.
Click Here – Get Free Investment Predictions
Sun Pharma Advanced Research Company Company Overview
What most investors miss: The FY26 net profit of approximately Rs 1,552 crore came almost entirely from a single sale of a US Rare-Paediatric-Disease Priority Review Voucher (PRV) for USD 195 million. This is a one-time event. Core operating revenue actually fell 51 percent in FY26 as research programmes transitioned. Investors treating the reported FY26 EPS of Rs 54.3 as a recurring earnings base will significantly overestimate SPARC's current earning power. The correct frame is pipeline valuation, not PE multiple.
Sun Pharma Advanced Research Company Limited (SPARC) was incorporated in 2007 as a spin-off from Sun Pharmaceutical Industries to house its novel drug discovery research operations. The company is focused on developing new chemical entities and new biological entities in therapeutic areas including oncology, dermatology, ophthalmology, and CNS. Sun Pharmaceutical Industries holds approximately 54 percent of SPARC. SPARC has received multiple FDA designations for its pipeline molecules.
Why Is the Sun Pharma Advanced Research Company Share Price Target Set at Rs 335 for 2027
Sun Pharma Backing Provides Clinical and Regulatory Infrastructure Access
Unlike standalone Indian biotechs, SPARC has access to Sun Pharma's global clinical trial networks, regulatory affairs teams, and manufacturing relationships. This infrastructure reduces the cost and time of moving molecules through Phase 1 and Phase 2 trials, making SPARC's research capital more efficient than a standalone entity. This structural advantage supports the SPARC share price target over the 2027 to 2030 window.
Priority Review Voucher Optionality Could Recur in the Pipeline
SPARC has sold a US PRV for USD 195 million in FY26. PRVs are awarded for drugs targeting rare paediatric diseases and can be sold to other pharmaceutical companies who use them to accelerate FDA review timelines for their own drugs. If SPARC's pipeline yields another rare disease designation, a second PRV sale would create another large one-time cash event that exceeds the SPARC share price target earnings assumptions.
Novel Molecule Pipeline in High-Value Therapeutic Areas
SPARC's research pipeline spans oncology, dermatology (novel retinoid molecules), ophthalmology, and CNS, all high-value therapeutic areas where successful drug approvals command premium pricing. A single successful Phase 3 programme outcome in any of these areas would be a step-change catalyst for the SPARC share price target well beyond the Rs 470 base case 2030 level.
Listed Vehicle for Novel Drug Discovery Is Rare in Indian Markets
SPARC is one of very few listed Indian companies primarily focused on novel drug discovery and development rather than generic manufacturing or CDMO services. For investors seeking exposure to India's emerging biotech innovation sector, SPARC is the most liquid and credible option. This scarcity premium provides a valuation floor independent of quarterly earnings, supporting the SPARC share price target.
FDA Designations Signal Pipeline Quality Above Generic Research Organisations
SPARC has received multiple FDA designations including orphan drug status and fast-track designations for pipeline molecules. These designations reduce the regulatory risk premium on the pipeline and provide access to priority FDA review timelines, potentially shortening the time from Phase 2 to commercialisation. Each new designation is a positive data point for the SPARC share price target thesis.
Sun Pharma Advanced Research Company Share Price Targets 2027, 2028 and 2030
Sun Pharma Advanced Research Company Share Price Target 2027: Rs 335
The SPARC share price target 2027 is Rs 335, representing approximately 33 percent upside from CMP Rs 251.04. Because SPARC's core operations are loss-making and FY26 EPS was distorted by a one-time PRV sale, this target is derived from the 5x EPS multiple applied to the inflated FY26 figure, extrapolated at 12 percent annual growth to reflect the pipeline maturation timeline. The 2027 catalyst is positive Phase 2 or Phase 3 data from a key pipeline programme.
Sun Pharma Advanced Research Company Share Price Target 2028: Rs 375
The SPARC share price target 2028 is Rs 375, implying approximately 49 percent upside from CMP. By 2028, SPARC's clinical pipeline should have advanced materially, with at least one molecule in Phase 3. Any positive interim readout from a Phase 3 oncology or dermatology programme would trigger a significant re-rating above the Rs 375 base case target.
Sun Pharma Advanced Research Company Share Price Target 2030: Rs 470
The SPARC share price target 2030 is Rs 470, implying approximately 87 percent upside from CMP and a 4-year CAGR of approximately 17 percent. By 2030, SPARC's pipeline should include at least one molecule at or near New Drug Application filing with the FDA, potentially generating milestone or royalty income. A second PRV sale, if another rare paediatric designation is awarded, would provide a large non-recurring cash event.
Bull Case and Bear Case for the Sun Pharma Advanced Research Company Share Price Target 2030
Bull Case: Rs 580
The bull case SPARC share price target of Rs 580 by 2030 requires a successful Phase 3 outcome in oncology or dermatology with commercial licensing to a large pharma partner for upfront payment and royalties, plus the possibility of a second PRV sale. In this scenario, SPARC transitions from a research company to a royalty-generating entity, warranting a biotech-style re-rating significantly above the current pipeline discount.
Bear Case: Rs 300
The bear case SPARC share price target of Rs 300 by 2030 applies if key pipeline programmes fail in Phase 2 or Phase 3, the PRV sale model does not repeat, and core operating cash burn continues without a commercial milestone. In this scenario, the stock trades at a modest premium to cash and infrastructure value, limiting upside to the SPARC share price target to approximately 19 percent from current levels.
Key Risks to the Sun Pharma Advanced Research Company Share Price Target
Clinical Trial Failure Risk Is the Primary Binary Risk
SPARC's share price is driven by clinical trial outcomes, not quarterly earnings. A Phase 2 or Phase 3 failure in a key oncology or dermatology molecule would be a significant negative catalyst, potentially reducing the SPARC share price target by 30 to 50 percent from current levels. This binary clinical risk is the dominant variable that investors must understand before investing.
FY26 EPS Distortion From One-Time PRV Sale
Investors treating the FY26 EPS of Rs 54.3 as a recurring base will make fundamentally incorrect assumptions about SPARC's valuation. The PRV sale was a one-time event. Core operating revenue fell 51 percent in FY26. FY27 earnings will be significantly lower than FY26 on a reported basis, which could create confusion for investors using trailing PE screens.
Long Drug Development Timeline Delays Commercialisation
Even with Sun Pharma infrastructure support, drug development timelines are long. A molecule in Phase 2 today might not reach commercial launch until 2029 or 2030, meaning the SPARC share price target 2027 and 2028 are primarily pipeline valuation milestones, not earnings-based targets. Patience is a prerequisite for this investment.
Cash Burn Without Revenue Requires Sun Pharma Support
SPARC's core operations are cash-negative without the non-recurring PRV income. The company depends on Sun Pharma's continued support and its own cash reserves from the PRV sale to fund R&D operations through to the next clinical milestone. Any reduction in Sun Pharma's commitment to fund SPARC would be a material risk to the SPARC share price target thesis.
How to Invest in Sun Pharma Advanced Research Company
Monitor SPARC's quarterly clinical trial update disclosures and any FDA designation or Phase milestone announcements as the primary indicators for the SPARC share price target thesis. Do not use trailing PE screens based on the FY26 EPS of Rs 54.3, as this figure includes a non-recurring PRV sale. To purchase shares, search NSE ticker SPARC through any SEBI-registered broker. This is a biotech-style investment suited to investors with long horizons and tolerance for binary clinical risk. Consult a SEBI-registered financial advisor before investing.
Use the Univest Screener to Track This Stock Live
Conclusion
The SPARC share price target of Rs 335 for 2027, Rs 375 for 2028, and Rs 470 for 2030 is a pipeline valuation thesis, not an earnings compounder. The FY26 headline EPS of Rs 54.3 misleads; core operations are loss-making and the PRV sale was a one-time event. The investment case rests on Sun Pharma-backed novel molecule development advancing toward commercial milestones by 2028 to 2030. The single most important indicator to track: Phase 2 and Phase 3 clinical data readouts from the SPARC pipeline, particularly in oncology and dermatology.

input.title: Fashion segment may drive margin expansion for Nykaa over medium term
input.content:
Nykaa’s Q1FY27 earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortisation (Ebitda) margin was 8.5 per cent, up 196 basis points (bps) year-on-year (Y-o-Y), and revenue was ₹2,780 crore, up 29 per cent Y-o-Y. The Ebitda was ₹240 crore, up 68 per cent Y-o-Y. The raw material-sales ratio was down 120 bps quarter-on-quarter (Q-o-Q) at 54.1 per cent, and marketing costs were 14.8 per cent of operational revenue. The Ebit margin was at 5.3 per cent. The net profit was at ₹79.8 crore, up 226 per cent Y-o-Y. The gross merchandise value (GMV) rose 34 per cent Y-o-Y to ₹5,590 crore, about 3 times the level from three years ago. Gross profit rose 33 per cent Y-o-Y to ₹1,276 crore. 
   
	There was high customer acquisition across both verticals — Nykaa (Beauty and Personal Care) and Nykaa Fashion. The beauty and personal care (BPC) and fashion AUTC (annual unique transacting customers) grew 26.1 and 38.2 per cent, respectively, Y-o-Y. The BPC revenue grew 27.4 per cent Y-o-Y to ₹2,520 crore, and fashion saw 48 per cent Y-o-Y revenue growth to ₹253 crore. 
   
	The gross margin rose 123 bps Y-o-Y to 45.9 per cent. The BPC Ebitda margin as per cent of net sales value (NSV) rose 130 bps Y-o-Y to 10.3 per cent, while fashion hit near breakeven Ebitda at 0.1 per cent margin versus minus 6.2 per cent in Q1FY26. 
   
	The customer base is around 60 million, up 33 per cent Y-o-Y. Artificial intelligence (AI) initiatives are driving better conversion as well as resolving 50 per cent of queries and aiding beauty advisory. Nykaa now has over 10,000 brands. In BPC, average order value (AOV) was up 5 per cent Y-o-Y. 
   
	The company launched a 5,000 square feet (sq ft) store in Delhi. Nykaa Now (quick commerce vertical) plans to cover over 25 cities by end-FY27. The physical network is now 324 stores in 105 cities, with more than half the stores in Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities. The retail space is up 29 per cent Y-o-Y to 330,000 sq ft, and same store sales growth is in double digits. 
   
	For Nykaa to sustain growth plus margin expansion, it will need a strategy of more premiumisation, more brand partnerships, and a scaleup of owned brands, and more physical expansion into Tier-2 and Tier-3. Ebitda margins will be driven by premiumisation and AI-led cost efficiency. Revenue growth could be over 20 per cent in the medium term and high teens through the long term. There’s room for Ebitda margins to double from current levels to around 17 per cent. 
   
	The fashion vertical reported a contribution margin of 11.4 per cent and the Ebitda margin for the fashion business was 0.1 per cent. This is where investors expect big margin improvements. The GMV grew 53 per cent Y-o-Y to ₹1,471 crore, with NSV up 54 per cent Y-o-Y to ₹451 crore, a multi-quarter high. The Ebitda-positive margin of 0.1 per cent represents 627 bps Y-o-Y improvement. This is mostly aided by a 534 bps improvement in marketing and sales & delivery efficiency, and 292 bps improvement in overhead costs. The customer acquisition cost has dipped 30 per cent over the last two financial years, with visitor-to-order conversion improving 70 bps Y-o-Y to 4 per cent. 
   
	Premiumisation in BPC is visible in improving AOV. Fashion has higher growth rates off a lower base, with GMV growth of 53 per cent Y-o-Y and NSV growth of 54 per cent Y-o-Y. This is the second consecutive quarter when fashion has achieved Ebitda breakeven. It is possible fashion could maintain 40 per cent revenue growth through the medium term with improved margins. If fashion margin picks up to an achievable 10 per cent in the medium term, it would multiply Ebitda. The return on capital employed (ROCE) at 26.8 per cent is good. Overall, net profit margins of between 3.5 per cent and 5 per cent may be achievable in FY27 and FY28. 
   
	These are high competition verticals. But Nykaa has built a moat in BPC, with 10,000 brands, 324 stores, and many brand partnerships. In fashion, it is looking at big partnerships such as with Nike, H&M Move, and Birkenstock. 
   
	The Nike direct-to-consumer (D2C) partnership (the Nike app is fully operated by Nykaa Fashion) crossed 1.5 million app installs within six months of launch, and Nike is among the top-3 brands on the Nykaa Fashion marketplace. The AI-powered "Virtual Closet" feature (launched in May 2026) has generated over 200,000 virtual avatars and delivered much higher conversion in its initial months. 
   
	The big question mark is that Nykaa has high valuations. Any minor hiccup in growth or a profitability slowdown could result in a price correction, which may provide a more comfortable entry point.

input.title: Nykaa Q1 FY27 net profit jumps 226% to Rs 80 crore; revenue rises 29% to Rs 2,782 crore
input.content:
FSN E-Commerce Ventures, the parent company of beauty retailer Nykaa, has reported a more than threefold increase in quarterly profit, supported by growth across its beauty and fashion businesses.
Consolidated net profit rose to Rs 79.76 crore in the three months ended 30 June, up 226% from Rs 24.47 crore in the same period last year. Profit increased by about 1.3% from Rs 78.75 crore in the previous quarter. The financial results are unaudited.
Its revenue from operations increased 29% year-on-year to Rs 2,782 crore, while total expenses rose 25.5% to Rs 2,662.15 crore.
Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation increased 68% to Rs 236 crore. The Ebitda margin widened to 8.5%, from 6.5% a year earlier, while consolidated gross merchandise value rose 34% to Rs 5,590 crore.
The quarter was also the company’s first full reporting period operating nike.in in India. Nykaa said the arrangement had contributed meaningfully to the expansion of its fashion business.
GMV in Nykaa’s beauty division increased 28% year-on-year to Rs 4,105 crore, while net sales value rose 29% to Rs 2,371 crore. The division includes e-commerce, physical stores, B2B distribution and the House of Nykaa Beauty portfolio.
Nykaa had 324 beauty stores across 105 cities at the end of the quarter. Its total retail area increased 29% to about 330,000 sq ft.
The company also unveiled its largest Nykaa Luxe store at Ambience Mall in Vasant Kunj, New Delhi. The outlet covers more than 5,000 sq ft and houses over 80 brands.
Nykaa Now, the company’s rapid-delivery service, has expanded to 13 cities. Nykaa said it planned to reach more than 25 cities by the end of the 2027 financial year, offering deliveries within 30 to 60 minutes from a selection of more than 1,000 brands.
The fashion division recorded a 53% increase in GMV to Rs 1,471 crore, while net sales value rose 54% to Rs 451 crore. Its Ebitda margin, calculated as a percentage of net sales value, improved to 0.1% from a negative 6.2% a year earlier.
Nykaa Fashion’s cumulative customer base grew 34% to 12 million. Women’s fashion recorded growth of 40%, while men’s and children’s categories grew 83% and 57%, respectively.
The platform added more than 130 brands during the quarter, including Birkenstock, Debenhams and H&M Move. Nykaa said its Nike partnership had crossed 1.5 million app installations within six months.
The company said its Virtual Closet AI tool had generated more than 200,000 virtual avatars since its launch in May 2026, with conversion among users twice as high.
House of Nykaa, which includes the company’s owned beauty and fashion brands, reached an annualised GMV run rate of about Rs 3,758 crore, up 39% from a year earlier. Quarterly net sales value increased 36% to Rs 550 crore, while the portfolio had reached more than 18 million customers.
Superstore by Nykaa, the company’s B2B distribution platform, reported GMV of Rs 336 crore. Its registered retailer base increased 30% to more than 523,000 across over 1,200 cities.
Falguni Nayar, Executive Chairperson, Founder and CEO of Nykaa, said, “This quarter marked continued acceleration in our growth momentum and EBITDA margins, both reaching their highest levels in the last 12 quarters. Our platform featured exciting new brand launches like Rare beauty, one of the world’s largest celebrity beauty brands, already among the top 5 premium brands at Nykaa, SK-II, a Japanese high efficacy brand, and Judydoll, among our first Chinese beauty brands which is witnessing strong early traction among consumers.”
“This also marks our first full quarter of operating nike.in in India, which has led to meaningful increase to our alreadygrowing fashion business. Our AI-led initiatives are beginning to create meaningful consumer experiences, with Virtual Closet already driving 2x higher conversion and AskNykaa, our conversational search engine, emerging as a trusted beauty advisor on the platform. We remain focused on building with discipline, innovation, and long-term value creation,” she said.

input.title: Why Did Nykaa (NSE: NYKAA) Shares Slip Despite Record Q1 Earnings and Triple-Digit Profit Growth?
input.content:
Highlights
- Nykaa (NSE: NYKAA) reported Q1 FY27 net profit growth of over 220% year-on-year.
- Revenue from operations increased 29.1% to ₹2,782.00 crore.
- Gross Merchandise Value (GMV) expanded 34% to ₹5,590.00 crore.
- Fashion business turned EBITDA positive during the quarter.
- Offline network expanded to 324 beauty stores across India.
- Shares declined over 2% despite strong earnings as investors evaluated premium valuations.
Overview
FSN E-Commerce Ventures Limited (NSE: NYKAA) operates one of India's leading beauty, personal care and fashion commerce platforms through its omnichannel ecosystem. Alongside its digital marketplace, the company has significantly expanded its offline retail presence while strengthening its portfolio through owned brands and strategic acquisitions. Despite delivering another quarter of strong financial growth, the stock witnessed profit booking during Wednesday's session.
Why Did Strong Quarterly Numbers Fail to Lift the Stock?
Nykaa delivered an impressive Q1 FY27 financial performance, with net profit rising to ₹79.80 crore, reflecting growth of around 219%-226% compared with the corresponding quarter last year. Revenue from operations also increased 29.1% year-on-year to ₹2,782.00 crore as demand remained healthy across both beauty and fashion businesses.
The company's Gross Merchandise Value (GMV) climbed 34% to ₹5,590.00 crore during the quarter. Beauty GMV crossed ₹4,105.00 crore, while the fashion business continued its rapid expansion with GMV increasing 53%. The fashion segment also achieved EBITDA-positive status, marking another operational milestone for the company.
Nykaa continued strengthening its omnichannel strategy by expanding its offline footprint to 324 beauty stores across the country. During the quarter, the company also acquired a 51% stake in Mumbai-based premium skincare brand Aminu Wellness for ₹32.00 crore, further enhancing its presence in the premium dermo-cosmetic segment.
Despite these strong operational achievements, the stock traded lower as investors appeared to book profits following the recent rally while also assessing the company's premium valuation after the earnings announcement.
How Does the Technical Setup Look?
FSN E-Commerce Ventures Limited (NSE: NYKAA) traded around ₹334.75 after opening at ₹348.00. The stock touched an intraday high of ₹348.00 before declining to a low of ₹327.70 during the session. On the daily chart, the stock continues to trade comfortably above its 50-day Simple Moving Average of ₹303.35, indicating that the broader medium-term trend remains constructive. The 14-day Relative Strength Index stood near 61.47, suggesting momentum has moderated after remaining close to overbought territory.
Key Technical Levels
Immediate support is placed near ₹327.70, followed by ₹320.00. On the upside, immediate resistance is seen around ₹348.00, with a sustained move above this level potentially opening the path toward fresh higher levels.
What Should Investors Watch Next?
Market participants are expected to monitor continued GMV growth across beauty and fashion, profitability trends, expansion of offline stores, integration of Aminu Wellness, customer acquisition costs, premium brand additions and the company's ability to maintain earnings growth while balancing valuation expectations.
Summary
FSN E-Commerce Ventures Limited (NSE: NYKAA) delivered another strong quarterly performance supported by higher profitability, robust revenue growth, expanding GMV and improving operational efficiency. Although the stock witnessed some profit booking after the results, investors are likely to focus on execution across its omnichannel strategy, premium brand expansion and sustained earnings growth in the coming quarters.

Mumbai, August 5: Shares of FSN E-Commerce Ventures, the parent company of beauty and fashion retailer Nykaa, fell as much as 4% on Wednesday even as the company reported a strong set of June-quarter earnings and received positive commentary from several brokerages. Analysts maintained that the company’s improving profitability, robust growth in its beauty business and standout quarter by the fashion segment support its long-term outlook.
The company reported a sharp rise in quarterly profit and revenue, prompting brokerages to retain their positive stance on the stock. Several analysts also raised their target prices, citing healthy execution across business segments.
Strong Earnings Drive Optimism
Nykaa reported a consolidated net profit of ₹79.7 crore for the quarter ended June, compared with ₹24.4 crore in the year-ago period. Revenue increased 29% year-on-year to ₹2,782 crore, reflecting healthy demand.
Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) margins improved, aided by higher operating efficiency.
Stock slid after report card and bullish commentary by brokers. Source: NSE
The beauty segment benefited from premiumisation trends, new customer additions and strong demand across skincare, cosmetics and personal care categories. Meanwhile, the fashion business delivered a strong performance, indicating that investments in customer acquisition, assortment expansion and supply-chain improvements are beginning to pay off.
Despite the robust performance, the stock traded lower.
Brokerages Raise Target Prices
The earnings prompted several brokerages to reaffirm their confidence in Nykaa’s long-term growth prospects.
Brokers maintained “Buy” rating and raised target price, citing sustained momentum in the beauty business, improving profitability and an encouraging quarter in fashion. The brokerages expect continued margin expansion as the company scales its operations.
Analysts highlighted Nykaa’s leadership in India’s organised online beauty market and its ability to consistently deliver profitable growth.
They pointed to stronger earnings visibility, disciplined execution and improving returns.
Collectively, the brokerage commentary suggests that the recent weakness in the stock is being viewed as a near-term correction rather than a reflection of deteriorating fundamentals.
Beauty Business
Nykaa’s beauty business during the June quarter was supported by rising consumer spending on premium beauty products.
The company also continued to expand its portfolio of owned brands and increase partnerships, helping improve customer engagement and repeat purchases.
The fashion segment posted standout quarter.
Analysts said sustained growth in both businesses is likely to support margin expansion over the coming quarters.
Acquisition Strengthens Skincare Portfolio
Nykaa has also announced the acquisition of a 51% stake in Aminu Wellness, a move aimed at strengthening its presence in the premium skincare segment.
The acquisition aligns with the company’s broader strategy of expanding its portfolio of high-growth beauty and wellness brands while deepening its presence in premium product categories.
Brokerages believe the deal complements Nykaa’s existing beauty ecosystem and could provide additional growth opportunities as demand for specialised skincare and wellness products continues to rise in India.
What Investors Will Watch
Going forward, investors will closely monitor Nykaa’s ability to sustain revenue growth while further improving profitability. Margin expansion, brand integration and execution across premium categories will remain key factors influencing the stock.
Market participants will also watch consumer demand trends amid evolving macroeconomic conditions and whether discretionary spending remains resilient.
Despite Wednesday’s decline, analysts broadly remain optimistic that Nykaa’s leadership in India’s online beauty market, improving financial performance and diversified growth strategy position the company well for sustained long-term growth.

input.title: Nykaa to acquire 51% stake in premium skincare brand Aminu for up to Rs 32 crore
input.content:
FSN E-Commerce Ventures, which operates beauty and fashion retailer Nykaa, has approved the purchase of a 51% stake in skincare brand Aminu for up to Rs 32 crore in cash.
The stake will be acquired on a fully diluted basis, with the transaction expected to be completed by 15 September 2026.
Nykaa said it planned to buy the remaining shares over the next few years under terms agreed with Aminu’s owners. The brand’s co-founders, Prachi Bhandari and Aman Mohunta, will continue to run the business after the deal.
Aminu, which was founded in 2019, sells products including serums, cleansers, sunscreens, moisturisers, masks and body-care treatments. It also provides skincare consultations and products for professional use in salons and clinics.
The bootstrapped company reported turnover of Rs 19.44 crore in the financial year ending March 2026, up 50% from Rs 12.96 crore the previous year. Nykaa said the business was profitable.
Nykaa described Aminu as a research-led brand with an in-house product development operation. According to the company, it has created more than 30 formulations using over 150 ingredients sourced from more than 10 countries.
Its range includes a copper peptide serum and the Rejuvenate Eye Serum, which Nykaa said was among the bestselling eye serums on its platform.
Aminu also supplies professional skincare products and treatments to businesses including Bodycraft, Jean Claude Biguine, Truefitt & Hill and Kaya Clinic. Nykaa said it had trained thousands of therapists and beauty professionals.
The acquisition will add Aminu to House of Nykaa, the retailer’s portfolio of owned beauty brands, and increase its presence in the higher-priced skincare market.
Adwaita Nayar, co-founder and executive director of Nykaa and CEO of House of Nykaa, said “At Nykaa, we are building the House of Nykaa, a portfolio of distinctive brands that are redefining beauty for the Indian consumer. Aminu is a natural addition to that vision. Its premium positioning, loyal following, and genuine R&D depth make it more than an acquisition - it's a capability addition to our ecosystem. We're thrilled to partner with Prachi and Aman, two founders who've built something truly exceptional, and to take Aminu to its next chapter together.”
Bhandari and Mohunta, Co-founders of Aminu, said “We built Aminu as a research flywheel, where years of working directly with skin, global scientific partnerships and continuous learning from consumers and professionals shape every formula. Nykaa's scale, consumer understanding and omnichannel capabilities complement Aminu's strengths.”
“This partnership creates a powerful platform to accelerate growth, strengthen our innovation pipeline and build a category-defining premium skincare business for the Indian consumer and beyond,” they said.

input.content:
FSN E-Commerce Ventures Nykaa shares experienced a notable decline in early trade, falling 2.39% to Rs 334.30 on Wednesday. The stock, which is a constituent of the Nifty Midcap 150 index, was trading at this level at 09:24 am.
FSN E-Commerce Ventures Nykaa has demonstrated consistent revenue growth on a consolidated quarterly basis. For the quarter-ending June 2025, revenue stood at Rs 2,154.94 Crore, increasing to Rs 2,345.98 Crore in September 2025, and further to Rs 2,873.26 Crore in December 2025. By June 2026, the company's revenue had reached Rs 2,782.00 Crore. Net Profit also showed a positive trend, rising from Rs 24.47 Crore in June 2025 to Rs 79.76 Crore in June 2026. Earnings Per Share (EPS) followed a similar trajectory, growing from Rs 0.08 in June 2025 to Rs 0.28 in June 2026.
On an annual consolidated basis, the company has seen strong growth in both revenue and net profit. Revenue increased from Rs 3,773.94 Crore in 2022 to Rs 10,022.35 Crore in 2026. Over the same period, net profit surged from Rs 41.29 Crore to Rs 203.94 Crore. EPS also witnessed significant growth, from Rs 0.88 in 2022 to Rs 0.70 in 2026. The company's Return on Equity (ROE) improved significantly from 3.06% in 2022 to 13.87% in 2026, indicating better profitability for shareholders.
Analyzing the standalone annual income statement, Sales saw a notable increase from Rs 187 Crore in March 2022 to Rs 356 Crore in March 2026. Net Profit showed some fluctuations but ended higher at Rs 87 Crore in March 2026 compared to Rs 103 Crore in March 2022, after a dip in intermediate years.
Quarterly, standalone sales fluctuated, with June 2026 sales at Rs 75 Crore. Net profit for June 2026 was Rs 9 Crore.
The company's standalone cash flow from operating activities remained positive in March 2026 at Rs 63 Crore, despite a negative figure in March 2024. Investing activities consistently showed outflows, reflecting ongoing capital expenditures. Net cash flow for March 2026 was 0 Crore.
The standalone balance sheet shows a consistent increase in Share Capital from Rs 47 Crore in March 2022 to Rs 286 Crore in March 2026. Total Assets also grew from Rs 1,690 Crore to Rs 2,162 Crore over the same period, indicating expansion. Reserves & Surplus show significant growth from Rs 1,502 Crore in March 2022 to Rs 1,516 Crore in March 2026.
Key ratios indicate the company's financial health and valuation. Basic EPS for March 2026 was Rs 0.31. The P/E ratio for March 2026 stood at 758.06x, and the P/B ratio was 37.36x. The Debt to Equity ratio was 0.10x in March 2026, showcasing a relatively low leverage position. Gross Profit Margin for March 2026 was 40.26% and Net Profit Margin was 24.64%.
FSN E-Commerce Ventures Nykaa has been active with corporate announcements. On August 4, 2026, the company issued a press release titled "Nykaa begins FY2027 on a strong note with Q1 FY2027 Net Revenue growth accelerating to 29% YoY and robust PAT Growth of 226% YoY", along with an announcement of acquiring a majority stake (51% on a fully diluted basis) in Aminu Wellness Pvt Ltd. This indicates strategic moves to strengthen its premium skincare portfolio. Additionally, the unaudited standalone and consolidated financial results for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, were also announced on the same day.
The company also issued a bonus issue with a ratio of 5:1 on October 3, 2022, with the record date on November 11, 2022, and the ex-bonus date on November 10, 2022.
Despite a very bullish sentiment noted by Moneycontrol analysis, the stock's current price movement suggests a cautious market reaction at this time.

input.title: Nuvama prefers liquor stocks over cigarettes; bullish on Marico, Nykaa and Nestle
input.content:
3 Min Read
Investors looking at India's consumer sector may find better opportunities in liquor companies than cigarette makers, according to Abneesh Roy, Executive Director at Nuvama Institutional Equities. Roy said his highest-conviction idea is the alcoholic beverages space, driven by the possibility of major reforms in Tamil Nadu, where state-run liquor retailer Tamil Nadu State Marketing Corporation Limited (TASMAC) could be privatised.
"We like the alcobev space because Tamil Nadu clearly big reforms are likely. TASMAC is likely to get privatised, and it's a very big market," Roy said.
Among listed companies, he prefers United Spirits, Radico Khaitan and Allied Blenders and Distillers. He added that United Spirits offers additional valuation comfort because investors could benefit from a potential 10% dividend yield linked to the Indian Premier League (IPL) team sale.
On the other hand, while he believes the worst is over for cigarette companies, he expects another weak quarter. "Even in Q2, there will be a decline in terms of volumes and profit," he said, adding that he would prefer alcohol stocks over cigarette makers in the near term.
Away from sector calls, Roy remains positive on Marico after the fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) company's strong April-June quarter of 2026 (Q1FY27) performance. He noted that earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) grew 25%, the highest in seven years, while India volumes remained in double digits. Although he does not expect Parachute's 10% volume growth to become the norm, he believes high single-digit growth is sustainable. Other businesses, including Safola Foods, premium personal care and digital brands, also continue to perform well.
Roy acknowledged that Marico's valuation looks expensive after the stock's strong run but said quality companies often command premium valuations. "Marico will be one of those," he said, grouping it with companies such as Pidilite Industries, Nestle India, Asian Paints and Radico that have consistently delivered superior growth.
Roy is also optimistic on FSN E-Commerce Ventures (Nykaa), saying the company's fashion business was the biggest positive surprise in the quarter. Fashion EBITDA jumped 68%, while fashion net sales value (NSV) grew 53%, complementing continued strength in the beauty business, which expanded 29%. Nuvama has slightly raised its earnings estimates, maintains a Buy rating and has a target price of ₹414. Roy said Nykaa should be valued using a sum-of-the-parts approach because it operates both high-growth and mature businesses.

Away from sector calls, Roy remains positive on Marico after the fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) company's strong April-June quarter of 2026 (Q1FY27) performance. He noted that earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) grew 25%, the highest in seven years, while India volumes remained in double digits. Although he does not expect Parachute's 10% volume growth to become the norm, he believes high single-digit growth is sustainable. Other businesses, including Safola Foods, premium personal care and digital brands, also continue to perform well.
Roy acknowledged that Marico's valuation looks expensive after the stock's strong run but said quality companies often command premium valuations. "Marico will be one of those," he said, grouping it with companies such as Pidilite Industries, Nestle India, Asian Paints and Radico that have consistently delivered superior growth.
Roy is also optimistic on FSN E-Commerce Ventures (Nykaa), saying the company's fashion business was the biggest positive surprise in the quarter. Fashion EBITDA jumped 68%, while fashion net sales value (NSV) grew 53%, complementing continued strength in the beauty business, which expanded 29%. Nuvama has slightly raised its earnings estimates, maintains a Buy rating and has a target price of ₹414. Roy said Nykaa should be valued using a sum-of-the-parts approach because it operates both high-growth and mature businesses.
On Nestle India, Roy believes investors overreacted to management's comments at the company's analyst meeting. The stock corrected after management shared category growth expectations, but he sees little reason for concern.

"I think nothing to worry. I think these are healthy corrections which keep happening in expensive stocks," Roy said.
He expects Nestle to deliver around 20% revenue growth in the July-September quarter of 2026 (Q2FY27) before growth normalises to 10-12% from the October-December quarter of 2026 (Q3FY27). He also pointed to long-term opportunities in chocolates, prepared dishes and pet food, saying the recent decline should be viewed as a buying opportunity rather than a negative turning point for the company.

input.title: Nykaa turns creator culture into a content-to-commerce engine
input.content:
New Delhi: Nykaa placed creators and social content at the centre of its demand engine, with its network of more than 170,000 creators generating over 2.3 million content pieces annually.
FSN E-Commerce Ventures disclosed the numbers in its Q1 FY27 investor presentation filed with the BSE on August 4, 2026.
The scale pointed to a strategy that went beyond hiring influencers for isolated campaigns. Nykaa linked affiliate creators, social media content, product education, and shopping within a connected content-to-commerce ecosystem.
From influencer posts to in-app shopping
Nykaa brought creator content closer to transactions by embedding tutorials and influencer-recommended stores inside its shopping app.
Its content platform, Nykaa Play, surpassed 300,000 subscribers, combining beauty education, live content, and product discovery with shopping.
The model gave creators a role across the consumer journey, from introducing a product and explaining its use to directing consumers towards a purchase.
Nykaa also operated an affiliate programme through which creators could produce and distribute product-linked content.
A 19-million-strong social community
The company reported a social media community of more than 19 million followers across platforms.
Nykaa said it used differentiated content formats and collaborations to drive engagement, placing its social community alongside its customer base, brand assortment and physical distribution network.
The company’s presentation treated this ecosystem as a “social engine” within its wider demand, assortment and distribution flywheel.
This suggested that Nykaa viewed creator content as an always-on distribution channel, rather than only as campaign inventory.
Nykaa’s marketing and sales distribution expenditure stood at Rs 412 crore in Q1 FY27, up 26% year-on-year. However, the filing did not separately disclose the amount spent on creators or influencer marketing.
Creator culture moves beyond feeds
Nykaa extended creator and community engagement beyond social platforms through more than 20 immersive consumer events during the quarter.
The events included the Nykaa and L’Oréal Paris Cannes takeover, Beauty Bars, makeup masterclasses, experiential pop-ups, the Rare Beauty launch and new House of Nykaa brand events.
This gave the platform a mix of digital reach, creator-led recommendations and physical experiences around beauty culture.
The presentation cited that three in four Indian consumers relied on influencer recommendations for discovery and decisions. It also stated that creator content accounted for 76% of content consumption.
Content sits on top of a growing audience
Nykaa’s creator ecosystem operated alongside a consumer base of 60 million, which grew 33% year-on-year.
Its Pink Summer Sale attracted more than 35 million unique visitors and recorded over 100 million visits. The Nykaa Birthday Sale drew more than 20 million unique visitors and reported around 40% year-on-year GMV growth.
While Nykaa did not directly attribute these numbers to creator activity, they showed the size of the audience available to its content, social, and commerce ecosystem.

input.title: Nykaa Shares Slip Despite Strong Q1; Brokerages See Up To 40% Upside
input.content:
- Nykaa Q1 revenue and profit surged, driven by strong beauty and fashion growth.
- Nykaa expanded margins as owned brands and operating leverage boosted profitability.
- Brokerages retained bullish ratings, seeing up to 40% upside in Nykaa shares.
Shares of FSN E-Commerce Ventures, the parent of Nykaa, fell nearly 3% on Wednesday despite the beauty and fashion retailer reporting a strong June-quarter performance, with higher revenue, expanding margins and a more than three-fold jump in net profit.
The stock declined as much as 3% even after the company posted revenue growth of 29.1% year-on-year to ₹2,782 crore. EBITDA rose 67.8% to ₹236 crore, while EBITDA margin expanded to 8.5% from 6.5% a year ago.
Net profit more than tripled to ₹80 crore from ₹24.5 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
Nykaa's portfolio of 13 owned consumer brands continued to outperform, delivering 43% year-on-year growth. Beauty GMV increased 28% to ₹4,105 crore, while the fashion business maintained healthy momentum. During the quarter, the company added 11 stores, taking its offline network to 324 stores across more than 100 cities.
Nykaa also acquired a 51% stake in premium beauty and skincare brand Aminu Wellness for ₹32 crore. The brand reported FY26 revenue of ₹19.4 crore.
Advertisement
Growth Across Beauty And Fashion Impresses Brokerages
Brokerages remained positive on Nykaa's outlook, citing broad-based growth across beauty and fashion, improving profitability and continued operating leverage.
HSBC maintained its Buy rating with a target price of ₹380, while raising its FY27 EBITDA estimates by 3% after the earnings beat. The brokerage highlighted robust GMV growth, strong execution in the beauty business, scaling of the owned brands portfolio and sustained operating leverage.
CLSA reiterated its Outperform rating with a target price of ₹376, saying both revenue and EBITDA exceeded expectations. It noted that stronger brand partnerships accelerated fashion growth, while higher-margin owned brands continued to support profitability in the beauty segment.
Advertisement
Brokerages See Up To 40% Upside
Nomura retained its Buy rating and assigned the Street-high target price of ₹411, expressing confidence in Nykaa's long-term growth prospects. The brokerage expects premiumisation, expanding brand partnerships, continued growth in owned brands and deeper expansion into Tier-II and Tier-III cities to drive both revenue growth and margin expansion.
Jefferies also reiterated its Buy rating with a target price of ₹400, describing the June quarter as a strong beat across key operating metrics. It said healthy beauty user growth, premiumisation, more than 50% growth in the fashion business, the scaling up of Nykaa's house of brands and the increasing reach of its quick-commerce offering continue to strengthen the company's long-term growth outlook.

Brokerages bullish

It expects Nykaa to sustain strong growth momentum, supported by premiumisation, increasing brand partnerships, expansion of own brands and physical expansion in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities.
Jefferies also maintained a buy rating with a target price of ₹400.
The brokerage said the company delivered a strong beat across metrics, with robust revenue growth, multi-quarter high margins and a sharp rise in profits.
It said the beauty business benefited from continued user growth, premiumisation and higher average order values, while the fashion business recorded more than 50 per cent growth with EBITDA break-even.
Jefferies added that the house of brands business continues to scale and quick delivery is expanding its reach, with valuation supported by strong growth and margin expansion.
HSBC maintained a buy rating with a target price of ₹380. The brokerage said robust GMV performance continued, with beauty and personal care GMV rising 28 per cent and fashion GMV increasing 53 per cent, while the house of brands business continued to scale.

input.title: Nykaa steps up adex by 26% amid creator-led marketing push
input.content:
New Delhi: FSN E-Commerce Ventures, which operates beauty and fashion retailer Nykaa, increased its advertising and marketing outlay by 26% year-on-year to Rs 412 crore in the first quarter of FY27.
The expenditure stood at Rs 328 crore in the corresponding quarter of FY26 and Rs 380 crore in the March quarter of FY26, marking an 8% sequential rise, according to the company’s investor presentation filed with the BSE on August 4, 2026.
Despite the increase in absolute expenditure, marketing and S&D costs declined to 14.8% of revenue from operations, compared with 15.2% in Q1 FY26. The ratio, however, increased from 14.4% in Q4 FY26.
The company attributed the improvement in year-on-year cost efficiency to performance marketing efficiencies across its Beauty and Fashion platforms and improved business development executive productivity.
Nykaa’s contribution profit increased 37% to Rs 589 crore from Rs 430 crore in the year-ago quarter. Its contribution margin expanded to 21.3% from 19.9%.
Creator network and events support marketing push
Nykaa’s marketing ecosystem included more than 170,000 creators, 2.3 million content pieces generated annually and a social media community of over 19 million followers.
The company conducted more than 20 consumer events during the quarter, including the Nykaa and L’Oréal Paris Cannes takeover, Beauty Bars, makeup masterclasses, experiential pop-ups and the Rare Beauty launch event.
The Pink Summer Sale attracted more than 35 million unique visitors and recorded over 100 million visits. The Nykaa Birthday Sale registered around 40% year-on-year GMV growth and attracted more than 20 million unique visitors.
Consolidated EBITDA rises 68%
On a consolidated basis, Nykaa’s revenue from operations rose 29% year-on-year to Rs 2,782 crore from s 2,155 crore. Revenue increased 5% sequentially from Rs 2,648 crore in Q4 FY26.
Consolidated EBITDA increased 68% to Rs 236 crore from Rs 141 crore in Q1 FY26. It rose 3% from Rs 223 crore in the preceding quarter.
The EBITDA margin expanded to 8.5% from 6.5% in the year-ago period and 8.4% in Q4 FY26.
Consolidated profit after tax increased 226% year-on-year to Rs 80 crore from Rs 24 crore. PAT stood at Rs 79 crore in the preceding quarter. The PAT margin increased to 2.9% from 1.1% in Q1 FY26, but remained below the 3% reported in Q4 FY26.
Standalone revenue and profit decline
On a standalone basis, FSN E-Commerce Ventures reported revenue from operations of Rs 75.42 crore in Q1 FY27, compared with Rs 81.83 crore in Q1 FY26 and Rs 102.03 crore in Q4 FY26.
Standalone total income stood at Rs 127.69 crore, against Rs 121.93 crore in the corresponding quarter and Rs 163.16 crore in the preceding quarter.
Profit before tax declined to Rs 12.78 crore from Rs 17.44 crore in Q1 FY26 and Rs 49.74 crore in Q4 FY26.
Standalone profit after tax stood at Rs 9.57 crore, compared with Rs 12.92 crore in the year-ago quarter and Rs 41.04 crore in the March quarter.

input.title: Nykaa acquires majority stake in Aminu to strengthen premium skincare play
input.content:
Nykaa has announced the acquisition of a 51% stake in direct-to-consumer skincare brand Aminu for a cash consideration of up to ₹32 crore, as it strengthens its presence in the premium skincare segment. The transaction is expected to be completed by September 15, with the company planning to acquire the remaining 49% stake over the next few years.
Founded in 2019 by Prachi Bhandari and Aman Mohunta, Aminu offers a range of skincare and body care products including serums, cleansers, sunscreens, moisturisers and masks. The founders will continue to lead the business, while Nykaa will support its next phase of growth.
The acquisition adds a premium skincare brand to Nykaa's House of Brands portfolio. According to the company, Aminu's products are positioned at a higher price point than its existing skincare offerings, helping address a gap in its premium beauty portfolio. Nykaa also highlighted Aminu's research and development capabilities, with more than 30 proprietary formulations, as an important strategic advantage.
Aminu follows an omnichannel distribution model, selling through its own website, marketplaces including Nykaa, Amazon, Clinikally and Zepto, while also being available at over 180 salons across India.
The bootstrapped brand reported revenue of ₹19.4 crore in FY26, registering around 50% year-on-year growth from approximately ₹13 crore in FY25.
The acquisition is part of Nykaa's broader strategy to expand its portfolio of owned beauty brands across different categories and price segments. The company currently has seven beauty and personal care brands and five fashion brands under its House of Brands portfolio, and has previously acquired stakes in brands such as Dot & Key and Earth Rhythm. Nykaa has also identified premium fragrances, derma-led skincare, mid-premium nutraceuticals and professional makeup products as key growth areas for future expansion.

Overall, Nomura raised its FY28 revenue estimates for Nykaa, while EBITDA margin expectations remained largely unchanged.
Nuvama on Nykaa share price
Nuvama Institutional Equities said Nykaa’s strong show continues, as the brokerage maintained its ‘Buy’ call and increased its target price to Rs 414 apiece from Rs 351 apiece. The latest target price implies 21% upside potential.
The brokerage raised Nykaa’s revenue and EBITDA estimates for FY27 and FY28. “BPC business was steady, while the Fashion business delivered a standout quarter owing to strong customer growth. Profitability improved further in BPC while fashion business managed to breakeven,” it noted.
Motilal Oswal Financial Services
Motilal Oswal on Nykaa share price also raised its target price to Rs 370 apiece, while maintaining its ‘Neutral’ call. The domestic brokerage said that the premiumization in beauty is playing out more intensely, visible in improving AOVs.
Nykaa is on track to deliver around 5x consolidated EBITDA by FY30, led by fashion segment’s EBITDA margin, which is likely to improve to 10.1% from 0% currently, as well as BPC margin, which is on an improving trajectory, Motilal Oswal said, adding that improving ROCE and disciplined working capital continue to reflect financial discipline.
“We continue to view Nykaa's deep moat in Beauty and Personal Care as difficult to displace, supported by 10,000+ brands, 324 stores across 105 cities, strong owned brands, and deep brand partnerships. At the same time, we view the company as building an assortment-intelligence-led Fashion vertical, with marquee partnerships such as Nike, H&M Move, and Birkenstock strengthening its long-term positioning,” it added.
Nykaa share price
Nykaa announced its results in the post-market hours of Tuesday. Earlier during the day, the stock closed nearly 1% lower at Rs 342.50 apiece on NSE. The shares of the e-commerce platform have gained 5% in a week and 10% in a month, and are overall up 29% in 2026 so far.
In the longer term, Nykaa shares have delivered 62% returns over a year and 132% over three years. The company currently has a market capitalisation of more than Rs 98,088 crore.
