This partnership provides a solid foundation for expanding the brand’s reach and supporting its long-term development in India.”
The launch comes as international fashion brands continue to gain traction in India, with consumers increasingly seeking premium apparel, global fashion trends, and international labels through online retail channels. Myntra currently offers a portfolio of more than 500 international brands on its platform.
Global SS Beauty Brands Limited (GSSBB), a subsidiary of Shoppers Stop Limited, has entered into an exclusive strategic partnership with INTERPARFUMS SA to distribute, develop, and grow its portfolio of prestige fragrance brands in India. The partnership marks a significant move in India's luxury beauty and fragrance market, with GSSBB taking responsibility for the distribution, market development, and brand-building of INTERPARFUMS SA’s fragrance portfolio across the country.
Founded in 1982, INTERPARFUMS SA designs, manufactures, and distributes prestige fragrances and fragrance-related products through licensing and other agreements with international brand owners. The company operates in more than 120 countries and manages fragrance brands including Coach, Montblanc, Jimmy Choo, Lacoste, Rochas, Lanvin, Karl Lagerfeld, and Van Cleef & Arpels.
The collaboration aims to strengthen the presence of global luxury fragrance brands in India, a market witnessing growing demand for premium beauty and personal care products. By combining INTERPARFUMS SA’s international fragrance portfolio with GSSBB’s retail expertise, market insights, and consumer reach, the companies plan to expand their footprint in the Indian luxury fragrance segment.
Philippe Benacin, Co-founder and CEO, INTERPARFUMS SA, said, “India is one of the most promising luxury fragrance markets globally, driven by a young, aspirational consumer base and a growing appreciation for prestigious international brands. At INTERPARFUMS our portfolio is built on decades of craftsmanship, innovation, and enduring brand equity. We are delighted to introduce our brands to Indian consumers with a partner that possesses deep market expertise and a strong understanding of the luxury beauty landscape. Global SS Beauty Brands brings the retail excellence and strategic insight needed to build our brands with purpose, and we look forward to a long-term, successful partnership.”
Biju Kassim, MD and CEO, Global SS Beauty Brands Ltd said, " Our partnership with INTERPARFUMS SA marks another important milestone in our journey to strengthen the luxury fragrance category in India. As consumer demand for globally renowned prestige brands continues to grow, our focus is on building these brands for the long term through thoughtful market development, meaningful consumer engagement, and exceptional retail experiences. INTERPARFUMS' portfolio represents some of the world's most iconic fragrance brands, and we are excited to partner with them to unlock their full potential in India while further reinforcing Global SS Beauty Brands as the partner of choice for leading global beauty brands.”
The agreement is expected to support the expansion of premium fragrance brands in India while strengthening GSSBB’s position in the luxury beauty retail and prestige fragrance categories.
Bhumika Realty, the real estate arm of Bhumika Group, has announced the signing of Lifestyle for a 24,000 sq. ft. anchor store at The Icon, Faridabad, further strengthening the retail mix at its flagship mixed-use development. The new store will span the ground and first floors of the project and is expected to bring one of India’s leading fashion and lifestyle retail destinations to consumers in the city.
Lifestyle, part of the Dubai-based Landmark Group, operates more than 170 stores across eight countries and has established a strong presence in the fashion and lifestyle retail segment. In India, the retailer has a network of over 77 stores across 44 cities, offering customers access to more than 300 international brands across categories including fashion, footwear, beauty, and accessories.
The addition of Lifestyle is expected to enhance the retail offering at The Icon, which is being developed as an integrated destination combining retail, entertainment, hospitality, and residential components.
Uddhav Poddar, CMD, Bhumika Group said, “Faridabad is evolving into an important consumption and retail market within the NCR, with consumers increasingly looking for leading brands and quality experiences closer to home. Bringing Lifestyle to The Icon is an important addition to our retail mix and reinforces our vision of creating a destination that combines leading retail, entertainment and hospitality. Along with PVR INOX, Lifestyle further strengthens the brand ecosystem we are building at The Icon.”
The announcement follows the recent addition of a 25,000 sq. ft. PVR INOX multiplex at the project, strengthening its entertainment component and supporting Bhumika Realty’s strategy of creating a comprehensive lifestyle destination in Faridabad.
The Icon has been designed by Bentel Associates, South Africa. The project is planned as a mixed-use development integrating premium retail spaces, entertainment options, hospitality offerings, and residential units within a single destination.
Pet care platform WAGR is broadening its offerings beyond pet products by bringing together shopping, AI-powered guidance, service discovery, and personalized pet information into a single ecosystem. The move comes as pet ownership in India continues to grow, with consumers increasingly seeking integrated solutions for nutrition, grooming, training, wellness, and healthcare needs.
The company aims to address challenges faced by pet parents who often rely on multiple platforms and service providers to manage different aspects of pet care. By combining products, guidance, and services in one place, WAGR is positioning itself as a comprehensive platform for pet owners.
WAGR currently offers products from established pet care brands including Royal Canin, Pedigree, Whiskas, Sheba, Drools, and Temptations, alongside emerging brands such as Bruni Boi, Cuddl, Cure By Design, Halalicious, Moe Puppy, and Let’s Wag. Its portfolio spans categories including pet food, treats, grooming products, wellness solutions, toys, accessories, and daily essentials for dogs and cats.
The company said its strategy is centered on supporting pet parents throughout their journey rather than focusing solely on product purchases.
Fredun Medhora, Director, WAGR said, “We don’t want WAGR to be another place where pet parents shop; we want it to become a companion they turn to. The opportunity is to bring together products, answers, trusted services and technology around the everyday reality of pet parenting. We are building for that future, even if it means taking bets the category has not taken before.”
As part of this approach, WAGR has introduced TOTO, an AI-powered pet-parenting companion designed to help users navigate everyday concerns related to feeding, nutrition, activity, grooming, behavior, and general pet care. The tool is intended to provide guidance and information, particularly for first-time pet owners, while helping them make more informed decisions. The company clarified that TOTO is not intended to provide veterinary diagnosis, treatment, or replace professional medical advice.
WAGR has also expanded its platform through its Discover feature, which connects pet parents with service providers such as groomers, trainers, walkers, boarding facilities, veterinary clinics, and other pet-care professionals. The initiative is aimed at simplifying the process of finding trusted service providers, a challenge often faced by new pet owners.
In addition, the platform’s Pet Profile feature allows users to maintain important pet information, health records, and other details in one place. According to the company, integrating pet profiles with shopping, guidance, and service discovery enables a more personalized experience for users.
L Catterton has acquired a minority stake in Bengaluru-based restaurant company Nandhana Foods, which operates the Nandhana Palace and RNR brands.
According to media reports, the investment is estimated at around USD 30 million, although the exact deal value and stake size have not been officially disclosed.
Nandhana Foods has built its business around Andhra and Karnataka cuisine and has a presence across Bengaluru and Chennai. The company operates more than 30 locations and was developed under the leadership of Dr. Ravichandar and his daughters Shweta, Ramya and Ravina.
The investment comes as regional restaurant chains continue to attract investor interest amid the expansion of India’s organised food services market. L Catterton said the partnership will support the company’s next phase of growth, with a focus on strengthening operations and expanding into existing and new markets.
“South Indian cuisine is one of the largest segments of India’s burgeoning food services market,” L Catterton said.
The investment firm said the segment is being supported by increasing per-capita spending on dining out and food delivery, along with a rise in consumption occasions. L Catterton also sees scope for Nandhana to expand its presence across South India and enter additional markets.
“We are thrilled to announce the partnership of L Catterton with Nandhana Palace, a legendary culinary institution that has been delighting food lovers across South India for over three decades,” said Sanjiv Mehta, Executive Chairman India, L Catterton, in a LinkedIn post.
The partnership is expected to focus on professionalising the business while retaining its established heritage and values. L Catterton also plans to work with the founding family on scaling operations and expanding the restaurant network.
The transaction adds to the growing investor activity in India’s foodservice sector, particularly around established regional brands with multi-city operations. For Nandhana, the partnership comes at a time when restaurant operators are looking to increase their footprint while building more structured business and operational systems.
Jewellery retailer BlueStone has appointed Amit Jain, Co-founder and Chief Executive Officer of CarDekho Group, as a Non-Executive Non-Independent Director, effective September 14, 2026.
The appointment was approved during the company’s 15th Annual General Meeting. Jain succeeds Sameer Dileep Nath, who retired by rotation and did not seek reappointment to the board.
Founded in 2011, BlueStone operates as an omnichannel jewellery retailer, combining its online platform with a growing network of physical stores across India. The company offers a wide range of jewellery products and has continued to strengthen its presence in the organised jewellery retail market.
BlueStone describes itself as India’s second-largest digital-first omnichannel jewellery brand. During the first quarter of FY27, the company expanded its retail footprint by opening 12 new stores, taking its total store count to 352 outlets across 139 cities. The brand currently serves customers across more than 12,660 PIN codes, with nearly half of its stores located in Tier II and Tier III cities.
The company also reported strong financial performance during the quarter. In Q1 FY27, BlueStone recorded Rs 737 crore in operating revenue, reflecting a 49 percent year-on-year growth. The jewellery retailer posted a net profit of Rs 6 crore, compared to a net loss of Rs 35 crore during the corresponding period last year, marking a return to profitability.
BlueStone's improving financial performance comes amid continued expansion in India's organised jewellery sector, where it competes with major players including CaratLane, Tanishq, Kalyan Jewellers, Senco Gold, PC Jeweller, and Thangamayil Jewellery.
With Amit Jain joining its board, BlueStone aims to strengthen its leadership team as it continues to scale its omnichannel jewellery business and expand its retail presence across the country.
Samsung India expects its digital appliances business to deliver double-digit year-on-year growth in the second half of 2026, supported by festive season demand and increasing consumer preference for premium home appliances, according to a senior company executive.
Ghufran Alam, Vice President, Digital Appliances Business, Samsung India, said the company has witnessed encouraging sales trends beginning with the Onam season and expects the momentum to continue through upcoming festivals, including Dussehra and Diwali.
The company remains optimistic about consumer spending despite inflationary concerns and global economic uncertainties.
Commenting on market demand, Alam said, "Independence Day sales, which were before the Onam period (August 26), we have seen robust demand. So, Diwali also, and coming festivals also, we see good growth prospects for the appliances business in India."
The Onam season, which traditionally marks the start of India's festive shopping period, delivered strong results for the home appliances sector. Samsung reported high double-digit growth during the period, reflecting sustained consumer interest across product categories.
On pricing, Samsung said it is closely monitoring commodity costs, including copper prices, but has not made any decision regarding price increases ahead of the festive season.
"Whether we are going to increase the price in Diwali or before the festival, we do not have any kind of, at this moment, we do not know currently, because it is all very dynamic," Alam noted.
The company also highlighted the growing trend of premiumisation within India's consumer electronics and home appliances market. Samsung said average selling prices are increasing at a faster pace than overall volumes, indicating stronger demand for premium products across both urban and rural markets. Flexible financing options such as no-cost EMI schemes are also encouraging consumers to upgrade to higher-value products.
Among key categories, room air conditioners (RACs) are expected to remain Samsung's fastest-growing segment during the second half of the year, followed by washing machines and refrigerators. The company attributed this growth to sustained cooling demand in southern India and increased festive purchases.
Within the refrigerator category, Samsung is witnessing stronger demand for French-door and side-by-side refrigerators, particularly models with capacities exceeding 450 litres. In washing machines, consumers are increasingly opting for larger-capacity products ranging between 10 kg and 14 kg across both front-load and top-load segments.
Ahead of the festive season, Samsung has expanded its premium appliance portfolio with the introduction of new air conditioner models, including a cassette AC and a room AC. The company has also upgraded the artificial intelligence capabilities of its Family Hub refrigerators through Gemini integration, enhancing food recognition features beyond the previously supported range.
Amazon has launched Alexa+ in India, introducing a new generative AI-powered version of its voice assistant designed to offer more natural conversations, personalized experiences, and deeper integration with smart home devices, shopping services, entertainment platforms, and daily utility applications. The company said Alexa+ is now available under Early Access at no additional cost for eligible Echo smart speakers, smart displays, Fire TV devices, and the Alexa mobile app. The launch marks Amazon's latest push into the rapidly growing artificial intelligence, smart home, voice technology, and digital assistant segments in India.
Teena Sidana, Country Manager for Alexa, Amazon India said, "Indian households are multi-generational, multilingual, and beautifully complex. Alexa+ was designed for that complexity. She understands intent, adapts to your household’s preferences, and lets each family member interact in the way that feels most natural to them. India is home to one of the most diverse set of customers in the world, and we're excited for them to experience how much smarter, personalized, and more intuitive Alexa+ has become. It was truly built around the way they live. We want to make everyday life simpler for hundreds of millions of people who speak, shop, and live differently from one another and build the world's best personal assistant.”
According to Amazon, Alexa+ has been built to understand conversational speech patterns and user intent, allowing customers to interact naturally without repeatedly using the wake word. The assistant supports English, Hindi, and Hinglish, enabling users to switch languages during conversations while maintaining context.
Amazon said additional Indian language support will be introduced in the future.
Alexa+ is designed to work with a range of connected devices and services used by Indian consumers. The platform supports smart home products from brands including Atomberg, Qubo, Dreame, and Wipro, enabling voice-based control of appliances and connected devices.
Users can also access recipe recommendations through Sanjeev Kapoor Recipes and discover music, podcasts, movies, and TV shows across platforms such as Amazon Music, Spotify, Apple Music, JioSaavn, Prime Video, and Netflix.
Amazon further revealed that integrations with EazyDiner, Swiggy, District by Zomato, MakeMyTrip, Home Triangle, and TripAdvisor will be introduced soon, expanding Alexa+'s capabilities across food delivery, restaurant reservations, travel bookings, home services, and event planning.
The company said Alexa+ uses voice and visual identification technologies to recognize individual family members and tailor responses based on preferences and routines. The assistant can remember dietary preferences, entertainment choices, and daily schedules, allowing it to provide customized recommendations and reminders for different household members.
Amazon has also integrated shopping-focused features into Alexa+, enabling customers to create shopping lists, track Amazon orders, receive price-drop alerts, compare products, summarize verified customer reviews, and discover related products through voice interactions.
The company added that customers will soon be able to order groceries and everyday essentials using voice commands through Amazon Now, completing purchases through natural conversations.
Amazon said Alexa+ has been developed with a strong focus on Indian languages, cultural references, and communication styles. The assistant can understand local expressions, relationship terms, measurements, and commonly used phrases that are part of everyday conversations across Indian households.
The company noted that a significant portion of the technology powering Alexa+'s cultural and linguistic understanding was developed by teams based in Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune, and Chennai.
Alexa+ is powered by Amazon Bedrock, which connects more than 70 large language models, including Amazon-developed AI models and models from Anthropic. Amazon said the platform automatically selects the most suitable model depending on the task being performed.
The company also highlighted privacy and security features, including access to the Alexa Privacy Dashboard, voice recording controls, microphone and camera settings, and transparency tools that allow customers to review interactions.
Alexa+ is currently available through eligible Echo devices, Fire TV products, and the Alexa app in India. Browser access is expected to be introduced at a later stage.
The service will remain free during the Early Access period. After Early Access concludes, Alexa+ will continue to be available at no additional cost for Prime plan members. For Prime Lite, Prime Shopping Edition, and non-Prime customers, access will be offered through a standalone subscription priced at Rs 2,000 per month or through an eligible Prime membership plan.
Amazon also introduced new Alexa+-optimized devices, including the Echo Show 8, Echo Show 11, Echo Dot Max, and Echo Studio, which have been designed with enhanced processing power and next-generation hardware capabilities.
Real estate major DLF Limited has appointed Nimit Porwal as Vice President, responsible for driving the growth and development of its DLF5 business in Gurugram. Porwal shared the update in a LinkedIn post, saying he was beginning a "new mandate" at a familiar organization and looked forward to contributing to DLF5's continued expansion.
In his new role, he will oversee business strategy, product development, project execution, and profit and loss (P&L) management across DLF5's luxury residential and retail portfolio. The appointment comes as DLF continues to strengthen its presence in India's luxury real estate, premium housing, and retail real estate segments.
Prior to joining DLF, Porwal served as Strategy and P&L Lead for Indore at Godrej Properties, where he led the company's entry into the city. His responsibilities included land acquisitions, project planning, residential project launches, office and team setup, along with sales and marketing operations. Porwal is no stranger to DLF. He previously spent nearly two years with the company as Cluster Business Head, leading business strategy, product management, and P&L operations for the DLF5 super-luxury portfolio.
During his earlier tenure, he led the conceptualization and launch of The Dahlias, a luxury residential project that generated topline revenue of more than Rs 30,000 crore. He also contributed to DLF5's master planning initiatives and played a role in the development strategy for projects such as The Grove and The Summit Plaza.
With experience across real estate development, asset management, investment risk management, and consulting, Porwal has also worked with CBRE India, Piramal Capital and Housing Finance, and KPMG India. The leadership appointment is expected to support DLF's ongoing focus on expanding its luxury residential, mixed-use, and retail real estate portfolio in Gurugram, a key market for the company's long-term growth strategy.
Tata Group-backed jewellery retailer CaratLane has launched a dedicated e-commerce platform for Australia, marking the company's latest step in expanding its international presence. The new website will allow customers across Australia to browse and purchase CaratLane's diamond and gold jewellery collections directly through a localized online platform.
The launch is aimed at improving accessibility for customers in Australia, particularly the Indian diaspora, while strengthening CaratLane's growing global jewellery business. The platform offers a localized shopping experience, including product discovery, online transactions, and nationwide delivery services.
Saumen Bhaumik, Managing Director, CaratLane said, “Indian consumers in Australia have long shown a strong desire for CaratLane designs, making this launch a natural progression for the brand. By introducing a localised platform, we’re removing cross-border friction to deliver a seamless shopping experience directly to their doorsteps, marking a major milestone in our global growth story. It’s part of our larger vision to make CaratLane the most loved jewellery brand amongst Indian women, and Australia plays a critical role in that journey.”
The Australia launch expands CaratLane's international footprint beyond its existing operations in markets including the United States, Canada, Singapore, and the United Kingdom. The company currently serves customers in more than 30 countries and has been increasing its focus on overseas growth through a mix of online and offline channels.
CaratLane has also been strengthening its retail network and omnichannel strategy in India. The jewellery retailer recently outlined plans to add new stores across multiple markets while continuing investments in digital capabilities and customer experience initiatives.
The Australia-focused platform will offer certified jewellery products supported by insured shipping and authenticity documentation. The move reflects the growing trend among Indian jewellery brands to expand internationally through digital commerce, targeting overseas consumers seeking access to Indian-designed jewellery and diamond collections. As global demand for Indian jewellery continues to rise, CaratLane's latest expansion underscores the increasing role of cross-border e-commerce and omnichannel retail strategies in driving growth for Indian jewellery brands.
EBG Group has announced its entry into India’s toy retail and children’s lifestyle market with the launch of Adhira and Appa Toys, a new homegrown toy brand focused on play, learning, and family experiences. The company plans to open its first retail store in Hyderabad by the end of 2026 and invest more than Rs 50 crore to expand the brand to 50 stores across India by 2027.
The brand will offer a wide range of products designed for children from infancy to pre-teen years, spanning categories such as STEM toys, educational toys, robotics kits, science kits, sensory-development products, puzzles, board games, arts and crafts, pretend-play toys, dolls, action figures, ride-ons, plush toys, outdoor play products, electronics, and collectibles.
Irfan Khan, Founder and Chairman, EBG Group said, “We are not building another toy store. We are building a world where children can explore, imagine, learn, and dream. For us, a good toy should create joy today, curiosity tomorrow, and memories that stay with a child for years. The first portfolio features 1,335 products for children from infancy through the pre-teen years. Parents will be able to choose from STEM and educational toys, construction and building sets, robotics and science kits, sensory-development toys, puzzles and board games, arts and crafts, pretend-play products, dolls and action figures, remote-control vehicles, ride-ons and tricycles, plush toys, outdoor play products, electronics and collectibles.”
The launch comes as India's toy manufacturing sector continues to gain momentum under the Government of India's Vocal for Local and Made in India initiatives. Adhira and Appa Toys said it is working with domestic manufacturing partners to develop products for Indian consumers while supporting local production capabilities.
According to government data, India became a net exporter of toys in FY 2025-26, with toy imports declining by 37.5 percent and toy exports increasing by 89.1 percent. Indian-made toys are being exported to markets including the United States, the United Kingdom, Germany, and the Netherlands, reflecting growing international demand for products manufactured in India.
The company's strategy aligns with the broader growth outlook for the toy industry. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman has previously encouraged Indian toy manufacturers to target opportunities beyond the projected $5 billion Indian toy market by 2034 and capture a larger share of the projected $179 billion global toy market by 2032.
Beyond retail expansion, Adhira and Appa Toys plans to integrate sustainability measures into its operations. The company will focus on domestic and regional sourcing, explore recyclable and reusable packaging solutions, reduce inventory-related wastage, and adopt energy-efficient practices where feasible.
Hari Haran Chandrasekharan, who leads the Adhira and Appa Toys vertical within EBG Group, highlighted sustainability and local sourcing as key focus areas supporting both operational efficiency and Indian manufacturing. The company also plans to expand beyond traditional toy retailing through Adhira and Appa Game Zones, experiential play areas, creative workshops, children's merchandise, gifting solutions, and parent-child engagement formats. An omnichannel platform is also under development to connect online and offline customer experiences.
EBG Group said its first Hyderabad store will serve as a pilot location to understand customer preferences and refine operational processes before scaling across major metropolitan markets and high-growth Tier I and Tier II cities. Future expansion will include flagship stores, mall-based formats, compact stores, and shop-in-shop models. As part of its domestic manufacturing strategy, Adhira and Appa Toys is collaborating with Aditi Toys, a Rajkot-based toy manufacturer, to strengthen local production capabilities and support India's growing toy ecosystem.
The initial public offering (IPO) of SS Retail Ltd, a multi-brand consumer electronics and mobile retail chain, opened for subscription on September 16 and will remain available for bidding until September 18. The public issue has attracted attention in the primary market, with the grey market premium (GMP) indicating potential listing gains of around 31 percent, reflecting strong investor interest ahead of the listing.
The company aims to raise Rs 500 crore through the IPO, comprising a fresh issue of Rs 360 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of Rs 140 crore. The IPO is priced in the range of Rs 403 to Rs 424 per share. Ahead of the public issue, SS Retail raised Rs 146 crore from anchor investors, with participation from institutional investors including ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund and Kotak Mutual Fund. The company allotted 34.52 lakh shares at Rs 424 apiece during the anchor round.
SS Retail operates a network of more than 500 stores across over 200 cities, primarily catering to consumers in Tier II and Tier III markets. The retailer focuses on the sale of mobile phones, accessories, and consumer electronics products.
According to market data, the grey market premium stood at around Rs 128 per share, indicating an estimated listing gain of nearly 30 percent over the upper price band. Market experts note that GMP is an unofficial indicator of investor sentiment and should not be considered a guarantee of listing performance. The company plans to utilize proceeds from the fresh issue for capital expenditure requirements and working capital needs as it continues to expand its retail presence.
SS Retail derives a significant portion of its business from Maharashtra and remains focused on the consumer electronics retail segment, a category witnessing growing demand across India's non-metro markets. Industry observers will be closely tracking subscription trends from retail, institutional, and high-net-worth investors over the three-day bidding period.
Amazon India has announced that its quick commerce service, Amazon Now, has crossed $1 billion in annualized gross sales in India during the past three-month period. The company said Amazon Now orders have doubled every quarter since launch, making it the fastest-growing e-commerce business unit in Amazon India's history.
Ahead of the festive season, Amazon has expanded Amazon Now to more than 60 cities and towns across India, increasing its footprint fourfold in less than 10 weeks. In addition to major metropolitan markets, the service is now available in locations including Padubidri, Tirupati, Guntur, Gurdaspur, Jalandhar, Vellore, Dharwad, Warangal, and Berhampur. The quick delivery service operates through a network of over 750 micro-fulfilment and urban fulfilment centers, enabling delivery of products within minutes.
Samir Kumar, Country Manager, Amazon India said, “In a short period of time, Amazon Now has crossed $1 billion in annualized gross sales in India, making it the fastest-growing e-commerce business unit in Amazon India’s history. We are humbled by the customer response, with orders doubling every quarter. We are on track to expand to 100 cities by Diwali, taking delivery-in-minutes from Gurdaspur and Hoshiarpur in the north to Vembayam and Alamcode in the south. Customers across the country can look forward to the widest selection delivered at the fastest speeds this festive season.”
The development follows Amazon's June 2026 announcement to build what it described as India's largest delivery-in-minutes network by expanding Amazon Now to more than 300 cities nationwide. The company continues to invest in its quick commerce and fulfilment infrastructure to support faster deliveries across categories. Amazon said the network enables sellers to offer tens of thousands of products for delivery within minutes or a few hours, more than one million products for same-day delivery, over four million products for next-day delivery, and millions more through Prime delivery services.
Amazon currently offers a broad range of products, including groceries, fresh fruits and vegetables, frozen food, personal care items, fashion and beauty products, small appliances, and home and kitchen essentials. The service is part of the growing quick commerce segment in India, where retailers and e-commerce platforms are expanding rapid delivery capabilities to meet rising consumer demand.
Fresh commerce platform Handpickd has expanded its product portfolio beyond fresh fruits and vegetables, entering the daily kitchen staples category with freshly prepared and additive-free food products. The company said it is strengthening its supply chain to offer consumers a wider range of fresh essentials, including made-to-order atta (flour), freshly pounded spices, cold-pressed oils, farm dairy products, small-batch spreads, fresh flowers, and ready-to-cook items.
Handpickd expects categories such as freshly milled flour and hand-pounded spices to play a significant role in its growth strategy over the coming year as demand for fresh, minimally processed food products continues to increase. The company operates on a zero-inventory model, designed to reduce storage time and connect consumers directly with sourcing and preparation processes. According to Handpickd, the approach focuses on local sourcing and faster delivery to maintain freshness and product quality.
Anant Goel, Founder and CEO, Handpickd said, “There are two sides to food being modified to last long. Something bad added to it. Or something good taken out. Product companies around the globe have been over investing in it for decades so they can make it centrally and distribute globally. Your local 'halwai' doesn't know that science. Neither does your local 'atta chakki'. The problem there is adulteration of raw material. Handpickd is tackling both in one go - Pure raw material, prepared clean and delivered fresh. Fresh food items that will go bad when they are supposed to because fresh is science-less.”
The company stated that every batch in its staples portfolio is sourced from selected farms and mills and prepared closer to the point of delivery. The model is intended to extend the same level of sourcing visibility and transparency that the platform currently offers in the fresh produce category.
The move comes as India's fresh food retail, grocery delivery, quick commerce, food technology, clean-label food, organic food, and direct-to-consumer grocery segments continue to witness rising consumer demand for transparency, quality, and minimally processed products.
Handpickd said the expansion forms part of its broader strategy to build a full-stack fresh commerce ecosystem covering a wider range of everyday household essentials. With the addition of staples, the company aims to strengthen its position in the growing fresh food delivery market while expanding beyond produce into high-frequency consumption categories.
Premium dairy brand Epigamia has announced key leadership appointments as it prepares for its next phase of growth, with plans to achieve an annualised revenue run rate of over Rs 1,000 crore in the next financial year and double its business over the next 24-30 months. The company has appointed Mansi Modi to lead its marketing function from the end of September, while Rahul Bhagat will take charge of manufacturing operations. The appointments come at a time when the company is expanding its footprint in India's dairy products, yogurt, healthy snacking, packaged food, quick commerce, and FMCG sectors.
Ritesh Gauba, CEO, Epigamia, said, “We are confident that with Mansi and Rahul joining in, their leadership will help us solidify our growth momentum and strengthen our market leadership. Our strong growth, and fundamentals is a testament to our focus on our core innovative products and brand strength. With Mansi and Rahul joining our leadership team, we want to expand into newer formats and keep focusing on our DNA of innovation.”
Rahul Bhagat brings experience in manufacturing and operations, having worked with companies including Danone, Britannia, ITC Foods, and Tata Consumer. At Epigamia, he will focus on strengthening manufacturing capabilities as the company scales its operations across India. Mansi Modi joins the company with more than 14 years of experience in marketing and brand leadership. Her previous roles include positions at Hindustan Unilever, Oziva, Airtel, and Britannia. She will work with the leadership team to support brand development and business growth initiatives.
Alongside the new appointments, Epigamia announced that Ankur Goel, Chief Operating Officer, will be stepping down from the company. According to the company, he is leaving after a decade in the startup ecosystem to focus on personal health and family commitments. Backed by the Mirchandani family, founder Rohan Mirchandani, and investors including Verlinvest, Sauce, and DSG Consumer Partners, Epigamia has built a presence in India's premium dairy market.
The company said it has expanded distribution to more than 150 cities and continues to strengthen its reach through modern trade, general trade, e-commerce, and quick commerce platforms, including Blinkit, Instamart, Amazon, and Zepto. The latest leadership changes come as the company looks to accelerate growth, expand product formats, and deepen its presence across India's organised dairy and packaged food market.
Horlicks has expanded its nutrition portfolio with the launch of Horlicks Protein Powder, targeting growing consumer demand for convenient, everyday protein intake beyond fitness-focused use cases. As awareness of protein consumption grows across India, consumers are increasingly seeking nutrition products they can easily incorporate into their daily routines.
Responding to this trend, Horlicks has introduced a new protein powder designed for on-the-go consumption, work schedules, travel, and busy lifestyles. The newly launched product delivers 24 g of protein and 4 g of prebiotic fibre per serving and is available in single-serve sachets aimed at improving convenience and portability.
Rajneet Kohli, Executive Director, Foods, Hindustan Unilever Limited said, “Horlicks has a legacy of over 100 years, built on strong science and nutrition credentials. As we continue to evolve with the changing needs of consumers, protein is a natural extension for the brand. We see an opportunity to make it more relevant and accessible for everyday lifestyles. When we spoke to consumers, one insight that really stood out was that ‘life is a gym’, whether it is rushing through a busy workday, navigating a long commute, carrying groceries or simply keeping up with everything the day demands. This insight led to our larger thought, ‘Your Day Is the Real Workout.’ With Horlicks Protein Powder, our ambition is to make quality protein easier to incorporate into the everyday lifestyles of millions of Indians.”
According to the company, the formulation is based on fermented yeast protein, a complete protein source that contains all nine essential amino acids required by the body. The product also has a PDCAAS (Protein Digestibility-Corrected Amino Acid Score) of 1.0, a globally recognised benchmark used to assess protein quality and digestibility.
The formulation includes inulin, a prebiotic fibre, and papain, a plant-derived digestive enzyme. Fermented yeast protein is also naturally lactose-free, catering to consumers looking for alternative protein sources.
Sujatha Jayaraman, Vice President and Head, Foods R&D and Regulatory Affairs, Hindustan Unilever Limited said, “As consumers become more aware of protein, the conversation also needs to move from simply how much protein a product contains to the quality and completeness of that protein. That thinking shaped the science behind Horlicks Protein Powder. Fermented yeast protein provides all nine essential amino acids, while the finished product has a PDCAAS score of 1.0, a recognised measure of protein quality and digestibility. We have complemented this with inulin, a prebiotic fibre, and papain, a plant-derived proteolytic enzyme that aids protein digestion. The result is a science-led formulation that brings together high-quality complete protein with ingredients selected to support protein digestion and gut-friendly nutrition in one product.”
The launch reflects a broader shift in the health and wellness, functional nutrition, protein supplements, and packaged nutrition segments, where brands are increasingly positioning protein as part of everyday nutrition rather than only sports and fitness-focused consumption.
Horlicks Protein Powder is available in Chocolate, Coffee, and Unflavored variants. Each 1 kg pack contains 28 single-serve sachets, eliminating the need for measuring scoops and making consumption more convenient throughout the day. The product is now available across retail stores and select e-commerce platforms in India.
India's retail fashion market is set to see a fresh festive offering as Max Fashion launches its Festive 2026 collection under Max Project New, bringing together traditional Indian craftsmanship, contemporary design, and inclusive fashion collaborations. The new festive collection features actor and brand ambassador Kalki Koechlin as the face and creative collaborator. Developed around themes of individuality, fusion fashion, and modern occasionwear, the collection combines heritage-inspired design with contemporary silhouettes aimed at today's festive fashion consumers.
Kalki Koechlin, Brand Ambassador, Max Fashion said, "Fashion has always been my way of saying something without saying it outright, and this collection let me do that on a much bigger scale. Both the drops in this collection, in their own way, are about looking at festive dressing differently. That felt worth being part of."
One of the key highlights of the collection is the fusion of Rajasthan's traditional Sanganeri hand block printing with Japanese-inspired floral motifs. The designs feature elements such as cherry blossoms, lotus medallions, Jaipuri block-print borders, geometric textures, and subtle gold detailing.
The collection traces its origins to Sanganer, Rajasthan, a hub known for hand block printing. Max Fashion said the first design was created entirely by artisans using traditional carving, colouring, and printing techniques. While the collection was later scaled for wider retail distribution, the craftsmanship remained central to its development. The colour palette includes powder pink, blush sakura, ivory, off-white, sage green, pista green, lavender, and coral shades, designed to suit both daytime and evening festive occasions.
The range includes fluid dresses, kurta sets, and kalidar silhouettes made from fabrics such as viscose blends, Chanderi blends, cotton dobby, and cotton flex. Design details include contrast piping, fabric buttons, potli accents, coordinated dupattas, zari work, mirror embellishments, beadwork, and tassel finishes. Alongside this craft-led collection, Max Fashion has introduced another line developed in partnership with the Kairassi Foundation, a Chennai-based organisation that supports artists with disabilities.
The collaboration showcases artworks created by Simron Raj, Pavithra, and Manas, whose original paintings have been adapted into wearable fashion pieces, including dresses, shirts, skirts, scarves, tote bags, and other apparel. According to the company, the garments were designed around the artwork, allowing the artists' visual identities to remain central to the collection.
Sumit Chandna, CEO, Max Fashion said, "Every festive season, we ask ourselves how to make the collection feel new, not just in design but in what it stands for. This year, that answer came from craft and creativity working together, from Sanganer's artisans to the artists we found through Kairassi. Max Project New is our way of building festive fashion that people actually connect with."
The retailer said the Festive 2026 collection reflects evolving consumer preferences for occasionwear that combines cultural influences, artistic expression, and contemporary styling. The collection will be available across Max Fashion stores, the brand's website, and mobile app across India from September, with a second launch scheduled for October.
Pricing starts at Rs 599 for menswear shirts and T-shirts, Rs 899 for womenswear dresses, skirts, and shirts, and Rs 999 for Indian wear categories including fusion dresses, fusion blazers, culottes, and kurta sets. Prices across the collection go up to Rs 1,999.
Da Milano Group has appointed Piyush Singh as its Group CEO as the company looks to accelerate growth and strengthen its presence across markets. Singh brings more than 18 years of experience across consumer businesses, retail, business strategy, transformation and leadership. Over the course of his career, he has worked on business growth initiatives, consumer-focused strategies and operational transformation across competitive markets.
The appointment comes as Da Milano Group continues to focus on expanding its business, strengthening its brand portfolio and enhancing customer engagement across channels. The company said Singh will play a key role in shaping and executing its growth strategy during the next phase of development.
Piyush Singh, Group CEO, Da Milano Group said, “I am delighted to join Da Milano Group at an exciting stage in its journey. The Group has built a strong presence in the luxury lifestyle space, and I look forward to working closely with the team to build on this foundation and unlock the next phase of growth. Our focus will be on strengthening our brands, deepening our customer connect, building operational excellence and creating sustainable value as we scale the business across markets and channels.”
In his new role, Singh will oversee initiatives focused on strengthening the company’s brand portfolio, improving operational efficiency across the value chain and driving business performance across retail and emerging channels. He will also be responsible for supporting the company’s long-term growth objectives and expanding its presence across multiple consumer touchpoints.
The leadership appointment reflects Da Milano Group’s ongoing efforts to build a stronger management structure as it expands its operations. The company is also exploring opportunities across retail, direct-to-consumer (D2C) platforms and emerging distribution channels as part of its broader business strategy. With Singh taking over as Group CEO, Da Milano Group aims to build on its existing market presence while pursuing new growth opportunities across the luxury accessories, lifestyle and fashion retail sectors.
India is assured to emerge as a global hub for gems and jewellery in the coming years, Union Home Minister Amit Shah said on Sunday, urging the industry to take the lead in building a complete, India-owned value chain for the emerging lab-grown diamond market.
India’s rich jewellery heritage
The Home Minister highlighted the contribution of Indian artisans and craftsmen to the development of the country's jewellery traditions over centuries.
He noted that royal patronage during the medieval period helped jewellery craftsmanship reach new heights, while regions such as Rajasthan and Kolkata developed distinctive traditions, including Kundan and Meenakari.
Jaipur, Shah said, continues to be renowned globally for its coloured gemstones.
Lab-Grown diamonds present new opportunity
According to Shah, changing consumer preferences and the emergence of lab-grown diamonds present a significant opportunity for India's gems and jewellery sector.
He said the era of lab-grown diamonds is set to emerge, with the market expected to grow to nearly 50 times the size of the current diamond market.
Shah stressed that the entire ecosystem and manufacturing value chain should be under Indian ownership, spanning the manufacture of machinery, production of lab-grown diamonds, jewellery manufacturing, branding and global retail.
“From manufacturing the machines to the showroom where the jewellery ultimately reaches a woman’s hand, India must have ownership of the entire ecosystem,” Shah said.
India Jewellery Park to drive investment
Shah said the India Jewellery Park is a landmark project expected to attract investments of around INR 50,000 crore and generate direct and indirect employment for one lakh people.
The project is expected to strengthen India's jewellery manufacturing ecosystem while creating opportunities across manufacturing, processing, design, branding and retail.
India’s growing global jewellery footprint
In his speech, the Union Home Minister also highlighted India's growing position in the global jewellery trade. He said India has emerged as a major source of jewellery imports for markets including the United States, the Middle East, Hong Kong and Europe.
Conclusion
India's gems and jewellery industry is at an important inflection point, with its traditional craftsmanship now intersecting with new-age opportunities such as lab-grown diamonds. Building an India-owned value chain could help the country move beyond its established strengths in manufacturing and craftsmanship towards greater control over technology, branding and global retail. With large-scale investments such as the India Jewellery Park, the sector could further strengthen India's position as a global jewellery hub while creating significant employment and business opportunities.
Reliance Consumer Products Limited (RCPL), the FMCG arm of Reliance Industries Limited, has launched its beverage brand Campa in Australia, marking the brand’s entry into a new international market. New Sunrise has become the first petrol and convenience retail network in Australia to introduce Campa across its stores.
The launch brings the beverage brand, which has a legacy spanning nearly five decades, to Australian consumers through the New Sunrise national retail network. The move is part of RCPL’s broader international expansion strategy as it continues to strengthen its presence in global consumer goods markets.
Since acquiring Campa in 2022 and reintroducing the brand in India in 2023, RCPL has expanded the portfolio beyond carbonated soft drinks to include juices and packaged drinking water. The company has been growing Campa’s presence across multiple beverage categories within the Indian FMCG and beverage sectors. Australia becomes the latest market in RCPL’s international expansion journey, following the company’s growing footprint across GCC countries, Nepal and Sri Lanka.
The initial Campa product range is now available nationwide through approximately 1,200 New Sunrise petrol and convenience stores. The partnership provides the brand with immediate access to a large retail distribution network and strengthens its reach within Australia’s convenience retail and on-the-go beverage segments.
The company believes the Australian market presents opportunities for value-focused beverage brands as consumers increasingly seek affordability, convenience and product variety. Through its partnership with New Sunrise, Campa will be positioned within a retail channel that serves a significant share of impulse and convenience purchases.
The rollout also highlights the growing international ambitions of Indian FMCG companies and beverage brands seeking expansion opportunities beyond domestic markets. With Australia now added to its international portfolio, RCPL continues to build Campa’s presence across key global markets. The launch is expected to support wider brand visibility and distribution while strengthening RCPL’s position in the global non-alcoholic beverages industry.
Amazon India has announced a major expansion of its logistics and supply chain network ahead of the festive shopping season, with plans to add 20 fulfilment centres, six sort centres and 150 delivery stations across the country. The expansion is aimed at strengthening the company's e-commerce infrastructure and enhancing its ability to manage higher order volumes during one of the busiest shopping periods of the year. The additional facilities are expected to improve inventory storage, order processing, and last-mile delivery capabilities across multiple regions.
With the planned additions, Amazon is increasing capacity across key stages of its operations network. Fulfilment centres will support inventory storage for sellers, while sort centres will help streamline package movement between facilities. The new delivery stations are expected to strengthen last-mile logistics and improve delivery efficiency in both metropolitan and emerging markets.
The announcement comes as online retailers prepare for increased consumer spending during festive sales events. E-commerce platforms typically experience a sharp rise in demand across categories such as electronics, smartphones, fashion, beauty, home appliances and consumer goods during this period.
Amazon has continued to invest in its logistics network in India, including fulfilment infrastructure, delivery operations and quick commerce capabilities. The company recently expanded its operations network, created more than 160,000 seasonal work opportunities and increased investments in fulfilment and delivery infrastructure to support growing customer demand.
The expanded network is also expected to support Amazon's seller ecosystem by enabling faster order fulfilment and wider reach across serviceable pin codes. The company currently serves millions of customers and works with a large base of sellers across India through its fulfilment, sorting and delivery infrastructure.
As competition intensifies in India's e-commerce and quick commerce sectors, logistics capacity has become a key area of investment for online retailers. Amazon's latest expansion highlights the industry's focus on warehousing, supply chain optimisation and last-mile delivery ahead of the festive shopping season.
Adie Broswon Group has expanded its flavoured vodka portfolio by launching MOOOZ Cranberry Vodka in Uttar Pradesh. The introduction of the new variant strengthens the company’s presence in North India and adds to its growing range of vodka offerings in the Indian alcohol beverage market.
Uttar Pradesh continues to be a key market for alcohol beverage companies due to its scale, evolving retail ecosystem, and increasing demand for premium and flavoured spirits. The launch of MOOOZ Cranberry Vodka aligns with the company’s efforts to expand distribution and reach consumers seeking new flavour profiles within the vodka category.
MOOOZ is produced in Punjab using rice grains and undergoes a triple distillation process along with a multi-stage filtration system. The brand has already established a presence in markets including Delhi, Punjab and Chandigarh and has been expanding across North India through new product launches and market entries.
The launch comes at a time when flavoured vodka is gaining traction in India, particularly among younger adult consumers and cocktail-focused occasions. Industry trends indicate increasing demand for innovative spirit categories, with flavoured variants emerging as an important growth segment within the vodka market.
The addition of Cranberry Vodka further broadens the MOOOZ portfolio, which has recently seen the introduction of new flavour-led variants as the company continues to diversify its offerings in the Indian spirits industry. With the Uttar Pradesh launch, Adie Broswon continues to strengthen its footprint across key markets in North India, focusing on portfolio expansion and wider availability in the country's evolving alcobev sector.
Parag Milk Foods is expanding its nutrition portfolio beyond conventional protein products, entering the snacking segment with Avvatar Popped Protein Chips as consumers increasingly look for convenient ways to include protein in everyday eating.
The launch marks the latest move under the company’s New Age Business, extending Avvatar from its existing range of protein powders, ready-to-drink beverages and bars into a familiar snacking format.
Akshali Shah, Executive Director, Parag Milk Foods Ltd., said, “This launch marks an important step in Parag Milk Foods’ evolution from a dairy-led company to a broader nutrition-led food business.”
The company said the expansion is aimed at creating more consumption occasions for protein, including those beyond traditional sports and active nutrition.
Avvatar Popped Chips are available in Magic Masala and Pudina flavours. The non-fried chips provide 10 g of protein in a 30 g pack and are priced at INR 60.
The product contains no added sugar, palm oil, or preservatives, positioning it within the growing better-for-you snacking space while retaining the convenience of a packaged snack.
The chips are being distributed through Avvatar’s website, quick-commerce platforms, vending machines, general trade and modern trade outlets.
For Parag Milk Foods, the launch forms part of a broader effort to use its experience in dairy and protein to enter adjacent food categories. Avvatar is expected to play a role in this expansion as the company looks to build its presence across different nutrition formats and consumption occasions.
“We see a significant opportunity to take our expertise in dairy and protein and build it into categories that are increasingly relevant to the way consumers eat today,” Shah said.
She added, “With Avvatar, we are extending protein beyond traditional nutrition formats and into everyday consumption occasions, including snacking.”
The company’s approach reflects the wider shift in the packaged food market, where protein is increasingly being incorporated into convenient, ready-to-consume products rather than remaining limited to specialised nutrition products.
Established in 1992, Parag Milk Foods has built its business around dairy products and operates manufacturing facilities at Manchar and Thorandale in Maharashtra and Palamner in Andhra Pradesh.
Its portfolio includes milk, ghee, dahi and paneer under Gowardhan, while Go offers products such as cheese, UHT milk, buttermilk, lassi and flavoured milkshakes. The company also operates Pride of Cows, a premium farm-to-home dairy brand.
Avvatar represents its sports nutrition business and focuses on whey protein products. With the addition of popped chips, the company is now extending the brand into everyday snacking.
The move signals Parag Milk Foods’ attempt to build a broader nutrition portfolio where protein can be consumed across different parts of the day, from specialised sports nutrition to convenient snacks.
“Our ambition is to build a holistic protein ecosystem that brings together nutrition, convenience and accessibility across formats and lifestyles,” Shah said.
She added that entering snacking is “a strategic step towards creating a larger, more contemporary food and nutrition business with protein at its core.”
The House of Rare, the company behind fashion brands Rare Rabbit, Rareism, Rare’Z and Rare Ones, is ramping up its growth plans through an aggressive retail expansion strategy, new category launches and a stronger omnichannel presence across India.
The fashion retailer is aiming to achieve revenue of nearly Rs 1,600 crore in the current fiscal year, marking a significant increase from Rs 1,100 crore recorded in the previous year. The growth target comes as the company continues to expand its physical footprint and diversify its product portfolio across multiple fashion segments.
Launched over a decade ago with the introduction of Rare Rabbit, The House of Rare has evolved into a multi-brand fashion platform covering menswear, womenswear, kidswear and sneakers. The company currently operates 210 stores across its portfolio and plans to increase the count to at least 285 stores by the end of this fiscal year. An additional 50 outlets are expected to be added in the following year.
Rare Rabbit continues to be the company’s largest business segment, contributing around 70-72 percent of overall revenue. Womenswear brand Rareism accounts for nearly 20 percent, while Rare’Z and Rare Ones together contribute approximately 8-9 percent.
As part of its diversification efforts, The House of Rare is entering several new product categories, including fragrances, women’s handbags, open footwear, ballerinas, heels, belts and jewellery. The fragrance range is scheduled to launch next month. Meanwhile, its men’s innerwear label, Innerv, already contributes about 3 percent of Rare Rabbit’s menswear business and is being scaled further.
Currently, The House of Rare has a presence across more than 1,100 points of sale. Around 97 percent of its outlets are company-owned and company-operated. Its stores typically span between 1,100 and 1,200 square feet, with capital expenditure averaging Rs 3,400-3,500 per square foot. Metro cities and Tier I markets contribute roughly 60-65 percent of total revenue, though the company sees substantial growth opportunities emerging from Tier II and Tier III cities.
Offline channels remain the primary revenue source, accounting for around 60 percent of total sales, while online channels contribute the remaining 40 percent. The average selling price online ranges between Rs 1,600 and Rs 1,800, whereas the average order value in physical stores stands at approximately Rs 4,500-5,000.
The company has also reported strong customer growth, with its customer base expanding by nearly 50 percent this year. Repeat customers currently account for around 40 percent of total shoppers.
Allied Blenders and Distillers Ltd (ABDL) is planning to enter the single malt whisky segment with an investment of up to Rs 115 crore. The company’s Management Committee has approved the additional capital infusion into its subsidiary, Minakshi Agro Industries LLP (MAILLP).
The investment will be used to set up a malt distillery-cum-maturation warehouse in Aurangabad, Maharashtra. The proposed facility is expected to have an annual production capacity of around 3 million bulk litres and is targeted to be commissioned by the third quarter of FY28.
The proposed facility will support ABDL’s planned entry into the provenance-led single malt whisky category. The company said the investment forms part of its broader strategy to expand its presence in premium spirits.
“The proposed investment is aligned with the Company's long-term strategic vision of expanding and strengthening its premium spirits portfolio through entry into the provenance-led Single Malt Whisky segment,” the company said.
The move comes as Indian consumers have shown growing interest in premium and luxury spirits, with domestic single malt brands gaining greater visibility in recent years. ABDL currently has a portfolio spanning whisky and other spirits and is seeking to add a new category to its business.
Alongside the Rs 115 crore investment, the company has approved an additional capital contribution of up to Rs 10 crore for previously approved projects under MAILLP.
The additional funding will address cost overruns linked to a bottling unit and a distillery. According to the company, the increase in project costs is partly due to higher prices of key metals. A marginal expansion of the bottling hall and mezzanine area is also planned to accommodate longer automated bottling lines.
ABDL is the company behind brands including Officer’s Choice and has operations across the Indian spirits market. The company is also present in international markets and exports to 39 countries, according to the company filing.
The Aurangabad facility is expected to add manufacturing capacity for single malt whisky once commissioned. The investment will also mark ABDL’s entry into a segment that requires longer maturation periods and dedicated production infrastructure.
With the proposed investment and ongoing capacity projects, the company is expanding its manufacturing base while adding premium categories to its spirits portfolio.

input.title: After Nykaa, Zee initiates music copyright fight with Blinkit
input.content:
Zee Entertainment Enterprises Limited has sued quick commerce platform Blinkit for allegedly using its copyrighted content on Instagram, court documents accessed by MediaNama show. The case could have wider implications for the commercial use of music on Instagram, given that Zee and Eternal, Blinkit’s parent company, are both major listed companies in their respective sectors.
What is the dispute about? In a lawsuit filed in the Delhi High Court on July 27, Zee argued that Blinkit created “infringing works” and then uploaded them to its Instagram account.
- Zee also placed on record screen recordings of the alleged infringements posted by Blinkit on social media.
- While Zee’s licensing agreement with Meta allows individuals to use its music in Instagram posts for non-commercial purposes, platforms often use Zee’s licensed music in Instagram Reels to promote their products.
- It is unclear whether Blinkit had secured prior authorisation from Zee to use its copyrighted songs for commercial purposes.
What’s next? The Delhi High Court issued summons to Blink Commerce Private Limited, which operates as Blinkit.
- Justice Jyoti Singh also directed Blinkit to file a written statement within 30 days of receiving the summons, along with affidavits either admitting or denying Zee’s claims.
- The case will next be heard on August 27.
Why this matters: This is at least the third instance this year of a company being accused of infringing Zee’s copyrighted content. In April, Zee sued fashion and beauty retailer Nykaa for allegedly using its copyrighted songs in Instagram Reels to promote its products without permission. The dispute is ongoing, and Zee is seeking damages of approximately Rs 2 crore over Nykaa’s alleged unauthorised use of its music.
Last month, the Delhi High Court passed a John Doe order directing Meta to remove several Facebook URLs hosting Zee’s copyrighted content.
Earlier this year, Zee also filed a commercial suit against rival JioStar in the Delhi High Court, alleging the unauthorised use of its sound recordings across digital platforms and satellite TV channels. The lawsuit alleges that JioStar continued to use Zee’s music content even after the licensing agreement between the two parties had expired.
Zee itself is also facing allegations of copyright infringement. In May, JioStar initiated legal action against Zee Entertainment for allegedly broadcasting 12 Bollywood films to which it holds the rights without permission. In its lawsuit, JioStar accused Zee of being a “habitual infringer”, claiming that it continues to “engage in the unauthorised broadcast and exploitation of the films”.

input.title: Nykaa net profit soars over 3X; VC funding remains modest
input.content:
Nykaa net profit soars over 3X; VC funding remains modest
Omnichannel beauty and fashion retailer Nykaa has clocked a more than 3x rise in net profit and a 29% rise in revenue for the first quarter of the 2026-27 fiscal year, driven by overall demand. Meanwhile, VC funding in India’s startup ecosystem declined in July.
Hello,
There’s a new startup in town. And it’s Profound.
Former Swiggy and Zomato leaders Anuj Rathi and Prashant Parashar have launched an AI startup named Profound. Profound is building an AI Rep, a personalised AI assistant that represents professionals. The platform is designed to help professionals gear up for career opportunities and meaningful connections.
“Just as actors have agents and athletes have managers, Profound gives each professional their own AI Rep,” said Anuj Rathi, Co-founder and CEO.
In other news, gaming and sports media platform Nazara Technologies has reported a net loss of Rs 82.47 crore for the first quarter of the year. Its CEO Nitish Mittersain has also stepped down from his position. However, he will continue to serve as MD, focusing on long-term strategy and portfolio direction.
When the government meets Meta’s global team, it will raise concerns pertaining to lapses in curbing child sexual abuse material as well as wrongful action on prominent accounts, said IT Secretary S Krishnan.
Moving on, as part of its $21-billion investment in cloud infrastructure in India, Amazon has outlined measures to improve the sustainability of its data centre operations.
Lastly, token consumption by businesses and consumers has soared in recent years. Token is the smallest piece of text or data that an AI model reads, processes, and generates. As employees burn through tokens, companies are struggling to manage their AI costs.

- Nykaa’s 3X rise in net profit
- VC funding in July

input.title: Nykaa says quick delivery isn’t hurting margins as Q1 profit jumps 226%
input.content:
Bengaluru: Nykaa said on Tuesday its rapid-delivery beauty offering Nykaa Now has achieved sufficient scale without hurting profitability, with higher purchase frequency and steady basket sizes offsetting the higher costs of quick commerce, as the company looked to ease investors’ concerns around the economics of the format. The service has expanded to 13 cities from just 3 a year earlier and is expected to reach 25 cities by the end of fiscal year 2027 (FY27), supported by Nykaa's network of 324 stores across 105 cities that serve as hyperlocal fulfilment hubs. Nykaa Now currently offers more than 1,000 beauty and personal care brands, according to the company’s investor presentation. “We don’t think this will be dilutive. The increase in purchase frequency and average order values staying consistent are offsetting the increase in fulfillment costs,” Anchit Nayar, chief executive of Nykaa Beauty, told analysts on Tuesday. “Despite Nykaa Now having become meaningful over the past several quarters, we’ve still shown improvement this quarter.” The comments came as FSN E-Commerce Ventures Ltd, Nykaa's parent, reported a 226% year-on-year jump in consolidated net profit to ₹80 crore in the June quarter, driven by accelerating growth across its beauty and fashion businesses as years of investment in assortment expansion and omnichannel retail began translating into stronger profitability. Revenue from operations rose 29% year-on-year to ₹2,782 crore in the quarter ended 30 June, while gross merchandise value (GMV) grew 34% to ₹5,590 crore. Ebidta (Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation, and Amortization) increased 68% to ₹236 crore, with Ebitda margin expanding to 8.5% from 6.5% a year earlier. Nykaa’s beauty business posted 29% year-on-year growth in net sales value (NSV) to ₹2,371 crore, while fashion grew 54% to ₹451 crore, aided by customer additions, a broader brand portfolio and its partnership with Nike. Fashion also reported positive Ebitda of ₹40 lakh, compared with a loss of ₹18 crore a year earlier, marking its first Ebitda-positive quarter. Beauty Ebitda rose 48% to ₹244 crore, with margin improving to 10.3% from 9%. Management attributed the broad-based growth to a combination of stronger consumer demand and sustained execution. “There’s no single reason. It’s a combination of a good market, strong execution and continuing to build the right platform, marketing and technology,” Nykaa’s founder, executive chairperson and chief executive Falguni Nayar said. Executives said continued customer acquisition, premiumisation, brand partnerships and technology-led improvements in merchandising and personalisation helped Nykaa outpace the broader market. The fashion business also continued to benefit from its strategic partnership with Nike, although management said the underlying platform—not the partnership alone—was driving growth. “We still retain our guidance of growing the fashion business three to three-and-a-half times over the next four to five years. The numbers you are seeing are largely reflective of the underlying platform’s growth,” said Abhijeet Dabas, chief executive of Nykaa Fashion. The company also highlighted improving marketing efficiency, with repeat customers accounting for a growing share of sales. “We are now seeing a higher share of revenue come from repeat customers,” Anchit Nayar said, adding that improved targeting and a stronger assortment had lowered customer acquisition costs, particularly in fashion. During the quarter, Nykaa’s consumer base grew 33% year-on-year to 60 million, while it added more than 160 brands across beauty and lifestyle, taking its portfolio to over 10,000 brands. It also opened 11 new stores, ending the quarter with 324 outlets across 105 cities, while its portfolio of owned brands grew 43% year-on-year. Management said the September quarter is likely to remain the strongest because of festive demand, although beauty remains less dependent on seasonal shopping than many discretionary categories because much of demand comes from everyday-use products. Separately, the board approved the acquisition of a 51% stake in Aminu Wellness Pvt. Ltd. for up to ₹32 crore to strengthen Nykaa’s premium skincare portfolio. The Mumbai-based company said Aminu’s premium dermocosmetic positioning, proprietary formulations and in-house research and development capabilities would strengthen its House of Nykaa portfolio, which currently spans 13 consumer brands. Founded in 2019, Aminu manufactures and sells skincare products across salons, clinics and direct-to-consumer channels. The company reported FY26 revenue of ₹19.4 crore, up from ₹8.4 crore three years earlier, and has built a portfolio of more than 30 products with over 30 proprietary formulations. Nykaa said it would acquire the remaining 49% stake over the next few years under the terms of the transaction, while Aminu’s founders, Prachi Bhandari and Aman Mohunta, would continue to run the business. The transaction is expected to close in the second quarter of FY27, subject to regulatory approvals.
