The emerging markets formulations sales were $311 million and accounted for 19.4% of the total consolidated sales. The rest of world (ROW) formulation sales were at $218 million, accounting for 13.6% of the total consolidated sales.
Global innovative medicines sales were at $351 million in the June quarter and they accounted for 21.9% of sales.
Sun Pharma's active pharmaceutical ingredients (API) portfolio supported its formulation business and AP customers across geographies, the company said. External sales of API were at ₹597.2 crore, it added.
"Recent semaglutide approvals in India, Brazil and South Africa underscore our capabilities in developing complex peptide products for patients globally. Organon shareholders have approved the proposed acquisition by Sun, which is on track to close in early 2027," Ganorkar added.

input.title: After JioStar and Nykaa, Zee sues Blinkit over alleged copyright infringement
input.content:
New Delhi: Zee Entertainment Enterprises has filed a copyright infringement suit against Blink Commerce, which operates quick-commerce platform Blinkit, over content posted on the company’s Instagram account.
According to Mint, in a July 27 court order, the Delhi High Court issued summons to Blinkit and sought its response to Zee’s application for an interim injunction. The matter will next be heard on August 14.
Justice Jyoti Singh allowed Zee to submit screen recordings of the disputed Instagram content as evidence in the case.
The order referred to a “pen drive consisting of screen recordings of the infringing works as created and uploaded by the Defendant on its Instagram account.”
Blinkit has been directed to file its written statement within 30 days of receiving the summons.
“Issue summons to the Defendant through all permissible modes,” the court said, adding that the written statement should be filed “within 30 days from the date of receipt of summons.”
The court has not yet examined the merits of Zee’s allegations or decided whether the content amounts to copyright infringement. At this stage, it has issued notice to Blinkit and sought its response to Zee’s request for interim relief.
The court also exempted Zee from the mandatory pre-institution mediation process after the broadcaster argued that the matter required urgent intervention.
“Having regard to the facts of the present case wherein urgent relief is prayed for... exemption is granted to the Plaintiff from Pre-Institution Mediation,” the order stated.
The case is the latest copyright action initiated by Zee as it looks to restrict the commercial use of its content by brands and digital platforms. The broadcaster has also filed similar cases against JioStar and beauty and fashion retailer Nykaa.
Zee filed its copyright suit against JioStar on April 14. It alleged that JioStar continued to host and commercially use content containing Zee’s copyrighted material after licensing agreements signed in 2017 and 2020 had expired.
The Delhi High Court has referred the Zee-JioStar dispute to the Delhi High Court Mediation and Conciliation Centre.
Zee also told the court that JioStar had proposed a one-month extension in November 2025 as a “precautionary measure” to cover any inadvertent use of its content.
However, Zee alleged that instances of infringement continued even after the extension ended. The case is still pending before the court.
In a separate suit filed on April 3, Zee accused Nykaa of using its copyrighted music in 12 promotional Instagram reels created to market products.
Zee argued that its music licensing arrangement with Meta only allows the use of its content in non-commercial and personal user posts. It alleged that the licence did not cover the commercial use of music in Nykaa’s promotional content.
Nykaa has asked the court to add Meta Platforms as a party to the proceedings. It has also sought the referral of the dispute to mediation.

input.title: Sun Pharma banks on specialty drug portfolio, India business to drive growth in FY27
input.content:
Sun Pharmaceutical Industries, India's largest drugmaker, is banking on its innovative medicines portfolio and domestic formulations business to drive growth through FY27, with management indicating that specialty products, new launches and pipeline expansion will remain its key growth engines.
The innovative medicines portfolio grew 12.8 percent year-on-year to $351 million in the June quarter and now contributes nearly 22 percent of consolidated sales, reinforcing its growing importance in Sun Pharma's revenue mix.
Sun Pharma on Friday reported a 27 percent year-on-year increase in consolidated net profit to Rs 2,894 crore for the quarter ended June 2026, aided by strong growth in its India formulations business and continued momentum in its global innovative medicines portfolio.
During the first-quarter earnings call, management said growth in the innovative medicines business would be driven by established brands such as Ilumya, Cequa and Odomzo, alongside recently launched products Leqselvi and Unloxcyt.
"We are expecting healthy growth to continue for innovative business in the US, driven by new launches," the management said, highlighting both Unloxcyt and Ilumya as key contributors.
Early launch metrics have been encouraging. Leqselvi crossed 1,000 prescribers in June and recorded its strongest month since launch, while Unloxcyt continues to secure formulary additions at cancer centres and integrated health systems. Sun said both products are witnessing month-on-month growth as physician confidence and patient access improve.
Leqselvi (deuruxolitinib) is an oral Janus kinase inhibitor used to treat severe hair loss caused by alopecia areata, while Unloxcyt (cosibelimab-ipdl) is an intravenous PD-L1 immunotherapy used to treat advanced skin cancer.
India business remains a key growth driver
The domestic formulations business continued to outperform, with sales rising 16 percent year-on-year. Management attributed the growth to broad-based performance across therapy areas, expansion of the field force and strong prescription generation.
About half of the domestic growth came from higher volumes and new product launches, indicating market share gains rather than price-led expansion.
Retains outlook
Sun Pharma management retained its full-year outlook despite a strong June quarter, signalling a measured stance on the rest of FY27.
CFO Jayashree Satagopan said the company would “stick on to the high single digit growth” guidance for the full year, cautioning that currency movements could influence reported numbers over the coming quarters.
Things to lookout
A key area to watch through FY27 will be semaglutide. Sun has rapidly established itself as the number two generic semaglutide injector player in India and is the only company offering the drug through an auto-injector device. Management said the product has received positive feedback from doctors and patients because it reduces needle anxiety and simplifies initiation.
The company is now taking the playbook overseas. Regulatory approvals have been secured in South Africa and Brazil, with the South African launch already underway and the Brazil rollout expected shortly through a partner. Importantly, management sounded confident on supply readiness. “We are well prepared,” it said, noting that API production, formulation manufacturing and device-component sourcing are all secured in-house or through established partnerships.
On the strategic front, all eyes remain on the proposed Organon acquisition. Sun said regulatory filings across markets have been completed, approvals have already been received in some countries, and Organon shareholders approved the transaction in July. The company reiterated that the deal remains on track for closure by early 2027, with an Integration Management Office already working on Day One preparedness.
“We expect the acquisition to be completed in Q4 of financial year ’27,” Dilip Shanghvi, Sun Pharma chairman said.
The Upcoming catalysts include Ilumya’s USFDA decision in psoriatic arthritis, GL0034 Phase-2 data in diabetes and potential regulatory progress for Nidlegy and Fibromun.
Nidlegy and Fibromun are targeted biopharmaceutical cancer treatments developed by Philogen and partnered globally with Sun Pharma, focusing on advanced skin cancers and soft-tissue sarcomas.

input.title: Sun Pharma: Q1 FY27 Consolidated Sales Rise 10.1% to ₹151,836 Million
input.content:
Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Limited announced its Q1 FY27 results, reporting consolidated sales of ₹151,836 million, a 10.1% increase year-over-year. Net profit for the quarter rose to ₹28,948 million. Key growth drivers included strong performance in India and the Innovative Medicines segment, with global sales showing robust momentum.
Sun Pharma Reports Strong Q1 FY27 Financials
Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Limited has released its financial results for the first quarter of FY27, ending June 30, 2026. The company reported consolidated sales of ₹151,836 million, marking a significant year-over-year growth of 10.1%. This performance underscores the company’s expanding market presence and product demand.
Key Financial Highlights
The net profit for the quarter reached ₹28,948 million, indicating a healthy increase in profitability. The company’s EBITDA stood at ₹44,177 million, with an EBITDA margin of 28.9%. Adjusted net profit was reported at ₹30,894 million, reflecting a growth of 3.1%. R&D investments for the quarter amounted to ₹8,264 million, representing 5.4% of sales.
Performance Drivers and Segmental Insights
Kirti Ganorkar, Managing Director, attributed the quarter’s performance to strong momentum in India and the Innovative Medicines division, which saw robust growth in the U.S. and international markets. India Formulations sales grew by 16% to ₹54,749 million, contributing 36.1% of total consolidated sales. Sun Pharma maintains its position as India’s No. 1 pharmaceutical company. U.S. Formulations sales were US$ 427 million, while Emerging Markets contributed US$ 311 million, up 4.2%. Rest of World Formulations recorded sales of US$ 218 million.
Innovative Medicines and R&D
Global Innovative Medicines sales increased by 12.8% to US$ 351 million, accounting for 21.9% of total sales. The company’s R&D pipeline continues to be a strategic focus, with ongoing investments in novel entities and a comprehensive product offering in the U.S. market. The update also provided details on the progress of the proposed acquisition by Sun of Organon, with an indicative closure expected by Q4FY27.
Source: BSE

input.title: Cyient CFO Expects Better Q2 Sales And Broad-Based Margin Recovery Ahead
input.content:
Cyient CFO Expects Better Q2 Sales And Broad-Based Margin Recovery Ahead
Cyient's CFO has outlined positive growth and margin recovery expectations for the coming quarters (as stated in the source alert; not independently verified). This strategic optimism is backed by the company's Q1 FY27 performance, which saw sequential recovery in consolidated revenues to ₹2,075.7 crore and a notable rise in operating margins.
Market snapshot: Cyient's Chief Financial Officer expects sales in Q2 to outperform Q1, with the October to March period yielding significantly higher revenue than April to September (as stated in the source alert; not independently verified). Additionally, margins are projected to recover in coming quarters, with steady growth holding in the key aerospace vertical (as stated in the source alert; not independently verified). This outlook follows the company's recent Q1 FY27 earnings, where sequential net profits jumped 89.96% to ₹104.1 crore.
Data Snapshot
- Consolidated Net Profit (PAT) grew 89.96% sequentially to ₹104.1 crore in Q1 FY27.
- Consolidated operating revenue grew 7.72% sequentially to ₹2,075.7 crore in Q1 FY27.
- Core Digital Engineering and Technology (DET) segment revenue rose 2.7% QoQ to ₹1,540 crore.
- Core DET segment EBIT margin expanded sequentially by 79 basis points to 13.2% in Q1 FY27.
What's Changed
- Consolidated net profit fell to ₹104.1 crore in Q1 FY27 from ₹153.8 crore in Q1 FY26, representing a de-growth of 32.31% YoY (derived: ₹104.1 crore vs ₹153.8 crore).
- Consolidated operating revenue rose to ₹2,075.7 crore in Q1 FY27 from ₹1,711.8 crore in Q1 FY26, representing a growth of 21.26% YoY (derived: ₹2,075.7 crore vs ₹1,711.8 crore).
Key Takeaways
- Profitability rebounded strongly on a sequential basis, with consolidated PAT surging 89.96% QoQ to ₹104.1 crore.
- Operating margins in the core Digital Engineering and Technology segment improved to 13.2% (+79bps QoQ) on cost management.
- Forward sales expectations are optimistic with Q2 seen outperforming Q1 and H2 projected to be seasonally stronger than H1 (as stated in the source alert; not independently verified).
- Steady sales traction is projected for the aerospace vertical at current levels, supporting broad-based margin recovery ahead (as stated in the source alert; not independently verified).
SAHI Perspective
Cyient's Q1 FY27 sequential performance indicates that its operational cost-rationalization programs are bearing fruit, driven by sequential EBIT margin expansion to 13.2% in the core DET segment. While the year-on-year bottom-line decline shows a lingering high-base challenge, the CFO's confident forward execution roadmap for Q2 and H2 (as stated in the source alert; not independently verified) should stabilize growth expectations. The successful conclusion of its ₹720 crore buyback program further aligns with the management's focus on capital efficiency.
Market Implications
The positive sequential recovery, paired with robust forward projections for H2 sales and margins (as stated in the source alert; not independently verified), is expected to offer a floor to Cyient's stock valuations. Continuous structural stability in the high-value aerospace division reduces dependency on volatile discretionary IT spending segments.
Trading Signals
Market Bias: Bullish
The bias is supported by a sharp 89.96% QoQ rebound in consolidated net profit to ₹104.1 crore and a 79 bps QoQ expansion in DET segment EBIT margins to 13.2% in Q1 FY27. Positive qualitative CFO commentary on Q2 sales and coming margin recovery (as stated in the source alert; not independently verified) adds momentum.
Overweight: IT Services, Engineering R&D Services
Trigger Factors:
- Sustaining the core DET segment EBIT margin above the 13% mark.
- Ramping up order intakes in the critical aerospace and transportation verticals.
Time Horizon: Medium-term (3-12 months)
Industry Context
The global Engineering Research & Development (ER&D) sector has faced pressure due to client decision delays. Cyient's business mix, anchored heavily in the safety-critical aerospace and transportation segments, provides a strong layer of defense relative to traditional IT service models.
Key Risks to Watch
- Sustained delays or slowdowns in client discretionary spending in weaker divisions like energy.
- Rupee appreciation impacting the realization of export-heavy revenues.
Recent Developments
In July 2026, Cyient announced its Q1 FY27 financial performance, highlighting a robust sequential performance. The company also recently concluded its ₹720 crore share buyback program via tender offer at ₹1,125 per share.
Closing Insight
With operating margins improving on cost optimization and a solid sequential recovery under its belt, Cyient is well-positioned. If the CFO's outlook of sequential sales acceleration and H2 performance gains materializes (as stated in the source alert; not independently verified), it will pave the way for a more sustainable valuation rerating.

input.title: Sun Pharma Near Record High Ahead of Q1 Results: Can Earnings Keep the Rally Alive?
input.content:
Quick Snapshot
- Sun Pharma will announce Q1 FY27 (April–June 2026) results on Friday, July 31, 2026, followed by an earnings call at 6:30 pm IST the same day.
- Brokerages peg Q1 revenue between ₹15,280 crore and ₹15,364 crore, up 10–11% YoY, while net profit is projected to fall 7–11% YoY on margin pressure.
- India formulations are seen growing in double digits even as the US generics business stays largely flat.
- The stock touched a fresh 52-week high of ₹2,017.25 on July 30, a day ahead of results, taking market cap to nearly ₹4.80 lakh crore.
- Organon shareholders have cleared their side of the $11.75-billion acquisition; regulatory approvals and integration progress remain the key overhang beyond the headline print.
Sun Pharmaceutical Industries shares scaled a fresh 52-week high of ₹2,017.25 on the BSE on July 30, just one trading session before the country’s largest drugmaker opens its Q1 FY27 earnings. The stock closed the day at ₹2,000.75 on the BSE, up 0.55%, and at ₹2,001.10 on the NSE, up 0.56%, with the day’s ₹1,988–₹2,017 range brushing against the 52-week band on both exchanges. Market capitalisation stood at roughly ₹4.80 lakh crore heading into the print.
Check Live: SUN PHARMACEUTICAL INDUSTRIES Share Price Chart
Why This Quarter Matters
Sun Pharma enters FY27 coming off its strongest annual sales and profit on record, FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹58,220 crore and net profit of ₹11,479 crore, both the highest in the company’s history per its own investor disclosures (see the five-year trend below).
With the stock now at a fresh 52-week high, investor attention is shifting from the quarterly print itself toward whether specialty medicines, India formulations and the pending Organon integration can sustain this next leg of growth. A miss on margins or cautious FY27 commentary could trigger sharper-than-usual volatility precisely because expectations, and the valuation, are already stretched.
When Will Sun Pharma Announce Q1 FY27 Results?
Sun Pharma confirmed via an exchange filing that it will announce results for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, on Friday, July 31, 2026. Management will host an hour-long earnings call at 6:30 pm IST the same day, with dial-in access via +91 22 6629 0049 or +91 22 7194 5729, an audio webcast, and a transcript to follow on the company website.
In the run-up, the company has filed a string of Regulation 30 disclosures with exchanges, an analyst/investor meet intimation on July 14, press releases on July 15 and July 24, and a mandatory newspaper publication notice on July 28, a fairly routine sequence ahead of a quarterly print.
Check More: SUN PHARMACEUTICAL INDUSTRIES Options Chart
Q1 FY27 Estimates: What Brokerages Expect
Analysts expect decent topline growth for the April-June quarter, driven by strong domestic performance, even as the US generic business stays largely flat and EM/RoW markets deliver healthy growth on branded generics and innovative products. Margin pressure from elevated input costs is expected to weigh on profitability, with average estimates pointing to a 7-11% YoY profit decline.
Source: Brokerage estimates compiled by Business Standard, July 29, 2026.
HDFC Securities attributes the muted US performance to the absence of gRevlimid contribution this year, while pegging India business growth at around 13% YoY. Kotak Institutional Equities expects gross margins to slip 60 basis points sequentially to 80.2%, with EBITDA growing 6% YoY even as margins contract 120 basis points to 28.2%.
Key Growth Drivers To Watch
Beyond the quarterly print, the performance of the recently-acquired Organon portfolio and progress on integrating the acquisition will be a key monitorable for analysts, according to MOFSL.
Sun Pharma agreed in April 2026 to acquire Organon in an all-cash deal valued at an enterprise value of $11.75 billion, its largest-ever acquisition, with Organon shareholders approving the transaction on July 24, 2026.
The deal, expected to close by early 2027 pending regulatory approvals, brings Organon’s women’s health, biosimilars and established-medicines portfolio, spread across more than 140 countries, into Sun Pharma’s fold, and is expected to lift combined annual revenue to roughly $12.4 billion.
Separately, the company’s specialty franchise in dermatology, ophthalmology and onco-dermatology continues to anchor its Global Innovative Medicines business, which the company says accounts for roughly a fifth of total sales.
Also Check: Nifty Pharma index constituents and performance
Key Risks And Overhangs
Margin pressure is the near-term drag analysts are flagging most consistently. HDFC Securities specifically cites cost escalation from higher input and freight costs as the reason it expects EBITDA margin to hold near 28.2%.
On the regulatory side, Sun Pharma received USFDA observations for its Dadra facility in June 2026, which management has characterised as largely procedural, with regulatory focus centred on remediation at both the Mohali and Dadra plants following recent inspections.
Any commentary on this during Friday’s call, alongside execution and financing details on the Organon deal, will likely matter as much to the stock as the headline revenue-profit print.
What Investors Should Watch
Sun Pharma’s Five-Year Financial Trend
Source: Sun Pharma investor presentation, FY22–FY26 consolidated financials.
On the valuation side, the stock’s consolidated TTM EPS of ₹47.97 and consolidated PE of 41.71 line up closely with the FY26 EPS of ₹47.8 above, while ROE stands at 11.16% and price-to-book at 20.35, per BSE data. Day turnover on the counter stood at ₹24.20 crore on July 30.
Also Read: Cipla Q1 FY27 results coverage
NiftyTrader Desk View
Source: BSE/NSE price data, July 30, 2026 close.
What To Watch After Results
Beyond revenue and profit, watch for management’s FY27 growth guidance, EBITDA margin trajectory, specialty sales momentum, any fresh update on the Dadra/Mohali USFDA status, and confirmation of regulatory progress on the Organon deal.
Track real-time institutional positioning ahead of the print on the NiftyTrader FII-DII Tracker.
Bottom Line
Sun Pharma heads into its Q1 FY27 results at a fresh 52-week high, with brokerages broadly aligned on low-double-digit revenue growth led by India formulations, offset by a YoY profit dip on margin pressure and a tough US comparison. The numbers themselves may matter less than management’s tone on Organon’s integration timeline and the regulatory status of its Dadra and Mohali plants.

input.title: Novartis India Limited Appoints Pharma Veteran Dr Vikas Gupta as MD, CEO
input.content:
Novartis India Limited Appoints Pharma Veteran Dr Vikas Gupta as MD, CEO
Mumbai: Dr Vikas Gupta has been appointed as new Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Novartis India Limited. He assumed the role in July 2026 and will lead the company's strategic growth, commercial operations, and healthcare innovation initiatives.
Novartis India Limited (NIL) is a publicly listed pharmaceutical company in India and is part of ChrysCapital, India’s leading Private Equity firm. NIL has a long-standing presence in the Indian healthcare sector and is engaged primarily in the marketing, distribution, and sale of pharmaceutical products across key therapeutic areas. The company is listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange and the National Stock Exchange of India . Headquartered in Mumbai, NIL focuses on bringing innovative and established medicines to patients and healthcare professionals throughout India.
Dr Gupta brings more than two decades of experience in the pharmaceutical industry, with a career spanning leadership positions across major Indian and multinational drug companies.
Before joining Novartis India, Dr Gupta served as Chief Executive Officer at Alkem Laboratories from September 2023 to July 2026. Prior to that, he spent nearly six years at Cipla, where he held senior leadership roles including India Rx Head and Senior Vice President.
Also Read: Novartis Signs USD 1.5 Billion Deal to Buy UK-Based Cancer Drug Developer Myricx Bio
A substantial part of his career was spent at Glenmark Pharmaceuticals, where he served in multiple leadership positions over an eight-year period, including Senior Vice President - Chronic Care, Vice President, and General Manager. During his tenure, he was responsible for large-scale business operations across therapeutic areas such as anti-infectives, respiratory care, and metabolic disorders. He also led sizeable sales and marketing teams and managed businesses with significant revenue responsibilities.
Earlier in his career, Dr Gupta worked at Ranbaxy Laboratories, holding positions including Head Sales - Ranbaxy Solus, Senior Manager Marketing, Country Manager for Myanmar, and Senior Brand Manager. His international assignment in Myanmar involved overseeing business operations, managing profitability and revenue targets, coordinating with regulatory and distribution stakeholders, and leading cross-functional teams.
Dr Vikas Gupta began his career at GTB Hospital, which provided the early foundation for his journey in healthcare and pharmaceuticals
According to his professional profile, Dr Gupta has extensive expertise in business transformation, sales and marketing strategy, commercial leadership, brand development, and organizational growth. His experience includes business expansion, market development and leading growth initiatives across established pharmaceuticals businesses,

input.title: ChrysCapital completes acquisition of controlling stake in Novartis India Limited; Vikas Gupta appointed MD & CEO
input.content:
ChrysCapital completes acquisition of controlling stake in Novartis India Limited; Vikas Gupta appointed MD & CEO
ADVERTISEMENT
Private equity firm ChrysCapital has completed the acquisition of a controlling 70.68% stake in Novartis India Ltd (NIL), marking its first majority-controlled investment in India's pharmaceutical sector.
The transaction, announced by the company on Wednesday, transfers control of the BSE-listed drugmaker from Swiss pharmaceutical major Novartis AG to ChrysCapital. The companies did not disclose the financial details of the transaction.
As part of the ownership transition, Novartis India has appointed Dr. Vikas Gupta as its Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer. The company also announced the appointment of Ramesh Ramadurai as Chairperson of the board, while Suchita Sharma and Shashank Sinha have joined as independent directors.
The acquisition signals ChrysCapital's entry into the branded pharmaceuticals space through majority ownership. The private equity firm said it intends to build a leading branded generics platform focused on the Indian market by leveraging the company's established portfolio and healthcare presence.
Novartis India has operated in the country for several decades and markets brands including Voveran, Calcium Sandoz and Tegrital across therapeutic areas such as pain management, calcium supplementation, gynaecology, neurosciences and transplant immunology.
"NIL has earned its place in Indian healthcare over many decades. Today we begin a new and exciting chapter in NIL's history. We carry forward decades of scientific rigour and physician trust—from that strong foundation and with ChrysCapital's backing we have the resources and focus to grow our portfolio with purpose, reach more patients, and build on what this organisation has always stood for," said Dr. Vikas Gupta, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer.
Kshitij Sheth, Managing Director at ChrysCapital Advisors, said the appointment of Gupta provides the company with the leadership required for its next phase of growth. "Combined with NIL's legacy brands and market standing, ChrysCapital believes the foundation for long-term value creation is firmly in place," he said.
The company said it will adopt a new name and corporate identity following its separation from Novartis AG, signalling the start of a new phase under ChrysCapital's ownership.
The acquisition follows the completion of ChrysCapital's purchase of Novartis AG's controlling stake in the listed company. However, the companies did not disclose the value of the deal or provide a timeline for the planned corporate rebranding.

input.title: Sun Pharma shares hit 52-week high as Brazil clears semaglutide injection for diabetes treatment
input.content:
Sun Pharma shares hit 52-week high as Brazil clears semaglutide injection for diabetes treatment
ADVERTISEMENT
Shares of Sun Pharmaceutical Industries hit 52-week high on Thursday after the company received regulatory approval in Brazil to manufacture and market its semaglutide injection for the treatment of adults with inadequately controlled Type 2 diabetes.
Cheering the news, Sun Pharma shares climbed as much as 1.36% to hit a new 52-week high of ₹2,017 on the BSE, taking its market capitalisation to over ₹4.82 lakh crore. The pharma heavyweight has rebounded 30% from its 52-week low of 1,547.25 on September 26, 2025. The stock has risen 17% in the calendar year 2026, while it added over 8% in a month.
In an exchange filing last evening, Sun Pharma said it has secured approval from the Brazilian Health Regulatory Agency (ANVISA) for its semaglutide injection, which will be used as an adjunct to diet and exercise for adults with inadequately controlled Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
The company plans to launch the product in Brazil over the next few days in partnership with Hypera Pharma, one of the country's leading pharmaceutical companies.
The drug will be available as a pre-filled, multi-dose injectable pen in two strengths - 2 mg/1.5 mL and 4 mg/3 mL - enabling flexible, once-weekly dosing.
"The approval of semaglutide in Brazil expands access to an evidence-based treatment option for people living with inadequately controlled Type 2 diabetes. It reflects the strength of our development and manufacturing capabilities and our commitment to delivering high-quality medicines across global markets," said Aalok Shanghvi, Chief Operating Officer, Sun Pharma.
Digvijay Singh, Regional Head, Brazil & LATAM, said the approval strengthens the company's diabetes portfolio in one of Latin America's largest pharmaceutical markets.
"This approval marks an important step in strengthening our diabetes portfolio in Brazil. We look forward to working closely with our partner to make this treatment option available to patients and support better diabetes care across the country," he said.
According to the company, the Brazilian semaglutide injectable market is valued at around $413 million, based on IQVIA MAT data for June 2026.
In a separate development, Sun Pharma last week informed stock exchanges that shareholders of Organon & Co. had approved proposals related to the company's proposed acquisition by Sun Pharmaceutical Holdings USA, an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of Sun Pharma. The shareholder nod marks a key milestone in the $11.75-billion all-cash deal announced in April, although the transaction remains subject to customary closing conditions, including regulatory approvals.
The acquisition is expected to close in early 2027 and will strengthen Sun Pharma's position among the world's top 25 pharmaceutical companies, with combined annual revenue of around $12.4 billion. It will also make the company a top-three player globally in women's health and among the top seven in biosimilars.
Organon, which was spun off from Merck (MSD outside the U.S. and Canada) in 2021, operates in over 140 countries and reported revenue of $6.2 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $1.9 billion for 2025.

input.title: ChrysCapital acquires Novartis India, appoints Vikas Gupta as CEO
input.content:
ChrysCapital acquires Novartis India, appoints Vikas Gupta as CEO
The private equity firm has taken control of the BSE-listed drugmaker, appointed Vikas Gupta as CEO and plans to build a branded generics platform in India
Listen to This Article
	Private equity firm ChrysCapital has completed the acquisition of a controlling 70.68 per cent stake in Novartis India from Swiss drugmaker Novartis AG, marking its first majority-controlled investment in India's pharmaceutical sector.
 
	The acquisition, announced on Thursday, gives ChrysCapital control of the BSE-listed company, which has a long-established portfolio of branded medicines across pain management, calcium supplementation, gynaecology, neurosciences and transplant immunology. Its brands include Voveran, Calcium Sandoz and Tegrital.
 
	Following the change in ownership, the company has appointed Vikas Gupta as chief executive officer and managing director to lead its next phase of growth. It has also appointed Ramesh Ramadurai, Suchita Sharma and Shashank Sinha as independent directors on its board.
 
	ChrysCapital said the company would adopt a new name and corporate identity as it separates from its former parent and seeks to build a leading branded generics platform in India.
 
	“This investment reflects our conviction in the long-term growth potential of India's branded pharmaceuticals market,” Kshitij Sheth, managing director at ChrysCapital Advisors, said in a statement, adding that the company was well positioned for long-term value creation under its new leadership.
Also Read
	Gupta said the company would build on its legacy of scientific rigour and physician trust while expanding its product portfolio and patient reach with ChrysCapital's backing.
	The transaction is among the largest recent private equity investments in India's pharmaceutical sector and follows Novartis AG's decision to divest its controlling stake in the listed Indian subsidiary as part of its global portfolio strategy.
 
	For the transaction, Kotak acted as the exclusive financial adviser to Novartis AG, while Freshfields and AZB & Partners served as legal advisers. Shardul Amarchand Mangaldas & Co advised ChrysCapital on the legal aspects of the deal, with Alvarez & Marsal, Dhruva Advisors and Price Waterhouse & Co acting as financial and tax advisers.
 
	Founded in 1999, ChrysCapital has raised about $8.5 billion across its investment funds and invested more than $5.6 billion in over 110 transactions across sectors, including healthcare, financial services, technology and manufacturing.

input.title: Sun Pharma Shares In Focus After Securing Entry into $400M+ Brazilian Diabetes Market
input.content:
Synopsis: One of India's largest pharmaceutical companies has received a major international regulatory approval that opens the doors to a fast-growing diabetes market worth over $400 million. The development not only expands its global diabetes portfolio but also strengthens its presence in Latin America through a strategic commercial partnership.
Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd. said it has received approval from Brazil’s health regulator, ANVISA, for the manufacture and marketing of the drug semaglutide injection for adults with inadequately controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus. This is another important milestone in its international speciality and diabetes business, as the company plans to launch the product commercially in the next few days through its partnership with Hypera Pharma.
Shares of Sun Pharmaceutical IndustriesLimited were trading at Rs 2,014.5, up by 1.22 percent from the previous close of Rs 1,989.9. The stock opened at an intraday high of Rs 2,014.4, with a day's low of Rs 1,988. The company currently has a market capitalisation of Rs 4,82,746 crore.
Brazil Approval Opens a Significant Growth Opportunity
The approval allows Sun Pharma to manufacture and commercialise semaglutide injection in Brazil as an adjunct to diet and exercise for adults whose Type 2 diabetes remains inadequately controlled.
The product will be launched as a pre-filled, multi-dose injectable pen in two dosage strengths—2 mg/1.5 mL and 4 mg/3 mL—enabling patients to receive once-weekly dosing, a treatment approach that has gained widespread acceptance globally because of its convenience and proven clinical efficacy.
Commercialisation will be through a partnership with one of Brazil’s leading pharmaceutical companies, Hypera Pharma. This will enable Sun Pharma to benefit from an established distribution network and accelerate market penetration after product launch.
Why Brazil Matters
The significance of the announcement extends far beyond a routine regulatory approval. The company said that the Brazilian market for the injectable diabetes drug semaglutide is worth about USD 413 million, making it one of the most attractive diabetes therapy markets in Latin America. Diabetes remains a global issue and the need for improved GLP-1 treatments like semaglutide has exploded. These medications are very effective at controlling blood sugar levels, and are administered weekly.
By entering this market, Sun Pharma strengthens its presence in a high-value therapeutic category while expanding its footprint across emerging international markets, an important pillar of the company's long-term growth strategy.
Why This Opportunity Could Be Bigger Than It Appears
The approval further broadens Sun Pharma's international diabetes franchise and highlights its growing capabilities in developing and manufacturing complex injectable therapies. Through its collaboration with Hypera Pharma, Sun aims to improve the availability of evidence-based diabetes treatment for patients across Brazil.
Unlike a conventional product approval, semaglutide represents one of the fastest-growing therapeutic categories globally. The GLP-1 receptor agonists segment has emerged as a growing segment of the diabetes treatment market, owing to the superior efficacy and patient convenience. Sun Pharma has secured regulatory approval to expand into Brazil, a large and fast-growing market where it has an existing commercial partner.
“More importantly, the approval underscores the company’s ability to successfully navigate complex international regulatory pathways for advanced injectable therapies.” These capabilities will strengthen its competitive positioning in Latin America and possibly facilitate future expansion into other regulated markets as demand for innovative diabetes therapies continues to grow.
Strategic Insight
The Brazil approval supports Sun Pharma's strategy of diversifying into high-value speciality and complex pharmaceuticals. Entering a USD 413 million market boosts the company's long-term international growth, but the immediate financial contribution depends on commercial adoption after launch.
Combined with its manufacturing capabilities and partnership-led market access strategy, the approval reinforces Sun Pharma's ability to scale differentiated products across key global markets.
Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Limited is India's largest pharmaceutical company and one of the world's leading specialty and generic drug manufacturers. The company operates in innovative medicines, generics and consumer healthcare, with a presence in over 100 countries. Its specialty portfolio spans dermatology, ophthalmology and onco-dermatology, while its vertically integrated manufacturing network supports the supply of high-quality medicines across global markets.

	According to IQVIA data cited by the company, Brazil's semaglutide injectable market was valued at about $413 million for the 12 months ended June 2026.

It reflects the strength of our development and manufacturing capabilities and our commitment to delivering high-quality medicines across global markets.”

input.title: Cyient: Q1 FY27 Revenue Flat, EBIT Up Marginally on Strong DET Performance
input.content:
Cyient Limited reported Q1 FY27 results with revenue at $219 million, a 4.5% sequential increase and 9.1% year-on-year in constant currency. DET segment revenue was $162.5 million, down 0.5% sequentially. EBIT margin improved to 13.2% driven by cost optimization and a stronger USD. The company also provided updates on the TAO Digital Solutions acquisition and detailed segment performance.
Cyient Reports Q1 FY27 Performance
Cyient Limited announced its financial results for the first quarter of Fiscal Year 2027 (Q1 FY27), concluding on June 30, 2026. The company reported group revenue of $219 million, marking a 4.5% increase sequentially and a 9.1% rise year-on-year in constant currency. In INR terms, group revenue was Rs.2076 Crores, up 7.7% quarter-on-quarter and 21.3% year-on-year.
Segment Performance Highlights
The DET (Digital, Engineering, and Technology) segment reported Q1 revenue of $162.5 million. This represents a 0.5% sequential decline and a 0.9% decrease year-on-year in constant currency. In INR, DET revenue was Rs.1540 Crores, up 2.7% quarter-on-quarter and 10.6% year-on-year. The EBIT margin for DET improved by 79 basis points sequentially and 114 basis points year-on-year to 13.2%.
Semiconductor and DLM Updates
The semiconductor business, which now includes Kinetic Technologies, saw its first quarter of consolidation. The combined revenue from Cyient and Kinetic Technologies was $17.9 million. The organic semiconductor business grew 5% quarter-on-quarter. The company also provided an update on the custom ASIC business with a pipeline of over $100 million and advancements in compound semiconductor initiatives, including seven new GaN powered chips. Cyient DLM reported its highest ever order book, supported by strong order inflow and a book-to-bill ratio exceeding 1.5. It also achieved sustained double-digit EBITDA margins for four consecutive quarters.
Financial and Strategic Developments
Cyient successfully completed its share buyback program, extinguishing 6.4 million equity shares. The company also announced significant progress on the acquisition of TAO Digital Solutions, with closing expected by August 2026. A financing agreement was signed with EAAA at a post-money valuation of $500 million, with $30 million of fresh capital raised. The company anticipates its EBIT target of 15% might be achieved slightly later than previously planned, possibly in H1 of next year.
Outlook and Investor Day
Management expressed optimism about the future, citing strong order book momentum and ongoing efforts in cost optimization and strategic investments. An Investor Day is scheduled for August 25, 2026, in Mumbai, where detailed discussions on strategy and growth priorities will take place.

Vikran Engineering has successfully commissioned the 132 kV Miao–Namsai transmission line in Arunachal Pradesh. - The project covers a span of approximately 41 km and was executed for the Power Grid Corporation of India Limited (PGCIL). - This completion strengthens the company’s execution track record, backed by a robust consolidated order book crossing ₹5,000 crore as of March 31, 2026.
Hirect secures maiden US traction motor order
Hirect Ltd (Formerly known as Hind Rectifiers Ltd) has secured its first order from the United States for traction motor assemblies, marking the company’s initial entry into the US market. This order, scheduled for execution in the 2026-2027 financial year, establishes a critical foothold in North America as the company pursues aggressive international expansion.

Sun Pharma wins marketing approval for semaglutide in Brazil
                    The product approved for the treatment of Type 2 diabetes, will be launched in the next few days in partnership with a local player Hypera Pharma.
                                    
            
        
                    
                    
                    
                                        Mumbai: Indian pharma major, Sun Pharmaceutical Industries has received approval from the Brazilian Health Regulatory Agency, ANVISA to manufacture and market its generic semaglutide injection in Brazil. 
The product is approved for the treatment of Type 2 diabetes and will be available as a pre‑filled, multi‑dose injectable pen in two strengths —2 mg and 4 mg.
Sun Pharma plans to launch the product in the next few days through a local partnership with Hypera Pharma.
Semaglutide, a blockbuster GLP-1 receptor against has lost its patent protection across multiple markets, such as Canada, India, Brazil etc, and generic drugmakers across the globe are rushing to ride the surge of the world’s fastest-growing therapeutic space.
As of June this year, Brazil’s semaglutide injectable market is estimated to be around $413 million according to IQVIA.
Sun Pharma is among the first wave of companies to enter the market and will face competition from several generic manufacturers, including Swiss major, Sandoz, whose brand ‘Owozy’ is also approved for distribution in the country.
Earlier this month, the company received approval to market the product in South Africa. Timeline for expansion into other target markets is yet to be disclosed.
“The approval of semaglutide in Brazil reflects the strength of our development and manufacturing capabilities to deliver high-quality medicines across global markets,” said Aalok Shanghvi, COO, Sun Pharma.
In India, the Mumbai-based drugmaker markets two brand Noveltreat (for weight-loss) and Sematrinity (for Type 2 diabetes). According to the latest industry estimates, the two brands have collectively racked up around Rs 13 crore from with net sales of 64,000 units since their launch in March.

input.title: ChrysCapital takes control of Novartis India, names Dr Vikas Gupta as MD & CEO
input.content:
Leadership
ChrysCapital takes control of Novartis India, names Dr Vikas Gupta as MD & CEO
Following its ₹1,376.8 crore acquisition of a controlling stake in Novartis India, ChrysCapital has appointed a new leadership team to drive the company's next phase of growth in branded generics.
ChrysCapital has completed the acquisition of a 70.68% controlling stake in Novartis India Limited (NIL) for ₹1,376.8 crore, marking its first majority-controlled investment in India's pharmaceutical sector.
Following the transaction, the private equity firm has appointed Dr Vikas Gupta as Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, signalling a leadership transition as the company prepares for its next phase of growth.
According to reporting by ScanX, the ownership change was announced on July 29, 2026, alongside the appointment of a new Board, with Ramesh Ramadurai taking over as Chairperson.
Leadership team takes charge after ownership change
The acquisition brings a refreshed leadership structure to Novartis India.
The new appointments include:
- Dr Vikas Gupta as Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer.
- Ramesh Ramadurai as Chairperson and Independent Director.
- Suchita Sharma as Independent Director.
- Shashank Sinha as Independent Director.
ChrysCapital plans to build Novartis India into a leading branded generics platform focused on the Indian market.
Commenting on his appointment, Dr Vikas Gupta said the company has built a strong legacy in Indian healthcare and will now begin a new phase backed by ChrysCapital's resources and strategic focus.
Deal marks ChrysCapital's entry into majority-controlled pharma investments
The acquisition represents ChrysCapital's first majority-controlled investment in the Indian pharmaceutical industry.
The acquiring consortium comprises:
- WaveRise Investments Limited
- ChrysCapital Fund X
- Two Infinity Partners
Following completion of the transaction, the shareholding structure is as follows:
ChrysCapital X, LLC and OceanEdge Investments Limited have been classified as Persons Acting in Concert (PACs) but do not directly hold shares.
Novartis AG exits promoter role
The transaction follows the exit of Novartis AG as the company's promoter.
Novartis AG transferred 1,74,50,680 equity shares through an off-market transaction dated February 19, 2026.
Following the sale:
- Novartis AG no longer holds shares in Novartis India.
- The company has been reclassified from the 'promoter' category to the 'public' category under Regulation 31A(10) of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015.
- The acquisition disclosures were made under Regulation 29 of the SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011.
Company prepares for next phase
Novartis India operates across therapeutic segments including:
- Pain management.
- Calcium supplementation.
- Gynaecology.
- Neurosciences.
- Transplant immunology.
Its portfolio includes brands such as Voveran, Calcium Sandoz and Tegrital.
The company also plans to adopt a new corporate identity and name following its separation from Novartis AG.
Kshitij Sheth, Managing Director at ChrysCapital Advisors, said the new management team will play a central role in executing the company's growth strategy.
With a new ownership structure, refreshed leadership team and plans to strengthen its branded generics business, Novartis India is entering a new chapter under ChrysCapital's stewardship.

input.title: ChrysCapital acquires a controlling stake in Novartis India, appoints new CEO
input.content:
Private equity firm ChrysCapital has acquired a 70.68% stake in the listed pharmaceutical trading and distribution company Novartis India Ltd (NIL) and has appointed Vikas Gupta as the new chief executive and managing director.
While the financial details of the deal haven't been disclosed, the transaction is pegged at about ₹1,446 crore, a person with direct knowledge of the deal said on condition of anonymity. The deal was first announced in February.
With this transaction, NIL, previously held by Swiss multinational Novartis AG, will adopt a new name and corporate identity to mark the company’s separation from its previous owners and the beginning of a new era, the companies said in a statement on Thursday.
“With ChrysCapital’s backing, we have the resources and focus to grow our portfolio with purpose, reach more patients, and build on what this organization has always stood for,” Gupta said.
NIL has also inducted Ramesh Ramadurai, Suchita Sharma, and Shashank Sinha to the board as independent directors.
In February, Novartis clarified that it will continue its presence in India through Novartis Healthcare Pvt. Ltd (NHPL), a wholly owned subsidiary of the Novartis group in the country.
NHPL includes the commercial arm of Novartis in India, the Novartis Corporate Centre in Hyderabad, and research and development teams that currently conduct clinical trials at more than 300 sites in the country.
NIL is an independent public company listed in India and is separate from NHPL. The transfer of Novartis AG shareholding in NIL will not impact NHPL operations, the company had said.
ChrysCapital's entry into pharma
The acquisition marks ChrysCapital's first majority-controlled investment in the Indian pharmaceutical sector and reflects the firm's strong conviction in the long-term growth potential of the country's branded pharmaceuticals market.
“Combined with NIL's legacy brands and market standing, ChrysCapital believes the foundation for long-term value creation is firmly in place,” Kshitij Sheth, managing director of ChrysCapital Advisors, added.
The transaction brings one of the country's longstanding pharmaceutical businesses under dedicated private equity ownership, with the ambition to build a leading branded-generics platform for the country.
Building on a proven track record in healthcare investments, ChrysCapital aims to leverage its sector expertise and extensive network to support NIL's next phase of growth and strengthen its position as a leading pharmaceutical business.
With a legacy spanning several decades, NIL has a portfolio of brands that operate across key therapeutic areas, including pain management, calcium supplementation, gynaecology, neurosciences, and transplant immunology. The brands include Voveran, Calcium Sandoz, Tegrital, etc.
Kotak acted as the exclusive financial advisor, and Ernst & Young advised Novartis AG on financial and tax due diligence. Alvarez & Marsal, Dhruva Advisors and Price Waterhouse & Co. were the financial and tax advisors for ChrysCapital.

input.title: Novartis India appoints Vikas Gupta as MD, CEO, signs key brand deals
input.content:
Novartis India appoints Vikas Gupta as MD, CEO, signs key brand deals
Novartis India Limited has finalized its leadership transition by appointing Dr. Vikas Gupta as Managing Director and CEO and Bhagwat Singh Deora as CFO. The Board approved critical agreements with Novartis AG, including a royalty-free license for the Tegrital trademark and a five-year distribution deal, securing product continuity post-acquisition by the ChrysCapital consortium.
*this image is generated using AI for illustrative purposes only.
Novartis India Limited has completed its transition under new ownership by appointing Dr. Vikas Gupta as Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer and Bhagwat Singh Deora as Chief Financial Officer, effective July 29, 2026. The Board of Directors also approved critical commercial agreements with Novartis AG, including a royalty-free license for the Tegrital trademark and a five-year distribution agreement for pharmaceutical products, ensuring operational continuity after the ChrysCapital consortium acquired 70.68% of the equity share capital.
The appointments were made during the company’s 247th Board meeting held on July 29, 2026, in compliance with Regulation 30 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015. Dr. Gupta, who initially joined as Additional Director and CEO, was immediately redesignated as Managing Director and CEO, subject to shareholder approval. Mr. Deora, a Chartered Accountant with over 20 years of experience in the pharmaceutical sector, joins from JB Pharma. These leadership changes follow the resignation of six outgoing directors, including former Chairperson Christopher David Snook and CFO Shilpa Shashank Joshi, as part of the governance restructuring triggered by the change in control.
Strategic Agreements and Brand Continuity
To secure its product portfolio post-acquisition, Novartis India executed three key agreements with Novartis entities on July 29, 2026. The most significant is the Tegrital Brand License Deed, which grants the company an exclusive, irrevocable, royalty-free, and non-assignable license to use the 'Tegrital' trademark in India. Under this deed, Novartis AG must automatically assign the trademark to the company at no additional cost, provided there is no material breach by the company. This ensures uninterrupted manufacturing, marketing, and sales of the Tegrital range of pharmaceutical products.
Additionally, the company signed a Distribution Agreement with Novartis Pharma Services AG, appointing it as the exclusive distributor to import and sell certain pharmaceutical products in India. This agreement has an initial term of five years, extendable by another five years subject to mutual consent. Supply prices are fixed for the first year, with subsequent pricing determined by a mechanism outlined in the contract. A separate Trademark Assignment and License Deed transferred ownership of other key brands, including Voveran, Macalvit, and Citromacalvit, to the company on a royalty-free basis.
Leadership and Committee Reconstitution
The new management team includes several senior appointments aimed at stabilizing operations and driving growth. Besides Dr. Gupta and Mr. Deora, the company appointed Jason D'Souza as President – M&A, Business Development & Investor Relations; Rahul Vijayvargiya as Chief Human Resource Officer; Masud Shaikh as Chief Supply Chain Officer; and Sumeet Rajput as President – Business Operations. All appointments took effect on July 29, 2026.
The Board also reconstituted its Risk Management Committee and Stakeholders Relationship Committee to align with the new director lineup. Shashank Sinha chairs the Risk Management Committee, while Ashok Bhatia leads the Stakeholders Relationship Committee. The company has adopted a new corporate email domain (nilpharma.co.in) and website to reflect its rebranding under the new management.
What the Numbers Show
The acquisition of 17,450,680 equity shares by the ChrysCapital consortium (WaveRise Investments Limited and ChrysCapital Fund X) solidifies their control with a 70.68% stake, reducing Novartis AG’s holding below the 10% threshold required for promoter classification. The execution of royalty-free brand licenses and long-term distribution agreements mitigates immediate revenue risks associated with the ownership transition, allowing the new management to focus on operational integration rather than renegotiating core supply chains. The appointment of experienced executives from major Indian pharmaceutical firms signals a strategy to leverage domestic market expertise for future growth.

input.title: Hidden risks of UPI Autopay: Nykaa AVP’s LinkedIn post sparks debate about free trials
input.content:
Lokesh Ahuja, AVP at Nykaa, has shared a cautionary story on LinkedIn. He recently taught his mother how to use UPI payments. He came across something that rang an alarm bell. Scrolling through her phone later, Ahuja spotted several AutoPay mandates. She unknowingly subscribed to multiple services through free trials. These offered zero cost during the initial 30-day period. However, they automatically charged users afterwards unless cancelled promptly. “And most people never notice a ₹79 deduction. Because it quietly disappears inside an account statement with a hundred other UPI transactions. That's the real product behind a free trial. Not the first free month,” he wrote. Lokesh Ahuja reflected on shifting parental concerns across generations. Parents once worried about children crossing roads safely. Now, children worry about their parents navigating the internet safely instead. “Strange how our parents once worried about us crossing the road. Now we worry about them crossing the internet,” he wrote. He later added, “Earlier, the biggest risk was buying the wrong thing. Today, it's agreeing to something you didn't fully understand. AutoPay mandates, app permissions, location access, recurring subscriptions.” According to Ahuja, they're all “tiny decisions” made in seconds. However, such decisions may trigger something for a longer period. “Digital literacy is no longer just about knowing how to use technology. It's also about knowing what you've agreed to,” he added. Lokesh Ahuja's LinkedIn post about hidden AutoPay mandates sparked wide engagement. One user agreed, calling free trials a “silent money drain” nationwide. Another user raised similar concerns regarding debit card charges. “Similarly, how many know that all banks provide debit cards and NOT the ATM cards, just because ATM cards are free, while Debit cards get charged about 800 to 1000 per annum. This is a pure theft, as over 60% of people use Debit Cards as ATM Cards only - they never do online transactions using Debit cards,” the user wrote. One user noted that payment pages would often redirect users to AutoPay. She calls it the “worst part” of the transaction. According to one user, people often notice deductions too late. “Even when people do notice, it's only when the transaction for the next month has already happened,” the user wrote. One user suggests automating reminders before trial periods actually end. Another user stresses the shift in generational trust around financial transactions. “The generation before us, our parents, worked on trust. You genuinely believed people and transacted. Our generation has grown up with mistrust. We are always looking around to see who will take us for a ride,” the user added. input.title: Smart Money Shift: FIIs Raised Stakes in 15 Large Caps as Lenskart Led the Buying
input.content:
Quick Snapshot
- FIIs raised holdings in 41 BSE largecap companies in the June 2026 quarter; 18 of them already have double-digit CY2026 gains, and 15 have full quarter-on-quarter FII disclosure with returns of 15%–49%.
- Lenskart Solutions saw the sharpest jump in foreign ownership, FII holding rose 850 basis points, from 4.26% to 12.76%, between March and June 2026.
- FIIs pumped over Rs 15,157 crore (~$1.8 billion) into Indian equities in the first weeks of July 2026, reversing roughly $30 billion in outflows from January–May, partly driven by money rotating out of AI-led rallies in Korea and Taiwan.
- Adani Power posted the biggest CY26 price gain at 49%, but its FII holding rose just 3 basis points — showing price momentum and institutional accumulation didn’t move together for every stock.
- IndusInd Bank’s Q1 FY27 net profit rose 72% year-on-year to Rs 1,037 crore as FII stake climbed to 29.17%, even as mutual fund holding eased over the same period, per Tijori Finance data.
- Q2 FY27 earnings, due from mid-October 2026, along with the AI-trade rotation and crude oil/rate trends, will be the next test for these flows.
FIIs Widen Bets on 15 Largecaps, but the Accumulation Story Is Elsewhere
FIIs increased their holdings in 41 BSE largecap companies during the June 2026 quarter compared with March 2026, according to ACE Equity data cited by ETMarkets. Of these, 18 companies have already delivered double-digit CY2026 returns, and 15 of them, the ones with full quarter-on-quarter FII disclosure, posted gains ranging from 15% to 49%.
A closer read of the same shareholding data shows the stocks with the biggest share-price rallies were not necessarily where FIIs added the most capital.
NiftyTrader Desk’s analysis of the underlying holding-percentage shifts shows Lenskart Solutions, Billionbrains Garage Ventures (Groww), and Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone (APSEZ) recorded the sharpest increases in FII ownership, a distinction that matters more for tracking institutional conviction than headline price gains alone.
Track live foreign and domestic institutional flows on the FII-DII Tracker.
Where FII Ownership Actually Rose the Most
Lenskart’s FII holding climbed 850 basis points, from 4.26% in March 2026 to 12.76% in June 2026 — the largest jump among the 15 stocks tracked. Independent shareholding trackers, including Kotak Neo, corroborate FII ownership in Lenskart at roughly 12.8% as of June 2026, close to the ACE Equity figure.
Groww’s parent, Billionbrains Garage Ventures, saw FII holding rise 438 basis points, from 2.51% to 6.89%, also broadly confirmed by Kotak Neo shareholding data at 6.9% for June 2026. APSEZ’s FII stake rose 233 basis points, from 13.25% to 15.58%, the third-sharpest increase in the group.
By contrast, Adani Power — the top price gainer at 49% YTD — saw FII holding inch up just 3 basis points (11.73% to 11.76%), and Adani Total Gas, up 15% YTD, saw a 2-basis-point rise. This gap between price performance and institutional stake-building suggests some of the year’s biggest rallies were driven more by retail and momentum buying than fresh FII conviction.
Why FIIs Turned Buyers in This Cohort
FIIs pumped more than Rs 15,157 crore, or roughly $1.8 billion, into Indian equities in the opening weeks of July 2026, according to NSDL data cited by Republic World — a sharp reversal after nearly Rs 2.3 lakh crore, or about $30 billion, in outflows between January and May.
Separate estimates from Jefferies put net FII buying at $1.8 billion through July 15, the first monthly net purchase since February, according to the brokerage’s Global Head of Equity Strategy Christopher Wood.
Wood attributed part of the reversal to money rotating out of AI-driven rallies in Korea and Taiwan and back into undervalued Indian largecaps, noting that a bigger, sustained return of foreign capital would require either the AI trade to cool further or Indian valuations to fall more sharply.
Separately, Republic World reported that blue-chip valuations had corrected 11%–15% from their highs, and that easing geopolitical risk and softer crude oil prices had also improved sentiment, citing Motilal Oswal Financial Services.
Company-specific catalysts played a role too. IndusInd Bank’s Q1 FY27 net profit rose 72% year-on-year to Rs 1,037 crore with improving asset quality, Outlook Business reported, and MD & CEO Rajiv Anand described the quarter as a “clear inflection point” after the bank’s 2025 accounting-lapse crisis, per Business Today.
Adani Ports handled 138.1 million tonnes of cargo in Q1 FY27, up 15% year-on-year, Business Today reported, supporting the stock’s FII accumulation. For Lenskart and Groww, both still within roughly a year of their public listings, rising FII stakes reflect growing institutional comfort with post-IPO earnings visibility.
Where DIIs Stand
Domestic institutional investors, mutual funds, insurers, and pension funds, have broadly continued to act as a buying cushion through 2026 via steady SIP and mutual fund inflows. However, DII behaviour within this specific 15-stock cohort was not uniform.
In IndusInd Bank’s case, mutual fund holding eased to 25.36% in the latest quarter from 27.55% previously, per Tijori Finance shareholding data, even as FII holding rose, pointing to a divergence between foreign and domestic fund managers on the stock’s recovery trajectory.
March vs June 2026: FII Holding Shift, CY26 Returns, and Key Triggers
Source: ACE Equity data via ETMarkets; ranked by FII holding change, not price return.
NiftyTrader Desk View
Check Live:
What Traders Are Watching Next
- Q2 FY27 earnings, due from mid-October 2026, will test whether IndusInd Bank’s recovery and Adani Ports’ cargo growth continue.
- Lenskart and Groww face post-listing lock-in expiries and valuation scrutiny as FII stakes climb from a low base.
- Adani Green Energy’s renewable capacity addition pace and PPA signings remain a watch point for sustaining its 37% YTD gain.
- Vodafone Idea’s AGR dues relief and government equity conversion outcomes stay the key swing factors.
- The Korea-Taiwan AI trade rotation and crude oil/global rate trajectories, which drove July’s FII reversal, could just as easily fade or reverse if conditions shift.
Track live foreign and domestic institutional flows on the FII-DII Tracker.
Bottom Line
The June 2026 quarter’s FII data offers more nuance than a simple list of price gainers. Lenskart, Groww, and Adani Ports saw the deepest institutional stake-building, while some of CY26’s biggest rallies, including Adani Power’s 49% run, saw barely any change in FII ownership.
With Q2 FY27 earnings, a still-fragile global rotation out of AI trades, and rate cues ahead, the direction of both FII and DII flows in this cohort will matter more than the headline returns already booked.

input.title: Sun Pharma partner Philogen resubmits Nidlegy application in Europe
input.content:
- Pharma Industry
- 2 min read
Sun Pharma partner Philogen resubmits Nidlegy application in Europe
                    The revised application includes additional Chemistry, Manufacturing and Controls (CMC) information intended to address the outstanding questions raised during the previous procedure.
                                    
            
        
                    
                    
                    
                                        Mumbai: Sun Pharma’s supply partner Philogen has announced to have submitted an updated Marketing Authorization Application (MAA) to the European Medicines Agency (EMA). for the approval of onco-derma therapy, Nidlegy (daromun) in Europe.
The company is seeking approval for treatment of adult patients with locally advanced, fully resectable melanoma.
Compared with the MAA submitted in June 2024, the updated dossier carries longer median patient follow-up data of its pivotal Phase 3 trial (PHL19IL2TNF-02/15) of 33 months as opposed to 21 months and includes additional post hoc analyses focused on event-free survival.
Further it also includes additional Chemistry, Manufacturing and Controls (CMC) information intended to address the outstanding questions raised during the previous procedure.
Sun Pharma holds exclusive rights to commercialize the drug across Europe, Australia, and New Zealand. Under the agreement, the two companies will share post-commercialization profit on 50:50 basis..
Philogen is responsible for the product's clinical development, regulatory filings, and manufacturing. The Italy-based drugmaker had retained the drug’s IP ownership and option to explore it for indications other than skin cancers.
Financial terms of the licensing agreement were not disclosed by Sun Pharma at the time of the announcement in 2023.
“Since the previous MAA procedure, our team has worked intensively to address the clinical and CMC questions raised during the review. We are encouraged by the data generated to date and have launched additional registrational studies in non-melanoma skin cancers,” said Prof. Dr. Dario Neri, CEO Philogen.
Nidlegy is a targeted immunotherapy which contains two active ingredients — L19IL2 and L19TNF.
The L19 antibody binds to the Extra Domain B of Fibronectin, a protein expressed in tumors but absent in most healthy tissues and delivers the two pro-inflammatory cytokines— IL-2 and TNF directly to the tumor site to disrupt tumor cells growth and trigger immune response.
In the trial, patients treated with the drug after surgery, demonstrated 41 per cent lower risk of relapse or death compared with those who underwent surgery alone.
Nidlegy is investigated in two Phase 3 clinical trials for the treatment of locally advanced melanoma, and in Phase 2 clinical trials for the treatment of High-Risk Basal Cell Carcinoma and other non-melanoma skin cancers.
According to the Phase2 Duncan study topline results presented at the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) in 2025, against basal cell carcinoma (BCC) and cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC) – types of non-melanoma skin cancer — the drug reported complete pathological responses in 52.6 per cent of patients.
                        
                                                                
                                        
                    
                    
                                            
                                        
                    
                    
                        
                    
                    
                
            The company is seeking approval for treatment of adult patients with locally advanced, fully resectable melanoma.
Compared with the MAA submitted in June 2024, the updated dossier carries longer median patient follow-up data of its pivotal Phase 3 trial (PHL19IL2TNF-02/15) of 33 months as opposed to 21 months and includes additional post hoc analyses focused on event-free survival.
Further it also includes additional Chemistry, Manufacturing and Controls (CMC) information intended to address the outstanding questions raised during the previous procedure.
Sun Pharma holds exclusive rights to commercialize the drug across Europe, Australia, and New Zealand. Under the agreement, the two companies will share post-commercialization profit on 50:50 basis..
Philogen is responsible for the product's clinical development, regulatory filings, and manufacturing. The Italy-based drugmaker had retained the drug’s IP ownership and option to explore it for indications other than skin cancers.
Financial terms of the licensing agreement were not disclosed by Sun Pharma at the time of the announcement in 2023.

input.title: Nykaa appoints former Instamart COO Ankit Jain to lead NYKAA NOW
input.content:
Indian beauty retailer Nykaa has appointed Ankit Jain to lead NYKAA NOW, its quick-commerce business, as the company expands its fulfilment and supply-chain operations.
Jain has more than 20 years of experience in supply chain and operations. He has previously worked at Unilever, Flipkart and Swiggy-owned Instamart, where he served as chief operating officer.
In his new role, Jain will oversee the expansion of NYKAA NOW across key markets and work to strengthen Nykaa’s fulfilment network through AI-led demand forecasting and logistics innovation.
NYKAA NOW promises delivery of beauty and personal-care products within 30 to 60 minutes. The service operates in 13 cities, including Mumbai, Delhi, Bengaluru and Kolkata.
Nykaa said it also planned to scale Nykaa Next Day and Nykaa Express as part of its wider fulfilment strategy.
Anchit Nayar, executive director and CEO of Nykaa Beauty, said customers increasingly expected “both speed and choice without compromise”.
“At Nykaa, we are building a differentiated fulfilment ecosystem powered by technology, AI and deep execution excellence. Ankit’s experience in scaling complex supply chain and quick commerce operations makes him uniquely positioned to help us strengthen our network, accelerate NYKAA NOW, and deliver exceptional customer experiences at scale,” he said.
Jain said Nykaa had built a strong foundation by combining consumer trust with innovation and technology.
“I am excited to join the company at a pivotal stage of its growth journey and look forward to building resilient, data-driven operations that enable greater speed, reliability and efficiency across the fulfilment network. Together, we have an opportunity to redefine beauty commerce by making the best beauty brands more accessible to customers across the country,” he said.

input.title: Nykaa Ropes In Ex-Instamart COO Ankit Jain To Helm Nykaa Now
input.content: Ex-Swiggy Instamart COO Ankit Jain has joined beauty and personal care major Nykaa to lead its quick commerce business Nykaa Now. According to his LinkedIn, Jain has joined Nykaa as a business head for Nykaa Now and an executive vice president for supply chain of Nykaa Beauty. The onboarding comes about a month after he exited Swiggy amid a top-deck churn for Instamart. Alongside him, chief business officer (CBO) Hari Kumar also resigned while CEO Amitesh Jha announced today that he would be stepping down and would be replaced by Myntra CEO Nandita Sinha. Prior to joining Swiggy back in May 2025, he held a SVP position at Walmart-backed ecommerce major Flipkart, where he spent nearly six years. Before that, he spent almost 15 years at Unilever. While Instamart onboarded ex-OYO Gautam Swaroop as its CBO days after Kumar's exit, it is yet to announce a replacement for Jain. Jain’s appointment comes as Nykaa aims to double down on quick commerce with Nykaa Now. In the ongoing fiscal year FY27, the BPC major plans to focus on marketing the offering more aggressively, Anchit Nayar, head of the company’s beauty ecommerce business, had said in the company’s Q4 FY26 earnings call. Back then, Nykaa Now had 75-80 dark stores covering almost 90% of pincodes in the top 7 metro cities. Nayar noted that a “meaningful percentage” of Nykaa’s orders in the top cities were already being delivered via Nykaa Now. Notably, Nykaa’s stock has been on a bull run ahead of its Q1 FY27 disclosures. In a filing with the exchanges earlier, the company said that it was expecting the June quarter to be one of its best-performing quarters yet, driven by growth in its beauty vertical and its fashion business picking up. While the beauty business is expected to see growth of over 25% in terms of net sales value (NSV), Nykaa projects over 50% NSV growth in fashion. The company also announced its FY30 growth strategy at its ‘Annual Investor Day 2026’ last month, outlining plans to achieve 2-3X revenue growth, 4-5X EBITDA growth, and over $5 Bn in gross merchandise value (GMV) in the next few years. Shares of Nykaa were trading 1.06% higher at ₹330.05 at 14:52 IST.

input.title: Quote of the day by Nykaa CEO Falguni Nayar: "My mindset was that before I turn 50 I had to start my own business, otherwise..."
input.content:
Falguni Nayar is the founder and CEO of Nykaa. She is a respected business leader and what many find remarkable is that she started the business when she was in her late 40s. For two decades, she worked as a investment banker and she left her high-flying career to finally take the entrepreneurial plunge. Nayar started Nykaa when she was near 50, proving that age is never a barrier to doing bigger and bolder things in life. She's a self-made entrepreneur who inspires so many people out there, especially women looking to take control of their financial and professional futures.
She once said, "My mindset was that before I turn 50 I had to start my own business, otherwise I will never do it. I was 48 at that time. Instead of seeing age as a handicap, I saw it as all the experience that came with it. My professional experience came in very handy. But entrepreneurship is also about learning new things. So I would like to tell women to please educate yourselves and be very open minded." An empowering quote indeed, let's decode what it really means.
What does the quote mean?
A lot of people believe that after a certain age, it is too late to start something new or take big career risks. Falguni Nayar’s quote reminds us that getting older isn't a limitation. An advanced age should actually be seen as a great advantage, for one is more wiser, has more years of real-world experience, wisdom, and skills.
So, instead of waiting for the "perfect time", or feeling intimidated to start something in more advanced stages of life, always remember that one can do anything at any age if there's a will and conviction. Success requires a commitment to continuous learning and self-education, regardless of where you are in life.
How is it relevant today?
Many young and mid-career professionals feel that they must achieve everything in their 20s or 30s. They feel impatient and quite hopeless if they don't see rewards coming soon their way.
Modern career paths are no longer linear; second careers, late-stage startups, and skill resets are becoming common and successful.
Social media often celebrates very young achievers. This explains why people who are older feel that they have been left behind, or are "too late" to the game.
Women in particular often pause, or delay their career ambitions due to family responsibilities, and when they grow older, they make their age an excuse for starting something new.
Continuous learning has become essential today, as industries and technology change rapidly.
Lessons from the quote
Older age should not be seen as a disadvantage. After all, with age comes valuable experience, wisdom, and maturity that young founders often lack.
It is never too late to reinvent yourself or start a brand-new journey.
Prior experience and fresh learning are a powerful combination for success.
Fear of time running out should be used as motivation to act, not as an excuse to give up.
Education and self-belief are the ultimate tools for empowerment, especially for women.
